items.statement: Tata Motors PV CNG penetration increased to 24% with Nexon CNG launch; EV personal segment offtakes up 15% YoY; market share >53% maintained
items.quote: Our multiple powertrain strategy continues to augur well. CNG penetration has now increased to 24% with Nexon CNG being the latest addition to the portfolio. Diesel and EV penetration remains stable.

items.statement: JLR expects VME may rise slightly from 4.2% over next couple of quarters; warranty costs expected to peak and decline; emissions costs may rise in FY26 if US/UK regulations unchanged
items.quote: VME, I think the industry is not showing any signs of becoming less competitive at the moment. So I think there probably is for a couple of quarters a little bit more room to the north on that. On the ﬂip side, I would expect warranty to have peaked at the level that it is this quarter and therefore to start coming down as some of the actions that we start to take in that space come true

items.statement: JLR China market outlook uncertain; jury out on whether cyclical rebound, stagnation or further decline; maintaining cautious dealer inventory levels
items.quote: I think in many regions of the worl d, it is okay. In China, it is not. And we need some time, I think, as the rest of the industry to work out whether what's going on in China is cyclical and it will rebounce, whether it will not rebounce or whether it will go further down from here. I think the jury's out on that. It would be too easy to say it will just rebound. So we are being cautious in

items.statement: Tata Motors demerger progressing; expecting NOC from Stock Exchange and SEBI soon; appointed date targeted July 1, effective date likely October 2025
items.quote: the demerger is progressing well. We are expecting the NOC from the Stock Exchange and SEBI any time now, all ﬁled and done. Operational activities are in an advanced stage and progressing as per plan. And , therefore, we are expecting to have the appointed date as July 1 st. If all goes well in terms of just dates from the honorable NCLT and eﬀective date is likely to be more like October this ye

items.statement: Q3 is peak tea margin pressure; expect easing from Q4 as price hikes flow through
items.quote: I think Q3 would be the peak of the pressure. Given that we've taken significant or decent amount of hikes as well. I think we would start to see the margin pressure ease off going forward.

items.statement: Tea margin pressure to continue till end of Q1 or early Q2 FY26 until new flush arrives
items.quote: We do expect this pressure t o continue till probably end of Q1, early Q2 until the new fl ush comes in, assuming that it will be normal

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA flat YoY due to tea margin pressure; normalized margins would have expanded 75-100 bps
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA was flat, primarily as a result of the tea margin pressure. Assuming India Tea margins were at the Q3 FY '24 level, our overall EBITDA margin for the quarter would have expanded at least 75 to 100 bps.

items.statement: Calibrated tea price increases cover ~40% of cost inflation; 60% gap remains
items.quote: We've taken calibrated price increases across the tea portfolio, probably compensated for about 40% of the tea price increase. The 60% is still out there.

items.statement: India Beverages volume grew 7% in Q3; mid-single-digit growth guided for medium term
items.quote: Packaged Beverages India volume up 7%, net revenue up 10%, marginal movement on market share.

items.statement: Growth businesses (Sampann, Soulfull, Capital Foods, Organic India) grew 89% and now contribute 27% of portfolio
items.quote: We have guided for 30% of our businesses being growth businesses growing at 30%. We grew at 89%, and now they will contribu te to 27% of our portfolio

items.statement: No commercial terms (royalty, investment) in Kurkure-Ching's partnership; only A&P spend by both parties
items.quote: We will put in a little bit of money on A&P. Pepsi will put in a little bit of money on A&P. But if your question i s, is there a commercial angle to this, is there a royalty, is there this thing? No, there is none

items.statement: Food services pilot done in 2 cities, expanding to 16 cities; pharma pilot in 10 cities, expanding to 40 cities
items.quote: Food services, we piloted in 2 cities. We are going to be in 16 next year. We are already in the phase of rolling out to 16. Pharma, we piloted in 10 cities, we're going to be in 40 next year.

items.statement: Coffee prices at 50-year highs (Robusta $5,400, Arabica $3.50); non-branded margins depend on demand impact triggering pricing
items.quote: You are right, coffee prices, sorry, yes, 5,400 and $3.5, right? Robusta and Arabica. These are 50-year highs. Not sure, I mean, where it is going from here. We remain very, very cautious on the inventory front, not wanting to be too long on the commodity.

items.statement: RTD volume grew 14% in Q3, December exit volume growth 39%; revenue down 2% due to re-indexed pricing
items.quote: Ready-to-drink portfolio, I'd point you to the left side graph where we had said that we will bring the trajectory back. Volume grew 39% for the month of December. Yes, value w as slightly down because we hav e re-indexed our pricing to be competitive in the market. 14% volume growth for the quarter, close to INR 160 crores of revenue

items.statement: International margins structural in UK/Canada; US improving via K-Cups, availability, key accounts, in-house sales team
items.quote: K., of course, we talked about it earlier. We did a lot of structural interventions, which are playing out now. U.S. margins are actually lower and largely... Sunil D’Souza: Improved. Ashish Goenka: Improved versus last year because overall coffee impact has not been that material in that market

items.statement: Tea input costs locked in for next 2 quarters; margin recovery depends on market pricing and new crop
items.quote: Since there are no fresh teas available, I think that input costs are pretty much locked in for the next 2 quarters. So, a large part of it will depend upon how the market prices move and b, how the tea season opens...

items.statement: Split route implementation started at quarter end; vacancies remain, retailer confidence and execution will take time to build
items.quote: split route implementation, I think by the time we got implementing it was end of the quarter, I think we're still -- there are still certain percentage of vacancies that I see on a daily basis. I think that's fully not there, A. Jay a nd the second thing is, I think putting in the salesperson is the easier part. Getting the confidence of the r etailers, getting the product knowledge up, building

items.quote: For India business, we are maintaining the volume growth guidance. And in accordance with how the volumes would be available to us, our sales would grow. And we are maintaining that even now

items.statement: ABS expansion Phase 1 of 50 KT by mid-2026, Phase 2 another 50 KT ahead of schedule

items.quote: We still believe and hold on to that number with some margin of error. However, we do believe in terms of ABS and SAN, t he investment outlay could be to the tune of about Rs. 500 crores. And for polystyrene, to the tune of about Rs. 150 crores

items.statement: Thailand plant at 55-60% utilization, 74 KT sales in CY24, capacity 125 KT net of SAN for ABS
items.quote: Ineos did about 74,000 tonnes of sales last y ear in the calendar year. So, overall, if you look at ABS and SAN and exclude the SAN used for ABS, the total capacity would be to tune of 125,000 tonnes

items.statement: Q3 margins lower due to higher PS mix and normalization of Q2 extraordinary gains; spreads intact year-on-year
items.quote: the margins in the second quarter, which was in September were a little bit higher on account of some extraordinary gains we had in that quarter. There were certain supply chain disruptions in that quarter on account of certain freights, which I had alluded to in the last call as well, those have normalized. So, those margins would not be the good benchmark to take . B ut if you consider year-on-y

items.statement: PS:GPPS:HIPS ratio shifted to 65:35; PS ~40% of volumes to consumer durables
items.quote: In terms of GP and kind of high impact polystyrene, we were running at about 50:50, today the ratio might be close to kind of 65:35 where 65% could be a general-purpose polystyrene and 35% would be high impact polystyrene.

items.statement: Q4 expected to be average based on historical industry trends
items.quote: We expect Q4 to be average based on historical industry trends.

items.statement: Global ABS/PS spreads deteriorated in last two quarters; India spreads better than global
items.quote: overall, the spreads have in fact deteriorated in the last two quart ers. They were very low of course in FY ’24, they slightly improved in FY ’25 in the first quarter, but they have in fact deteriorated in the last two quarters. If you look at the spreads in India versus the global spreads, Indian spreads are much better or at least our spreads are much better

items.statement: Thailand acquisition completed Jan 17, 2025 for $22M; no major capex planned currently
items.quote: Styrenix entered a SPA with Ineos Styrolution Group GmbH on 9th of December, '24, for acquiring 100% shareholding of any of Ineos Styrolution (Thailand) Co., Limited, located in Thailand. The acquisition transaction has been successfully completed on 17th of January, 2025.

items.statement: Odisha facility expansion is on track and will raise combined capacity from 3.52 crore to 3.82 crore cases.
items.quote: Currently we are at 35.2 million cases, that's 3.52 crore cases combined capacity. And after the Odisha's capacity comes on stream, the capacity will rise up to 3.82 crore cases.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 12.5% delivered in Q3 and nine months FY25; management expects to maintain similar margins going forward.
items.quote: I think this year we have delivered more EBITDA margin as compared to last year. So, I think we should be able to maintain these kind of margins going forward.

items.statement: Management is optimistic about the upcoming summer season and targets high-potential markets including UP, Rajasthan, Delhi, Jharkhand, and the Northeast.
items.quote: We remain optimistic about the upcoming summer season and the opportunity it presents for growth. We are heavily focused on expanding our footprint in high potential markets, such as UP, Rajasthan, Delhi, Jharkhand, and the Northeast.

items.statement: Capacity utilization for nine months: SDBL 73%, Woodpecker 65%, Odisha 64%; lean season: SDBL 58%, Hassan 60%, Odisha 34%.
items.quote: Production capacity of all facilities was significantly utilized during nine months, where SDBL stood at 73%, Woodpecker stood at 65%, and the unit at Odisha stood at 64%. In the lean season, our capacity utilization stood at the following, which is 58% for SDBL, 60% for Hassan, and 34% for the Odisha plant.

items.statement: Confident of delivering 12% EBITDA margin in Q4 FY25 exit quarter
items.quote: As promised earlier, for a 12% EBITDA for exit quarter, I am quite confident that we will deliver this promise.

items.statement: Targeting 15% EBITDA margin for FY26 with higher brand spend
items.quote: FY26, I always said that we should be able to do 15%, by spending more on the brand because whatever initiatives we are doing today, if you see brand visibility is low, most of the spend what we are doing today is on the performance marketing in e-commerce.

items.statement: Guiding for 50% gross margin in Q4 FY25 exit quarter and 52-53% in FY26
items.quote: In exit quarter, I guided for 50% which I am still guiding for.

items.statement: Moderate capex of Rs. 32-35 crore incurred in 9M FY25
items.quote: Remaining is in the cash to cash equivalent.

items.statement: Bangladesh capacity utilization at 60% in Q3, expected to reach 85% with upright production start
items.quote: For the quarter three our utilization was at 60%, it is profitable because we have done quite a lot of work in reducing the overall cost there, including manpower, because manpower is the largest cost.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 150 bps sequentially in Q3; 3% of Q4 EBITDA improvement from gross margin, balance from operating leverage
items.quote: The gross margin improved by 150 bps, giving confidence on various initiatives which are underway, further cementing on this front.

items.statement: Implemented MOP for VIP brand across all channels to protect offline business; no discounting on VIP products
items.quote: That is in place for VIP. So if you see VIP, it is sold at a MOP, which is the minimum price at which they cannot sell below that, so it's an MOP now for any product of VIP across all the channels, there is no discounting.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow 8-10%; volume growth to translate to value growth next year as liquidation impact reduces
items.quote: I would say may be industry growth, and industry is expected to grow 8% to 10%, so that is the kind of growth you can consider at this point of time.

items.statement: Hard luggage share at 63% of revenue; Carlton salience increasing with 25 new exclusive stores planned in 6 months
items.quote: Hard luggage continues to be the fastest growing category, having share of 63% in the overall performance.

items.statement: Intense competition in hard luggage from new D2C entrants; pricing pressure may be new normal
items.quote: In fact, I believe that every six months there is one new player entering into this market, but which also gives us the confidence that the market is doing well, and therefore so many entrants.

items.statement: No equity infusion planned; debt reduced by Rs. 87 crore in 9M FY25; short-term borrowing rating unchanged
items.quote: If you look into it our short term borrowing rating remains the same at the highest level. It's the long term which was impacted and today we are having all the working capital loans having the short term in nature.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by Rs. 224 crore in 9M FY25 to Rs. 692 crore; slow-moving inventory at Rs. 80-100 crore; target Rs. 500-550 crore by June 2025
items.quote: We have reduced our inventory overall by Rs. 224 crore. If I have to talk about the slow moving, it is in the range of around Rs. 80 to Rs. 100 crore now and hopefully this should be meaningfully reduced in quarter four.

items.statement: BCG project targeting Rs. 250 crore bottom-line improvement; 50% complete with full-year impact in FY26
items.quote: The project is to add Rs. 250 crore to the bottom line in a nutshell. We are 50% through, and it's working around, so basically, increase gross margin, reduce cost, supply chain, secondary freight across all areas.

items.statement: Market share at 38%, gained 2% in last year; targeting stable 40% then further 1-2% increase
items.quote: As we said, definitely in last one year we have gained 2% market share, but we are still below the industry growth, that is something where we want to do better than industry, and that is the only part where the market share can go up.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of ~Rs. 200 crore generated in 9M FY25; used for debt prepayment, interest, and capex
items.quote: If I look from the operating cash flow perspective, it is around Rs. 200 odd crore we generated in the period of nine months, and the utilization of that is towards our prepayment of the debt VIP Industries Limited – 29th January, 2025 to the tune of Rs. 86 to Rs. 87 crore, interest and some moderate CAPEX we incur of Rs. 32 to Rs. 35 crore

items.statement: Plan to add 50 stores in next 12 months, focusing on top 20 cities; current store count at 410
items.quote: We want to increase by 50 stores in next 12 months, and to start we will be focusing mostly on the top 20 cities.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 246 bps YoY to 53.1% in Q3 FY25 due to elevated raw material costs for butyl reclaim and fixed quarterly/annual pricing preventing cost pass-through.
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter were 53.1%, a decline of 246 bps on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins to stabilize and return to normal historical levels as product mix optimization and revised pricing effective January 1st offset raw material cost increases.
items.quote: However, looking ahead, a strategic optimization of the product mix as well as the reversion and the pricing for customers, which is now effective January 1st, is expected to help offset the rise in the raw material costs. And our gross margin will stabilize and return to the normal levels that we've seen in the past.

items.statement: Shareholders approved raising additional INR 150 crores via QIP of equity shares to fund expansion of tyre recycling ecosystem.
items.quote: Furthermore, I'm pleased to announce that our shareholders have also approved the raising of an additional INR 150 crores through the issuance of equity shares via a qualified institutional placement.

items.statement: Domestic reclaim rubber consumption grew ~10% in H1 FY25 vs overall rubber consumption growth of 3%, indicating increased adoption in tyre and non-tyre segments.
items.quote: The consumption of the Reclaim Rubber in the country has gone up by about 10% during the first half of FY '25 against an overall rubber consumption growth of 3%.

items.statement: New higher-grade reclaim rubber line volumes growing month-on-month but utilization sub-50% pending tyre company approvals expected within this or next quarter; non-tyre segment showing promise.
items.quote: However, we still don't have any significant tyre company approvals for that at the moment. So therefore, while we have started supplying from there, the utilization levels are currently sub 50%, but we are expecting approvals to come through either within this or the next quarter, which will allow us to improve dramatically the utilization levels there.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on virgin butyl rubber imposed in September 2024 increased butyl tube waste prices (key raw material), and fixed quarterly/annual pricing contracts prevented immediate cost pass-through, significantly reducing gross margins
items.quote: Since our pricing for customers is fixed on a quarterly basis and in some cases, even annual basis, some of the higher costs were not able to be passed on to the customers as a result of which we have seen a significant reduction in the gross margins as far as GRP is concerned.

items.statement: EPR credits stock valued at ~INR 180 million at minimum support price as of Dec 2024; INR 121 million income recognized YTD FY25 from credit sales; sales timing depends on tyre industry buying patterns.
items.quote: As of December 2024, the stock of EPR credits now that there is a floor price and now that there is more visibility and transparency on the price mechanism, those credits calculated at the minimum support price adjusted for transaction costs is valued at a pproximately INR 180 million

items.statement: Employee costs reduced from 12.5% to 11.2% YoY in Q3 due to automation; renewable power saved INR 0.5 crore vs grid; biofuel switch saved cumulative INR 2.5 crores YTD.
items.quote: Automation initiatives have enabled us to optimize workforce utilization and reduce manpower costs while maintaining productivity levels. And as a result, our employee costs have come down from about 12.5% to about 11.2% (factually corrected) during the quarter on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Repurpose polyolefins subsidiary gaining major brand approvals (paints, lubricants, FMCG, white goods, automotive OEMs); operating at suboptimal capacity pending April 1, 2025 recycled plastics mandate; expected turnaround post-regulation.
items.quote: As we expect that the demand will shoot up post March, April of this year once the regulation kicks in, the utilizations will improve, and therefore, the business will not continue to bleed or make losses.

items.statement: EPR credits currently trading near floor price of INR 2.52/kg (ceiling INR 8.4/kg) as most credits are for 70% requirement year; base and ceiling prices set by regulation.
items.quote: the business at the base price is set at INR 2.52, and the ceiling is set at INR 8.4 a kg. Currently, most of the credits that are being bought are of the year where the requirement was 70%. So therefore, they're trading closer to the floor prices at the moment.

items.statement: Plastic recycling business expected to be high fixed asset turnover with lower EBITDA margin but better ROCE than current business; margin clarity depends on pace of recycled plastics mandate implementation from April 1, 2025.
items.quote: it will be a high fixed asset turn business with a lower EBITDA margin, but generate an ROCE, which will be better than the current ROCE of the business.

items.statement: Iron ore dispatches for FY25 expected at 10 million tons
items.quote: Yes, that's pretty correct.

items.statement: Iron ore production target of 25 million tons in FY26 after EC approval
items.quote: We are fully mobilized to mine and dispatch 25 million tons with the expectation that the EC shall be received in time by the end of this current quarter.

items.statement: FY28 iron ore mix of 10 million tons DSO and 15 million tons beneficiated ore
items.value: 10 million tons DSO and 15 million tons beneficiated
items.quote: In the year FY '28, the mix would be 10 million tons of DSO and 15 million tons of beneficiated ore.

items.statement: Capex spent INR 2,700 crores in 9M FY25 and INR 4,400 crores total to date
items.quote: On the capex front, the company has spent INR2,700 crores in the 9 months FY '25 and a total of INR4,400 crores till date.

items.statement: Capex target INR 5,000 crores by FY25 end and INR 6,000-6,500 crores annually for next 2 years
items.quote: In terms of capex, we should be doing around INR5,000 crores by this year's end. That has to be done around INR4,400 crores, so we should be reaching around INR 5,000 crores by this year end. And going forward in the next 2 years, yes, we should be doing more than that at around INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores every year of capex to achieve all these projects of ours.

items.statement: Iron ore sales of 10 million tons for FY25 largely contracted
items.quote: Most of our material is sold for this year of 10 million tons.

items.statement: Iron ore EBITDA per ton INR 2,021 in Q3 FY25, up 21% YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA per ton for quarter 3 FY '25 was INR 2,021, marking a 21% year -on-year increase.

items.statement: MDO integration expected to yield INR 400-500 per ton cost savings from April 2025
items.quote: So, the entire business comes into this company from 1st April 2025. So, it will be for the next financial year.

items.statement: No price cuts taken in December-January; 10 million tons sold for FY25
items.quote: Price cut. We haven't taken any price cut. Most of our material is sold for this year of 10 million tons. So, we don't see any price cut on the anvil.

items.statement: Steel demand growing 7-9% but oversupply pressuring DRI realizations
items.quote: The demand is still 7%, 8%, 9% growth.

items.statement: Long-term vision: 25 million tons iron ore, 10 million sold, 15 million converted to ~4.5 million tons steel and pellets
items.quote: So out of 25 million, around 10 million will be sold . Balance will be converted into steel and selling around 4.5 million tons of steel and rest will be semi-products, and around 15 million tons will be sold as pellets or iron ore, mostly pellets.

items.statement: EC approval process takes 60-70 days after public hearing; worst case expectation
items.quote: The whole process, should take 60 to 70 days, to complete.

items.statement: BHQ beneficiation plant first phase (15 million tons) targeted for FY27 commissioning
items.quote: And physically, we feel '27 the first phase would be completed.

items.statement: Future fundraises expected for both Lloyds Metals and Thriveni entities
items.quote: There would be some fundraises in both the companies.

items.statement: Revenue target INR 40,000 crores by FY28-29 excludes MDO revenue; MDO revenue over and above
items.quote: It'll be over and above.

items.statement: Renewable power tied up at INR 4.50-4.75/unit vs grid cost INR 8.50/unit
items.quote: So, the landed cost of this power is around INR4.50- INR4.75 per unit. And the landing cost of MSEDCL cost is around INR8.50, number one.

items.statement: Wholesale loan book expected to run down completely in next 12-15 months, faster than earlier 4-year estimate
items.quote: I think the whole rundown may happen in the next 12 to 15 months, so a lot faster compared to what we had thought.

items.statement: ARC business will only do syndicated deals (2.5%-15% commitment) and retail NPA resolution; no turnaround risk
items.quote: So, we're going to stop the financing o f projects or takeover of assets where we have to be responsible for the turnaround

items.statement: AMC business burn phase to continue 2-2.5 years; breakeven expected at INR20,000-25,000 crores equity AUM
items.quote: And once we cross around INR20,000 crores to INR25,000 crores of equity, we should reach breakeven and build out from that.

items.statement: Private credit syndication targets INR3,000 crores steady-state book earning 400-500 bps spread plus fees
items.quote: you should model anywhere between a 400 to 500 basis points spread on the capital that we should be able to deploy, including fees.

items.statement: Cash surplus of INR3,500-4,000 crores in mutual funds to be deployed into syndication, loan against shares and margin trade finance
items.quote: we have probably INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores in mutual funds, which is earning a lower yield and it should be a much higher yield once we start deploying that cash into the syndication side.

items.statement: Investment banking pipeline strong with close to two dozen DRHPs filed and equal number being filed
items.quote: We have close to two dozen DRHPs filed, subject to market conditions, we should be able to launch them, and we are also in the process of filing an equal amount of DRHPs.

items.statement: Wholesale real estate provision coverage increased to 93% from 54% as of March 2024
items.quote: The provision coverage ratio on the real estate loan book has increased from 54% as of March 31, 2024 to 93% as of December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Overall gross NPA provision coverage increased to 84% from 70% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The provision coverage ratio on the overall gross NPA to increase from 70% to 84% as of December 2024.

items.statement: Affordable home loan balance transfer rate at 1% per month (12% annualized), down from 1.5% per month last year
items.quote: BT rate continues to be 1% a month. It was last year, 1.5% a month, meaning 18% a year was a BT out. That has come down a bit.

items.statement: Real estate demand remains strong; inventory rise is mostly new launches, not ready inventory; larger players gaining market share
items.quote: But having said that, I think the demand for real estate still remains strong. A lot of the inventory that comes as total inventory in terms of calculation is not ready inventory, it's new launches.

items.statement: SEBI margin finance book grew 38% YoY to ~INR2,100 crores; loan against shares restarted with INR600 crores disbursed last quarter
items.quote: Our SEBI margin finance book sa w an increase of 38% Y -o-Y with approximately INR2,100 crores, and our mutual fund AUM grew 3x and is now approximately INR13,800 crores

items.statement: Wholesale real estate NPAs stable at INR685 crores; 50% expected resolution this calendar year, balance next calendar year
items.quote: in almost 50% of the portfolio, we are pretty much in advanced stage. So, when I say advanced stages, we should see resolution this calendar year. And in the balance, 50%, we should see it in the following calendar year.

items.statement: ARC provisions only on 6-monthly review cycle (Sep/Mar); no significant additional provisioning expected beyond standard requirements
items.quote: We don't have significant assets that require more provision because we have taken a lot of the upfront provision where we felt there will be weakness in the recovery in the March quarter of last year itself.

items.statement: RBI approval received for ARC purchase; awaiting approval to take 90% control of Credit Solutions (currently 46%)
items.quote: We already have the RBI approval to buy the ARC in the Credit Solutions. And we are hoping that this quarter, RBI will give us the approvals to take control of Credit Solutions and have 90% ownership.

items.statement: FY25 CapEx guidance INR 50 crore; 72-75% achieved by Q3 (INR 36 crore assets); FY26 CapEx planned INR 100 crore funded by debt and internal accruals
items.quote: We have a very ambitious CapEx of INR 100 crores for the next financial year. But see, honestly, when we started this CapEx journey, even a INR 50 crores CapEx was a very aggressive thing which we had claimed. But as you can see in our P &L reports, the segmented assets, we have achieved INR 36 crores of assets by Q3 only. So , we are 72%, 75% done with our CapEx for this financial year.

items.statement: Current machine order book INR 25-30 crore to be fulfilled in Q4 FY25, pushing CapEx above FY25 guidance
items.quote: In terms of machine values, we already have around INR 25-30 crores of machine orders, which we have to fulfill in this quarter. So , this shall take our CapEx above our guidance for this financial year.

items.statement: Crane rental yield 2.2-2.3%/month on gross block (revenue 2.7-2.85%); man-lifter yield 2.65-2.75%/month (revenue 3.7-3.9%); blended annual revenue yield 29-34%
items.quote: the cranes generally give us a base rental yield of 2.2% per month on the gross block and the ma n-lifters generally give us a rental yield of around 2.65-2.7% EBITDA margins on the gross block. So, if you see, we are able to generate revenue of around 2.7-2.8% on a monthly basis and the EBITDAs are left with us are 2.2% in the cranes. Man-lifters we are able to generate revenues of around 3.7-3.9

items.statement: Receiving 10-15 machine requirements daily; expects massive demand boom for next 10-15 years driven by blue-chip client capacity expansions (Tata, Jindal, etc.)
items.quote: We are getting requirements of 10-15 machines every single day. And honestly, I personally feel as a business owner and seeing the on-ground stuff, which is happening in India, the next 10-15 years there is going to be a massive boom in this industry, not only for us, but also for other players.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 60 days; bill discounting available with blue-chip clients; depreciation on SLM over 7-8 years; Q3 fleet utilization 100%
items.quote: Generally, our working capital requirement is of 60 days. If you go to any subcontractor, their payment generally comes in 5 to 6 months. items.statement: Company is net cash with INR 176 crores cash balance; no borrowings after IPO proceeds matured in October.
items.quote: Our cash position at this point of time is INR176 crores.

items.statement: Three active acquisition conversations ongoing (one large, two smaller); no guarantee of closure; organic growth target of 15-20% excludes inorganic additions.
items.quote: We have 3 active conversations that are going on right now and of varying -- one is a fairly large transaction, the other 2 are slightly smaller.

items.statement: Management expects continued growth acceleration across segments, with flight GTV growing 70%+ and significant headroom given current market share position
items.quote: I think, look, if you had asked this question one year back, I don't think I would have told you that we would grow flight GTV at 70% plus. So I think we've managed to surprise ourselves, and I think I give a Le Travenues Technology Limited - January 28, 2025 lot of credit on that to the hard work of the team, the product, the tech behind the scenes

items.statement: Maha Kumbh driving exceptional demand with passenger segments to Prayagraj growing 4.62x in first 24 days of January vs same period last year
items.quote: Even as of January as we speak, we are continuing to see strong momentum thanks to the Maha Kumbh, the largest congregation of humanity on the planet. Just to share a few statistics with you, our overall passenger segments for Prayagraj in the first 24 days of January alone have grown 4.62 times compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Spiritual tourism showing 100-150% YoY growth in train bookings across multiple destinations
items.quote: In fact, spiritual tourism as an overall vector for growth has shown remarkable potential for us, with many destinations such as Varanasi, Gaya, Shirdi, Puri, Haridwar, Katra, Vaishno Devi recently seeing a 100% to 150% growth in train bookings if one compares year over year.

items.statement: Group contribution margin percentage decreased from 45% to 42% due to growth acceleration investments
items.quote: However, the contribution margin percentage slightly decreased this quarter, from 45% to 42%, due to our investment in accelerating growth, something which Rajnish talked about in detail.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA increased to INR 24.3 crores from INR 19.5 crores, maintaining double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA, excluding other income and ESOP expenses, increased to INR 24.3 crores, up from INR 19.5 crores.

items.statement: Contribution margin mix diversified with trains 39%, buses 33%, flights 27% of group contribution margin
items.quote: Last quarter, if you examine the contribution margin, with all three lines of businesses contributing more evenly in the mix, trains constitute 39%, buses constitute 33%, and flights 27% of the overall contribution margin mix, making ixigo a very well-diversified OTA.

items.statement: Technology costs growing >50% YoY with investments in AI tools, custom-built AI agents, and re-engineering of existing stacks
items.quote: Some of these investments in technology and AI initiatives, it's hard to figure out what kind of impact it will create in the future because if you think about what's happening today in terms of technology, the world is sitting at a

items.statement: GTV crossed INR 4,036.3 crores, up 48% YoY; 9-month YTD EBITDA doubled from INR 34.3 crores to INR 68.2 crores
items.quote: With overall Gross Transaction Value or GTV crossing INR 4036.3 crores this quarter, a 48% increase Y-o-Y and our overall revenue from operations reaching INR 241.8 crores, a 42% increase Y-o-Y for Q3 and a sequential increase of 17% compared to Q2.

items.statement: Flight and bus searches for Prayagraj grew nearly 14x, train searches nearly 10x during Maha Kumbh period
items.quote: Our flight and bus searches have grown nearly 14 times for travel to Prayagraj and train searches nearly 10 times, reflecting exceptionally.

items.statement: Value-added services attached rate at 29.85% last quarter; Travel Guarantee launched with positive initial uptake
items.quote: Value-added services constitute an important part of our business with our attached rate for all value-added services at 29.85% last quarter. On that front, we also launched Travel Guarantee last quarter.

items.statement: Share of loss from associate Fresh Bus was INR 1.9 crores vs INR 2.1 crores loss in Q3 FY24; tax expense shifted from credit to expense due to deferred tax credit reversal
items.quote: Our share of loss from our associate, Fresh Bus, was INR 1.9 crores, compared to a loss of INR 2.1 crores in Q3 FY'24. Tax expenses shifted from a credit of INR 16.7 crores last year, to an expense of INR 5.9 crores this year, largely due to deferred tax credit reversal.

items.statement: Tier 1 to Tier 1 flight passenger segments grew ~68% YoY in Q3; international flight segments grew 61% YoY
items.quote: Tier 1 to Tier 1 flight passenger segments for us have grown with a similar momentum as our NBU flights, bookings over 68% year-on-year Q3, and we have seen our international flight segments growing at 61% year-on-year in Q3.

items.statement: Added 4 State Road Transport Corporations and 200+ private bus operators on AbhiBus in Q3; Abhi Assured operators increased 3x YoY
items.quote: We have also expanded our bus supply with 4 State Road Transport Corporations, or SRTCs, and 200-plus private bus operators being added on AbhiBus in Q3. And the number of our Abhi Assured operators has also gone 3x compared to what it was last year.

items.statement: AI chatbot Tara handling 1.59 million customer queries per quarter end-to-end without human intervention, covering ~92% of chat support reach-outs
items.quote: For the group, Tara is now handling 1.59 million customer queries per quarter end-to-end without any human intervention across the group. This is almost like 92% of all our customer support reach-outs over chat.

items.statement: Monthly active users across ixigo, ConfirmTkt, and AbhiBus crossed 86 million; 31 million passenger segments booked in Q3; 30+ million app downloads
items.quote: Our own data shows that we crossed 86 million monthly active users across ixigo, ConfirmTkt, and AbhiBus, and 31 million passenger segments were booked in Q3. We got over 30 million app downloads last quarter with a growing proportion of our users starting to book flights, buses, trains, and even hotels with us.

items.statement: Average transaction value (ATV) per segment improved nearly 15% to INR 1,282 from INR 1,115 YoY; gross tick rate stable at 7.47%
items.quote: The average transaction value, which I will define here as ATV per segment, is another essential metric. I see that as an indicator of our share of the customer wallet. ATV improved nearly 15% to INR 1,282 crores from INR 1,115 crores year-over-year.

items.statement: Customer inducement costs (discount + branding + performance) targeted around 3.5% of GTV internally, not formal guidance
items.quote: We would look at it as wanting it to be around 3.5%, which is a combination of discount plus branding plus performance.

items.statement: Technology and AI investments plus new hotels vertical build-out will continue for next few quarters, may reduce profit margin by a few percentage points
items.quote: I would still guide for this investment to be there for the next few quarters. And it might take a few percentage points away from the PM that we are generating.

items.statement: Technology costs grown over 50% year-on-year; investments in AI agents for internal efficiency, re-architecting operations, and hotels vertical build-out
items.quote: Some of these investments in technology and AI initiatives, it's hard to figure out what kind of impact it will create in the future because if you think about what's happening today in terms of technology, the world is sitting at an inflection point.

items.statement: Bus bookings to Prayagraj increased almost 14 times year-on-year due to Maha Kumbh; bus growing at twice the velocity of incumbent
items.quote: Prayagraj, which again is in the North, right? I mean, we saw an almost 14 times increase in bus booking Y-o-Y towards Prayagraj, thanks to the Maha Kumbh.

items.statement: Marketing spend focused on conversions and high-quality users; CAC recovered from second transaction; offline spend discretionary within guardrails
items.quote: Most of the marketing acquisition we do from the second transaction itself, we are able to get back the kind of money that we are spending to acquire those users.

items.statement: Hotels business in product-market fit discovery phase; will take few quarters to scale; trains took 10 years to crack
items.quote: I don't think we're going to crack hotels in a year. So in that sense, we are seeing month on month growth. We are seeing quarter on quarter growth there, but of a much smaller base obviously.

items.statement: GTV run rate reached close to 2 billion ARR in less than two years after taking almost 16 years to reach first billion
items.quote: It took us almost 16 years to get to our first billion run rate of GTV, but it has taken us less than two years to get to close to 2 billion GTV ARR.

items.statement: Operational assets of 2,540 MW give run-rate annual EBITDA of INR 1,750-1,800 crores
items.quote: 2,540 MW, which is operational for us will give us a run rate annual project to bid of around INR 1,750 to INR 1,800 crores.

items.statement: Target 6,970 MW operational capacity by FY27-28
items.quote: We will make all efforts to prepone this, but in the base case we have 6,970 MW of capacity which we will be operating by FY'27-28.

items.statement: Pre-tax ROCE at 14.5% from operational assets
items.quote: In terms of the ROCE, which is basically pre-tax ROCE, we do 14.5%.

items.statement: Total contracted portfolio 6.97 GW; won 1,900 MW in FY25 (1,000 MW FDRE, 600 MW solar, 300 MW hybrid)
items.quote: We have won 1,900 MW of capacity in this financial year. So, our total contracted portfolio is 6.97 GW.

items.statement: 350 MW (50 MW wind + 300 MW solar merchant) targeting commissioning in Q4 FY25, worst case April 2025
items.quote: We are doing our best to commission the 350 MW in this quarter. So, that is the intent that 350 MW gets fully commissioned. Of course, we will do our best to try and do that. It may spill over to April, 350 MW in worst case.

items.statement: 1,200 MW project gross block INR 4,600 crores (net of EPC margin)
items.quote: It is INR 4,600 crores. If you, if you look at the, I think the actual CAPEX, so INR 4,600 crores.

items.statement: Management expects around 10% volume growth next financial year with CNG and industrial/commercial as main contributors
items.quote: Now maybe next year, we will not be able to have that much number, but we are comfortable that around 10% numbers we will be able to clock next financial year also and which will be definitely -- CNG will be a main contributor in that growth along with industrial and commercial segment.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated volume growth of 12-13% for FY25 and double-digit growth for FY26
items.quote: If you add on UEPL because it has a small volume, but the growth is much higher there, maybe more plus 20%. So collectively on a consolidated basis, we are around 12% growth as of now, 12% to 12.5%. So in the year-end we expect it to be around 13% or 13.5%. Next year also we definitely should be in -- at least in the double digit, yes.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA per SCM to remain in INR9-12 range depending on LNG prices and contracts
items.quote: So it is not very off the mark of the guidance which we have given about INR10 to INR12. So we expect similar range to continue and depending on the price of LNG, Henry Hub and other contracts. We may be very comfortable in this range, INR9 to INR11 or INR10 to INR12 range.

items.statement: MGL spent INR650+ crores in 9M FY25 and expects INR200-250 crores more in Q4; UEPL to spend INR125-150 crores in FY25 and INR150-200 crores in FY26
items.quote: As far as MGL is concerned, already INR650 crores plus capex has been done in this 9 months period and we expect anywhere between INR200 to INR250 additional capex in Q4 as well. Out of these, major will be on steel and low-pressure pipelines. And roughly INR200 crores or plus, minus 10% on CNG. And balance is on steel grid and LMC, last mile connectivity.

items.statement: UEPL standalone capex guidance: INR125-150 crores for FY25, INR150-200 crores for FY26
items.quote: See, UEPL standalone should spend in the range of around this year, at least INR125 crores to INR150 crores. And it will be further up maybe next year because we have now have the ground and the groundwork is done. So we'll be able to do more capex on CNG stations et cetera. And it could go from INR150 crores to INR200 crores next financial year.

items.statement: Battery JV with IBC: Phase 1 (1 GW) to start revenue in 1.5 years, targeting INR900-1000 crores revenue per GW at 18% IRR
items.quote: is INR1,000 crores revenue will be there, it is around that number or 1 gigawatt factory. Probal Sen: Sorry, sir, INR1,000 crores per gigawatt? Management: Yes, around that number INR900 crores to INR1,000

items.statement: Mumbai High Court order on phasing out diesel/petrol vehicles could drive CNG growth to 15-20% if implemented favorably
items.quote: We can see a growth of around 15% to 20% in case everything goes in favor of CNG.

items.statement: APM gas allocation cut by 7% per annum from April 2025, to be replaced by NWG at NWG prices on pro-rata basis
items.quote: Earlier was the r e-allocation, means two cuts were there. Now in our information, as far as we understand the next r e-allocation or re -adjustments will happen somewhere from 1st of April because around 7% per annum is recommended to be reduced from APM and put into NWG.

items.statement: Forex impact: INR0.22-0.25 per SCM cost increase per rupee depreciation; partially naturally hedged via industrial/commercial pricing linked to alternate fuels
items.quote: Roughly, my estimate is -- yes, you are right in that sense. It adds around INR 0.22 to INR0.25 per rupee increase on our overall company basis, a rough ballpark number.

items.statement: UEPL merger approved by Board Oct 2024, submitted to NCLT Dec 2024, interim order reserved Jan 17 2025
items.quote: A scheme of amalgamation or merger of UEPL with MGL was approved by the Board in October '24 last year and the scheme was submitted to NCLT Mumbai on 6 December, 2024. And the matter was heard by the Mumbai bench on January 17, 2025 and they've reserved the pronouncement of its interim order.

items.statement: Interim dividend of 120% (INR12 per equity share) approved for FY25
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board has approved an interim dividend at the rate of 120% that is INR12 per equity share for the current financial year.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle penetration at 9.5-10% (38,000 of 4 lakh vehicles); potential volume churner if court order implemented
items.quote: Within that, if I take number of commercial vehicles which are mostly on diesel are going to get impacte d initially. And that number is around 4 lakh in our geographies. And currently, we have around 38,000 such commercial vehicles already on CNG which is about 9.5%, 10% penetration.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix: 2+ MMSCMD APM, 1.45 MMSCMD Henry Hub, 0.5 MMSCMD HPHT, 0.1 MMSCMD Brent-linked, small NWG spot
items.quote: As of today, that means in January, we have already tied up Henry Hub contracts, all contracts -- put together around 1.45 mmscmd. HPHT is around 0.5 million, okay? And rest is spot and whatever NWG have.

items.statement: Industrial margins under pressure due to LDO/FO price declines and 10% committed discount to new customers; commercial margins better linked to LPG prices
items.quote: If you look at current industrial margins compared to the last quarter because of the LSHS and LDO prices going down, has gone down slightly. Whereas in case of commercial, where most of the customers are linked to commercial LPG 19 kgs where prices have s lightly gone up, the margin is better.

items.statement: EV battery JV risk mitigated by government protection (like solar), strong Korean partner, local manufacturing edge in lifecycle management
items.quote: We have seen with solar PV cells to promote indigenous PV manufacturing, the government has supported the industry quite a lot. Having said that, we are very much confident that we will be able to source very competitive raw material, lithium-ion and other products, which are required for battery cell manufacturing. We have a very strong partner-- South Korean partner.

items.statement: Guides 20-25% AuM growth long-term; confident of ~20% in FY25 with Jan at 15-20% trajectory
items.quote: We continue to guide on a 20 – 25% of an AuM growth on a long-term basis. I think the traction which we got in the Q3 and the numbers in Jan really give us confidence on delivering the guided AuM growth of ~20.

items.statement: Targets opex-to-assets below 3% with ~20 bps annual reduction; achieved 42 bps YoY improvement to 3.21% in 9MFY25
items.quote: At the beginning of the financial year we have guided that we will bring down opex to assets ratio by ~20 bps every year to reach below 3%. I am happy to report a remarkable improvement in the Opex to Assets ratio by 42 bps Y -o-Y to 3.21% in 9MFY25 as a result of our cost optimisation strategy.

items.statement: Guides credit cost below 25 bps on sustainable basis; 9MFY25 at 15 bps vs 19 bps in 9MFY24
items.quote: We continue to guide credit cost of below 25 bps on sustainable basis.

items.statement: Incremental business yield up 25+ bps across products; disbursement yield improving QoQ; 25 bps BPLR hike in Oct fully accounted
items.quote: Our focus continues to underwrite quality business with risk adjusted return as a result our incremental business yield has gone up by 25 bps+ across products.

items.statement: Demand uptick post-elections in PMAY affordable supply and self-construction; Tier 3-5 markets strong; Jan showing green shoots
items.quote: Yes. Demand has to see an uptick and specifically in certain segments and verticals as I speak of the PMAY -led affordable supply, which is there.

items.statement: ~60% of AuM <Rs15L ticket; targeting 45% <Rs10L (currently 30-35%); <Rs10L yields ~200 bps higher; home loan yield 11.5-12%, non-home 250 bps higher
items.quote: Our aim presently is to get to the 45%. Currently, we are hovering between 30% to 35% of the loans which are less than Rs. 10 lakhs in ticket size.

items.statement: Asset quality pristine: 1+ DPD 3.85% (<4% guided), GNPA 1.14%, NNPA 0.81%; BT-out at 5.4%; ECL model upgraded to Deloitte Bolt-on with Vasicek macro factors
items.quote: Our asset quality remains within the guided range with 1 day past due below 4% at 3.85% in Q3 FY25 and Gross Stage 3 & Net Stage 3 under 1.25% stood at 1.14% and 0.81% respectively.

items.statement: Opened 6 branches in 9MFY25; adding 20+ in Q4 FY25 mainly Karnataka & UP; accelerating branch expansion in calendar year
items.quote: We have opened 6 new branches during 9MFY25 and opening another 20+ branches in this quarter predominantly in the states of Karnataka and UP.

items.statement: Raised Rs 6.3 bn NCDs from IFC in Q3 (largest ever); total borrowings Rs 172 bn at 8.41% for 9MFY25; 51% bank borrowings EBLR/short-MCLR linked for fast repricing
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have successfully raised NCDs amounting to Rs 6.3 bn from the IFC in Q3. This is largest NCD raised by company till date.

items.statement: Aspires to reach Rs 500 bn AUM in next 4-5 years and become Pan-India player while continuing cost optimization
items.quote: We aspire to reach a milestone of Rs. 500 bn in assets under management in the next 4 to 5 years and broaden our horizons as a Pan-India player and continue our cost optimization strategy.

items.statement: Room AC industry expected to grow at 19% CAGR over next five years to reach higher penetration levels
items.quote: So, the CAGR projected by various studies are at 19% over the next five years in order to reach a penetration level that India should have. So, 19% CAGR is the guidance.

items.statement: Segment-I margin guidance 7% to 7.5%, Segment-II margin guidance 8% to 8.5%
items.quote: The margin guideline was 7% to 7.5% in Segment-I, 8% to 8.5% Segment-II. Unless and until something dramatically changes, let us say commodity prices crash, the margin can go up.

items.statement: Target to achieve 15% market share in Room AC within a couple of years while maintaining 8.5% operating margin
items.quote: Our immediate goal is 15% market share. Our goal is to keep that operating margin intact of 8.5%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 750 cr to Rs. 800 cr over around three years for manufacturing, product development and digitalization
items.quote: The CAPEX amount over a period of around three years will be in the region of around Rs. 750 cr to Rs. 800 cr, and that will be moving towards both manufacturing as well as product development, and certain amount of digitalization.

items.statement: Carried forward order book at record high of Rs. 6,801.99 cr as of December 31, 2024, up 12.8% year-on-year
items.quote: Carried forward order book as of December 31, 2024, is at a record high of Rs. 6,801.99 cr as compared to Rs. 6,038.53 cr as on December 31, 2023. This was a growth of 12.8%.

items.statement: Segment-II margins improved 100 bps to 8.1% in Q3 FY25 driven by Room AC scale benefits
items.quote: Overall margins in this segment registered a strong 100 bps improvement in the current quarter, which, as you have seen, was 8.1% in the current quarter as compared to 7.1% in the last corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Energy label change due January 1, 2026; products already developed, no pre-buying in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The energy label change is from 1st January 2026, and 1st January, 2025, no change has happened. What can happen potentially is somewhere in festival season it can be pre-launched that the future-ready or like that, that can happen.

items.statement: Room AC demand strong in Q3 FY25 due to festive season; industry likely to close above 15 million units, Blue Star above 1.5 million units in FY25
items.value: above 15 million units industry, above 1.5 million units Blue Star
items.quote: All that we know is that it is very likely the industry closes above 15 million, and we will close much higher than 1.5 million this year. And that we are aware and more or less this guidance can be given.

items.statement: Affluent customers moving up value chain to heavy duty and Wi-Fi enabled ACs, improving SKU margins
items.quote: The second one is connected with the affluent customers moving up the value chain. So, we are very clearly seeing year-after-year heavy duty air conditioner or Wi-Fi enabled air conditioner, these going up.

items.statement: Headwinds from rupee depreciation, commodity price escalation, supply chain disruptions, and liquidity issues in certain market segments
items.quote: However, there are headwinds owing to depreciation of Indian rupee, escalations in commodity prices, and possible supply chain disruptions due to huge demand. We have strong mitigation action in place to tackle these challenges.

items.statement: Segment-III Professional Electronics and Industrial Systems expected to revive in FY26 as CAPEX cycle picks up
items.quote: The challenges in this segment continues to impact revenue growth and profitability, and we expect to revive in FY26. Therefore, we are focused on controlling cost and managing working capital.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity modular; HP plant at ~600,000 units, Sri City scaling from 300,000 to 600,000, can scale up to 1.8-2.4 million units as demand grows
items.quote: the capacity at HP plant was already in the region of around 600,000, and at Sri City we were investing, we started with 300,000, we will now reach up to 600,000 and as and when we want, we can scale it up. So, in the current year also the capital investments have happened and this will keep happening as we see the demand. We can go up to around 1.8 million to 2.4 million as the demand scales up.

items.statement: Confident of closing Q4 FY25 on a high note, delivering good results for third consecutive year
items.quote: We are confident that we will close the forthcoming quarter also on a high note, which means for the third year in succession, we will deliver good results for the whole financial year.

items.statement: PLI benefits eligible for ~Rs. 75-80 cr over four years for ~Rs. 155 cr investment; on track to fully avail Phase-1 benefits
items.quote: we have indicated earlier that we are eligible for somewhere close to over a four-year period Rs. 78 cr of PLI benefits for eligible investment of somewhere around Rs. 155 cr or something, I do not remember the exact figure, but it is in the order of around between Rs. 75 cr to Rs. 80 cr, and we are on track on that.

items.statement: Expect sequential improvement in demand over next few months on back of infrastructure investments, good harvest and government initiatives in upcoming budget
items.quote: We expect sequential improvement in demand over the next few months on the back of increase in infrastructure investments, good harvest and government init iatives to spur growth in the upcoming budget

items.statement: Expect mid-single digit value growth in Q4 with margin maintenance
items.quote: for quarter 4, o ur intent is at a mid-single digit top- line growth, we will try to maintain our margins for quarter 4

items.statement: Invested in aseptic PET line for coconut water under Activ portfolio
items.quote: As far as Coconut Water is concerned under Activ, there also w e have invested in an aseptic pet line and coming out in a pet bottle besides tetra pack which wi ll give us huge growth in the beverage

items.statement: Operating profit increased 2.1% and PAT grew 1.8% YoY in Q3 FY25 despite inflationary pressures
items.quote: Operating profit increased by 2.1% and PAT grew by 1.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect 5% inflation going forward, will take calibrated price increases to maintain margins
items.quote: We expect a 5% inflation to actually hit us. So, whether it is SLEs, SLAs, Oral Care, so inflation will hit us and fruit concentrates also that we are purchasing because Indian currency will depreciate.

items.statement: Targeting 20-21% margin levels in FY26 through premium mix, premiumization, cost savings and price increases
items.quote: our attempt will be to go to around 20-21% lev els. That's what we were aiming at. I think the levers to achieve that would be changing the mi x of the product portfolio that we sell

items.statement: Took judicious price increases in portfolio to mitigate inflationary pressures in Q3
items.quote: We faced inflationary pressures this quarter and took judicious price increases in our portfolio.

items.statement: Plan consumer offer to reduce nectar prices from Rs 130 to around Rs 100 and launch economical range with RPI of 2 vs colas
items.quote: We are proposing, or we have already designed to do a consumer offer to reduce the prices from Rs. 130 to around Rs. 100, but this will happen by way of consumer offer, not by reducing prices.

items.statement: Rural outperformed urban for fourth consecutive quarter; rural grew 2% vs urban 0.6% in Q3
items.quote: If the overall India business is grown by 1.7%, urban business has grown by 0.6% and rural business has grown by 2%. So, the difference between the two is 140 bps for us.

items.statement: Oral Care grew 9.1% with Red franchise and Meswak driving double-digit growth; Gels grew 50% YoY
items.quote: The Oral Care portfolio recorded a growth of 9.1% driven by str ong double-digit growth in the Red franchise and Meswak. The Gels toothpaste portfolio has rec eived a good response in the market, recording a 50% year-on-year growth in this quarter

items.statement: Hair Oil grew 3.1% with coconut and perfumed oils gaining 125 and 236 bps market share respectively; overall share at 18% highest ever
items.quote: Within Hair Oils, both coconut and perfumed oils grew ahead of the category, gaining market share of 125 an d 236 bps respectively, taking our overall Hair Oil shares to around 18%, the highest ever

items.statement: Foods business strong with Culinary and Badshah domestic growing 30% and 15% respectively
items.quote: The Foods business demonstrated strong performance with the Culinary and Badshah domestic portfolio growing at 30% and 15% respectively.

items.statement: Revised strategic vision cycle from 4 years to 3 years due to volatile geopolitical landscape and uncertain macro indicators; partnered with McKinsey
items.quote: In light of the volatile geopolitical landscape and uncertain macroeconomic indicators, we have revised our strategic vision cycle from 4 years to 3 years. We have partnered with leading consultancy firm McKinsey & Company to refine and align our strategy for the next three years.

items.statement: Beverage nectar portfolio under pressure from Cola wars with RPI worsening from 2 to 2.7; category declined 16% in Nielsen terms
items.quote: the category is declined by around 16% and our decline is around 8 to 9% in the Nielsen ter ms. We have gained market shares of around 320 basis points in Juices and Nectar category

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores with INR6,200 crores spent in 9 months
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: Capacity expansion on track to reach 140 million tons by FY28 with 118 million tons by FY26
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18.4% in Q3 FY25 at INR1,712 crores with EBITDA per ton of INR1,038
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: Operational cost reduced to INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25 driven by 7% energy cost decline and 6% freight reduction
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Target to reduce total cost to INR3,650-3,700 per ton by FY28 from current INR4,600 level
items.quote: Our end-state target is to drop down the total cost to about INR3,700-3,800 over the next couple of years, that's the target.

items.statement: Industry demand growth was tepid at 1.5-2% in H1 FY25 but expected to rebound to 4-5% for full year
items.quote: The improved consumption demand in housing and infrastructure segments and increased government spendings are poised to reverse the tepid 1.5% to 2% cement demand growth during H1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Blended cement at 82% and premium products increased 400 bps to 26% of trade sales volume
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna assets currently at sub-40% and sub-50% utilization, expected to reach 70%+ in FY26
items.quote: My estimate is in the next financial year, both the assets should go up, I think Sanghi earlier and Penna because it's also in the market where it takes time to ramp up. But both of them should hit 70% plus utilization levels in the next financial year.

items.statement: Net worth increased to INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores with nil debt and AAA rating
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: 200 MW solar plant at Khavda commissioned in Q3 FY25, targeting 218 MW WHRS by March 2025
items.quote: 200-megawatt solar power, the project in Gujarat, Khavda, has been commissioned in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition at advanced stage, expected to add capacity to 104 million tons by Q4 FY25
items.quote: With Orient acquisition at advanced stage, the total capacity by Q4 FY '25 to hit 104 million tons.

items.statement: Incentive income expected to rise from INR400-500 crores annually to INR600-650 crores with new capacities
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR8,755 crores as of December 31, Orient acquisition outflow ~INR4,000 crores in Q4
items.quote: In terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 21.5% from 15.8%, targeting 60% of power needs from green sources by FY28
items.quote: The share of green power in power mix has increased to 21.5% from 15.8%.

items.statement: India realisations QoQ expected flat unless budget or safeguards provide upside; coking coal costs expected $10/t lower in 4Q vs 3Q
items.quote: On realisations, we are seeing India realisations QoQ being flat, unless there's something significant in the budget or safeguards which come, then there should be an upside. Otherwise, at minimum, we see it flat. In terms of costs, as far as India is concerned, coking coal costs are expected to be about $10 per ton lower in 4Q vs. 3Q.

items.statement: TSUK breakeven targeted in first two quarters of FY2026, focusing on June 2025; cost takeout and redundancies ongoing

items.quote: By September of 2026, we would have completed Kalinganagar and then the full benefit will start coming in. These capital expenditures, whether it is UK or Netherlands, do have their own timeframe, especially Netherlands, I think it's clearly about 1.5 years behind because the permitting time will also be building before any capex is spent.

items.statement: India capex FY2026 includes ~Rs. 3,000 crore for Kalinganagar completion, blast furnace relining at Jamshedpur, Ludhiana EAF, UK EAF spend starting; Neelachal expansion proposal to Board in few months; Kalinganagar 8 to 13 MTPA and Meramand
items.quote: for next year is concerned, the elements that will be there is certainly some part of the Kalinganagar expansion, which will be about Rs. 3,000 crores along with ancillary spend on that expansion. items.statement: NINL EBITDA margin improved from 13% in 2Q to 20% in 3Q on 17% volume growth QoQ and conversion cost reduction ~Rs. 3,000/t QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 13% in 2Q to 20% in 3Q on account of rise in volumes by about 17% QoQ and as an outcome of cost efficiency through reduction in conversion costs, which reduced by about Rs. 3,000 per ton QoQ.

items.statement: Netherlands transformation program targeting cost takeouts of a couple hundred million euros over multi-year, focusing on productivity, fixed/variable efficiency, mill availability, product mix; impact visible from 1Q FY26
items.quote: The transformation program is focused on productivity, cost takeouts, both fixed and variable efficiency, including availability of the mills in terms of benchmarks and optimi sing the product mix. [inaudible] I think it is also not a one-year cost takeout program. It will be multiyear, but we will want to take as much advantage of that in the next year, and it will run into a couple of hundred mi

items.statement: India steel demand growing but momentum eased; domestic prices under pressure from cheap imports; DGTR safeguard investigation initiated; China exports 111 Mt in 2024
items.quote: India steel demand continued to grow but momentum eased, and domestic prices remained under pressure due to cheap imports. The DGTR (Director General of Trade Remedies), has initiated investigation to consider safeguard duty. In 2024, several nations relied on trade measures such as antidumping duty to combat the impact of steel imports, particularly from China.

items.statement: Sukinda mine surrender process underway with state permissions received; will remove MDPA pressures and improve FAMD business stability; further optimisation planned
items.quote: Work is going on in surrender of the mine. We have got some of the permissions that we needed from the state government, but we are still going through the procedures. Once we surrender the mines, we won't have the MDPA pressures, and there will be a better balance between our ability to produce, grow more, and ability to convert them. That brings business to a better level of stability than we've

items.statement: UCP segment margin guidance: aim to retain high single digit in Q4 and by year-end
items.quote: Generally, we will remain around this high-single digit, our endeavor would be by the end of the year as a Company. And on the segment also, we will try and retain a high single digit in the last quarter as well.

items.statement: Chennai AC plant: ~Rs 400 cr spent; additional Rs 400-450 cr earmarked for compressor manufacturing and ramping capacity to 1.5-2 mn units over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Besides this, we have also earmarked additional roughly around Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores which is for compressor manufacturing as well as ramping up our production in Chennai factory from 1 million to take it to 1.5 million and then 2 million.

items.statement: Compressor capex ~Rs 250 cr, pending technological partnership; other Chennai ramp-up investments to complete in 10-12 months
items.quote: Compressor capex is about Rs. 250-odd crores, which will take a while. As we are looking for some technological partnership, etc. Unless it is done, we will not be able to commence production of compressors.

items.statement: UCP segment margin dipped to 5.9% in Q3 due to higher ad/ISD spend to gain market share; nine-month segment PBT up 30% to Rs 548 cr
items.quote: Firstly, when you are asking why there is pressure on UCP margin. So, we were trying to gain market share, and therefore, we were spending money on ISDs, BTL advertisement, ATL advertisement.

items.statement: No price hike taken in Q3; will evaluate passing on commodity/forex pressure via value engineering and selective price increases later
items.quote: No, we have not taken any price hike in the last quarter, Quarter 3. Because as it is, it's a leaner quarter for especially the air conditioners. And as I told you that our endeavor is to increase the scale of the numbers.

items.statement: Expect robust demand for all product categories in upcoming summer; optimistic on volume growth and market share gains
items.quote: With the summers around the corner, we remain optimistic and expect robust demand for all our product categories. And we hope that the demand will remain strong and positive consumer sentiments will further support the volume.

items.statement: UCP Q3 mix: RAC ~60%, Commercial Refrigeration ~15%, Air Coolers ~5%, Commercial AC balance
items.quote: So, the current quarter, as a part of Segment A: UCP, RAC has been around 60%-odd, commercial refrigeration has been around 15%, air cooler has been around 5%, and commercial air condition has been balance.

items.statement: Voltbek JV: volume growth 59% in Q3, 56% in 9M; market share >10% in washing machines (semi-auto 16.7%), 5.1% in refrigerators; targeting EBITDA breakeven by March 2025
items.quote: We had anticipated that by the end of this year, in the last quarter probably, we will be reaching the EBITDA breakeven, which our endeavor is still there, probably by the month of March, we should be able to hit that number.

items.statement: Peak annual depreciation after full capitalization of CR and Chennai plants estimated at Rs 70-75 cr company-wide
items.quote: It should be roughly about Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 75 crores for the full year, company wide.

items.statement: PLI benefits for Chennai plant expected from next fiscal year (FY26); some residual Pantnagar benefit may accrue in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, I think for Chennai plant, if you are asking in particular, next year onwards, the benefits will start accruing. So, in the next quarter, I do not think anything is coming in from Chennai. But yes, some leftover for Pantnagar, which we have already spent, could get in, in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA run rate achieved in Q3 FY25 should be taken as base for next 4-5 quarters; additional developments will only add to earnings
items.quote: But EBITDA -- stand-alone EBITDA run rate, which we have achieved in December '24 quarter should be taken as a base for the next 4, 5 quarters, because all additional developments that will happen will only add further to the earnings of Jindal Drilling.

items.statement: Order book of INR1,636 crores given rig-wise with day rates and contract duration; year-wise breakup provided
items.quote: Thereafter, our order book of INR1,636 crores is given rig-wise with day rates and contract duration.

items.statement: Acquisition of Jindal Pioneer rig for $75 million purchase price expected to conclude within Q4 FY25; no debt on the rig
items.quote: $75 million is the purchase price.

items.statement: Operating margins at 34% in Q3 FY25 expected to normalize at this rate and increase further after Pioneer acquisition
items.quote: Yes, definitely. And margins will increase further once the acquisition of Jindal Pioneer goes through.

items.statement: ONGC press release hiring BP Exploration as technical services provider indicates increased exploration activity and expected higher capex in oil & gas sector
items.quote: This is a clear indication that ONGC wants to increase exploration activities. And the fact that they have issued a press release means that further capital expenditure in the oil and gas sector is expected.

items.statement: All five rigs deployed in Bombay High; Jindal Supreme deployed 75 days in Q3, full 90 days in Q4; Jindal Explorer contract ends May or Sep 2025
items.quote: Bombay High. All five rigs are deployed in Bombay High.

items.statement: Only risk is securing contracts from ONGC; once awarded, contracts are firm, not renegotiated or canceled
items.quote: The only risk in this industry is securing a contract from ONGC. There is no other risk which cannot be addressed apart from the ability to secure a contract from ONGC.

items.statement: Net cash position doubled to INR101 crores in 9 months; gross debt INR156 crores, cash INR257 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Our net cash position has doubled in last 9 months from INR51 crores to INR101 crores.

items.quote: Jindal Pioneer, March 2015.

items.quote: Therefore, people are still reluctant to build new rigs due to the long gestation period.

items.quote: The up cycle in the oil and gas industry started after the Russia -Ukraine war, in February 2022.

items.statement: Only capex planned is Jindal Pioneer acquisition; reassessment after transaction concludes; consolidation of rented rigs preferred growth path
items.quote: The only capex which we are doing is acquisition of Jindal Pioneer, which is expected in this quarter.

items.statement: Day rates function of international market and Indian competition; last purchase price not confirmed indicator; cannot comment on Explorer renewal rate
items.quote: We cannot say that, because usually day rates are a function of the international market and the competition available in the Indian market.

items.statement: Directional drilling and mud logging services are small high-margin divisions but not scalable; no diversification planned beyond rig operations
items.quote: In addition to operating jack -up rigs, offshore jack -up Jindal Drilling & Industries Limited 29 January 2025 rigs with ONGC, we also have directional drilling and mud logging services, which are small divisions and give good margin, but it is not possible to scale those businesses up

items.statement: Aim to grow overall volumes by at least 12% in FY26 on a FY25 base of ~190,000 tons
items.quote: We do aim to grow by at least 12% overall.

items.statement: Expect FY25 total volume to reach around 190,000 tons by March
items.quote: Yes, we should be able to do that.

items.statement: Management sees Q3 as margin bottom; expects improvement from One Usha Martin initiatives by September 2025
items.quote: To be straight to you, I think this is the bottom of the margin. And with the various initiatives of One Usha Martin where we are looking at rationalizing our cost across all our subsidiaries.

items.statement: Galfan (Gal Star) zinc-aluminum line commissioned, under trial production; full benefits expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: I am happy to say that we have commissioned our plant, and it is under trial production, and we hope to stabilize the operations in this quarter, and we should start getting the full benefits of this from Q1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Zero capex planned for regular LRPC; focus only on plasticated and galvanized LRPC conversion
items.quote: No CAPEX at all. Zero CAPEX.

items.quote: The replacement market is almost 80% to 85% of the demand. It is not 50%-55%, in most products, 80%-85% of the market is replacement.

items.quote: The area where we see a lot of competition as well as demand challenges coming is the oil and offshore. This is because of the competition and because of the lower demand; the competition is being aggressive to trying to get i.e everybody's trying to get a pie of the same market.

items.quote: The implementation has already started, and we aim to complete this transition by September, 2025.

items.quote: We have been supplying there through our Brunton wire plant but now by having this facility, I think, there is a fairly good demand, and we expect good orders to flow in. And next year we should be having a significant increase in volume from that market.

items.statement: CE certification obtained for ropeway/Parvat Mala projects; only Indian company with manufacturing capability and certification; demand medium to long term
items.quote: As of today, we are the only Company with the manufacturing capability to produce these ropes. To the best of our knowledge, we are also the only Company in India with CE Certification for this.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 168 crore (28% of annualized EBITDA) as of Dec 2024; manageable despite ongoing capex
items.quote: As at 31st December 2024, our net debt stood at Rs. 168 crore which is 28% of our annualized operating EBITDA. Despite ongoing capital expenditure initiatives including expansions in Ranchi and Thailand and upgrades at the UK facility, our debt level remains well within manageable limits.

items.statement: Aiming for EBITDA margins between 13% and 14% for FY26
items.quote: FY '26, we are aiming for EBITDA margins between 13% and 14%, which highlights our commitment to maintaining financial health and enhancing operational efficiency

items.statement: Revenue target of roughly INR 4,000 crores on consolidated basis achievable in 3 years
items.quote: the revenue guidance, what we had given, obviously, we revised it down in last quarter because of the fallen prices to say, roughly around INR 4,000 crores of revenue on a consol basis is still achievable in 3 years' time

items.statement: Expect to inch towards 15% EBITDA margins in 2 years if current situation remains
items.quote: we should definitely start inching towards 15% EBITDA margins, frankly speaking
