items.quote: During 9 months FY '25, the company incurred cap ex of INR136 crores, mainly towards capacity expansion, backward integration and new product launches. We anticipate a total capex of around INR 200 crores for the full year

items.statement: Sayakha greenfield project to commence trial production in February, operating leverage expected from subsequent quarter
items.quote: the greenfield project at Sayakha, Gujarat for Specialty Chemicals, which is also related to the backward integration, will commence trial production in this quarter, most probably in the month of February itself. With this, the operating leverage is expected to kick in from the subsequent quarter with improved capacity utilization.

items.statement: Tarapur greenfield project ramp up to 500+ tons per month by end of March 2025, total sequential ramp-up of 1,600 metric tons per month by end of FY26
items.quote: There had been certain teething issues in Tarapur greenfield project, which are sorted now, and we expect to ramp up the production to 500- plus tons per month by end of March '25. In total, we will have a sequential ramp -up of capacity of 1,600 metric tons per month by end of FY '26.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement expected sequentially as raw material and selling prices have stabilized after 90-100 days inventory FIFO impact
items.quote: So now that it has stabilized, I think, the margin -- gross margin should in fact improve on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 15% to 20% for FY26 with help of salicylic acid capacity
items.quote: Yes. So volume growth, we will definitely try for 15% to 20%, no doubt about that. We'll try to -- with the help of salicylic acid, I hope we'll get to those numbers.

items.statement: Formulation segment expects flattish growth next quarter but strong order book for next 2 quarters with export-driven growth, 30% capacity added via brownfield expansion
items.quote: in the very short term in the next coming quarter, we are expecting a flattish growth. But over the next -- for the next financial year, we have pressed up our capacities. So we recently completed a brownfield expansion in the Formulation segment, which has added about 30% additional capacities, for which revenues will start kicking in from Q1.

items.statement: Meaningful contribution from US FDA plant may not come in FY26, likely starting FY27 due to regulated market gestation period
items.quote: the meaningful contribution may not come from FY '26 itself. Probably it will start flowing-in in FY '27.

items.statement: Solar power SPV to generate 8.9 million renewable units per annum, commence operations by end of H1 FY26, saving INR 3.6 crores annually for Gujarat plant
items.quote: This solar plant will give us approximately 8.9 millio n renewable units per annum, and it is expected to commence the operation by end of H1 FY '26. This can result to a full year annual saving of around INR 3.6 crores for our Gujarat plant.

items.statement: Targeting 200-250 crore top line in FY26 from toys business at full utilization
items.quote: I think we should be expecting that, and that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Phase-2 toys expansion planned for H2 FY26 with ~100 crore investment for injection moulded toys plant
items.quote: We anticipate an investment of about Rs. 100 crores for this phase, and we intend to leverage the benefits of the Production Link Incentive Scheme in addition to the newly introduced toy policy.

items.statement: Auto business has no fixed order book; POs come as replenishment schedules from CV OEMs
items.quote: In any automotive business, there is not an order book given for the entire upcoming month. There is always a schedule given, and the POs keep coming in, as in when the stock has to be replenished.

items.statement: Toys segment EBITDA margin expected at 22-24% at optimum capacity across toys, preschool furniture, outdoor play equipment
items.quote: It is about a 22% to 24% blended between toys, preschool furniture, outdoor play equipment. This should be the EBITDA that one should operate on, on optimum capacity.

items.statement: Budget reduced duty on electronic components for battery-operated toys; will benefit Phase-2 expansion
items.quote: Now, it has come down. If you are importing with the intent to add these components, say, in a particular toy. So, hence, this is, to us, personally, this will come up under our Phase-2 of the expansion plan.

items.statement: Toys demand strong; Q4 FY25 targeting 4x prior capacity utilization with 30 tons/day capacity yielding 60-70 lakh/day value
items.quote: We should be doing or closing this Quarter at about 4x of what our capacity used to be and we are on track to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: Phase-2 expansion to add injection moulded toys including battery-operated cars and role-play toys
items.quote: This phase will involve the production of injection moulded toys, including battery operated cars and role play toys.

items.statement: Auto business tied to CV market cycle; down 22-24% in 9M FY25, expects 4-6% CAGR long-term
items.quote: We are about 22% to 24% behind in terms of numbers if you take up a 9-month runaway.

items.statement: May raise more funds via preferential/warrants as opportunities arise; currently reducing debt
items.quote: See, all of this is very dynamic. It all depends on what opportunities come in. So, yes, we may be raising more funds, but as and when required.

items.statement: Air filtration subsidiary signed 10-year exclusive license with Mann+Hummel; pilots at IIT Delhi and GD Goenka showed >80% PM reduction
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that it has entered into a 10-year exclusive licensing agreement with Mann + Hummel for the manufacturing and distribution of air purifiers across India.

items.statement: Industry cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1 supported by pro-infra and housing budget
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores with INR6,200 crores spent in 9 months and INR2,000-2,500 crores expected in Q4
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: Capex plan includes 40 new grinding units to reach 140-150 million tons capacity with progressive cost benefits each quarter
items.quote: Mind you, our number of locations, we'll add almost 40 new grinding units over Ambuja Cements Ltd., ACC Ltd. and the plan period when we hit 140 million, 150 million tons

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 18.4% in Q3 FY25 with EBITDA per ton of INR1,038
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: Operational cost reduced to INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25 driven by 7% decline in energy cost and 6% decline in logistics cost
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Target to reduce total cost to INR3,650-3,700 per ton by FY28 from current INR4,600 through green power, waste heat recovery, captive coal mines and logistics optimization
items.quote: Our end-state target is to drop down the total cost to about INR3,700-3,800 over the next couple of years, that's the target.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 21.5% from 15.8% with target of 60% green power for 140 million tons capacity and 83% for clinkerisation by FY28
items.quote: Both WHRS and solar power would ensure that 60% of our power requirements are -- of the planned 140 million tons would be through green power. However, on clinkerisation, the share of green power will further rise to 83%.

items.statement: Logistics cost reduced 6% to INR1,239 per ton with lead distance down 4km to 285km and direct dispatch up 700bps to 57%
items.quote: Because of these initiatives, our logistics costs have been reduced by 6% to INR1,239 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,322 per ton in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Ambuja Cements to grow faster than industry with traditional volumes growing 7% vs industry 5% and new capacity volumes growing 11%
items.quote: The traditional volume that we have, where there is no new capacity, it has grown at about 7%, which is slightly higher than the industry growth. And wherever we are having new capacity, we have grown much more at 11%.

items.statement: Blended cements at 82% and premium products as percentage of trade sales volume increased 400bps to 26%
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna acquired assets currently at sub-40% and sub-50% utilization with cost 10-15% higher than Ambuja; expected to reach 70%+ utilization next financial year
items.quote: So, I would say it's at least about 10% to 15% higher than Ambuja cost. Penna would be also the same. So, we expect 10% to 15% -- 15% maybe reduction in the cost of both the companies on a per ton basis.

items.quote: In terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Incentive income expected to rise from INR400-500 crores annually to INR600-650 crores prospectively with new capacities; INR4,500 crores total incentive bucket to be received over 7-9 years
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in and giving the benefit of incentives.

items.statement: Net worth increased to ~INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores in April with nil debt and AAA rating; tangible assets 75% of net worth and 15% cash equivalents
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.quote: Already, we have announced one set of transactions to merge some entities, including Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi. So, if you see out of all the entities, we've already announced 3 entities, which is currently under regulatory approval stage.

items.statement: Expect 12% revenue growth for FY25 while maintaining operating leverage
items.quote: Factoring in these challenges for FY25, we now expect 12% revenue growth while maintaining operating leverage.

items.quote: From FY26 onwards, we aim for an early teen revenue growth along with operating leverage.

items.quote: From the gross margin point of view, we expect the gross margin to be in the region of around 62% in the medium term.

items.quote: Owing to a surge in demand of high-end jewelry, gross margin came in at 61.3%, which is 110 basis points lower YoY.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% in Q3 FY25, up 40 bps YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% this quarter, which is 40 basis points higher than last year.

items.statement: Expect gross margin to continue above 60% in upcoming quarters and years
items.quote: And we expect that our gross margin will continue to be above 60% in upcoming quarters and years.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds contribute 8.9% of quarterly sales vs 0.2% a year ago
items.quote: Owing to the consumer demand towards lab-grown diamonds, we have successfully scaled our offering, which contributes to 8.9% of quarterly sales versus 0.2% a year ago.

items.statement: Expect lab-grown diamond sales to be double digit around 10-12% for foreseeable future
items.quote: So, we expect it to be double digit for about 10%, 12% for foreseeable future.

items.quote: In the US, revenue grew by 3.6% Y oY, boosted by strong festive season and improving consumer confidence

items.statement: UK revenue up 6.5% with Ideal World making significant contribution
items.quote: In the UK, the revenue was up 6.5% with Ideal World making a significant contribution.

items.statement: Germany posted 30.7% YoY revenue growth with operations achieving breakeven
items.quote: Germany continued its robust performance, posting a 30.7% Yo Y revenue growth. With operations achieving breakeven this quarter, we are confident about maintaining this momentum in Q4 as

items.quote: TV revenue grew by 6% year-over-year, and digital revenue grew by 12% year-over-year. Digital sales is contributing 40% of total B2C revenue.

items.statement: Mindful of macroeconomic trends, particularly muted consumer sentiments in UK and Europe
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain mindful of macroeconomic trends, particularly the muted consumer sentiments in UK and Europe.

items.statement: No major CAPEX for next two to three years
items.quote: And given now we don't have any major CAPEX for next two, three years, can we expect an increase in dividend in the years to come for next two, three years?

items.statement: Chetak 35-Series to achieve EBITDA breakeven at unit level from February as scale builds
items.quote: A major swing into the profitability zone will be achieved in Q4 as the 35-Series acquires scale beginning February.

items.statement: OBD-2B compliance cost impact ~1% on motorcycle portfolio, slightly higher on entry-level
items.quote: But pristine OBD 2B impact would be about 1%.

items.statement: Commodity basket flattish net in Q3; slight inflation ahead led by alloys and noble metals
items.quote: I think we're looking at very slight inflation, led by alloys and in a few miscellaneous categories. But like I said, it's a slight inflation. Steel and other metals look balanced, but I think what we need to watch out and see is really the noble metals, rhodium, palladium and platinum are all showing some signs of stiffness.

items.statement: Freedom CNG motorcycle retailed ~50,000 units since August launch; adoption faster where pump density high
items.quote: Till date, we have retailed almost 50,000 bikes since the start in August. Customer adoption is good with the product delivering all benefits as w as conceptualized, designed and manufactured.

items.statement: Green energy portfolio (EV + CNG) at 44% of domestic revenue; EV portfolio at 22% of domestic revenue
items.quote: In fact, our green energy portfolio comprising greener fuels of electric and CNG across two-wheelers and three-wheelers is at 44% of our domestic revenue.

items.statement: Chetak EV market share rose from 13% to 22% YoY in Q3; 35-Series launch to drive upper-half share
items.quote: From a market share of 13% in quarter 3 FY24, Chetak has clocked the market share of 22% in quarter 3, a rise of almost 10 percentage points.

items.statement: Currency volatility in South Asia and Africa a watch item for exports; KTM exports down 50% due to overseas restructuring
items.quote: Going forward, in export, we still need to be watchful of the currency-led volatility, particularly in South Asia and Africa. But barring that, we expect exports to continue to grow at 20% plus levels on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Bajaj Auto Technology Limited (BATL) fully operational with 500+ employees; will develop EV tech, electronics, software, fuel cells for captive use and partners
items.quote: BATL is now fully operati onal and already employs over 500 people. Source of BATL revenue will be the royalty from its IP and charges for other services rendered to Bajaj Auto Limited and its partner

items.statement: Expect further contraction in Q4 FY25 with recovery likely from next month onwards
items.quote: Looking a head, we expect some further contraction in the next quarter as sudden headwinds persist. However, we are taking proactive steps to mitigate risk and enhance efficiency, ensuring that we are well positioned for a recovery when conditions improve, which is likely from next month onwards.

items.statement: Kalinganagar Phase-1 construction to start next month; Rs. 200 crore already ordered, Rs. 400 crore more by March-April; first furnace power-up by June 2026
items.quote: by March and April we are going to release us around the order of Rs. 400 crores and we have already released the order of around Rs. 200 crores and we are expecting to power up our first furnace by around first quarter of 26-27 by April to June. The June we are expecting, June 26 we are expecting to power up one smelter, and the other smelter with a gap of three months.

items.statement: Ferrochrome prices bottomed out; expect uptick from March 2025 and Q1 FY26 as Chinese prices stabilize and stainless steel destocking ends
items.quote: the last quarter , there is a steep fall of ferrochrome prices, and the realization is decreased. So, we are expecting similar prices for the next two months . Anything from March onwards there will be a uptick in the prices and now there is a rollover of the same prices. So, we are expecting the bottom up as happened in both Chinese and European markets. So, we are Indian Metals and anticipating

items.statement: No plans for overseas chromite mine acquisitions (South Africa/Indonesia); sufficient domestic ore and expansion capacity
items.quote: No, I don't see any opportunity there because we have enough ore here itself. And we have enough plant to expand our capacity in India. So, no point in going outside and exploring opportunities there, because it's an unknown terrain.

items.statement: Expect to reach 10 GW capacity by end of FY25
items.quote: We are on track to reach 10 GW of capacity by the end of FY25.

items.statement: Capex spent in 9M FY25 is ₹6,200 cr; full year FY25 capex expected close to ₹10,000 cr
items.quote: For the first 9 months, the total capex that has been spent is about ₹ 6,200 cr. And we are expecting to end the full year with close to ₹ 10,000 cr.

items.statement: Additional capex for 2.4 GW O2 Power under-construction and pipeline projects expected between ₹13,000 cr and ₹14,000 cr
items.quote: As guided earlier, the additional capex of 2.4 GW of under-construction and pipeline projects is expected to be between ₹ 13,000 crores and ₹ 14,000 crores.

items.statement: Locked-in generation capacity now 28.3 GW including 7.8 GW under construction with signed PPAs, 3.9 GW expecting PPAs soon, and 8.3 GW under acquisition
items.quote: With all of the above, our locked-in generation capacity is now 28.3 GW.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA ₹1,115 cr, down 9% YoY; 9M FY25 EBITDA ~₹4,600 cr, flat YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹ 1,115 cr, which was down by 9%.

items.statement: Net debt at end of Dec ₹26,500 cr; Net Debt to TTM EBITDA 4.5x; operating net debt to EBITDA 2.8x
items.quote: We reported a Net Debt to TTM EBITDA of 4.5x.

items.quote: The power demand for the country grew at 4.5% in the first 9 months of the current fiscal 2025. In the third quarter, we have seen a demand growth mo derating at 2.7

items.quote: In the quarter gone by, we have added 377 MW of capacity to our organic renewal projects, which is entirely wind and represents 47% of the country's wind capacity addition of 800 MW in the third quarter.

items.quote: KSK, historical number is available last financial year in fiscal 2024, they had done an EBITDA of INR2,600 crores. So that is, in a way, public domain information.

items.statement: Day-ahead market prices decreased 26% YoY to ₹3.71/unit vs ₹5/unit in Q3 FY24; short-term realization at premium to exchange prices
items.quote: The day-ahead market prices have decreased 26% year-on-year to ₹ 3.71 per unit as compared to ₹ 5 per unit in Q3 of last year.

items.statement: CERC order Jan 23 on infirm power not expected to significantly impact Ind-Barath Unit 2 commissioning; confident of ramping to full capacity quickly based on Unit 1 learnings
items.quote: See, yes, this new regulation which has come, it is not going to have any significant impact because we have to see what it says that there is a ramp-up of the unit, and whenever we are working on the project, the entire process that has in case of Ind-Barath, there has been a very good learning while ramping up to full capacity, the first unit. And we are in a position to ramp this unit to full c

items.statement: Structurally expect strong power demand in medium term; government and private investment likely to increase, positive for power sector
items.quote: We see the things to be better in the coming year with what we see, expect and we are reading that maybe more of government spend and also the private investment likely to increase now, which will basically have a positive impact on the power sector.

items.statement: Raised equity capital at start of fiscal year to build war chest and protect balance sheet for growth
items.quote: And hence, in order to prepare ourselves better, we had gone ahead and raised capital and equity capital raise at the start of the fiscal year. It was precisely with this intention to build a war chest and ensure that the balance sheet is healthy to protect the growth.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of close to Rs. 5,000 crore
items.quote: So, in FY26, we are looking at revenue of close to Rs. 5,000 crore. I think that is what we have targeted.

items.statement: FY27-28 revenue target of Rs. 8,000-10,000 crore intact
items.quote: Yes, definitely that target is completely intact. And that's what I was coming to where in terms of the wheel business, the container business, the auto business, the brake business will constitute a substantial part of those revenues.

items.statement: Wagon volume target of 9,000 units for FY25 and 10,000 units for FY26
items.quote: But I was very clear that we would be doing close to 9,000 odd wagons in this financial year and I am very confident that we will be achieving those numbers. And for the next financial year I had mentioned that yes our target is to go to up to 10,000 wagons

items.statement: Jupiter Tatravagonka revenue to double to ~Rs. 300 crore in FY25 and double again in FY26
items.quote: So, we have achieved Rs. 225 crore of turnover as against, when we had acquired the company that done a business of about Rs. 120 odd crore and I think they had some losses also that year. So, it's a substantial turnaround for us and we expect to close this year close to about Rs. 300 crore.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 6,320 crore as of December 31, 2024
items.quote: Our order book stood at Rs 6,320 crore as of December 31st, 2024, reinforcing our growth potential and providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to improve in FY26 over FY25's ~14.5%
items.quote: I think our margins , again I will not give out any definite numbers, but what I can very confidently say is that the margins profile will be better than th is financial year.

items.statement: Target wagons <50% of revenue by FY27-28; wheel, container, auto, brake businesses to drive mix shift
items.quote: As I have always m aintained that by '27-'28, we want wagons to be less than 50% of our revenues, and I think that is where we are working towards.

items.statement: Overwhelming demand for TEZ e-LCV with 500+ order confirmations; commercial launch Feb 26, 2025
items.quote: Commercial launch of the product scheduled on 26th February 2025 and w e are proud to say that we already have order confirmations for over 500 T EZ vehicles.

items.statement: Initial orders received for lithium-ion battery systems for railways and BESS; expect substantial growth in 2-3 years

items.statement: Orissa wheel project on track using prior QIP funds; backward integration to create >Rs. 2,000 crore opportunity with exports to Europe
items.quote: And once the Orissa project for the backward integration kicks in, then as I have already mentioned that this would be a more than Rs. 2,000 crore opportunity for us with substantial exports to the European market.

items.statement: No significant exposure to North America; European market unaffected by potential Trump tariffs
items.quote: Yes, see as we don't have much exposure to the North American market , lot of our sales is domestic and otherwise also exposure is mainly to the European market . So, we don't see any kind of challenges in the European market with regard to any action with Mr. Trump takes.

items.statement: JVs to turn profitable from next year due to sustainable localization
items.quote: The JVs will start to earn profit from next year onwards on account of sustainable localization of manufacturing processes.

items.statement: Interim milestone 333: $3 billion order book, ~$2.2 billion turnover, 3% PAT in about 2 years (FY27)
items.quote: in about 2 years from now, we should have an order book in hand of about $3 billion. And at that level, we should do a turnov er of close to US$2.2 billion and generate 3% PAT of the company

items.statement: Full-year FY25 PAT expected ~2%; FY27 full-year PAT target 3%
items.quote: Currently we're at about 1.5%. If I just talk about the full year, we should be closer to 2% or so approximately and then we have to add that 1% extra post our investment, so nothing to be excluded.

items.quote: And in terms of the outlook for next year, we are looking at investing half of what we have done this year. So, this should actually come down to about 50% to 60% of what we have done this year.

items.quote: This acquisition involves an equity investment of INR41 crores with some confirmatory diligences underway. And this investment is payable in tranches over 1 year. items.statement: Overall order book ~$425 million, up 16% YoY; design-led sourcing order book up 25% YoY
items.quote: currently we have an order book of about 425 million on an overall order book basis, while the order book has a growth of 16% overall. But what is important is that in design-led sourcing, which is our main business contributing to more than 87% of revenue, the growth is actually 25% over the same period last year.

items.statement: BCG cost transformation targets 1-2% savings (3-4% high side) on 50-55% of cost base; success-fee basis
items.quote: we beli eve from the scale that we have built up, there is potential to get synergies on a high side of 3% to 4%, but surely about 1% to 2% savings from this cost base are surely achievable

items.statement: Q3 FY25 normalized PAT margin 2.6%; 9M FY25 normalized PAT margin 3.4%
items.quote: Our normalized PAT after adjusting for new businesses, stood at INR78 crores for Q3 FY '25 and INR289 crores for the 9-month period, with margins of 2.6% and 3.4%, respectively.

items.statement: Management expects around 10% volume growth next financial year with CNG and industrial segments as main contributors
items.quote: Now maybe next year, we will not be able to have that much number, but we are comfortable that around 10% numbers we will be able to clock next financial year also and which will be definitely -- CNG will be a main contributor in that growth along with industrial and commercial segment.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated volume growth of 12-13% for FY25 and double-digit growth for FY26
items.quote: If you add on UEPL because it has a small volume, but the growth is much higher there, maybe more plus 20%. So collectively on a consolidated basis, we are around 12% growth as of now, 12% to 12.5%. So in the year-end we expect it to be around 13% or 13.5%. Next year also we definitely should be in -- at least in the double digit, yes.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA per SCM to remain in INR9-12 range depending on gas prices and contracts
items.quote: So it is not very off the mark of the guidance which we have given about INR10 to INR12. So we expect similar range to continue and depending on the price of LNG, Henry Hub and other contracts. We may be very comfortable in this range, INR9 to INR11 or INR10 to INR12 range.

items.statement: MGL spent INR650+ crores in 9M FY25 and expects INR200-250 crores more in Q4; UEPL to spend INR125-150 crores in FY25 and INR150-200 crores in FY26
items.quote: As far as MGL is concerned, already INR650 crores plus capex has been done in this 9 months period and we expect anywhere between INR200 to INR250 additional capex in Q4 as well. Out of these, major will be on steel and low-pressure pipelines. And roughly INR200 crores or plus, minus 10% on CNG. And balance is on steel grid and LMC, last mile connectivity.

items.statement: UEPL standalone capex guidance: INR125-150 crores for FY25 and INR150-200 crores for FY26
items.quote: See, UEPL standalone should spend in the range of around this year, at least INR125 crores to INR150 crores. And it will be further up maybe next year because we have now have the ground and the groundwork is done. So we'll be able to do more capex on CNG stations et cetera. And it could go from INR150 crores to INR200 crores next financial year.

items.statement: CNG volume grew 11.44% YoY for 9M FY25; Industrial & Commercial grew 25.52%; Domestic PNG grew 7.23%

items.quote: There has been some impact because we were reassessing our portfolio and the price hike has happened in late of November. And second rise has happened somewhere in January. So there were some delayed response. And secondly, we have contracted some midterm gas also on -- from the existing suppliers for giving a repeat order. Thirdly, some reinstatement of APM gas has happened as late as 16th of Jan

items.quote: So as of now, considering the indices, with respect to Henry Hub, it ranges between $9.5 to around $10.5. HPHT is around -- that is I think available in the public domain, including transportation, it should go around $11, which has $1 per MMBTU transportation and around $10.25 or so as a basic rate.

items.statement: Bombay HC order on phasing out diesel/petrol vehicles could drive CNG growth to 15-20% if implemented favorably; 4 lakh commercial vehicles in GA with 9.5% CNG penetration
items.quote: We can see a growth of around 15% to 20% in case everything goes in favor of CNG.

items.statement: GA-3 volumes grew ~50% YoY to 0.245 MMSCMD for 9M FY25; GA-2 double-digit growth; GA-1 4-5% growth
items.quote: If you look at the growth in GA-3, last year average was around 0.163 and we are today at 0.245 which is a growth of almost 49%, 50% over the last year average. So that is a growth in GA-3. If you consider GA-1 and GA-2, GA-2 is double digit and GA-1 is in the normal range of 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Forex impact: ~INR0.22-0.25 per SCM per rupee depreciation; gas contracts unhedged but partially naturally hedged via fuel price linkages
items.quote: Roughly, my estimate is -- yes, you are right in that sense. It adds around INR 0.22 to INR0.25 per rupee increase on our overall company basis, a rough ballpark number.

items.statement: APM allocation may face further ~7% annual reduction from April 2025, replaced by NWG at NWG prices on pro-rata basis
items.quote: Now in our information, as far as we understand the next r e-allocation or re - adjustments will happen somewhere from 1st of April because around 7% per annum is recommended to be reduced from APM and put into NWG. items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of 120% (INR12 per equity share) for FY25
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board has approved an interim dividend at the rate of 120% that is INR12 per equity share for the current financial year.

items.statement: UEPL merger with MGL approved by Board Oct 2024, submitted to NCLT Dec 6 2024, interim order reserved Jan 17 2025
items.quote: A scheme of amalgamation or merger of UEPL with MGL was approved by the Board in October '24 last year and the scheme was submitted to NCLT Mumbai on 6 December, 2024. And the matter was heard by the Mumbai bench on January 17, 2025 and they've reserved the pronouncement of its interim order.

items.statement: Target secured mix of 55%+ by FY27
items.quote: We endeavored to achieve a secured mix of 55% plus by FY27.

items.statement: NIM guided range 7% to 7.5% for FY25
items.quote: On a nine month basis, NIM was stable at 7.3%, which is within our guided range of 7% to 7.5% for this financial year.

items.statement: Credit cost target 2% near term, 1.5-1.6% by FY27
items.quote: As we see the stabilizing of the microfinance industry, our credit cost expectation in the near future will be around 2% overall for the portfolio and by FY27 with the shift in secured, I think we expect it to be between 1.5% to 1.6%.

items.statement: ROA target around 2%
items.quote: Our focus is to see that our ROA remains as close to 2%. That is our focus.

items.statement: Investing in technology and training for productivity
items.quote: While we hire new talent, it is equally important to up -skill and re-skill the existing employ ee base to enhance productivity and efficiency for which the Bank is investing on training and development and also on cutting -edge technology and digital solutions

items.statement: Gross advances Rs 1.32 lakh crore, up 14% YoY
items.quote: As of December 2024, gross advances totaled Rs. 1.32 lakh crore, a growth of 14% year-on-year and 1% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Deposits Rs 1.41 lakh crore, up 20% YoY
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, total deposits stood at Rs. 1.41 lakh crore as against Rs. 1.17 lakh crore in the previous year, same quarter, a growth of 20% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: NIM 6.9% in Q3 FY25, 7.3% 9M FY25
items.quote: Our net interest margin (NIM) for the quarter was 6.9% compared to 7.4% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cost of funds slightly higher due to competitive deposit market
items.quote: The deposit market continued to be competitive, resulting in slightly higher cost of funds.

items.statement: EEB disbursements moderated in Q4 FY25 with guardrails
items.quote: Definitely it would not be as aggressive as we have done it in the past, it would be moderated.

items.statement: Secured book 49% of advances, grew 34% YoY
items.quote: Our secured book now constitutes nearly 49% of total advances.

items.statement: EEB slippages Rs 1,196 crore in Q3, expect similar in Q4, lower from Q1 FY26
items.quote: May not be Rs. 1200 crores, maybe close to Rs. 1000 or maybe like that. But slippages, we are seeing the trend, but at the same time as you are witnessing, you see that our SMA-0 book is improving.

items.statement: Karnataka EEB portfolio Rs 740 crore, ~13% delinquent, not major risk
items.quote: Our Karnataka portfolio is only Rs. 740 crores out of total EEB portfolio of Rs. 56,000 crores, so which is very small and ~13% of which is now delinquent.

items.statement: Technical write-off Rs 1,266 crore in EEB portfolio
items.quote: First, we did a technical write-off of Rs. 1,266 crores in the EEB portfolio, as a result of which an incremental provision of Rs. 336 crores was made during the quarter.

items.statement: ESOP accounting change one-off Rs 166 crore in staff expenses
items.quote: The last one off was relating to the staff expenses wherein we had a one off of Rs. 166 crores on account of change in accounting policy with respect to ESOPs, Employee Stock Option Plans.

items.statement: CGFMU payout Rs 538 crore and Assam govt Rs 52 crore one-off gains
items.quote: Firstly, we received the claim payout from CGFMU stands for credit guarantee funds for micro units and the total income booked on account of the same is Rs. 538 crores. Second, we received a net amount of Rs. 52 crores against microfinance loans from the Assam government.

items.statement: Gross margins sustaining 31-33% range driven by premiumization and mix
items.quote: Gross margins are now sustaining a range of 31% to 33% as we spe ak, which is driven by premiumization, channel reorganization and a better product mix

items.quote: Our operating EBITDA margins for the quarter rose to 7.5%, which is up 98 basis points on year-on-year with almost 25% of value growth.

items.statement: Expect high single-digit operating EBITDA margins in next 4 quarters
items.quote: In 4 months -- 4 quarters, we should definitely see some high single digits operating EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Target gross margin improvement to 32-34% range over next 4 quarters
items.quote: We definitely see 100 basis point improvement on that range also. We could look at 32% to 34%, and that will slow down.

items.statement: Expect good summer season with early onset in North and East
items.quote: Right now, we are all expecting and our complete belief is that the summer will be a good one.

items.statement: BLDC and IoT fans contribute ~20% of ceiling fan revenue YTD, growing ~25%
items.quote: At a full year YTD basis, now BLDC and IoT contribute almost 20% of the overall ceiling fans category and growing at almost about 25%.

items.statement: Premium decorative fans at ~30-31%, target 45%
items.quote: Our premium in Deco category is approximately 30%, 31% now, and our ambition is to take it to closer to 45%.

items.statement: Value-added lighting products contribute ~50% of lighting revenue, up 400 bps YoY
items.quote: These now contribute almost 50%, which is an improvement of almost 400 basis points on a year-on-year basis, and the traditional lamps do the balance.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant operations stabilized, ready for season demand
items.quote: With our Hyderabad plant operations now stabilized, we are ready for season demand.

items.statement: B2B lighting growing high double-digits, aggressive on tender business
items.quote: The B2B segment in Lighting has also shown promising growth. We are actively working on several infrastructural projects delivering high double-digit growth.

items.statement: EPR cost impact factored in, partially absorbed and partially passed through
items.quote: EPR has been factored in. Some bit of it is absorbed as cost, some bit of is passed. We've always maintained that whatever we need to pass to the consumers, we will not shy away from it.

items.statement: DTM states revenue share 30% vs 70% MD states in fans
items.quote: Master distributor is 70, and DTM is 30. And that's from a fans only perspective.

items.statement: Lighting B2B revenue share 20%, B2C 80%, B2B growing faster
items.quote: Our current split between a B2C and a B2B is about 80:20. Ideally we would want it to move up, but that's where we are, and we are building both the size of the business together.

items.statement: Price erosion in commoditized lighting (bulbs, battens) continues
items.quote: The one part, which we basically com moditized bulbs and battens, those are the ones which are under price erosion

items.statement: 3-year business plan to be shared by April-May
items.quote: As far as for 3-year plan, we will be sharing with all of you by April, May, what will come back.

items.quote: From a 10.2% in quarter 1 to 11.8% in quarter 2, it's at 9.2% and if you look at from an industry average, right now, anything if you look at any of the peers and all, they are all in the range of 9% to 9.5%.

items.statement: Guides 20-25% AuM growth long-term; confident of ~20% in FY25 with Jan at 15-20% trajectory
items.quote: We continue to guide on a 20 – 25% of an AuM growth on a long-term basis. I think the traction which we got in the Q3 and the numbers in Jan really give us confidence on delivering the guided AuM growth of ~20.

items.statement: Targets opex-to-assets below 3% with ~20 bps annual reduction; achieved 42 bps YoY improvement to 3.21% in 9MFY25
items.quote: At the beginning of the financial year we have guided that we will bring down opex to assets ratio by ~20 bps every year to reach below 3%. I am happy to report a remarkable improvement in the Opex to Assets ratio by 42 bps Y -o-Y to 3.21% in 9MFY25 as a result of our cost optimisation strategy.

items.statement: Guides credit cost below 25 bps on sustainable basis; improved to 15 bps in 9MFY25
items.quote: Credit costs improved further to 15 bps in 9MFY25 vs 19bps in 9MFY24. We continue to guide credit cost of below 25 bps on sustainable basis.

items.statement: NIM expanded >10 bps YoY to 7.75% in Q3FY25; spread improved 4 bps QoQ to 5.72%
items.quote: Our calculated spread has improved by 4 bps sequentially to 5.72% in Q3FY2 5. Our NIMs expanded more than 10 bps Y -o-Y during the quarter to 7.75%.

items.statement: Incremental business yield up 25+ bps across products; disbursement yield improving QoQ and narrowing gap with book yield
items.quote: Our focus continues to underwrite quality business with risk adjusted return as a result our incremental business yield has gone up by 25 bps+ across products.

items.statement: Raised BPLR by 25 bps in Q3FY25; AUM yield expanded 14 bps QoQ to 13.18%; cost of borrowings up 9 bps QoQ to 8.24%
items.quote: Our spread improved by 5 bps to 4.94% driven by a 14 -bps expansion in the AUM yield to 13.18% on account of 25 bps increased in BPLR in Q3FY25; whereas our cost of borrowings increased by 9 bps Q-o-Q to 8.24%.

items.statement: Demand uptick post-elections in PMAY-led affordable supply and self-construction; strong in Tier 3-5 markets
items.quote: Yes. Demand has to see an uptick and specifically in certain segments and verticals as I speak of the PMAY -led affordable supply, which is there.

items.statement: ~60% of AuM below Rs 15 lakh ticket; targeting 45% share of sub-Rs 10 lakh loans (currently 30-35%) for better risk-adjusted yield
items.quote: Our aim presently is to get to the 45%. Currently, we are hovering between 30% to 35% of the loans which are less than Rs. 10 lakhs in ticket size.

items.statement: Asset quality pristine: 1+ DPD 3.85%, GNPA 1.14%; BT-out at 5.4%; ECL model upgraded to Deloitte Bolt-on with Vasicek macro factors
items.quote: Our asset quality remains within the guided range with 1 day past due below 4% at 3.85% in Q3 FY25 and Gross Stage 3 & Net Stage 3 under 1.25% stood at 1.14% and 0.81% respectively.

items.statement: Opened 6 branches in 9MFY25; adding 20+ in Q4 FY25 mainly in Karnataka and UP; accelerating branch expansion in calendar year
items.quote: We have opened 6 new branches during 9MFY25 and opening another 20+ branches in this quarter predominantly in the states of Karnataka and UP. We will be accelerating our branch expansion strategy by opening more branches in the calendar year.

items.statement: Raised Rs 6.3 bn NCDs from IFC in Q3 (largest ever); total borrowings Rs 46.2 bn at 8.41% in 9MFY25; liquidity Rs 18.95 bn cash/CC + Rs 22.8 bn unavailed sanctions
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have successfully raised NCDs amounting to Rs 6.3 bn from the IFC in Q3. This is largest NCD raised by company till date.

items.statement: Aspires to reach Rs 500 bn AUM in next 4-5 years and become Pan-India player while continuing cost optimization
items.quote: We aspire to reach a milestone of Rs. 500 bn in assets under management in the next 4 to 5 years and broaden our horizons as a Pan-India player and continue our cost optimization strategy.

items.statement: Karnataka E-Khata challenges stabilising; branches opening after stabilisation; 20k+ customers in state with ULB-allotted affordable supply
items.quote: I think that easing out of E -Khatas are moving across. It has started now really getting stabilised. And as we go forward, we will see that really becoming stable over a period of time.

items.statement: Tech platforms fully upgraded and stabilising; AI-driven predictive models for BT-out and collections; voice bots deployed; login-to-sanction TAT cut from 13 to 7 days
items.quote: We have completed upgradation of all major tech platforms which are now stabilizing, this was one of the fastest tech implementations in the industry.

items.statement: Home loan yield 11.5-12%; non-home loan 250 bps higher; MSME 75 bps above LAP; new disbursement yield 30-35 bps below book yield
items.quote: Home loan versus, let's say, non -home loan, which is MSME LAP, there is always difference of 250 bps between home loan to non-home loan. Yes, MSME businesses give us another 75 bps better pricing than the LAP portfolio.

items.statement: Expect double-digit RevPAR growth on existing portfolio and will add through new assets and inventories
items.quote: I see no reason why that commentary needs to change. Very confident that we will deliver double-digit RevPAR growths on our existing portfolio. And we will add through new assets and new inventories.

items.statement: Capital expenditure under current plan of around INR20 billion for next 3 years largely funded through internal accruals
items.quote: The company has been actively investing in its growth and has a capital expenditure under the current plan of around INR20 billion for the next 3 years. This will be largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Goa hotel capex roughly INR1.4 crore per key for 175-180 keys, approvals in 3-4 months, construction start before or after monsoon, 30 months to completion
items.quote: So roughly the capex is going to be about 1.4 crores per room, per key. We are planning about, around 175 to 180 keys or rooms.

items.statement: Powai Phase 2 commercial capex roughly INR800 crore, INR200 crore spent, balance INR600 crore over next 3 quarters
items.quote: So Powai, which is the Powai second -- Phase 2, is roughly 800 crores of capex spend, out of which we have already spent close to 200 crores, so 600 crores is the balance capex which we might be spending in next 3 quarters.

items.statement: Residential project pending cost INR300-odd crore, new sales opportunity INR500 crore plus receivables, net cash flows INR400-450 crore after repaying promoters
items.quote: I think the residential project is about -- cost is -- pending cost is 300-odd crores. And new sales opportunity is 500 crores plus the receivables, so together, we'll end up with about 400 crores to 450 crores of net cash flows after repaying the promoters.

items.statement: Lease confirmations of additional 400,000 square feet in the quarter, confident of reaching full potential of commercial inventory within a couple of quarters
items.quote: Additionally, we achieved significant leasing momentum with lease confirmations of an additional 400,000 square feet in the quarter.

items.statement: Hospitality EBITDA margin 46.1% for quarter, consolidated EBITDA margin 45.5%, expect margin improvement as Dukes and Four Points renovations stabilize and Courtyard Aravali ramps up
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter for Hospitality division was at 46.1%, with well-managed utilities and payroll costs.

items.statement: Commercial annuity EBITDA margin 79%, exit monthly run rate INR20 crore in December 2024, expect 90% flow-through to EBITDA when fully leased
items.quote: The EBITDA for the division was at INR455 million, with 79% margins.

items.statement: ADR rose 18% to almost INR13,000, occupancy stable at 70%, RevPAR grew 16% to over INR9,000, same-store RevPAR up 17%
items.quote: In the Hospitality segment, ADRs have risen by 18% to almost INR13,000 levels for the first time.

items.statement: Bangalore ADR grew 31%, occupancy up 4%, RevPAR up 40-odd percent; Hyderabad Westin ADR grew 28%, growth structural not one-off
items.quote: Bangalore has improved by -- ADR by 31%. You're right. And our occ upancy has also improved by 4% , which is a 40 -odd-percent growth in the RevPAR in that particular

items.statement: Foreign room nights up 5% YoY to 72,684 in Q3, domestic traffic growing strongly, expect foreign travel growth supported by new Mumbai airport opening
items.quote: Your number of foreigner room nights in Q3 this year was 72,684 versus 69,326 room nights, foreign room nights, last year.

items.statement: Wedding demand strong in Q4 and Q1 next year, significant weddings in Q1 unlike last year, Q4 as good or better than last year
items.quote: And in fact, the good point is that, this time in quarter 4 and quarter 1 of next year, we see weddings being strong. Last year, we didn't have any weddings in Q1 and Q2, but this year, we see significant weddings even in Q1.

items.statement: Phased opening of The Dukes Retreat: 73 rooms, restaurant, bar, pool operational; Four Points Navi Mumbai renovation 20% complete, full completion by July 2025; Taj at Delhi Terminal 3 expected Q2 FY27; Bangalore Marriott new inventory rele
items.quote: The phased opening of The Dukes Retreat continues, 73 rooms -- I repeat. 73 rooms, a restaurant, a bar and a pool are already operational.

items.statement: Plan to reposition Courtyard by Marriott Aravali to Marriott brand over next 6 months, creating new high-energy F&B experiences at JW Marriott Sahar, Westin Powai, Dukes Retreat
items.quote: We are also working on our plans to upwardly reposition the spectacular Courtyard by Marriott Aravali to the Marriott brand.

items.statement: Trivandrum project timelines fluid, not included in INR20 billion capex plan, indicative cost INR1 crore per key for 150-room Phase 1 with convention center
items.quote: Trivandrum is a little fluid, as I mentioned earlier, so we'll not put that number as yet. We will see how that paces up.

items.statement: Net debt INR15.8 billion as of Dec 31, average cost of finance 8.53% (down 34 bps from Mar 24), peak debt expected INR19-20 billion with announced pipeline, hotels debt-free, debt largely on office assets
items.quote: The net debt as on December 31 was at INR15.8 billion. We closed the quarter with an average cost of finance standing at 8.53%, a reduction of 34 bps from March '24.

items.statement: Maintain revenue growth guidance of 18-22% for FY25; raise EBITDA margin outlook from 20.5%+ to 21%+
items.quote: At a high level, first, we maintain and reiterate our guidance for the revenue we had given at the beginning of the year between 18% to 22%. We have raised our EBITDA outlook from 20.5% + to 21% +, and that is reflected also in the EBITDA margin for this quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 21.1% vs 20.8% previous quarter
items.quote: EBITDA is 21.1% versus 20.8% last quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 deal wins of $236 million, balanced across geographies led by Europe
items.quote: The overall deal wins have been $236 million during the quarter, are largely balanced, driven more by Europe and followed by US and Asia.

items.statement: Pipeline increased ~20% quarter-on-quarter led by Europe, driven by large deals and new client engagements across verticals
items.quote: So actually, I'm saying it is a quarter -on-quarter 20%. growth It is not year-on-year, the increase in the pipeline. And yes, it's a very significant number. It's a 20% increase in the pipeline, and it is led by Europe.

items.statement: Expect Europe growth to return by Q4 FY25 or latest Q1 FY26 based on strong pipeline and deal closures
items.quote: So I think the growth will come back latest by quarter 1, if not quarter 4. I hope it will return by quarter 4.

items.statement: Revenue mix improving with growth driven by Asia, Powertrain and Connected vehicles; per-person productivity up year-on-year
items.quote: The overall growth during this quarter is driven by Asia, Powertrain and Connected vehicles. The revenue mix has really improved. And mainly our productivity continued to improve.

items.statement: SDV opportunity extends beyond EV to digital cockpit, autonomous driving, cybersecurity and conventional powertrain
items.quote: The SDV, as you look at it, it is much beyond EV in that sense. And if you actually ask me, the largest growth will be driven for us in terms of digital cockpit and autonomous in the next few years.

items.statement: No QIP planned in short term; acquisitions to be funded through internal accruals and borrowing
items.quote: On the M&A side, we continue to engage with few companies. but looking at their sizes and what we see currently, we do not see that we will opt for QIP in the short term. So we believe some of these acquisitions, we will do through internal accruals on the basis of strong cash flow and borrowing.

items.statement: No significant visa/immigration challenges expected; well prepared to increase local presence as needed
items.quote: We do not see any significant challenges in terms of visa, etcetera, basically because we believe it is about the talent and not about the immigration. And so we believe that there will be a continued mobility for short-term projects as needed.

items.statement: Cash increased from INR 9.68B to INR 14.2B in Q3; DSO improved to 42 days; interim dividend raised to INR 2.5/share
items.value: INR 14.2B cash; 42 days DSO; INR 2.5/share dividend
items.quote: The cash for the quarter has increased from INR9.68 billion last quarter to INR14.2 billion this quarter. This is a significant cash generation during the quarter. It's an exceptional one. Our DSO is 42 days, which we typically are about 45 days. So significant cash generation during the quarter. We have interim dividend of INR2.5 per share as compared to INR2.1 per share last year

items.statement: Positive conversations with 8 new clients; pipeline broad-based across passenger cars, off-highway, commercial and semi-con for automotive
items.quote: We have positive conversations going with 8 new clients, which we have been pursuing and that has resulted into broad-based pipeline for KPIT. It is across the vertical. I mean it is, of course, led by Passenger cars, but there is a meaningful pipeline in off -highway, commercial and semi-con for automotive.

items.statement: Other expense up 11% sequentially due to one-off investments in AI, competency development and consultants for off-highway/commercial verticals
items.quote: It's an absolutely one-off kind of a thing increase, but we continue to do that. So I think we had a substantial additional expense during this quarter, where we have actually had a significant investment into both the technology as well as management development, both for AI and competencies.

items.statement: Honda-Nissan merger seen as positive opportunity to expand partnership to Nissan and drive cost reduction programs
items.quote: We actually look at this as a greater opportunity, not only from the work that we are doing for Honda, many of the things that we are doing for Honda where Honda is leading the way. So we believe that if all of this goes through, there could be opportunities for us to bring the Nissan part of the partnership also up to speed with what has been done.

items.statement: Geography mix shift to Asia not a margin headwind; improving revenue mix toward license/platform/outcome-based models with better margins; AI-driven productivity gains expected
items.quote: And on top of it, I may also say that we are also improving our mix of revenue towards either license , platforms outcome -based revenues, where the margins are better. And so we feel comfortable at this point of time.

items.statement: Committed to cumulative capex plan of INR6,000 crores by FY28 for battery materials business
items.quote: We are committed to our cumulative capex plan of INR6,000 crores by FY '28, as we had indicated earlier.

items.statement: R-32 capacity expansion of up to 30,000 tons with Phase 1 of 20,000 tons by Q4 FY26 at INR150 crores
items.quote: We are looking at almost setting up a capacity of 30,000 tons, okay? So -- and we have time in terms of till we can utilize this quota.

items.statement: Salt plant expansion underway as part of existing INR6,000 crore EV capex plan, no additional capex
items.quote: The -- our intent of giving the statement about salt was it's not an additional capex . Our capex plan is still what we had indicated INR 6,000 crores.

items.statement: AHF capacity expansion planned for next year, not included in R-32 INR150 crore capex
items.quote: Yes, we have a plan for AHF as well, Dhruv. Of course , in next quarter, I think we'll share our capex plan for the next year, and then we'll talk about it.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer commercial sales expected from Q4 FY25 after legacy player plant shutdown in Dec 2024
items.quote: As we understand, the plant is shut down in December last year, which is December '24. So that is already shut. We have already gone through the qualifications on various grades. We have received qualifications, and we expect now that into commercial sales in quarter 4 onwards.

items.statement: Battery materials business targets ~25% EBITDA margins and 2x asset turnover at optimal utilization
items.quote: At optimal utilization level, this business is expected to achieve around 2x asset turnover and approximately 25% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Power cost reduction of 10-12% (~INR100 crores) expected from FY26 via renewable energy aggregation
items.quote: Currently, our power cost stood at around INR 800 crores. So we expect a reduction of 10% to 12% -- 10% to 12% reduction. That is around INR100 crores.

items.statement: Weighted average power cost expected at INR4.5/unit with 80% renewable energy at INR4/unit
items.quote: The power purchase agreement that we are -- we have signed for the new energy -- renewable energy is at INR 4. So that would constitute more than 80% of our total requirement. So to that extent, the power -- the weighted average will be in the range of around INR4.5.

items.statement: US EV market projected at 1 in 4 cars sold being electric by 2025, Europe battery capacity to reach 800 GWh by 2030
items.quote: By 2025, it is projected that 1 in 4 cars sold in U.S. will be electric. Also, the U.S. mark et has evolved to a position where long-term vehicle ownership economics are gradually turning in favor of EVs.

items.statement: Domestic EV demand supported by Maharashtra petrol/diesel ban panel and Delhi 2027 last-mile EV transition
items.quote: Recently, based on our estimates, the capacity, which has been announced are in excess of 300 gigawatt hour, providing an additional upside potential in the domestic markets for ESS and EV.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer margin improvement driven by increasing fraction of value-added and new polymers
items.quote: And when coming back to margin improvement, margin improvement is purely by product mix, as our overall fraction of our value -added products and the new polymers are increasing, the margins would keep on going up.

items.statement: R-22 refrigerant prices improved in Q3 with further pickup expected; R-125 prices and volumes to improve going forward
items.quote: Within f luorochemicals segment, refrigerant gas prices, particularly for R- 22, improved during the quarter with further pickup expected going forward. For R-125, which is primarily exported to U.S., Q3 is seasonally weak quarter, but both prices and volumes are expected to improve going forward.

items.statement: MDC prices improved in Q3 but expected muted near-term due to new Indian capacities
items.quote: MDC prices have improved during the quarter. However, it is expected to be muted in near term because of additional capacities being commissioned in India.

items.statement: IRA subsidy uncertainty in US but customer investment plans remain intact for next 3-5 years
items.quote: And we have been talking to our customers. And most of our customers' plan in terms of their investment and setting up the capacities is still there. So based on their investment and their capacities, we fairly -- we have a visibility that at least in the next 3 to 5 years, the plan that we had given is going to be intact, okay?

items.statement: Fluoropolymer full capacity utilization expected by end of FY26
items.quote: We expect our full capacity utilization to be there by the end of FY '26, yes.

items.statement: Management targets 15% CAGR growth over three years and aims to beat Q3 performance in Q4 FY25
items.quote: And then going forward on a three- year basis, I think we already had kind of indicated about a 15% CAGR growth. So largely, I thi nk we will try to kind of embark on that kind of a trajectory

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin impacted by Rs 57.1M LTIP and Rs 100M non-recurring costs; adjusted EBITDA margin 11.9%
items.quote: Operating margins were impacted marginally, owing to t he impact of Rs. 57.1 million of long -term incentive plan which pertained to the period July to December 2024

items.statement: Nine months FY25 EBITDA margin 12% vs 12.5% prior year; adjusted for related party transactions 12.33%
items.quote: EBITDA margin though contracted marginally from 12.5% in nine months FY '24 to 12% in nine months FY '25.

items.statement: Overall pricing stable with marginal increase in Q3; no significant decline
items.quote: So, this quarter, I think we have on an overall basis, we have seen pricing, I think, pretty much stable and marginally increase. So, there isn't any much significant decline.

items.statement: Domestic NLD volumes declined due to competitor platform recovery; ILD and rest of world grew mid-teens
items.quote: I think the domestic volumes have come off a little bit. That's largely because I think till Q2, I mean for a particular bank, we were getting their entire share of traffic while there were two CPaaS players empaneled with the bank.

items.statement: New product revenue grew 150% over 11 quarters; next-gen products up 21% YoY; WhatsApp pricing change impacted new product growth
items.quote: We have delivered 150% growth in the new product revenue, 60% growth in revenue excluding new products over the last 11 quarters.

items.statement: Telesign revenue Rs 298 crores in nine months FY25; Vodafone volumes growing on enterprise side
items.quote: Yes, so on a nine-month basis, I think with Telesign, we have done close to about Rs. 298 crores-odd of business.

items.statement: Retired loan in early December reducing interest cost; cash and equivalents Rs 9,303M, net cash Rs 7,457M as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs. 9,303 million and net cash was Rs. 7,457 million as on December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Contingent liability on exclusive firewall contract in Southeast Asia due to sanctions and social media bans; renegotiation ongoing
items.quote: So, I think this is the contract I think where, so this is actually an exclusive firewall contract in Southeast Asia, where what has actually happened is th ere have been challenges in terms of, I think, increased sanction conditions where a lot of social media apps have been banned

items.statement: Proximus Global formed combining BICS, Telesign, Route Mobile; leadership changes: Rajdip MD, Gautam CEO, Raj Gill Group CFO
items.quote: As you may have seen in the recent announcement, Proximus Group has c reated Proximus Global, which brings together BICS, Telesign, and Route Mobile under a single umbrella

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs 3 per share recommended; CFO to EBITDA conversion 102% for nine months FY25
items.quote: Considering the superlative performance, the Board has recommended an interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share.

items.statement: Digital identity solutions with Telesign stack in sandbox testing; DPDP law navigation ongoing; $1M revenue currently via Masivian
items.quote: We were doing close to $1 million, already with them. And as I think we have highlighted, I think TeleSign has a significantly more evolved digital identity stack.

items.statement: RCS deployment with Robi Axiata in Bangladesh; metro ticketing solution replicated in Indonesia via Proximus Global footprint
items.quote: We as a company are probably the first Indian company who have deployed the RCS map server with Robi Axiata in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Employee cost: LTIP impact Rs 5.77 crores in Q3 (two quarters); run rate Rs 3 crores/quarter for CY25; total operating base Rs 110 crores/quarter
items.quote: Going forward on a quarterly basis, that run rate will be about Rs. 3 crores till the end of the calendar year.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guidance ~20% for FY25; nine months FY25 at 21.2% vs 15.1% prior year
items.quote: And in terms of the effective tax rate, I think it is fair to assume it to be in the vicinity of 20%.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Target AUM of INR 20,000 crore by Mar'27 implying 27-30% CAGR from FY24
items.quote: INR 20,000 crores is a number that we are looking to hit by Mar'27.

items.statement: Aim to average INR 500 crore monthly disbursements next year vs INR 400 crore currently
items.quote: Next year, we are looking to average close to INR 500 crores.

items.statement: Spreads guided at 5% to 5.25% range
items.quote: The spreads will remain in the 5% to 5.25% range that we have been guiding all along.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 30-40 bps medium term
items.quote: We continue to maintain our conservative medium-term cost -- credit cost guidance of 30 basis points to 40 basis points as we focus on growth.

items.statement: Operating cost to assets expected to remain range bound at 2.7-2.8%
items.quote: We expect this ratio to remain range bound within 2.7% to 2.8% as we focus on growth and expansion.

items.statement: Insurance commission expected at INR 15-18 crore per quarter going ahead
items.quote: We expect the insurance commission to be in the range of INR 15 crore to INR 18 crore per quarter going ahead.

items.statement: Co-lending to contribute around 10% of disbursements in medium term
items.quote: We expect co-lending to contribute around 10% of disbursements in the medium term.

items.statement: Plan to add 30-40 branches in FY26 with 50-50 split between new and existing markets
items.quote: Largely in a year, we try to target about 30 to 40 branches. A similar number will be there next year as well.

items.statement: Board approved equity raise of up to INR 1,250 crore to support growth to INR 20,000 crore AUM by Mar'27
items.quote: The Board has approved raising equity capital of up to INR 1,250 crore.

items.statement: NIM compressed 24 bps QoQ to 4.9% due to higher borrowing cost, liquidity, leverage and lower realized yields
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q3 was at 4.9%. NIM have compressed by 24 basis points on a QoQ basis.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing ex co-lending rose marginally to 8.4%; 35 bps rate hike in August on 40% of customer base
items.quote: As we had expected, the cost of borrowing, excluding co-lending has gone up marginally to 8.4%.

items.statement: No structural stress seen; collections in January as good as any previous month; delinquency uptick seasonal/temporary
items.quote: Collections, if we actually track day-to-day daily collections throughout the month and how the collection is moving every month, we are not seeing any difference in the way customers are paying.

items.statement: Early warning signals from portfolio analysis and market observations led to tighter credit filters impacting INR 10-15 cr disbursements
items.quote: Based on some inputs that we have got for certain products, we have tightened the norms, we have increased the number of filters in the process.

items.statement: ROE expected to dip to 15.5% post equity raise then recover to 17-17.5% in 8-10 quarters; 3-year average ROE targeted at 16-16.5%
items.quote: We should go down to 15.5% and then aim to pick up back to 17%- 17.5% in about 8 to 10 quarters.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration of INR 35,000 crore AUM by 2030 with higher co-lending and LAP share
items.quote: Broadly, we are looking at an INR 35,000 crores kind of a number by 2030.

items.statement: Maintain 15-20% year-on-year AUM growth guidance for NBFC
items.quote: So, we continue to maintain the same guidance which we gave earlier about 15 to 20% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Expect to achieve 15-20% AUM growth in Q4 FY25 based on seasonal trend
items.quote: Our last quarter is always heavy. If you see our last 2-3 years operating numbers. So, given that trend, we expect that we would be able to achieve 15-20% of AUM.

items.statement: Comfortable with 3-3.5x debt-to-equity leverage; can grow loan book to Rs 2400-2500 cr without equity infusion
items.period: next year or couple of years
items.quote: Yes, without any further equity infusion, we can do with 3 or 3.5 times leverage, we can reach our loan book of about 2400 or 2500 crores.

items.statement: Tightened underwriting policies; reduced approval rates due to higher delinquencies in sector
items.quote: So, number one, we have tightened our underwriting policies during the year. As you might know, you must have seen higher delinquencies in the other NBFC and banks.

items.statement: Shifted focus from Prime LAP to Micro LAP for higher yield, scalability, and less bank competition
items.quote: Secondly, as I discussed in last quarter's earning call also, we have shifted our focus from Prime LAP to Micro LAP.

items.statement: LAP disbursements dropped to Rs 65 cr in 9M FY25 vs Rs 250 cr in FY24; Rs 60 cr foreclosed
items.quote: Last year, we did disbursement of around 250 crores under the LAP product, but during this year, 9 months, we have disbursed almost 65 crores and essentially that almost 60 crores of LAP book is also foreclosed during the current year.

items.statement: Target unsecured book reduction from 34-35% to 30% of on-book AUM in next 1-2 years
items.period: next year or couple of years
items.quote: Currently on the on-book AUM, our unsecured book constitutes around 34 or 35% of on-book AUM. And then we want to bring it down to 30 in the next year or couple of years.

items.statement: No major stress seen in loan book; quality satisfactory compared to peers
items.quote: So, we have not seen any major stress. If you look at the stress that we have been witnessing in other lenders balance sheet. So, we are quite confident and satisfied with the quality of the book if you compare it with the peers.

items.statement: Regulatory changes (weekly settlement closure) hit broking-trading segment in Q3 FY25
items.quote: SEBI's did certain regulatory changes, closing down weekly settlements, which were running 5 weekly settlements. They made only one for one exchange and one monthly settlement. So, in our broking, distribution and trading, we have affected.

items.statement: Vehicle pickup slowdown impacted insurance broking revenue in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Insurance broking, in that sense, pickup of vehicles was slowed down in the economy and that was slowed down. Because of that, insurance broking has been affected in 3rd quarter.

items.statement: Expect regulatory impact to minimize in Q4 FY25; investors adapting to monthly contracts
items.quote: I think in 4th quarter, certain segments will do well. We are quite hopeful and investors also changes their methodology considering regulatory changes. So, the effect done by regulatory changes will be minimized in 4th Quarter.

items.statement: Planning to expand margin trading funding and focus on Nifty/BSE Sensex monthly derivative contracts
items.quote: Third, I think margin trading funding products will do much better. So, we are gearing up to for that product also and generally, investors adopted the changes very fast in India and I think this will be improved in the existing contracts or monthly contracts and Nifty, which is there, and in BSE, BSE Sensex is there as a derivative product.

items.statement: 9M FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 26.2%; PAT margin 10.5%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA was reported at approximately Rs. 355.4 crore, an increase of approximately 24.3% year-on-year basis and EBITDA margin stood at 26.2%. Net profit after tax was reported at approximately Rs. 142.7 crore, while the PAT margin stood at about 10.5% approximately.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 24.5%; PAT margin 9.6%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA was reported at approximately Rs. 111.8 crore and the EBITDA margin showed at around 24.5%. Net profit after tax reported was Rs. 43.9 crore, while the PAT margin stood at 9.6%.

items.statement: NBFC AUM Rs 1285.8 cr, up 20.9% YoY; Gross NPA 2.27%, Net NPA 1.16%
items.quote: Our loan AUM increased to Rs. 1285.8 crore, an increase of 20.9% year-on-year basis. The Gross NPA and net NPA were at 2.27% and 1.16% respectively.

items.quote: The way to look at it is that technical outsourcing is primarily linked to government projects. items.statement: Qualcomm partnership revenue impact expected after at least one year due to automotive OEM development cycles
items.quote: This is given that it's for automotive OEMs, the impact on revenue will be seen post 1 year at least.

items.quote: Your number is right.

items.quote: The company continues to report industry -leading gross margin of 67.3% and healthy EBITDA margin of 47.4%. The company reported best -in-class PAT margin of around 30.9%.

items.statement: Gross store additions target 170,000-180,000 sq ft for FY25; net additions lower due to closures
items.quote: So, at the gross level, we will be doing a decent amount of opening, close to about 1,70,000, 1,80,000 square feet, which is what we've been focusing on for the entire financial year. So, from a gross perspective, we are on track.

items.statement: FY26 store expansion depends on rental market stabilization; pipeline strong but signing delayed
items.quote: If things stable earlier than we anticipate, then we will definitely try to open more stores. However, if the rentals remain at similar levels, then it is difficult to comment on the scale at which we will be opening stores next year.

items.statement: Excluding AP & Telangana, SSSG was ~10% for Q2+Q3 combined; Q3 alone ~5% ex AP/Telangana
items.quote: Broadly what we saw is about 10% growth in L2L when we see the last 2 quarters, excluding of AP, Telangana. So our SSSG was about 10% in Q2 and Q3 combined when we exclude AP, Telangana.

items.statement: Tier 2/3 cities outperformed metros by ~5% delta; trend reversed positively from Q1
items.quote: Broadly, I think Tier 2, Tier 3 has a 5% delta over metros. So that's the sort of improvement we've seen. But the encouraging piece is that the trend was the other way around for many quarters up until Q1.

items.statement: Mohey productivity reached near Manyavar levels (25-30% area, 25-30% sales); Twamev growing strongly in metros
items.quote: Earlier, it used to achieve close to 70% of Manyavar's productivity within that area. But now what we are witnessing with all the new stores and even the older stores, we have reached almost Manyavar's productivity.

items.statement: ASP grew ~1-1.5% in Q3; premium and value ends growing, middle segment weak
items.quote: At a company level, our ASP has grown by about 1% or 1.5%. But if you see from a market angle, this has been quite varied. So we see both the premium end growing and the bottom end growing from our company's perspective.

items.statement: Middle-class discretionary spending weak; AP & Telangana macro headwinds persist
items.quote: We don't feel that competition per se has played a big role. But yes, we do feel at a macro level, there are some headwinds where the middle class is definitely sort of not back at the level of consumption when it comes to apparel as they used to be.

items.statement: Rental inflation in core markets delaying store signings; other brands signing at high rents
items.quote: The challenge lies in core markets where demand is already high, where the prices are becoming very difficult. So those are the kind of markets where the pain lies in terms of rental inflation.

items.statement: January trends similar to Q3; only 15 days of normal trading observed so far

items.quote: It's about 3% to 4%, but our growth has been very strong in the online segment. We have been growing probably the fastest in that as a channel. And overall, about 70-odd percent growth is what we've seen in Q3 when it comes to online.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance raised to INR 510-520 crores from earlier INR 475-500 crores

items.quote: Our focus on expansion of NIM, NII and increasing fee income will be the key drivers for our targeted ROA -- annualized ROA of 1.4% plus for FY '25.

items.statement: Intend to expand CD ratio to mid- to high 80s in FY26
items.quote: We intend to expand our CD ratios to mid- to the high 80s in FY '26.

items.statement: Aspirational ROE target of mid- to high teens
items.quote: Our endeavour is to be hit the next capital market when we have ROEs in the mid to the high teens.

items.statement: NIM increased to 4.3% in Q3 FY25 from 3.9% a year ago
items.quote: NIM has increased to 4.3% in Q3 FY '25 against 3.9% in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 6% and cost of deposits at 5.9% in Q3 FY25, flat QoQ
