items.quote: Going forward, in Q4, I'm anticipating our fee income to be in the range of 0.85% or rather 0.9% to 1% in the Q4.

items.statement: Company aims to continue 20-25% average annual growth with specialty wire vertical as additional driver
items.quote: So, sir as a company, even in the last 10 years we have grown at 20 % to25% on an average, which is what we want to continue going ahead . With this we are also adding specialty wire vertical which is a new vertical and which is also one of our main focus areas.

items.statement: Dadri expansion increased from 3.5 to 4.2 lakh tonnes with additional Rs 70-80 crore investment
items.period: first two quarters of next year
items.quote: Now we have increased that by about 20% to 4. 2 lakh tonnes. This is owning to some demand that we are looking at in different products from our customers. Therefore our investment will also increase by about ₹ 70 to 80 crores in total.

items.statement: Stainless steel rod backward integration land acquisition in Sanand Gujarat finalized, equipment orders within 2 months, production in FY27
items.quote: Within a week we should have the possession on the land. And apart from that, even the equipment's, we are in daily touch with our manufacturers and we should be able to finalize some orders within the next two months. After this, it will take us about 15 to 18 months to really establish them and start production.

items.statement: Specialty wire pilot project 20,000 tonnes capacity with Rs 150 crore invested for steel cord
items.quote: With a 150 crore CAPEX that we have almost already done is only for steel cord .

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical selling 100-120 tonnes in first month January with expedited approvals for hose wire and steel cord
items.quote: We have got very good response, and in fact as we speak, we are able to sell about 100 to120 tonnes within this first month January.

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical targets 20-25% EBITDA margin versus current lower margins
items.quote: The revenue potential of this product for us right now is about ₹300 crore, in which if you look at the current prices, or the prices that were prevailing in the market till now, it has been about 20% to25% kind of an EBITDA that we look at, which is fairly different from our current numbers.

items.statement: Strong demand across all sectors in Q4 with automotive gaining market share despite seasonal slowdown
items.quote: So right now, it is all about producing more, because sales is not a challenge. So even in Q4 we see a good demand from our customers coming across all products, not just one, all high carbon stainless steel as well as low carbon we see a good response.

items.statement: Consolidation of group companies drove 25-30% volume growth in Q3 with 10-15% organic volume increase
items.quote: So you will see about 25% to 30% kind of a growth here, in which I would say most of it has come because of consolidation. So about 10% to 15% is the volume increase that we have done quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Raw material price fluctuations and geopolitical risks persist as challenges
items.quote: While challenges like fluctuating raw material prices and geopolitical risk persist, we see immense opportunity in both domestic as well as the export market.

items.statement: Natural hedge model with 70-75% orders backed by inventory or supplier orders, cost-plus pricing passes raw material changes to customers
items.quote: So, sir what we try to do is we try to create a kind of a natural hedge in our business model, wherein whatever orders we have is we already have either inventory or pending orders from our raw material suppliers. So therefore we try to keep about a 70% to 75% of our pending orders and stock booked against firm orders.

items.statement: IHT wire investment expedited with orders placed, targeting Q1 commissioning
items.quote: We were supposed to start investment in IHT wire by mid of next year, but we have already placed some orders, and we will hopefully do something within the first quarter.

items.statement: Dadri facility at 30% utilization with 80% of 3.5 lakh tonne capacity commissioned, full commissioning in 2 months
items.quote: We have now touched about 30% kind of a utilization level in Dadri. Deepesh Kashyap: And sir capacity is how much right now? Pranav Bansal: Sir the capacity, I would say about 80% of our capacity has already been commissioned, and the balance is also being commissioning w ithin the next two months, we should be able to commission the complete 3.5 lakh

items.statement: Export revenue reached Rs 250 crore in 9M FY25 versus Rs 219 crore in corresponding period
items.quote: Our export also accounted to about 250 crores till the end of Q 3 as against 219 crores compared to the corresponding year underscoring strong international demand from our products and new product offering.

items.statement: Working capital optimization through bill discounting to start next quarter or Q1 next year after consolidation
items.period: next quarter or Q1 of next year
items.quote: But after the consolidation of Balaji and Bansal High Carbon within Bansal Wire, now we see that maybe next quarter, or from Q 1 of next year we will start utilization which will bring our debt level down as well.

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical includes steel cord (import substitute), hose wire, bead wire, and IHT wire for EVs
items.quote: the main product in specialty wire vertical is a product that we call steel cord. Now, steel cord is a product that, we will be the first and the only Indian company to make this product t ill now. This is used in tyres

items.statement: Revised full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance to 30% from 25%
items.quote: In the light of 33% year-on-year top-line growth reported for the first 9 -months of FY25, we are revising our full-year guidance to 30% growth from 25% for FY25.

items.statement: Pre-IND AS EBITDA guidance for FY25 is INR950-980 million
items.quote: We are on track to close the financial year with an EBITDA of around INR950-INR980 million.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance 7-8% and PAT margin 3-4% on pre-IND AS basis
items.quote: And on the guidance on the EBITDA margin, it will be between 7% to 8%. And on the PAT side, it will be between 3 to 4%.

items.statement: Targeting 25-30% revenue growth with 8-10% L2L growth as balanced strategy
items.quote: We would like to grow ourselves between 25%-30% in terms of revenue with an L2L growth of around 8 %-10%.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at INR60-65 crores for 40-50 stores plus INR15-20 crores for tech/infra
items.quote: So you can expect anything between INR60-65 crores on that side, and apart from that if there is any other capex expansion going in the warehouse or the infra side that will be the additional cost on that.

items.statement: Net store additions of 37 in 9M FY25; expect 45-50 net additions for full FY25
items.quote: We now expect to add between 45-50 stores by the end of this fiscal year, further strengthening our footprint and positioning us for continued growth.

items.statement: Store-level pre-IND AS EBITDA margin improved to 14.23% in 9M FY25 from 14.08%
items.quote: So for the first 9 months, it is around 14.23% against 14.08% last year , for the full 9 months , including new stores.

items.statement: Corporate overheads increased 0.85% of sales to INR60-65 crores in 9M FY25 from INR40-45 crores
items.quote: So, approximately around INR60 crores-INR65 crores has been the corporate overheads for the first 9 months, against which last year it was around INR40 crores-INR45 crores.

items.statement: Private label margin premium only 0.5% due to aggressive pricing for market share
items.quote: Against which, 0.5% has been the higher margin that we are earning on private labels. But as a strategy, because we want to expand our footprint in all the areas and expand our private label brands in all the areas. As a strategy, we are going for an aggressive pricing.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook for Q4 FY25 driven by wedding season and Eid
items.quote: With the wedding season and the Eid approaching, we expect a strong performance in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Private label contribution 44% in 9M FY25 vs 37% in 9M FY24; apparel 87%, general merchandise 13%
items.quote: Private label contribution was at 38% in Q3 FY25 vs 35% in Q3 FY24 and 44% in 9 -months FY25 vs 37% in 9-months FY24. Our inventory per square feet has reduced by INR200 sq. ft from last year.

items.statement: Insurance claim of INR48 crores pending from Q1 fire incident; expected by March end
items.quote: So, around INR48 crores is the expectation amount from the insurance company which is due as of now. So, that fund is also utilized in this limit.

items.statement: Net debt INR100 crores (bank borrowings) plus INR16 crores bill acceptance; cash INR14.63 crores
items.quote: So, net debt is INR100 crores -- bank borrowings is INR100 crores, and bill acceptance is INR16 crores, total debt in books is INR116 crores, and cash and bank balance is INR14.63 crores.

items.statement: Inventory reduced to INR2,100 per sq ft from INR2,300; inventory days 112; creditor days 72 vs 83 last year
items.quote: In terms of inventory, we have reduced our inventory by INR200 per square feet from last year. So we were at INR2300 per square feet inventory, 9 -months FY24, which is around INR2100 per square feet as on 9-months FY25.

items.statement: 90% full-price sales in 9M FY25; mature store sales INR9,000/sq ft annualized
items.quote: 90% is the full price sale through for the first 9 months.

items.statement: Order book at end of Q3 FY25 stood at INR19,971 crores; INR12,244 crores under execution, INR4,642 crores awaiting appointed dates, INR3,084 crores L1 status
items.quote: At the end of third quarter, the order book stood in INR19,971 crores. INR12,244 crores worth of the projects are under execution, INR4,642 crores awaiting appointed dates and the rest that is INR3,084 crores include one project each of roads and OFC that are having L1 status.

items.statement: Declared L1 for Maharashtra road project INR1,947 crores and Western Railway project INR222 crores in January; 13 projects worth INR13,992 crores submitted and expected to open soon
items.quote: On a separate note, I'm happy to share that we have been declared L1 for the road project in Maharashtra, amounting to INR1,947 crores and a Rail Project of Western Railways amounting INR222 crores for this month that is in January. As on date, the company has submitted 13 highway, railway and ropeway projects amounting to INR13,992 crores, which are expected to be opened soon.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow target revised to INR17,000 crores from INR20,000 crores; FY26 order inflow target INR20,000 crores
items.quote: Current year, we are targeting almost INR17,000 crores of the orders in flow, right? Yes. So next year -- I mean, this year, our target -- original target was INR20,000 crores, so we'll try to stick with that for next year as well.

items.statement: FY25 capex not more than INR125 crores (INR30-40 crores remaining in Q4); FY26 capex maximum INR150 crores
items.quote: The capex, we are not expecting more than -- for the full year not more than INR125 crores. So maybe another INR30 crores, INR40 crores for the current year or for next year, again, because capex, we are, I would say, fairly -- capex is already having we are in our balance sheet, so we don't expect much -- I mean, there is not significant difference from what we have been doing for last 2 years, s

items.statement: Awarding activity muted in first 3 quarters with underbidding up to 40%; expect decent flow of large projects in Q4 FY25 given budget allocation; targeting INR1,35,000 crores pipeline across highways, tunnels, metro, power transmission, rai
items.quote: This year, awarding activity is a little muted in the first 3 quarters, also the instance of underbidding up to 40% persist. Having said that, looking at the central government's budgetary allocation towards infrastructure, we expect a decent flow of awarding utilities, especially large projects coming in the last quarter. The company is targeting an order pipeline of approximately INR1,35,000 cro

items.statement: Diversifying beyond roads into transmission, ropeway, tunneling, metros, telecom; road share of new orders not more than 30-40%; will bid for BOT annuity and BOT toll projects
items.quote: we are not targeting 50%. I would say road would be not more than 30% or 40% because given the competition so far, it has not yet come to that level, right? So what we believe is that we'll be bidding into different, different sectors, maybe transmission, ropeway, then road also. And then, Tunneling is also there, right

items.statement: InvIT income INR178 crores YTD FY25, INR39-40 crores in Q3, expecting INR60 crores in Q4; FY26-27 run rate INR200-250 crores
items.quote: for last quarter -- I mean, the quarter ended December 2024, we have received that in -- around INR39 crores or INR40 crores from InvIT, right, for the -- so far -- I mean, for the year, it is INR178 crores, the income which we have received from the InvIT, right? For last quarter, it was INR39 crores or INR40-odd crores. On -- in current quarter -- I mean, in Q4 for the current fiscal, we are exp

items.statement: Phase-2 brownfield expansion capex of Rs. 700 crores; Rs. 480 crores spent till 31 Dec 2024; minor delay of 2-3 months due to manpower and equipment supply delays
items.quote: On the ongoing brownfield expansion to reach capacities of 1 million tons of DI pipes, out of our planned CAPEX of Rs. 700 crores for Phase-2, we have already spent Rs. 480 crores till 31st of December. There is a minor delay of around 2-3 months on account of manpower shortage and delays in supply of equipment, and we are hopeful to reach installed capacity of 9 lakh tons by the end of March 2025

items.statement: Order book of around 8.5 months, approximately 6 lakh tons of DI pipes
items.quote: So, we have around 8-1/2 months of order book at the moment, so around 6 lakh tons of DI pipes.

items.statement: Demand for DI pipes remains robust driven by River Linking, Viksit Bharat, Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0; momentary government spending pause expected to reverse post Budget
items.quote: The demand for DI pipes and fittings continues to be robust on account of initiatives like River Linking, Viksit Bharat Vision, Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0. Although there is a pause for some time from the government on spending, which has been seen across all sectors, we are optimistic the government will continue to push towards infrastructure spending from the upcoming Union Budget FY2025-

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 16%-18% range; currently at 16.7% standalone
items.quote: I think historically, if you see these, we have always hit a margin of 15%-18%. At the moment, we are at 16.7%. I think these are pretty stable numbers which we should be able to carry on for the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Coking coal prices down $35-$40; iron ore prices up; net raw material cost impact neutralized
items.quote: Actually, in the raw material front, on the coke front, and coking coals and all that, there has been a downward trend. And the price correction to the tune of some $35-$40 has come down, but at the same time, as far as iron ore is concerned, there has been a upward trend, so practically on raw material front, they have neutralized each other, more or less.

items.statement: US export business hit due to market slowdown and tariff concerns; now only 1% of exports vs 5% earlier; no immediate local manufacturing solution
items.quote: So, there is an overall slowdown in the US market for our product as a whole. And secondly, because of the impending possibilities of tariffs that to come and Made in America programs that are there. The customers are a little apprehensive in buying non-American products right now.

items.statement: Fittings volume increased ~3,000 tons in 9M FY25 vs prior year; targeting 25,000 tons; expanding coatings/linings portfolio
items.quote: In fact, let me highlight the fittings numbers, we have already seen an increase of approximately 3000 tons this Financial Year, 9 months average as opposed to last year and this is all owing to the addition of new product lines. So as such, we are looking at going up to 25,000 odd tons over there.

items.statement: Anti-subsidy refund of Rs. 23 crores received from European Commission in Q3; ongoing annual process, amount varies
items.quote: So, Sir, this is on account of anti-subsidy refund that we have got from the European Commission. There is an anti-subsidy duty that they avail on us, but we keep applying for refunds and we have managed to get a refund of Rs. 23 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: JSW coal block asset valuation and categorization ongoing; mine handed over but underground infrastructure nil; claim of Rs. 1,200 crores, majority expected to be realized
items.quote: Our claim is of Rs. 1200 crores so the way it is going on we are optimistic that the majority of this will be realized.

items.statement: Odisha greenfield project ~4-5 lakh tons capacity; realistic timeline FY27-28
items.quote: I think somewhere between FY27-28 is a bit more realistic.

items.statement: No demand-supply mismatch expected for next 3 years; live orders indicate demand will surpass supply once fund flows restart
items.quote: I am not really concerned about demand supply mismatch whether supply is more at least for the next 3 years. There might be temporary blips like we have seen in the last quarter, but that is very momentary. The kind of live orders in the market, once the fund flow start we will go back to a situation where demand is surpassing supply.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 and FY26 EBITDA margin expected to hold at 16%-18% range; difficult to give per-ton rupee guidance
items.quote: Sir, I think it will be difficult for me to give you an exact number in terms of rupees per ton, but as a percentage, I think we will be able to hold on to the performance we had so far.

items.statement: Momentary slowdown in Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0 tender outflows in Q3-Q4 FY25; expect recovery post Budget and in new financial year
items.quote: Definitely, there was a bit of a slowdown in Q3 and even in Q4FY25. As of now, it is not at the same pace that it was at say last quarter 3 and quarter 4. But as with all other infrastructure spending such as railway and highways, we are pretty sure that come the new Financial Year and even the last one or two months of this quarter with the budget coming out tomorrow, there will be a good allocat

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores with INR6,200 crores spent in 9 months
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: Capacity expansion to 140 million tons by FY28 on track with Orient acquisition taking capacity to 97 million tons
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18.4% in Q3 FY25 with EBITDA per ton of INR1,038
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: Operational cost at INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25, targeting INR3,650-3,700 by FY28
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Driven by better fuel management and structural initiatives, our power and fuel costs have decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 last year.

items.statement: Logistics costs reduced 6% to INR1,239 per ton in Q3 FY25 from INR1,322 per ton in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Because of these initiatives, our logistics costs have been reduced by 6% to INR1,239 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,322 per ton in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 21.5% from 15.8%, targeting 60% of power requirements through green power by FY28
items.quote: Both WHRS and solar power would ensure that 60% of our power requirements are -- of the planned 140 million tons would be through green power.

items.statement: Industry demand growth was tepid 1.5-2% in H1 FY25, expected to rebound to 4-5% in FY25
items.quote: The improved consumption demand in housing and infrastructure segments and increased government spendings are poised to reverse the tepid 1.5% to 2% cement demand growth during H1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Blended cements at 82%, premium products as percentage of trade sales volume increased 400 bps to 26%
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna assets currently at sub-40% and sub-50% utilization, expected to reach 70%+ in next financial year
items.quote: My estimate is in the next financial year, both the assets should go up, I think Sanghi earlier and Penna because it's also in the market where it takes time to ramp up. But both of them should hit 70% plus utilization levels in the next financial year.

items.statement: Net worth increased to almost INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores in April, company remains nil debt with AAA rating
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition cash outflow around INR4,000 crores in Q4 FY25, open offer separate later
items.quote: in terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Incentive income expected to increase from INR400-500 crores annually to INR600-650 crores prospectively with new capacities
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in and giving the benefit of incentives.

items.statement: 200 MW solar power project at Khavda, Gujarat commissioned in Q3 FY25, 1000 MW RE target by June 2026
items.quote: 200-megawatt solar power, the project in Gujarat, Khavda, has been commissioned in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 631 million tons of new limestone reserves secured in Q3 FY25, one mine in MP and one in Karnataka
items.quote: To secure our limestone supplies in Q3 FY '25, we have won bids for another 2 mines having reserves of 631 million tons, one in MP and one in Karnataka.

items.statement: Expect to launch at least 1 million sq ft of retail GLA each year from FY27 onwards and deliver on pipeline by FY2030
items.quote: we expect to launch at least 1 million square feet each year from 2027 onwards as well. And we are well to deliver on that pipeline that we had anticipated by FY 2030.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex was Rs 1,758 crores including Rs 965 crores for land acquisitions and Rs 793 crores construction cost
items.quote: Capital expenditure for 9MFY25 was at Rs. 1,758 crores which includes acquisition of three assets, mainly the Mittal land (in Bangalore), Coimbatore and Chandigarh, total amount is Rs. 965 crores and the total construction cost is around Rs. 793 crores.

items.statement: Palladium Mumbai expansion 250,000 sq ft is about 90% leased; rental impact expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Yes, it's about 90% leased. We are holding onto some space, because as the retailers commence their operations there, there is the opportunity to extract premium rentals from the last remaining space.

items.statement: St Regis Mumbai Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin about 49%; Courtyard Agra EBITDA margin 37%
items.quote: Income for Q3 FY25 at The St. Regis, Mumbai, was Rs. 148 crores with an EBITDA of Rs. 72 crores, representing healthy EBITDA margins at about 49%.

items.statement: Residential pricing at Rs 26,100 per sq ft for 9M FY25; management will not drop pricing to accelerate sales
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier in my communication, we are currently at about Rs. 26,100 or thereabouts per square foot is the current pricing. And we have really inched it forward, we have set a new benchmark

items.statement: January consumption extraordinary across portfolio; confident of significant consumption growth ahead
items.quote: Well, i f we go by how January has panned out for us, it's been extraordinary across the portfolio. So I cannot crystal gaze, on how the consumption will be for the rest of the year. But we are very, very confident that we are going to continue to see a significant growth in consumption

items.statement: Retail strategy: premiumization, category upgradation, F&B densification, optimized store sizes, new brands like Bershka
items.quote: We are now again at that same point where all of these assets we need to be working on premiumization, category upgradation, and of course optimizing the store size, introducing newer brands.

items.statement: Unseasonal heavy rains in Bangalore and Chennai impacted Q3 consumption by ~1.5% (Rs 55-60 crores)
items.quote: It is our estimate that our overall consumption would have been higher by about 1 .5%, approximating about Rs. 55 to Rs. 60 crores in Q3 FY25 had we not seen this unusual weather change.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA at 1.1x; average cost of borrowing reduced to 8.64% (20 bps lower vs Mar 2024)
items.quote: We reduced our average cost of borrowing to 8.64%, which is around 20 bps reduction as compared to March 2024, and we remain committed to the future optimization of our debt cost

items.statement: Thane retail mall 1.3M sq ft GLA; hope to break ground in calendar 2025 after approvals
items.quote: We are currently in the state of approvals, etc. and we hope that during this calendar year we will be able to break ground once we get all our approvals in place.

items.statement: Kolkata residential project One Belvedere launch expected mid to end Q1 FY26; work already commenced
items.quote: So, One Belvedere is the product , that's the name of our product . W e expect to launch it towards the middle or end of Q1 of FY26. And work is commencing over there already.

items.statement: Office portfolio to reach nearly 5 million sq ft by 2025 across Pune, Bangalore, Chennai
items.quote: Our office developments in Pune, Bangalore and Chenn ai will take our total commercial office portfolio to nearly 5 million square feet, in 2025.

items.statement: Core business 9M FY25 operating revenue Rs 2,613 crores (+19% YoY), EBITDA Rs 1,601 crores (+21% YoY)
items.quote: For 9M FY25, operating revenue from our core businesses stood at Rs. 2,613 crores, up 19% versus 9M FY24. EBITDA for the nine months from our core businesses was at Rs. 1,601 crores, up 21% versus 9M FY24.

items.statement: Retail consumption 9M FY25 Rs 10,500 crores (+23% YoY); Q3 FY25 consumption Rs 4,000+ crores (+21% YoY)
items.quote: Consumption reached Rs. 10,500 crores during the first nine months of this fiscal year, up 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Trading occupancy 91% in Dec 2024 (up from 87% in Mar); new malls ramping fast: Palladium Ahmedabad 97%, Phoenix Mall of Millennium Pune 91%, Phoenix Mall of Asia 81%
items.quote: Trading occupancy continues to build strong momentum reaching 91% in December 2024, up 87% from March. Our newly launched malls are ramping up at an impressive pace, contributing significantly to this growth.

items.statement: Targeting at least 12% EBITDA margin overall for next financial year FY26
items.quote: Going forward, for the next financial year, we are targeting at least an EBITDA level overall with both garment chipping in very well since the restructuring has been done, Fabric growing, we expect the EBITDA level overall, regardless of what happens to the Yarn market to be at least 12%.

items.statement: Expecting 20% year-on-year growth in garment business for next 2-3 years without adding capacity
items.quote: So we are now looking at, in fact, in our garment business, a 20% growth year-on-year going forward for the next 2, 3 years without adding any more capacity.

items.statement: Expecting 20% year-on-year growth in Fabric division going forward
items.quote: We are expecting growth within the Fabric division of 20% going forward year-on-year and about similar growth in the Garment business.

items.statement: Capex plan for next year is INR50 crores in plant and machinery, with INR45 crores for Fabric, INR3 crores for Yarn, INR2 crores for Garment
items.quote: Our capex plan for the next year is about INR50 crores. Kavita Gandhi: In plant and machinery. Ravindra Toshniwal: In plant and machinery alone, out of which we are expecting to invest about INR45 crores into Fabric business, INR3 crores or so in the Yarn balancing and modernization and about INR2 crores in Garment

items.statement: Overall capex including infrastructure, power, civil and environmental enhancements expected at INR80-100 crores for next year in phased manner
items.quote: So overall, if we look at in the next year, we are looking at a capex of around INR80 crores to INR100 crores, all put together, but it will get into the phase manner.

items.statement: Order book looks good with inquiries and orders flowing in for Garment division, confident of completing existing orders on time
items.quote: We have inquiries and orders flowing in for our Garment division. The order book looks good, and we are confident of completing existing orders on time and continuing to get new orders.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 10.7% year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in quarter 3 FY '25 stood at 10.7%. This is an improvement over year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin expected to be more or less same as Q3 at around 11.7%
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA level of, I think, 11.7% almost in quarter 3. And quarter 4, we expect to do more or less the same or we'll see what it comes to, but we are expecting it to be more or less the same.

items.statement: Domestic demand subdued during Diwali and wedding season but company grew by substituting Chinese imports
items.quote: If we speak about the domestic market, the demand has been subdued in general, even across the last Diwali and the whole wedding season, the last wedding season, it wasn't great at all. And still we did manage growth within that in our fabric business.

items.statement: Export demand strong with good tailwinds from Bangladesh challenges and China Plus One, but margin pressure limits order conversion

items.statement: IT development costs (MySIS, SIS Core, SalesMAX) are expensed as revenue expenditure, not capitalized.

items.quote: This is just to clarify, the international businesses are an integral part of SIS's future plans. And as you see, the results have also been good. There is no plan to sell any part of the international business.

items.statement: No clear view on future receivables or goodwill write-offs; audit committee reviews quarterly.

items.statement: Targets OCF/EBITDA conversion of 60-65% long-term; Q3's >100% was exceptional due to IT refunds.
items.quote: What we can deliver as a fast-growing Company is 60% to 65%. If you see historically, over the last 7 years, we have always delivered on an average more than 50%.

items.statement: VProtect installations ~1,000 this quarter; run rate varies (up to 3,000/qtr earlier).

items.statement: Invested in Metropolitan Stock Exchange at Rs. 2 per share for ~5% equity stake

items.statement: Kakinada phosphoric acid and sulfuric acid project to be commissioned by Q4 next year.

items.statement: Multi product plant at Ankleshwar to be commissioned in 18 months.

items.statement: Expect 40% jump in fertilizer margin in 2 years after Kakinada plants, including SSP portfolio.
items.quote: And as and when this plant gets commissioned, the improved conversion cost efficiency and the value addition what we have and our ability to secure rock from our captive mines, we should be able to achieve this sort of improvement in the EBITDA margin probably in 2 years down the line. And that also includes the portfolio of SSP.

items.statement: Aim for 60% of SSP volume from urea SSP and Gro Plus, blended margin Rs. 2,500 per ton.
items.quote: From the value-added products, both urea SSP and Gro Plus when we reach scale, I expect 60% to come from these 2 products. And balance 20%, 25% will come from normal granulated SSP with zinc and balance can be powder SSP.

items.statement: Blended SSP margin expected to go to Rs. 2,500 per ton with increased value-added products.
items.quote: So blended margin with this sort of a combination of 60:40 should go to Rs. 2,500 per ton. Currently, base SSP is powder SSP and granulated SSP in the range of Rs. 1,500 to Rs. 1,800.

items.statement: Aim to reach 1 million ton SSP capacity in 2 years, with 8 lakh tons next year.
items.quote: This year, we had some challenges in availability of sulfuric acid, and we couldn't scale up the volume. But going forward, our aim would be to reach 1 million ton capacity in 2 years' time, probably taking it to 8 lakh tons next year and thereafter 1 million ton, and that too with focus on these specialty grades, which are as good as any other NPK products.

items.statement: Q4 volumes to align with market demand, not double-digit growth.
items.quote: So it won't be a double-digit growth. It will be as per our plan. And as you know, fourth quarter, we generally take annual turnaround.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth from debottlenecking, Ennore, and imports; scale up in next 2 years.
items.quote: See, it will be a combination of both. Very difficult to put a number, but we have been carrying out some debottlenecking of our facilities at Kakinada as well as Vizag. And that will be really adding to the volume increase next year.

items.statement: Phos acid price for Q3 fixed at $1,055, $5 reduction over previous quarter.

items.quote: It used to be in the $80, $85 range, that has moved up to $100. And we do have a combination of annual contracts and the spot contracts. So if you can say the average around $90 to $100 has been the sulfuric acid price if they import.

items.statement: 9-month benefit of Rs. 180 crores from sulfuric acid value addition.
items.quote: I may not have an exact number for the quarter, but I can say roughly Rs. 180 crores is the 9 months benefit we have realized on account of sulfuric acid value addition.

items.statement: Dhaksha drone order book about Rs. 250 crores, awaiting PDI for shipment.
items.quote: Here, as you know, we had received the orders from the emergency procurement t eam on defence and the order book is about Rs. 250-odd crores. Dhaksha is awaiting the PDI so that the shipment of these drones can be made.

items.statement: Unique grade share of total fertilizer volume this quarter was 34%.

items.statement: FY26 top line growth around 15% excluding Bayer molecules, plus Bayer revenue.
items.quote: I think other than Bayer molecules, it should be around 15%.

items.quote: That's right. That's right. We stick to that.

items.quote: You see, gross margin in the range of 38% to 39%, I feel is sustainable, right? And beyond that, in this year, exceptionally is in the range of around 40%.

items.statement: Maintaining gross margin in FY26 will be difficult as FY25 was best in 5 years.
items.quote: You see, in the gross margin, continuous improvement is really very difficult. This year, the gross margin is almost best in the last 5 years. So, maintaining the gross margin would be really difficult task in the year FY '26.

items.statement: Bayer product revenues to grow 15% year-on-year for first 5 years from FY27.
items.quote: For FY '27 onwards, yes, we are looking at 15% growth in the pr oduct revenues year-on-year for first 5 years.

items.statement: Bayer products combined potential up to INR 250 crores in value.
items.quote: In terms of value, both the products combined can go up to INR 250 crores.

items.statement: FY27 top line contribution from Bayer products INR 175-200 crores.
items.quote: Top line contribution from these 2 products in FY '27 when the full revenue will come from the books of Dhanuka will be in the range of INR 175 crores to INR 200 crores.

items.statement: No new fresh capex in Dahej plant due to low viability.
items.quote: Right now, the commercial viability is slightly on the lower side , and the fresh CAPEX is not justified for low viability products. So, we have not gone ahead for any new fresh CAPEX in Dahej plant.

items.statement: Dahej FY26 revenue expected INR 60-70 crores with only bifenthrin.
items.quote: Yes. For FY '26, we are looking at revenue in the range of INR 60 crores to INR 70 crores. And assuming only bifenthrin over there and the efforts around that is, of course, domestic sales is there, and we are looking at international reg istrations.

items.statement: Next fiscal year launching 1 rice herbicide and 1 new fungicide for grapes/horticulture, plus 9(4) products.
items.quote: In the next financial year, we will be launching 1 rice herbicide and a new fungicide for grapes and horticultural crops. These are the 2 new 9(3) introductions, plus a few 9(4) products Me-Too introductions, as identified by our portfolio gap.

items.statement: Raw material prices overall stable, no major changes foreseen near future.
items.quote: But overall, in general, the prices are stable , and in near future, we don't foresee any major change in the prices.

items.statement: No major corrections expected in raw material prices for kharif in next few months.
items.quote: So, as of now, like you said earlier, most prices appear to be balanced. Many product prices have already shown upward trend for kharif. So , we are looking at no further corrections, not major corrections for sure in the next few months.

items.statement: Rabi offtake in December and January not great due to low pest and disease pressure.
items.quote: Overall, January, and if I may say, December, both the months have not been very great in terms of rabi offtake, and the pest pressure, disease pressure has been pretty low in North India as well as in West India, includ ing chilli of South India.

items.statement: Tariff impact uncertain; China front-loaded markets, may lower prices further.
items.quote: Now impact of tariffs from U.S. will have another side of it, which is if China will not be able to export to U.S., then Chinese prices will come down further for other countries. Now will that happen or not, we are yet to see and a few more months before we can really understand and break through or see through the impact.

items.statement: Acquisition cost ~INR 160 crores capitalized in Q4; INR 50 crores loan taken.
items.quote: You see the overall cost would be around INR 160 crores, which will be capitalized in Q4.

items.statement: Shifting one Bayer molecule manufacturing to India takes 2-3 years for regulatory approvals.
items.quote: Right. So, one of the molecules we are planning to shift for sure, that will take about 1.5, 2 years to get the regulatory approvals, because it doesn't have an India manufacturing approval to date. So, it will take roughly 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Expects sharp growth in collections and operating cash flow in Q4.
items.quote: Slightly lower deliveries in the third quarter were part of the reason that cash flows for the quarter saw quarter -on-quarter decline, but we have a lot of deliveries and other construction milestones planned in the fourth quarter and expect to see a sharp growth in both collections and operating cash flow in the current quarter.

items.statement: Expects record year for cash flows and earnings.
items.quote: We also expect to deliver a record year from the point of view of cash flows and earnings.

items.statement: Net debt cap of INR10,000 crores; current gearing 0.23.
items.quote: So we would like to have an upper cap of about INR10,000 crores of net debt and currently our gearing is about 0.23.

items.statement: Added 12 new projects YTD with booking value potential INR23,450 crores.
items.quote: From a business development perspective, I'm happy to announce that Godrej Properties has added 12 new projects in the year-to-date, with a total estimated saleable area of approximately 16.9 million square feet and total estimated booking value potential of INR23,450 crores as against our annual guidance of INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: Embedded margins tracking similar to slightly above last year.
items.quote: But as of now, it's tracking similar to slightly above last year's numbers.

items.statement: Strong sales at attractive price points above underwriting; margins should expand.
items.quote: We've also been looking at pricing. So these are not -- these are strong sales at attractive price points above what we underwrote. So in that sense, margin should expand as a result of these.

items.statement: Markets remain strong; no fundamental demand weakening seen.
items.quote: But as of now, nothing we're seeing confirms us that fundamentally demand is weakening and there's anything to be overly concerned about.

items.statement: Sees strong demand in premium and luxury segments.
items.quote: Today, if you see, because of the economic growth and what we're seeing in terms of our own sales ratio, we have seen very strong demand in the premium segment, and to some extent, even in the luxury segment.

items.statement: May reconfigure product sizes in 2-3 years based on market.
items.quote: But yes, 2 to 3 years from today, there will be, of course, an opportunity to reconfigure your product. So in certain cities, you may want to reduce the sizes, and in certain cities, you may want to or certain micro markets, you may want to maintain your sizes.

items.statement: Approval delays for Worli project; may launch this year or next.
items.quote: We're still hoping to get it done this year. But I think the reason we haven't mentioned that as one of the launches is there is some uncertainty on final approval time.

items.statement: NGT ban in NCR moved billing milestones from Q3 to Q4.
items.quote: And, Praveen, because of NGT ban that you would be aware in NCR, some of the billing milestones had moved from quarter 3 to quarter 4.

items.statement: Raised INR6,000 crores equity via QIP; net debt-to-equity improved to 0.23.
items.quote: Towards the end of the year, we raised INR6,000 crores of equity for growth capital through the largest ever QIP by a real estate company in India. As a result, our net debt -to-equity ratio has improved to 0.23 from 0.72 at the start of the calendar year.

items.statement: New launches contributed 70% to presales in 9M FY25.
items.quote: Parikshit, to your question, new launches to presale is like 70% for 9 months and 68% for the quarter.

items.statement: Sustenance sales crossed last full-year figures with 40% YoY growth.
items.quote: And just to add on to that, we've already crossed last full -year sustenance figures already. In fact, the year-on-year growth is about 40%.

items.statement: Maintains FY25 execution guidance of 800 MW, on track.
items.quote: So we continue to maintain our guidance for FY '25 of 800 megawatts. And we believe that we are on track to achieve that.

items.statement: Maintains FY26 execution guidance of 1,200+ MW.
items.quote: No, we are maintaining still the guidance of 1,200 plus, that kind of thing. With the order book that we have and the kind of planning we have, including on the ground and especially on our development, et cetera, we are very confident to deliver that.

items.statement: Initiatives to add 100-200 bps to FY26 EBITDA margin over guidance.
items.quote: Just adding to it, so these initiatives which we have taken, so that will add 100 to 200 basis points in the next financial year, in FY '26.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 and FY27 is INR50-75 crores.
items.quote: So broadly, the capex guidance, which we've given for FY '26 and FY '27 is between INR50 crores to INR75 crores.

items.statement: Order book of 3.3 GW covers next 2 years.
items.quote: As on date, we have 3.3 gigawatts around order book, which mostly covers broadly if I see that for the next 2 years or so.

items.statement: Order book split: ~1 GW equipment supply, balance EPC.
items.quote: So pure equipment sale is roughly around 1 gigawatt and balance is EPC.

items.statement: 4 MW turbine commercial production expected H2 FY26 or Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So basically, as I see that we are on track and we are working on 4 megawatts. And what we see possibly the commercial production will start more in the second half of, or possibly go towards more quarter 4 '26.

items.statement: C&I demand expected 3-4 GW per year.
items.quote: Over and above that, what we expect is that C&I should be anywhere between 3 to 5 gigawatts -- 3 to 4 gigawatts every year going ahead because we see a very strong demand from many of our customers who are C&I players because a lot of them, who export to t he markets such as Europe and all, have to have all of their supply chain green

items.statement: On-ground execution challenges are usual, not abnormal.
items.quote: I think as I said, it is as usual. It is not that they have come down. When you do -- these are infrastructure projects and you are doing in northern part of this country. So issues keep coming, whether it is land or whether it is connectivity, whether bui lding up lines, but these are regular

items.statement: Nacelle unit, cranes, transformer lines to be commissioned in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that we will commission our nacelle manufacturing unit, operationalize our initial few cranes and commence our transformer manufacturing lines, all within quarter 4 FY '25.

items.statement: Demerger of substation business expected in 6-9 months.
items.quote: And we still expect we will get the demerger happen within the next 6 to 9 months' time.

items.statement: Merger of Inox Wind and Inox Wind Energy in final stages, hearing early February.
items.quote: So the Inox Wind and Inox Wind Energy Limited merger are in the final stages. The next date of hearing is in the early February, and that can -- we expect to get it completed in this hearing.

items.statement: Rediff expected to contribute 2-4% of revenue, growing to 10% in coming years.
items.quote: Further, we anticipate Rediff contributing to 2% to 4% of our revenue with the potential to grow to 10% in coming years.

items.statement: AI business expected to contribute 5-10% of net revenue within 2-3 years.
items.quote: Our dedicated AI business under a new subsidiary will advance multiple AI-driven innovation that will contribute to 5% to 10% of our net revenue within the coming 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Capex for data centers is INR20-50 crores per megawatt.
items.value: INR20 crores to INR50 crores per megawatt
items.quote: Our investment strategy with a capex of INR20 crores to INR50 crores per megawatt, ensures cost efficiency, operational flexibility and scalable growth, enabling us to adapt to the evolving market demands.

items.statement: First operational 2-megawatt data center, scaling to 10 megawatts in medium term.
items.quote: Under our Infibeam Quantum Edge brand, we are establishing a network of localized small-scale data centers, starting with our first operational 2-megawatt data center facility. And in the medium term, we'll plan to scale it to 10 me gawatts with a long-term vision of reaching higher numbers.

items.statement: International revenue expected to be 20-25% of overall revenue in next 2 years.
items.quote: I think we've already communicated. We think that international in the next 2 years should account for 20% to 25% of the overall revenue. We are focused on international growth, and we see a lot of potential there.

items.statement: TPAP license applied, RediffPay rollout expected this quarter.
items.quote: But we expect that we'll be able to roll out this quarter.

items.statement: Net payment take rate increased to 11.1 basis points.
items.quote: Our net payment take rate increased to 11.1 basis poin ts, enhancing our profitability this quarter.

items.statement: Onboarded approximately 1.8 lakh new merchants in Q3, 2,000 per day.
items.quote: On the operational front, during Q3, we onboarded approximately 1.8 lakh new merchants, expanding our network across industries and geogr aphies. That is 2,000 merchants a day, fully KYC.

items.statement: Competition creates downward pressure on margins.
items.quote: See basically, the way we see this is there are a lot of downward pressure because of competition, as you just mentio ned, because it's a very competitive industry. And so there will be pressures on margins, downward pressures in margins.

items.statement: Data center ROI expected less than 24 months.
items.quote: So I think the forward investment we make is not a huge one and the ROI on such opportunities is less than 24 months.

items.statement: No additional capex for this year; next year's capex budgeted and evolving.
items.quote: We already have budgeted for next year. There is no additional capex for this year. But for next year, we will have budgeted a capex for this and currently, it's evolving.

items.statement: No update on UPI dues from government since April 2024; no UPI dues claimed for 2 years.
items.quote: So basically, last -- from April of 2024, there's no update from the government on the UPI dues that are there. We are in any way not claimed any UPI dues for the last 2 calendar years.

items.statement: On track to open 8 to 10 additional stores by end of FY25, surpassing guidance.
items.quote: In this financial FY '25 we have already opened 22 stores and surpassing our guidance, we are on track to open 8 to 10 additional stores by the end of financial year '25.

items.statement: Confident to surpass target of 200 stores by FY26.
items.quote: We are confident to surpass the target of 200 stores by FY '26.

items.statement: Hoping to add another 8 stores this financial year.
items.quote: And this financial year, we are hoping to add another 8 stores.

items.statement: 175 stores definite possibility by end of FY25, trying to open more.
items.quote: 175 will be a definite possibility. And we are trying, in fact, so many stores are going under work in progress. So, 175, we are definitely going to achieve, and we are trying to, in fact, open more stores even more than 175 stores.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin around 8% to 10%.
items.quote: Sustainable margin will be around 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Expect to maintain gross margin in coming quarters.
items.quote: But we expect that we are going to again maintain this gross margin in coming quarters.

items.statement: Expecting growth in February to March.
items.quote: But we are expecting growth in coming February to March.

items.statement: Very bullish on upcoming season, building inventory for summer.
items.quote: We are very bullish on this aspect Devanshu. In fact, we have already started building up our inventory because, as you know, approaching the summer, of course, it becomes very difficult for you to build on the inventories for air condition, refrigerators and other cooling products.

items.statement: Expecting very good Q1 for company due to summer and Kumbh mela.
items.quote: So, the entire money, we are expecting that with this summer, it will be a very, very good Q1 for our company.

items.statement: January demand flattish, expecting growth in February to March.
items.quote: Generally, it has been flat flattish. So, it has been flattish. Of course, we are in growth, but I'll say, I'll put it as flattish only. But we are expecting growth in coming February to March.

items.statement: IT and mobility share increased due to sluggish demand.
items.quote: Yes. That has been because whenever there is a sluggish demand then the IT and mobility, they have their share of counters will get bigger.

items.statement: Sluggish demand due to high inflation and interest, expected to ease.
items.quote: In my opinion, in fact, there has been a sluggish demand. This is only because of the macroeconomic in nature. In the sense with high inflation and high interest, this is the main factor. And I think in coming months, I think it is going to ease off.

items.statement: Utilized INR282 crores from fund raise for inventory and capex.
items.quote: We have already utilized INR282 crores and we have already filed all the details, you can find it from there.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for 9 months FY25 at 15%.
items.quote: The same-store sales growth for 9 months FY '25 stands at impressive 15%.

items.statement: SSG in Q3 was 13%.
items.quote: SSG in this quarter was 13%.

items.statement: Targets 0.8 million tonnes steel volume for FY25 and 1 million tonnes for FY26.
items.quote: We are fully geared to meet our annual target of 0.8 million tonnes for FY '25 and are setting our sights for 1 million tonnes in FY '26.

items.statement: Aims to sustain 20%+ top-line growth and 3%+ EBITDA margin in FY26.
items.quote: See, top-line, we would like to sustain the 20% plus. The EBITDA, we would definitely be 3% plus.

items.statement: Plans to increase non-steel share from 10% to 20-25% in next five years.
items.quote: Today, the non-steel is about 10%, but our target in the next five years is to take it up to 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Expects to return to 3%+ EBITDA margin this quarter if steel prices remain steady.
items.quote: And if this quarter is a fairly steady period, we are fairly confident we will be back in the 3% plus kind of EBITDA this quarter itself.

items.statement: Aims to improve retail EBITDA margin by at least 1% in a couple of years.
items.quote: In a couple of years, definitely we would like that to go by at least 1% at this point.

items.statement: Anticipates completing demerger process by H1 FY26.
items.quote: Subject to the results of this meeting and subsequent regulatory processes, we anticipate completing the entire demerger process by H1 FY '26.

items.statement: Steel prices declined ~10% year-to-date, causing inventory losses of Rs. 22 crores in 9M FY25.
items.quote: We experienced a blended 6% decrease in realizations in Q2, followed by a further 3% reduction in Q3, resulting in an approximate total decline of approximately 10% in steel prices year-to-date.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin was 2.84%, down from 3.42% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: Despite our best efforts to operate efficiently in the face of such headwinds, our EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 2.84%, lower compared to 3.42% in Q3 FY '24 and relatively flat compared to Q2 of FY '25.

items.statement: Non-steel segment achieved record sales of Rs. 154 crores in Q3, up 19% YoY.
items.quote: This quarter, we achieved record sales of Rs. 154 crores in this segment, reflecting a 19% year-on-year growth in Q3, and even higher 29% growth in nine months FY '25.

items.statement: Steel prices are flattening out; some price increases from JSW etc. are talked about for this month.
items.quote: As of now, there is some talk of some increases from the JSW, etc., for this month. And it all depends on the global steel cycle, etc.

items.statement: Steel EBITDA margin was around 2.5% and non-steel around 5.5%.
items.quote: Yes, 2.5%, steel was around 2.5% and non-steel was around 5.5%.

items.statement: Steel price fluctuations are a risk; diversification into non-steel will mitigate it.
items.quote: I think what really will help us as we diversify more and more into the non-steel, I mean, this steel price fluctuation will get mitigated to a certain extent.

items.statement: Group level debt as of Q3 end is around Rs. 500 crores.
items.quote: Our group level debt as on quarter end Q3, it is around Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 36 to 33, target to bring down to 30.
items.quote: See, if you look at the number of days of working capital despite the last year, we started at about 36 days, which has come down to around 33. Our target is to bring it down to 30, number one.

items.statement: Cost of debt is approximately 9%-9.5%.
items.quote: Approximately around 9%-9.5% is our present cost of debt.

items.statement: Expects some debt reduction this quarter and tangible results from Q1 next year.
items.quote: We could see some reduction hopefully in this quarter itself and definitely tangible results from Q1 next year.

items.statement: Board approved asset-light built-to-suit 500-bed hospital in Thane, to be commissioned in 2028.
items.quote: Our Board has accorded its approval to enter into an asset -light ‘built-to-suit’ agreement for a 500 -bed hospital at a prime location in Thane , to be set up by the partner as per our specifications on a built -up area of appr oximately 6 lakh square feet. The hospital is expected to be commissioned in 2028.

items.statement: Board approved increasing capacity of Mohali (Zirakpur) hospital to 400 beds from 250 beds.
items.quote: The Board has also provided its approval for enhancing the capacity of our upcoming asset-light ‘built-to-suit’ hospital in Mohali (Zirakpur) to 400 beds from 250 beds planned previously.

items.statement: 128 beds at Max Lucknow: 64 beds commissioned in January 2025, balance 64 beds to be added in February 2025.
items.quote: 128 beds at Max Lucknow – 64 beds have been commissioned in January 2025, and the balance 64 beds will be added in February 2025.

items.statement: 127 beds at Max Nagpur: 12 beds added in October 2024; environmental clearance expected by March 2025; project completion in 24 months thereafter.
items.quote: 127 beds at Max Nagpur – 12 beds have been added in October 2024. For the balance beds on additional floors, we are expecting the environmental clearance (EC) to come by March 2025. Project completion should take another 24 months thereafter.

items.statement: 268 beds at Nanavati Phase 1: interior fit-out in progress; completion expected within next 3 to 4 months.
items.quote: 268 beds at Nanavati in Phase 1 – Interior fit -out work s are in progress currently. The project continues to be on schedule and we expect completion within the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: 400 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex): majority structural work complete; completion expected within Q1 FY'26.
items.quote: 400 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex) – Majority of the structural work is complete. The project is on track and we expect its completion within Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: 155 beds at Mohali: interior work in progress; completion expected by Q1 FY'26.
items.quote: 155 beds at Moha li – Interior work is in progress and we expect its completion again by Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: 500 beds at Sector-56 Gurgaon: structural work in progress; first phase of 300 beds expected by end of Q3 FY'26.
items.quote: 500 beds at Sector-56 Gurgaon – Structural work is in progress. We expect completion of the first phase of 300 beds by the end of Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: 367 beds at Patparganj: post environmental clearance, tendering in progress; project largely on schedule.
items.quote: Thereafter, 367 beds at Patparganj – Post receipt of environmental clearance (EC), tendering work is in progress currently. This project is largely on schedule.

items.statement: 550 beds at Max Vikrant (Saket Complex): forest approval delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings; all other statutory approvals in place.
items.quote: 550 beds at Max Vikrant (Saket Complex) – Forest approval is delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings in relation to tree felling involving DD A and the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi for the past 6 months. They have not permitted anybody to remove any trees in Delhi, but we think that this should get fairly resolved soon. All other statutory approvals are in place.

items.statement: 400 beds at Zirakpur, Mohali: fire department NOC received; project expected to be completed within 30 months.
items.quote: 400 beds at Zirakpur, M ohali – No objection certificate (NOC) from fire department has been received. Project is expected to be completed within 30 months.

items.statement: Upper limit for net debt-to-EBITDA is 2.5x; currently at 0.65x after Jaypee acquisition.
items.quote: So, our upper limit is 2.5 x net debt-to-EBITDA, but we are far from that. The new ones that we have announced such as Mohali (Zirakpur) as well as Thane, they are both asset-light models.

items.statement: Looking at Rs. 500-600 crore CAPEX over next 3-4 months towards brownfields.
items.quote: Now other than that, we are looking at Rs. 500-600 crore over the next 3-4 months of CAPEX towards the brownfields and then thereafter.

items.statement: Expecting price increase on institutional side, long overdue, should come within a month or two.
items.quote: We are not expecting a price increase on the insurance side , we were looking at a price increase on the institutional side. We are still expecting that as it is long overdue. Our belief is that it should come within a month or two.

items.statement: Expecting revisions in CGHS rates that will impact other PSU business; hope it comes this quarter.
items.quote: That's right. We are expecting some revisions to come up in CGHS rates that will also impact the other PSU business. The gap earlier used to be 44% betw een our cash rates and our institutional , and now it has come down to 36%.

items.statement: For asset-light model, EBITDA margin should be lesser by 5-6% on pre Ind AS basis.
items.quote: It should depend on what the maturity of the hospital is, but I think it should be lesser by 5-6%.

items.statement: Expects total net store additions of 300 in current financial year.
items.quote: We expect a total of 300 net store additions in the current financial year.

items.statement: Plans at least 600 store additions next year.
items.quote: No, I think it will be at least 600 stores for -- I don't think it will be less than 600 stores.

items.statement: Private label to increase by ~1% per quarter on MRP basis.
items.quote: So think about the private label as going up by roughly around 1% every quarter on the volume basis, which is on MRP basis, which means additional margin of roughly around 15 to 20 basis points maximum per quarter.

items.statement: Every 1% increase in private label MRP adds ~20 bps to gross margin.
items.quote: And that would mean possibly -- and if nothing else changed, I would say 1% growth in gross margin because every 1% in MRP, I think, increases our margin by around 20 basis points.

items.statement: Current margin level is sustainable; no significant dip expected from store additions.
items.quote: No, I think we are at a fairly sustainable kind of margin level for the company out there. Now the only reason which can change it is if we add a ton of stores -- new stores.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth expected at 4-5% steady state.
items.quote: 4% to 5% is what we are looking at, actually. That is a number at least we can be at a steady state as far as the profitability is concerned.

items.statement: Private label discount average ~50-51%, no plan to reduce significantly.
items.quote: About our private label discount itself, we advertise a 50% to 80% discount based on the molecule. And I think the average discount tough comes out to around 50%, 51%, that's all, because most of the higher selling drugs are all around the 50% discount.

items.statement: Adding 10 smaller warehouses of 30,000-50,000 sq ft.
items.quote: I think a total of 10 smaller warehouses, anywhere between 30,000 to 50,000 square foot kind of leases. That includes the ones I've already talked about.

items.statement: Muted growth partly due to seasonality and holidays; expects recovery.
items.quote: But yes, outside of that and a little bit of seasonal, I would say, effect having plenty of holiday season and all, especially in January and all, we did see a slightly, I would say, lesser sale than expected, but I expect that to get back.

items.statement: Cannibalization from new stores accepted; focus on store-level EBITDA.
items.quote: Some amount of cannibalization is always going to be there when we do this when we set up so many stores. But I'm fairly comfortable in saying that we should growth on the 2-plus year stores also at; inflation and slightly above that.

items.statement: Private label pharma share at 17.6% of GMV; non-pharma ~8%.
items.quote: Yes. So the private level itself on a GMV basis is around 17.6% right now on the Pharma side. If you look at the net sales side, I think it's around 1.6%.

items.statement: Private label share varies by region: metros ~7-8%, smaller towns ~20%.
items.quote: To give you an idea, I think Maharashtra, which is as urban as you can get, it's probably at around 7% or 8%. I think Bombay and all are at 7% or 8% for us on the Pharma side private label or maybe slightly less.

items.statement: Private label share in chronic and acute segments similar to regular brands.
items.quote: But to give you an idea, the number of -- I would say, the private label share of chronic versus acute is exactly the same as it is for the regular brands. So I think 60% to 70% of our sales are private label comes from the chronic segment.

items.statement: No drag from quick commerce if customers pay delivery fee; monitoring situation.
items.quote: As long as the customer is willing to pay the delivery fee, I don't think there will be a drag at all. If the delivery were to be 100% free, today we charge around INR 20.

items.statement: Will open close to 70-80 branches in full year.
items.quote: the guidance remains the same, we will be opening close to 70, 80 branches in a full year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for the year is 0.75% to 1%.
items.quote: the credit cost as we guided was 0.75% to 1%, our credit cost for this quarter is 0.69%.

items.statement: Will maintain cost-to-income around 35% to 36% including credit cost.
items.quote: we are maintaining our numbers and we will continue to operate at around the 35% to 36% kind of cost -to-income. And when we mean cost -to-income, we include the credit cost as well.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 75 to 100 basis points for the business model.
items.quote: our guidance to you on the credi t cost is typically that the business model of Five Star can take a credit cost or will have to operate at a credit cost of around 75 to 100 basis points and I think we continue to maintain that same view

items.statement: No change in growth guidance for Q4 or next financial year.
items.quote: I think our guidance stands. So, we are not changing our guidance at this point of time, be it for Q4 or be it for the next financial year.

items.statement: Will revisit business outlook at end of March quarter.
items.quote: we will revisit our business outlook at the end of March quarter. So, I'll come out with the outlook in the April earnings call more clearly.

items.statement: Expect Q4 to be better than Q3.
items.quote: we are very confident that Q4 will be better than Q3.

items.statement: Expect to be back to business as usual in Q4.
items.quote: given that Q4 typically tends to be the best quarter for any financial institution, so we expect to be back to business as usual in Q4.

items.statement: No significant increase in credit cost in Q4.
items.quote: I don't think you will see any kind of significant increase in the credit cost in Q4.

items.statement: 30+ DPD to be at similar levels in Q4.
items.quote: I think it could be in similar levels is what we feel at this point of time.

items.statement: Will maintain appropriate level of provisions in coming quarters.
items.quote: we will continue to keep maintaini ng the appropriate level of provisions in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Eventual credit losses should not exceed 25 to 50 basis points.
items.quote: eventual credit losses… and th is is something that we have been guiding for the last many years since our DRHP was there, it should not be more than 25 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: No guidance for growth acceleration; existing guidance stands for next year.
items.quote: at this point of time, we are not guiding you for any acceleration. We will have to wait and see what are the focus areas both for the government as well as how does it gets translated into actions from an RBI perspective.

items.statement: Will come back on growth guidance in April earnings call.
items.quote: we will come back after the March quarter depending upon the environment around us and the regulatory thought process we will take appropriate steps is what we said in the last quarter, that remains the same. So, we will come back on the April earning call.

items.statement: No change in credit cost guidance of 75 to 100 basis points.
items.quote: even then we are not changing the guidance at this point of time. How you will see it, moving in a trajectory is something that we will also have to see when it will probably touch a 75 or 100.

items.statement: Will take technical write-offs as appropriate in consultation with board and auditors.
items.quote: We will continue to keep taking this depending on what we believe is the appropriate number for the Company both in consultation with the board and as well as the auditors.

items.statement: Targets 10 GW O&M portfolio in 3-4 years, with 7 GW organic and 3 GW inorganic.
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our target of 10 gigawatts in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Aims to double portfolio to 6 GW in a couple of years.
items.quote: in a couple of years, our target is to double it to 6 gigawatt.

items.statement: Maintains full-year EBITDA margin guidance of 50%.
items.quote: But on a full year basis, 50% guidance remains.

items.statement: Expects to commission 300-400 MW in Q4 FY25, reaching ~4 GW portfolio.
items.quote: we will commission near to about 300-400 megawatt in quarter 4. So broadly by FY '25, and we will be 4 gigawatt portfolio plus minus 100 megawatt, 200 megawatt here and there

items.statement: Plans to commission 1,200 MW in FY26 and 2,000 MW in FY27, reaching 7.2 GW organically.
items.quote: then we will get commissioned 1200 megawatts in subsequent year and then 2 gigawatts. So organically, our portfolio will increase to somewhere around 7.2 gigawatts.

items.statement: Hopes to acquire 2-3 GW inorganically in next 12-18 months.
items.quote: we are very hopeful that around 2 to 3 gigawatts when we acquire in next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Utilized ~INR300 crores of fundraise, plans to use another INR200-250 crores in 2-3 months.
items.quote: We intend to utilize another INR200, INR250 over the period of next 2 to 3 months.

items.statement: Demerger expected to complete within this calendar year, making balance sheet asset-light.
items.quote: We are hopeful that within this calendar year we will have the demerger of the business.

items.statement: Inox Green shareholders will receive 10% of Resco, with total 20% owned by Inox Green shareholders.
items.quote: the minority shareholder of Inox Green will get 10% in the consolidated entity. So currently, 50% is owned by the minority shareholders in Inox Green, so if we take our math accordingly, then the 20% shares of the Resco will be owned by the Inox Green shareholders

items.statement: Company has accumulated tax losses of INR700 crores.
items.quote: INR700 odd crores is the tax losses, which the company carries.

items.statement: Solar O&M to start contributing from next FY, with margins lower than wind but higher than industry due to synergies.
items.quote: Basically, the execution on solar is expected in the next FY. So as soon as the time line of 8 to 9 months, the project commissioning, so it will be taken over by Inox Green.

items.statement: NCLT acquisitions are lengthy but yield clean companies without hidden liabilities.
items.quote: the NCLT process, the bankruptcy route, is something that takes time. It is a little lengthy process. But then also the advantages that we get the company clean without any hidden liabilities

items.statement: Total fundraise was INR1,050 crores, with INR550 crores received and balance callable.
items.quote: the total was INR1,050 crores, as you would remember. And that’s obviously, we have received. Manish, correct me if I'm wrong. INR550-odd crores already in the company.

items.statement: Committed investment over INR1,000 crores; INR350 crores already deployed.
items.quote: We are committed to investment of over INR1,000 crores, of which INR350 crores have already been deployed.

items.statement: 25,000 new spindles to commence operations by June 2025.
items.quote: The addition of 25,000 new spindles is progressing as per schedule with operations expected to commence by June 2025.

items.statement: New project for 40 knitting machines at capex of INR38 crores.
items.quote: We have undertaken a new project to set up 40 knitting machines in our existing location at a capex of INR38 crores.

items.statement: By 2029-30, 30-35% of revenues from value-added segment.
items.quote: So the idea is by 2029, '30, we have almost 30% to 35% of our revenues coming from the value-added segment.

items.statement: After INR1,000 crores capex, 70% revenue from spinning, 30% from fabric and value-added.
items.quote: See, as I said earlier, overall, still, I would say, 70% of the revenue will come from spinning and around 30% of the revenue will come from the fabric and the value-added segment.

items.statement: Incremental capital in knitted fabric to give 13% to 14% ROCEs.
items.quote: So basis our estimates, probably the incremental capital will give us almost 13% to 14% ROCEs on going into the knitted fabric.

items.statement: New knitting investment ROCE around 13.5%, margins 3% to 4% extra.
items.quote: Our ROCE on the new investment, which we have just got approval will be around 13.5%. And our margins should be in the range of around 3% to 4% extra margin will get generated out of this number of these new investments.

items.statement: Incremental value addition INR14 crores, EBIT INR7 crores on INR38 crores investment.
items.quote: So it will be approximately in terms of the value, almost INR14 crores will be the incremental value addition that we'll get. On an EBIT level, approximately INR7 crores will be the value that we get on the incremental basis on this INR38 crores investment.

items.statement: Expect to operate at same levels as current 9 months.
items.quote: As of now, we believe that we'll operate more or less at the same levels where we are -- we have closed this current 9 months.

items.statement: Seeing export inquiries, waiting for conversion into orders.
items.quote: We have started getting those inquiries, and we are waiting for it to get converted into orders.

items.statement: Cotton prices expected to remain stable, supporting domestic textile industry.
items.quote: Yarn prices have mostly remained range bound, and it is expected that the cotton prices will remain stable, which shall support the domestic textile industry.

items.statement: Demand remains sluggish, longest period of sluggishness in yarn market.
items.quote: See, the demand still remains sluggish. So -- and this is probably the longest period of sluggishness in yarn market that we are seeing, almost now 2 years.

items.statement: Capex to be financed by internal accruals and bank finance, debt equity within 0.5:1.
items.quote: So both from the internal accruals plus bank finance, we'll be able to finance this capex. But we'll remain very much within those declared boundaries of debt equity of not more than 1:1, rather we'll maintain within 0.5:1 kind of numbers.

items.statement: No plans to monetize noncore assets as internal accruals sufficient.
items.quote: As and when if we feel there is any need, we'll look at that. But as of now, there are no plans to monetize as of now.

items.statement: Aiming for mid-teens revenue growth for the next couple of years.
items.quote: Going ahead, our company is aiming for mid-teens revenue growth for the next couple of years, driven by the expansion of new store locations across both new and established markets, depending upon a rebound in the industry demand for premium and mid-premium brands.

items.statement: Expects high single-digit growth for the full year FY25.
items.quote: We already mentioned that we would grow in high single-digit growth.

items.statement: Aspiring for mid-teens growth in the next financial year.
items.quote: Depending on market conditions again, but we are aspiring for mid-teens growth in the next financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected in the range of 27% to 30%.
items.quote: EBITDA should be in the range of 27% to 30%, Ruchita.

items.statement: Plans to open 20-25 stores in FY26, with potential for 40-50 depending on market.
items.quote: Ruchita, we intend to even now this year, open about 20, 25 stores, and we will be ready to open even 40 or 50 depending on how the market pans out.

items.statement: Expects to open 18-20 net stores by end of FY25.
items.quote: By the end of the year, I think we are confident that we should be able to open between -- at a gross level -- I mean, net level, sorry, about 18 to 20 stores.

items.statement: No price hike in the last year; future hikes depend on raw material costs and inflation.
items.quote: There hasn't been any price hike in the last year. But depending on the raw material costs and inflation, et cetera, price hike is a function of that.

items.statement: Constant premiumization in product mix is ongoing.
items.quote: However, there is a constant premiumization that's happening in the brand in terms of the product mix, et cetera, which is a constant work in progress and -- something that keeps going on.

items.statement: Expects consumption to improve with recent tax reductions.
items.quote: Additionally, we expect consumption to improve with the recent boost given by tax reductions.

items.statement: Faced subdued demand for premium and mid-premium branded apparel due to reduced discretionary spending.
items.quote: Despite facing challenges such as subdued demand for premium and mid-premium branded apparel, primarily driven by reduced discretionary spending and weaker consumer sentiment, impacting overall industry consumption.

items.statement: Aims to double business in 5 years, possibly a year less or more.
items.quote: See internally double in the 5-year period. However, depending on market, it could take a year less or a year more to achieve that.

items.statement: No plans to launch value products; may consider other categories in 2-3 years.
