items.statement: Total spent on Kakinada project till Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: Total amount spent on Kakinada project, including assets capitalized till December 31, 2024 is ₹1,340 crores.

items.statement: No massive dip in margin expected despite Kakinada expenses.
items.quote: So, considering all that, also considering Kakinada would have a little operational additional expenses, we don't see a massive dip in the entire margin.

items.statement: Pricing pressures in generics expected to gradually ease.
items.quote: In our generic business, despite the ongoing price pressures affecting the industry, we have maintained stability, while we expect this pressure to gradually ease as we continue to strengthen our overall performance.

items.statement: Increase in demand for several molecules, market normalizing.
items.quote: And the customers who have stocked for a long time have slowly started buying again. So we are seeing normalization of the market, provided there's no more global surprises or wars everywhere, I hope things would again ease out and things will become back to normal.

items.statement: Aims for generics and custom synthesis to be 50-50 mix.
items.quote: See, the wishful thinking is we would want our generics and custom synthesis to be 50%, 50% and that's where our efforts are always towards, like we don't only run behind the custom synthesis. We also run behind our generic business.

items.statement: No tariffs on India currently; will take strategic decisions if they come.
items.quote: So, as of now, we haven't seen any tariffs for India. So I don't think we are having anything to worry about at this point in time. And as and when it comes, we would be taking proper strategic decisions concerning that.

items.statement: Cash on books as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, we have cash on books of ₹3,659 crores, receivables of ₹2,366 crores, and inventories of ₹2,986 crores.

items.statement: New tax regime at 25% effective from current financial year.
items.quote: So, we are looking at a 25% tax regime that was the new regime. So , it would be 25% for the year from here on.

items.statement: Constant currency growth for nine months at 22%.
items.quote: Our constant currency growth for the nine months period has been at 22%, whereas it is negative 10% for the corresponding period of nine months of previous year.

items.statement: Product mix for generics to custom synthesis in Q3: 47% and 53%.
items.quote: For the current quarter, the product mix for generics to custom synthesis is 47% and 53%, respectively.

items.statement: Nutraceutical business revenue for nine months and Q3.
items.quote: Our Nutraceutical business amounted to ₹ 576 crores for the current nine months period and ₹ 170 crores for the current quarter.

items.statement: Material consumption at 40% of sales revenue for nine months.
items.quote: Material consumption continues to remain at 40% of the sales revenue for the nine months period of the current financial year.

items.statement: Forex gain for nine months period.
items.quote: We have a Forex gain of ₹38 crores for the current nine months period as against a gain of ₹ 32 crores in the corresponding nine months period of the previous year.

items.statement: Maintains outlook for transition to growth in second half of this year and into next fiscal.
items.quote: With performance delivery in line with our expectations and with the strengthening of building blocks for future growth across our businesses, we maintain our outlook for a transition to growth in the second half of this year and into next fiscal with impr oved visibility across all businesses.

items.statement: Expects Q4 and next fiscal to build on sequential revenue growth, driven by new product launches.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect performance in the fourth quarter and into the next fiscal to build upon the sequential revenue growth in Q3, driven by new product launches across markets, including the launch of our generic GLP, Liraglutide, in the UK and the EU, as well as additional new product launches, particularly in the United States.

items.statement: Fiscal 2026 will start seeing growth in Generics.
items.quote: Yes. Fiscal 2026 itself you will start seeing this growth.

items.statement: Expects Sema approvals in some markets by end of calendar 2026.
items.quote: My expectation is that we should start receiving approvals in some of these markets by end of calendar 2026.

items.statement: Expects U.S. Liraglutide review to complete by middle of this calendar year, followed by launch.
items.quote: And then subsequently, during the second half of year, we also expect an approval in the U.S. That product was filed from the injectable facility in Biologics, which has now received the VAI status and the review of the DMF for th e API was complete and FDA is now reviewing the other data packs, and we expect that review to complete by middle of this calendar year, followed by a launch.

items.statement: Maintains EBITDA margin guidance of 22% to 23% for Biocon Biologics.
items.quote: And we continue to have an EBITDA margin of 22% to 23%. So that is, in my view, a very sustainable guidance that we have given in the past, and Biocon Biologics stays to that.

items.statement: Building own injectable facility to be commissioned in Q1 next fiscal.
items.quote: We are building our own injectable facility, which will be commissioned in the first quarter of next fiscal, followed by, first, the qualification and then we will take the batches.

items.statement: Insulin drug product capacity doubled, coming online end of this quarter.
items.quote: We made investments over the years and the most recent investment that you are referring to has doubled our capacity for drug product, which is expected to come online any time end of this quarter.

items.statement: Expanding insulin drug substance capacity in Malaysia, expected to double in a couple of years.
items.quote: We are also expanding our insulin drug substance, which we had guided in the past, and that's underway. Once that's completed, we expect to see a doubling of that drug substance capacity in Malaysia as well.

items.statement: Q3 Biocon Biologics EBITDA margin was 22% excluding forex impact.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 487 crore, and this includes a non -cash Forex translation loss of INR 20 crores. Excluding the Forex impact, the EBITDA margin stood at 22%.

items.statement: Q3 group core operating margin was 26%.
items.quote: Group core EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 1,007 crore, up 4% from last year and with a healthy core operating margin of 26%.

items.statement: Price erosion in line with budget; oncology portfolio holding strong.
items.quote: I think the price erosion is in line with what we had budgeted for. And in addition, Shyam, I think one adjustment you need to make in the reported numbers is the removal of the BFI revenues.

items.statement: U.S. biotech market dynamics stabilizing, albeit slightly later than expected.
items.quote: Growth in the quarter suggests that market dynamics, particularly in U.S. biotech, are now stabilizing, albeit slightly later than expected.

items.statement: Market share for Ogivri doubled to 22% and Fulphila rose to 23%.
items.quote: Our Oncology franchise, comprising of Ogivri, biosimilar Trastuzumab and Fulphila, biosimilar Pegfilgrastim, have seen significant increases in demand with the market share for Ogivri doubling to 22% from 11% last year, while Fulphila rose to 23% from 19% last year.

items.statement: Net debt at Biocon Biologics approximately USD 1.25 billion, expected to increase to USD 1.3 billion.
items.quote: And at Biocon Biologics, that's roughly USD 1.25 billion. This is now in December. So, you will add another USD 65 million of the commercial paper, so that will get you to USD 1.3 billion.

items.statement: Biocon acquired 1.5% stake in BBL, increasing holding to about 72%.
items.quote: Yes, Peter. I think we will get closer to 72% after the acquisition.

items.statement: Biocon standalone expects mid-teen growth, with peptides contributing from Liraglutide in FY26 and Semaglutide in FY27.
items.quote: I had addressed a previous question where I had reaffirmed that we are looking at the mid-teen kind of growth. There could be periods when it's higher, there could be periods when it's lower.

items.statement: Biocon standalone EBITDA margin expected to reach 13-14% in 1-2 years, from 10-12% guidance.
items.quote: And directionally, what I have guided for is an EBITDA margin of 10% to 12%. I mean, of course, it's gone down this quarter because of, again, increased R&D and expenses, but we will get closer to 13%, 14% in 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics EBITDA margin sustainable at 22-23%, possibly 25%.
items.quote: And the EBITDA would be in the mid-20s, so some 22%, 23%, maybe 25%. I think we have been in that range, and we want to make sure that we continue to deliver to that.

items.statement: R&D spend to be 7-9% of revenue, with cyclical phasing.
items.quote: We want to make sure that we have always said that we will continue to invest about 7% to 9% in R&D. We will have healthy strong gross margins and core EBITDAs in the mid-30s, which is where we are.

items.statement: Ustekinumab launch accelerated by 4 months, moving from FY26 to early FY26.
items.quote: If you noticed, when I say the Ustekinumab is global, and we are looking to launch that product globally, we have been able to accelerate the Ustekinumab launch by almost 4 months. So, it's moved from the next financial year, which is FY 2026, into maybe early FY 2026.

items.statement: Five new launches in U.S. and three globally in the year ahead.
items.quote: The year ahead, we have 5 new launches coming up in the U.S. and 3 globally. So certainly, whenever you have a new product launch, you will see a slightly better-than-expected performance.

items.statement: Cranbury facility capacity expansion to be ready by middle of this calendar year.
items.quote: We are also expanding the capacity of that facility, which will be ready by the middle of this calendar year, and we will use that facility for our future filings.

items.statement: Insulin demand continues and is complementary to GLP-1s, with increased opportunity in emerging markets and U.S.
items.quote: We are seeing a continued demand. We are seeing an increased focus on this. Globally, there is a requirement for this product, which continues to be there.

items.statement: Semaglutide global market opportunity expected at almost USD 50 billion in global sales.
items.quote: And if I may add one more thing that we know the volume of the market opportunity for Semaglutide, which is expected at almost USD 50 billion in global sales and not fully penetrated in many parts of the world.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics revenue split: 40% North America, 35% Europe/Japan/Australia, 25% emerging markets.
items.quote: If you look at it roughly, our business is between advanced markets and emerging markets about 75%-25%. And between the advanced markets, if I were to take a split between North America and Europe, Japan, Australia, you roughly see it biased slightly towards the U.S., maybe 40%-35% is what it would be between North America and the rest of advanced markets.

items.statement: Viatris settlement fully closed with USD 160 million paid, funded through existing liquidity.
items.quote: I think the Viatris settlement, Love, was about the deferred payment that we had to work on. And like we have said, we have been able to close out the entire USD 335 million, USD 175 million of that we had closed previously, which we had indicated and now we have closed the remaining USD 160 million.

items.statement: Investor liquidity options being managed, IPO one option, no quantification provided.
items.quote: We have a number of investors. We are working with all of them. We are looking to align their interest and satisfy them. And IPO clearly is one of the options that we have to do that.

items.statement: Tacrolimus China tender expected to open end of this calendar year with supplies in 2026.
items.quote: And I think we are expecting that tender to open sometime end of this calendar year with supplies commencing in 2026. We will, of course, be up against some of the other local Chinese companies.

items.statement: Semaglutide filings to start by first quarter of next fiscal, Canada by middle of this calendar year.
items.period: first quarter of next fiscal, middle of this calendar year
items.quote: As I mentioned, the filing has not started in any of the country. It will start by first quarter of next fiscal. Canada will be closer to the second quarter because Canada has additional SKUs, which are not there in some of the other markets.

items.statement: Advances book to grow by about 12% during FY25.
items.quote: The bank will definitely try to strike a balance between book quality growth and also hope to see the advances book grow by about 12% during FY '25 on a consolidated overall basis.

items.statement: NIM expected to improve by at least 10 to 20 bps.
items.quote: And we expect that the NIM would improve by at least about 10 to 20 bps, depending on the kind of churn that we are doing in the corporate low-yielding loans as well as the retail loans that we are booking.

items.statement: Overall portfolio loan yield to increase by at least 20 to 30 bps.
items.quote: So considering the potential churn, we expect that there will be an overall portf olio loan yield increase of at least about 20 to 30 bps as we go forward

items.statement: Credit cost targeted to remain lower than 0.5% for FY25.
items.quote: And we believe that we would be closing out lesser than 0.5% for the entire financial year 2025.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio projected to come down to about 55% in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: I think the bank projects to have a cost-to income ratio come down to about 55% in the upcom ing quarters

items.statement: ROA expected to close FY25 between 1.1% to 1.2%.
items.quote: and we expect to close this f inancial year anywhere between 1.1% to 1.2% and 1.2% has been the

items.statement: NIM target for FY25 is 3.2% to 3.4%.
items.quote: And last but not the least, we have already given that in the investor presentation in terms of the overall NIM target which would be 3.2% to 3.4%.

items.statement: ROE expected to be 12.5% to 13% in FY26.
items.quote: And on the ROE, we would want to kind of be in the 12.5% to 13% as we go into FY '26.

items.statement: Slippages to remain well below 2% for FY25.
items.quote: So the target for FY '25 would be that slippages will remain well below the 2% mark.

items.statement: GNPA and NNPA to become closer to 3% and 1% by end of FY25.
items.quote: So we have committed to the investors in the past, and we continue to stay with that commitment that we would become closer to 3% and closer to 1%, as far as these two, which is the GNPA and the NNPA is concerned, by the end of this financial year and in the following quarter.

items.statement: Deposit growth target of 8% to 10% for FY25.
items.quote: I think we will very well be in target to do that 8% to 10% of growth as far as the overall deposit is concerned from the INR 92,000 crores to the number that we are talking about.

items.statement: Advances to cross INR 1 lakh crores by June 2026.
items.quote: So we would be closer to INR 1 lakh crores definitely by June '26, if not crossing INR 1 lakh crores.

items.statement: PCR to improve by at least 1% every quarter.
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, we are committed to kind of improving PCR by 1% every quarter, at least a minimum of 1%.

items.statement: NIM improvement of 10 to 12 bps expected, with real churn in FY26.
items.quote: And we'll start seeing an improvement in the NIM, as I called out earlier, which is a 10 to 12 bps and the real churn on the overall advances will happen, which will be in FY '26.

items.statement: Operating profit expected to surpass previous year's INR 1,306 crores.

items.quote: However, notwithstanding the above, we expect these markets to recover and come back to their original levels in the medium term soon.

items.statement: Confident short-term domestic situation will correct in the near term.

items.statement: Employee cost percentage to be at par with FY24 next year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve gradually quarter-to-quarter.
items.quote: So with this, the EBITDA margin will improve gradually quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Bathware segment to grow around 10% this year.

items.statement: Nepal plant utilization to reach 80-85% by March-April.
items.quote: And hopefully, as we gradually go up, the capacity will be ramped up to about 80%, 85% by end of March, April.

items.statement: Nepal interest rate locked at 9%, down from 14%.
items.quote: And we have locked all our interest liability at 9%. So when we conceived the plant it was 14%, so it's a -- 5% is a big saving.

items.statement: Dividend payout to remain 40-50% in near to medium term.
items.quote: In our dividend policy, we have clearly stated it has to be around 40% to 50%. So sometime it can be 40%, it can be 50%.

items.quote: I can give you certain numbers like, let's say, for U.K., the freight, which was 1,600 before this problem had gone up to 4,000. It has now come back to 1,750.

items.statement: Advertising cost for December quarter around INR30-32 crores.
items.quote: December should be in the range of roughly INR30 crores as an advertising cost. INR30 crores, INR32 crores basically.

items.quote: We had set high single-digit growth in revenues. And long term margins which would be in the high single-digit.

items.quote: You are right, we had guided that this year we will end the total domestic business above 400 crores. We are likely to be there 430-440 crores, out of which the B2C will be 300 crores.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for the year is 10-20%.
items.quote: So, you know, if you see while for the last three, four years, we have been guiding a 15% or so plus volume growth, at the start of the year, considering the volatility in the market, the high prices, we had indicated that this time our guidance will be between 10 to 20%.

items.statement: Long-term volume growth guidance of 15% is maintained.
items.quote: As long as the consumption is intact, I think things should settle down and probably should not impact our long-term growth guidance of 15%. So, that we are committed.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected to be 15-20% until volume growth returns to 15-20%.
items.quote: So, we are very confident of maintaining this EBITDA growth of 15 to 20% till we are back into the volume growth of 15 to 20%, which then will again drive EBITDA at the same level.

items.statement: No CAPEX planned for next year; capacity building done for three years.
items.quote: I don't think so we will have any CAPEX in next year. We are done with our CAPEX for the next three years or so because most of our capacity building is over now.

items.statement: 7,000 metric ton capacity to be commissioned this quarter.
items.quote: This quarter we will commission that capacity.

items.statement: B2C segment expected to yield higher margins than B2B over long term.
items.quote: But having said so, we are confident that over a long period of time, definitely the B2C segment, the branded segment will help us gain more margins than the B2B setup.

items.statement: Taken 30-40% price increases in larger packs; another 10-15% lag remains.
items.quote: Having said so, in the larger packs, we already have taken almost 30 to 40% price increases in the last 1, 1.5 years, and I think another 10 to 15% lag is still left, but we will wait and watch for the leaders that how do they take this forward and accordingly we will formulate our price increases as strategy.

items.statement: 10-15% grammage cut in LUPs in last 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: There have been grammages cut over a period of time, not very much because, you know, there is a certain cup of coffee that you have to deliver with one LUP. So, we don't have a lot of leeway to cut grammages, but yes, there has been 10 to 15% grammage cut that has happened in LUPs in the last 1, 1.5 years.

items.statement: Coffee prices not expected to soften until Brazilian crop in May-June.
items.quote: So, probably we will have to wait for, you know, other crops to come in, which is Brazilian crop in May-June. That's the time we will see how the trend goes, but as of now the prices are not, you know, softening.

items.statement: Volume growth this quarter was 3-4%, YTD around 10%.
items.quote: So, volume growth, if you see this quarter has been marginal around 3 to 4% or so, and the YTD if you see the first quarter, we were around 13-14%, the second quarter was around 9-10%. So, we are on a YTD basis close to close to 10% of volume growth.

items.statement: 30-35% of sales from LUPs.
items.quote: The second question is as far as LUPs are concerned, almost today our 30 to 35% of our sales come from LUPs which is still reasonable considering that, you know, some of the leaders, their sales are almost 50 to 60% of their sales are LUPs.

items.statement: Working capital high at 1,200 crores due to high coffee prices.
items.quote: So, you know, working capital, yes, it remains high because of, it's almost 1,200 crores as we speak. It remains high because of the high coffee prices.

items.statement: Total debt around 2,000 crores; long-term debt 790-800 crores.
items.quote: And I told you the debt numbers, 1,200 crores of working capital. Long-term debt is around 790 to 800 crores as of now. Total is around 2,000 crores of debt.

items.statement: Peak debt not to exceed 2,200 crores in next two years; annual repayment 150-200 crores.
items.quote: I don't see the peak debt levels going beyond 2,200 crores in the next year or the year after that also. In fact, it should start reducing because we will be repaying it.

items.statement: Post-renovation, first full year revenues expected at INR170 crores with EBITDA north of INR60 crores.
items.value: INR170 crores, EBITDA north of INR60 crores
items.quote: So where potentially post-renovation, in the first full year, we're looking at revenues of about INR170 crores with an EBITDA north of INR60 crores.

items.statement: Post-renovation ADRs expected to improve to INR9,500 to INR10,500.
items.quote: Post-renovation, we expect our ADRs to significantly improve to INR9,500 to INR10,500 mark.

items.statement: Post-renovation ADR increase can lead to about 30% increase in revenues.
items.quote: But once we are finished, completed the renovation, we can look at the INR9,500 to INR10,500 mark, which can easily lead to about a 30% increase in our revenues.

items.statement: Courtyard by Marriott renovation: 56 new guest rooms on floors 6 and 7, gym/spa on 8, rooftop bar with pool on 9, operational by end of June.
items.quote: The interiors of the remaining four floors are being completed as we speak, and by the end of June, we expect 56 new guest rooms to be added to the sixth and seventh floor, and a brand new state-of-the-art gym and spa facility is on the eighth floor, and a rooftop bar with a pool on the ninth floor.

items.statement: Marriott convention center and select guest rooms renovation to begin April 2025, phase-wise over two years.
items.quote: In the Marriott property, the convention center and select guest rooms attached to the convention center will undergo renovation from April 2025. The Marriott property will undergo renovation in a phase-wise manner over two years, keeping in mind that it is a fully operational hotel.

items.statement: Entire renovation expected to be completed by 2027.
items.quote: And we're expecting the entire renovation to be completed by 2027.

items.statement: In metro cities supply growing 3-4% per year while demand growing 10-12% every year.
items.quote: Even in Hyderabad, there have been a lot of reports about how supply is only growing at about 3% to 4% per year, whereas the demand is growing at about 10%, 12% every year.

items.statement: Over next three to four years, great increase in demand expected.
items.quote: So that way, this is a great sign for us that over the next three to four years, we can see a great increase in demand.

items.statement: Evaluating another hotel in Hyderabad; expanding portfolio to three hotels very soon.
items.quote: So, currently as we speak, we are evaluating another hotel in Hyderabad. Once we have the definitive agreement signed, we will make that announcement. But we are looking at expanding our portfolio to three hotels very, very soon.

items.statement: Rights issue subscribed close to 112%, reflecting strong investor confidence.
items.quote: Also, we would like to state that the company's recent rights issue received an overwhelming response and was subscribed to close to 112%, reflecting strong investor confidence and demand.

items.statement: Flow-through profit from additional ADR jump is almost 95%.
items.quote: And majority of this is driven by the room business, which was typically the flow-through profit in this additional ADR jump is almost about 95%.

items.statement: Occupancy at about 70%, can improve a few percentage points post-renovation.
items.quote: While this is something that we've been able to beat and achieve in the current year in itself, we're almost at about a 70% occupancy mark. And we can see that going forward, once the product is also renovated, we can see a few percentage points improvement.

items.statement: Targeting roughly 20% to 25% CAGR EBITDA over 3 to 5 years.
items.quote: Our focus is on sustainable mid- to long-term growth targeting roughly 20% to 25% CAGR EBITDA over 3 to 5 year’s time frame.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance unchanged at INR1,300 to INR1,500 crore.
items.quote: Our projected capital expenditure for FY '25 remains unchanged as we have m entioned in the last quarter, INR1,300 to INR1,500 crore, with over INR380 crore spent in Q3 and about INR1,020 crore in the 9-month year -till-date time frame

items.statement: FY26 capex to be a bit lower than INR1,000 crore.
items.quote: As regards FY '26, the capex would be a number which will be a bit lower than INR1,000 crore.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA guidance based on 14% to 15% margin assumption.
items.quote: So that number of EBITDA is based on EBITDA assumption of 14% to 15%, right, so you can back calculate the revenue on the basis of that and Arun, as I had mentioned previously, we like to focus on absolute EBITDA and not necessarily give revenue guidance because bulk of our raw materials are linked to crude, right, benzene, aniline, which are 2 of our largest raw materials.

items.statement: Cost reduction plan 30-40% complete, to finish in 12-18 months.
items.quote: I think we are kind of 30% -40% there in terms of that journey. I think there still remains a lot of what's to be done, but we are confident of completing that exercise, as I mentioned in the last call, in the next sort of 12 to 18 months kind of time frame.

items.statement: Representative gross margin around 13%.
items.quote: I think more representative gross margin number is potentially in the range of, I think, 13% -odd kind of a range.

items.statement: Pricing pressure continues in agrochemical intermediates and other chains.
items.quote: However, pricing pressure continues across various product chains, especially in agrochemical intermediates.

items.statement: Non-energy volumes grew 14% Y-o-Y and 8% Q-o-Q.
items.quote: Volumes in the non-energy business grew by 14% Y -o-Y and 8% Q-o-Q, while the growth in the energy business came in at 10% quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: MMA volumes ramp-up gradual but consistent.
items.quote: As indicated in previous communications, the ramp-up of MMA volumes will be gradual but consistent.

items.statement: Developing new products in ethylation value chain and backward integration.
items.quote: And further, in order to diversify our product base and to augment our utilization levels, we are engaged in the development of new products, especially within the ethylation value chain where we recently exp anded our capacity.

items.statement: Uncertainty in 2025 demand due to potential U.S. policy changes.
items.quote: Despite s ome uncertainty surrounding 2025 demand due to potential U.S. policy changes, we remain focused on increasing our market share in the global markets, especially in the U.S. and Japan, for polymer and additives segment.

items.statement: Committed INR100 crore to JV, INR50 crore each partner.
items.quote: So for the first year, both partners put toget her have committed INR100 crore, INR50 crore each, into the joint venture.

items.statement: Renewable share in power purchase to exceed 75% by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: With this, AIL's renewable share in total power purchase is expected to exceed 75% by Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Targeting 14% to 15% ROCE and ROIC in 3-year plan.
items.quote: And as we have indicated in our mid-term guidance, our objective is to hit 14%, 15% kind of ROCE and ROIC numbers. And I think we remain quite confident of hitting those numbers in our 3-year plan.

items.statement: NCB capacity utilization to ramp to 80%-plus next financial year.
items.quote: And in the coming financial year, we expect to ramp that up to 80%-plus kind of level.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY25 marginally negative or near zero; FY26 low single-digit.
items.value: marginally negative or about closer to 0; low single-digit
items.quote: The tax rate in this year, considering that a lot of projects are getting commercialized and there will be some IT depreciation benefits; will continue to remain the way it is currently. So it will be marginally negative and or about closer to 0. Next year, it should be in a more like a low single -digit kind of range, at least at this point of time.

items.statement: Anticipates high teens revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years, with EBITDA margins crossing 20%.
items.quote: I think we are anticipating a growth in the next 3 to 5 years of high teens per year-on-year CAGR if you were to project ourselves out and we were sitting together here in FY '28, 3-4 years from now, and we have to review where the business was in FY '24 and where we are stepwise, we'll get there.

items.statement: Aims to cross 20% EBITDA margin barrier and go beyond.
items.quote: Our aim is to cross the 20% barrier, which we were historically doing about 2, 3 years ago. So, our target is to cross that first and go beyond that also, yes.

items.statement: FY25 capex to be INR140-150 crores; FY26 plan INR150-200 crores annually.
items.quote: Absolutely. We are sticking to what we have said earlier. It will be INR140 crores to INR150 crores.

items.statement: 30-40% of capex for replacement, balance for debottleneck growth.
items.quote: See, 30% to 40% will be replacement capex. The balance will be the debottleneck growth capex.

items.statement: CDMO expected to overtake generics, moving towards 60-40 revenue split.
items.quote: But from a going forward, I think CDMO will overtake the generics business. So, it may be working towards a 60-40 type of split from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Two NCE products close to launch by end FY26/early FY27; others in FY27 and beyond.
items.quote: Out of that, two products are very close to launch, which we expected to be launched in -- towards the end of financial year FY '26. And the others will get launched if everything goes well, in FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: Animal Health validation to complete in next 2 quarters; commercial sales from FY26.
items.quote: We expect to complete the validation of the por tfolio in the upcoming 2 quarters, which will assist us in securing the product registration in various countries and ultimately enable the launch of these products across several global markets

items.statement: Animal Health business targeted to exceed INR400 crores over next 5 years.
items.quote: So, we really see a significant amount of growth in excess of INR400-plus crores of business over the next 5 years. So that's the long-term plan that we have and even grow it beyond that.

items.statement: Animal Health contribution margins expected 45% plus, with some products 55%.
items.quote: So, the margins will be -- on the contribution side, I would estimate the margins to be 45% plus, right? Because the portfolio in the Animal Health business is a mix.

items.statement: NCE or CDMO type products in Animal Health to have gross margins in excess of 50%.
items.quote: Yes, certainly. I mean, like I said, is that the NCE type or the CDMO type products will be in excess of 50% in terms of gross margins, right?

items.statement: Crop protection industry expected to stabilize in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Despite the ongoing challenges such as pricing pressure from competitors, especially from China, the global crop protection industry is expected to stabilize in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: API business recovery expected to remain steady in coming quarters.
items.quote: For our API business, we are witnessing recovery on the back of improved volume uptakes, which is expected to remain steady in the coming quarters.

items.statement: CDMO offtake improvements expected to persist and improve in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: On the CDMO front, we have seen consistently improvements in offtake from key innovators, a trend that is expected to persist and improve in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Intense pricing pressure and dumping from Chinese competitors for generics and commodities.
items.quote: Although China Plus One is expected to strengthen in the current operating environment, intense pricing pressure and dumping continues from the Chinese competitors for generics and commodity products.

items.statement: U.S. tariffs on Chinese chemicals create volatile situation; impact uncertain.
items.quote: So, look, of course, we've heard the news this morning about 10% tariffs on chemical companies in China. We're obviously looking at that. Those are in addition to supposedly 25% already existing tariffs that they have in place.

items.statement: R&D investment maintained at 4.5-5% of revenue.
items.quote: Additionally, we are consistently investing about 4.5% to 5% of our revenue into our R&D to drive innovation in products and services that meet the changing demands of all our customers.

items.statement: Reduced full-year MDF margin guidance to 13-14% from earlier 16% plus.
items.quote: As a result, we are reducing our full year margin guidance to 13 -14% as against earlier of 16% plus.

items.statement: Expects Q4 revenue substantially better and margins stronger.
items.quote: However, in the fourth quarter, we believe that the revenue will substantially be better and margins will be stronger.

items.statement: HDF flooring line delayed by 6 months; equipment to arrive March, fully functional May 2025.
items.quote: Construction of our HDF flooring line has been delayed by 6 months due to the late arrival of major equipment, which is likely to arrive in the month of March and will be fully functional in the month of May '25.

items.statement: Glue plant construction likely to be completed this quarter.
items.quote: Construction of our glue plant is also likely to be completed in this quarter.

items.statement: Aims to cross 10% margin in Q4 due to cost actions, price hike, and better volumes.
items.quote: With all these factors, I mean, definitely, we believe that we should be crossing 10% margin for quarter 4.

items.statement: Took 1.5% MDF price increase in Q3; no further MDF price hike as of now.
items.quote: MDF price increase is around 1.5% during the quarter. And on the plywood side -- plywood, you are saying in the last quarter?

items.statement: Took 1.5% plywood price increase in Q3; taking another 1.5% in Q4.
items.quote: Q3, the price increase was around 1.5%. And we are also taking another price increase during this quarter, which will also be in the range of 1.5%.

items.statement: Demand not picked up; liquidity bigger issue than demand.
items.quote: I think the demand scenario is that it has not really picked up. But added to that, the major problem, what we saw that, even if the demand was there in pockets, liquidity was a serious challenge.

items.statement: Expects positive outlook for panel and plywood business due to BIS regulations and organized shift.
items.quote: But for sure, I see now going forward, things will be very, very positive for panel business and for plywood business. A, because of the implementation of BIS regulations, which will definitely curb imports in the near term.

items.statement: Lost about 1.5% volume due to stringent receivables policy.
items.quote: So I could clearly see that we would have lost maybe easily 1.5% of volume just because we wanted to be controlling our receivables.

items.statement: Announced INR134 crores plywood capex adding 13.5 million sq meters capacity, 25% increase.
items.quote: It's already announced. I think INR134 crores, to be very precise is the number what we have declared. This will give us a new capacity of 13.5 million square meters, which is almost an addition of 25% capacity over our present manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Plywood volume growth target around 7% plus for FY25.
items.quote: So FY '25, the volume, I think we are at around 5.7% right now. And with quarter 4, we will try to be anywhere around 7% plus.

items.statement: MDF volume growth target around 50% for full year FY25.
items.quote: And for MDF, we had initially targeted almost a 50% growth over last year. We should be around that number for the full year.

items.statement: Adding flooring line to MDF to increase value-added sales and improve product mix.
items.quote: Number two, we are adding a flooring line to our existing MDF line. which will help us increase the value-added sales and help us improve the product mix further.

items.statement: Expects net debt around INR450 crores at year-end, net debt-to-equity around 0.55.
items.quote: At the year -end, our debt on a cautious approach would be around INR450 crores as guided earlier, which means our net debt -to-equity ratio at the year-end would be around 0.55 despite expansion and setting up of 2 new line of businesses.

items.statement: Samet JV expected to touch INR80-100 crores revenue in coming year.
items.quote: But just a ballpark number, I would say that definitely, we feel that touching anywhere around INR80 crores to INR100 crores in the coming year is a number which is doable.

items.statement: Expects to meet FY26 revenue target of INR600 crores based on seeding activities, new products, and JV benefits.
items.quote: Nevertheless, for FY '26, we are still expecting to meet what you mentioned, based on the seeding activities which I mentioned that we have done in recent quarters. So we have a good line-up of the products, which we have recently launched plus new products in pipeline. And the benefits from the joint ventures. So yes, so that looks more than achievable, I would say.

items.statement: Morris Co. JV benefits expected from Q2 or Q3 next financial year when new Kolkata facility operational.
items.quote: The JV with Morris Co. is advancing well, and we anticipate benefits to start accruing from Q2 or Q3 of next financial year, once our new manufacturing facility becomes operational, which is expected within the same timeframe in Kolkata.

items.statement: Aims to increase non-pen contribution from less than 10% to 30% in medium term.
items.quote: So, currently the contribution of non-pen would be less than 10%. So, which is quite, you know, lopsided I would say towards the core category. So, I think ideally, we are looking at least in the medium term 70-30 kind of a ratio.

items.statement: Non-pen categories margins expected to be lower due to outsourcing.
items.quote: Honestly, you know, it will be a little lower because these non-stationary and non-pen categories are mostly outsourced.

items.statement: Reintroduced three products at INR5 price point without new investment to counter competition.
items.quote: Absolutely. So, we have actually reintroduced three products, which we had in the past, not really, -- we had actually discontinued, but we did some cost engineering and then reintroduced three products at that price point without any new investment.

items.statement: Export realizations are 5-10% better than domestic.
items.quote: In the range of 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Pen category growth expected around 5-6%, driven by premiumization and market share gains.
items.quote: So, well, of course, the market estimates are that the category growth is -- of course, it is slightly stunted, but it is still more than 5%. So it could be around 5% to 6%. But definitely the growth will come mainly from the premiumization. And of course, we are also looking at gaining market share from the competition.

items.statement: Gross margin has room to increase; 50-50 in-house vs outsourced production model affects margins.
items.quote: So, if you compare to our peers, definitely the gross margin, we still have room in increasing our gross margin. But one significant difference is that the peers which you are mentioning, it's mostly their in-house production. Whereas in our case, it is a kind of a 50-50 model.

items.statement: Markers and mechanical pencils to launch in Q1 FY26; Linc calculators launched in Q4.
items.quote: Markers and mechanical pencils are set for launch in Q1 FY '26, further strengthening our presence in writing instruments. Lin c calculators launched in Q4 cater to the affordable segment, expanding our customer reach

items.statement: Active outlets currently about 100,000; trying to activate more from enrolled 250,000.
items.quote: So currently the active outlets are about 100,000 outlets. So as such there has been no increase if you say lately. It is just that we are trying to make these 250,000 outlets which are enrolled trying to make some of them active every month.

items.statement: Non-pen products reached about 15,000-20,000 outlets.
items.quote: I think about what? 15,000, 20,000 outlets.

items.statement: Pentonic average realization should increase with new products at INR20, INR30, INR40.
items.quote: So, the Pentonic average realization should increase because, as I mentioned in my opening remarks that, we have launched several new products in Pentonic portfolio at price range of INR20, INR30, INR40 and they are taking a little longer time to get the desired traction. So, we are heading for a better realization going forward in the Pentonic portfolio.

items.statement: Expects double-digit top line growth and EBITDA growth in sync or faster for FY26.
items.quote: Double-digit growth. I think we remain double-digit growth on our top line and EBITDA growth to be in sync or faster than our top line growth.

items.statement: Targets 17-18% EBITDA margin in next 6-8 quarters.
items.quote: So, in next, I think 6 to 8 quarters, we should see us touching a much higher level of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Gross margins have improved for 6-7 quarters and are expected to continue improving.
items.quote: So gross margins, we've been very, very focused on driving it back to the levels. And I think October, December numbers would reasonably matched October, December '21 kind of level.

items.statement: Price increases taken across multiple products due to commodity cost inflation.
items.quote: Yes. So there would be a price increase across multiple products wherever we are seeing the costs going up, largely commodity-led products, we are taking whatever required price increases.

items.statement: Urban demand setback seen as temporary; revival anticipated in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect that the demand setback, especially in urban areas is temporary in nature and anticipate a revival in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Smaller packs growing faster, especially in Personal Care.
items.quote: It's small. We don't share those specifics, but it's building up much faster. In some of the categories like Personal Care, we've seen a very smart uptick of that, which is driven by, like I mentioned, small packs being low unit price, but also consumer behaviour, which is shifting to onetime use packs for freshness and experience.

items.statement: Naturell acquisition expected to be EPS accretive in FY26.
items.quote: And we believe FY '26, we could have an EPS accretive on this business.

items.statement: Online channels contribute 10-11% of revenue and growing faster.
items.quote: So first of all, from the online business perspective, about 10% to 11% of our revenue comes from selling in online platforms. And that's been growing at a much faster pace than the rest of the business, and we are quite conscious of the fact that since the consumers are shifting to this, we should be ahead of the curve.

items.statement: Food service (HoReCa) channel accounts for 8-10% of sales.
items.quote: So B2B, how would you define B2B? If you are saying food service -- if you're looking for food service, which is largely the HoReCa channel, that would be about 8% to 10% range.

items.statement: Working capital intensity expected to increase as e-commerce and modern trade share rises.
items.quote: Yes. Yes. Umesh Parikh: Yes, that's how we see it. That's right

items.statement: Deferred tax liability of INR3.5-4 crores to be recorded in Q4.
items.quote: And about INR3.5 crores to INR4 crores, you can assume as a deferred tax liability getting recorded in the Q4 as well.

items.statement: Company expects 20%+ growth as new normal, with 50-100 bps annual margin improvement over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So, now we see that the new normal for this Company should be 20% plus growth. And today for us, maybe if you look at let us say predictability, let's say predictable growth for this Company, as we have seen already four year growth cycle now, from FY22 to 25 numbers which will be almost we are 9 months over.

items.statement: Nine-month capex Rs. 222 crores; full-year budget Rs. 300 crores; new plants to cost Rs. 400-500 crores over 18-20 months.
items.quote: So, this year we have done around close in 9 months Rs. 222 crores of CAPEX and budget of Rs. 300 crores. And probably another few more months of CAPEX and FY26 will then probably our CAPEX cycle for the old plants which were established between 23 and 24 will be over and then we will focus on the new plants which we are establishing , three new plants which were establishing.

items.statement: Dialysis machine run rate 40-50 per month; FY25 installations 300-350, next year to double.
items.quote: No, we will not be able to do 500 installations this year. This year we will be able to do between 300 and 350 installations. I don't have a real figure, but it should be around 350 plus. And then next year maybe we will double the installations.

items.statement: EBITDA margin projected at 27% for FY25, with 100-150 bps improvement over last year.
items.quote: And on the margin side, I think, we have already projected close to 27% EBITDA margin for this year. Last year, we were close to 26% this year, 100 bps improvement, 100-150 bps.

items.statement: Domestic price hikes typically 3-4% per year.
items.quote: It depends. So, sometimes the contracts are longer, you don't get a price hike. But typically, we can take between 3% to 4% price hike per year.

items.statement: Domestic business expected to end FY25 with over 20% overall growth.
items.quote: And hopefully, the current financial year, we should e nd up more than 20% overall growth rate in the domestic business.

items.statement: Exports growing at 28% in nine months, 30% in Q3; on track to deliver committed growth.
items.quote: Exports in the first nine months have shown a great growth. They have been growing at around 28% closely. And if you look at the quarter itself, it's grown by around 30%. So, overall, we are on track to deliver the committed growth.

items.statement: Europe expected to end FY25 with 27-28% growth.
items.quote: Europe has overall grown by around 30% in nine months. Last quarter growth was around 20%. And I think overall we should end up between 27 %-28% growth for Europe by the end of the year, which is a very healthy growth.

items.statement: Renal business targeting 20-25% market share by 2030.
items.quote: But our target is to maybe reach let's say, by 2030 around 20% to 25% of the market share.

items.statement: US business first stronger wave expected in FY27.
items.quote: We see the first stronger wave coming in FY27 because we have some more products to be included in the list, and they're undergoing some clinical trials and regulatory approval, and they will also start contributing to revenue maybe end of this year or early next year.

items.statement: US tariffs expected to be neutral for company as they apply equally to all countries.
items.quote: So, they don't impact India as such, but I think as these tariffs are also in China and maybe even if it comes on India, it will be neutral for us because it will be equally applicable to all the countries. So, we don't expect any impact of this tariffs.

items.statement: QIP proceeds: Rs. 500 crores for new capex, part designated for acquisition.
items.quote: Correct. There's a segmentation of QIP proceeds, so Rs. 500 crores is for new CAPEX, and that is where we will be using it.

items.statement: New plants to be commissioned in 18-21 months.
items.quote: And then all the QIP proceeds will be used for the three new plan ts, which are under construction right now , and will go live in 18 to 21 months.

items.statement: Solar power JV operational by September-October, aiming for green power.
items.quote: And hopefully this will be operational by end of September, October. And after that, most of the polymed manufacturing facility will be running on green power.

items.statement: Total EBITDA to be 1.5x FY25 in FY26, with at least 300 bps margin expansion.

items.statement: Individual adjusted first-year premium grew 25% in 9M FY25.

items.statement: Total APE expanded by 17% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Retained order inflow guidance of Rs. 20,000-22,000 crore.

items.statement: Expects Q4 margin around 9.5%, which is sustainable.
items.quote: So, this margin, whatever we gave the guidance now revised to 9.25% as you said, we are expecting the margin should be around 9.5% in t his quarter 4, so that the reason we thought it will be around 9.25%. So, this at the moment it is sustainable.

items.statement: Expects Q4 revenue to be similar or slightly less year-on-year.
items.quote: It will be similar, or it will be little less.

items.statement: Expects Q4 consolidated execution between Rs. 6,000-6,400 crores.
items.quote: Now, the 4th Quarter , the execution would be on consol idated between Rs. 6,000-Rs. 6,400 crores, we are expecting.

items.statement: L1 project pipeline is roughly Rs. 9,000-10,000 crores.
items.quote: The L1 project in the pipeline is roughly about Rs. 9,000-Rs. 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Prospective project pipeline is about Rs. 2.45 lakh crore across verticals and states.
items.quote: I am happy to share with you this prospective pipeline of project the value is about Rs. 2.45 lakh crore. It is in all the verticals, all the seven verticals in which we operate and it is in almost all the states, large states at least.

items.statement: Incurred Rs. 253 crores capex against budgeted Rs. 250 crores for regular projects.
items.quote: We have incurred a CAPEX of Rs. 253 crores in the current financial year as against the budgeted CAPEX of Rs. 250 crores for regular projects.

items.statement: Expects to spend up to Rs. 250 crores capex limit for the year.
items.quote: It was Rs. 250 crores and we have spent so far Rs. 223 crores. We expect that we will be spending up to that limit.

items.statement: Slow execution due to elections and elongated billing/payment cycles.
items.quote: We have witnessed the slow pace of execution due to general elections and elections in some of the states. Additionally, some of our projects have seen elongated billing and payment cycles, leading to a slowdown in execution.

items.statement: Debt increased due to payment slowdown and higher unbilled revenue.
items.quote: We have already explained you that there is a slowdown in the payment mechanism because of these elections and all that is the reason if you see the d ebt level has increased. At the same time, my unbilled revenue also got increased.

items.statement: Expects debt to decline from current Rs. 2,415 crores, possibly to Rs. 1,500 or 1,000 crores.
items.quote: So, at this moment, we cannot tell, but there will be some decline in the present level of debt we are expecting.

items.statement: Expects to receive Rs. 1,150 crores from AP capital city projects by end of March.
items.quote: So, AP exposure there are two parts, the first part about Capital City projects, we have pending of Rs. 1,150 crores that we expect to receive by end of March.

items.statement: Expects to realize Rs. 374 crores loan from Vizag deal in next couple of years.
items.quote: And as far as the loan is concerned about Rs. 374 is the loan amount and in the current year, we received about Rs. 15 crores against the interest amount and this Rs. 374 crores also, we are expecting to get realized in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Maintains H2 volume growth guidance of 7-8%.
items.quote: We are looking for the entire year, our volume growth of 7% to 8% in H2. We are looking at it over there.

items.statement: Maintains H2 EBITDA increase guidance of INR150 per tonne.
items.quote: And we are also keeping our projection of what we said about H2 EBITDA increase, which we had indicated between first half to second half, H2 average would be about INR 150 increase in the EBITDA, and we are maintaining that and no change in that.

items.statement: Full year capex expected at INR500 crores.
items.quote: Capex for the whole year, we are looking at a number of INR500 crores.

items.statement: 9-month capex around INR300 crores.
items.quote: 9 months, it is around INR300 crores.

items.statement: Incentive accrual for the year expected around INR100 crores.
items.quote: For this year, as guided earlier, we are expecting total incentive accrual to be around INR 100 crores.

items.statement: 9-month incentive accruals around INR60 crores.
items.quote: For 9 months, that accruals is around INR60 crores.

items.statement: Own coal usage was 15% in Q3.
items.quote: Yes. Our own coal was to the tune of 15% in this quarter.

items.statement: Captive coal share to rise to 30-32% after Bikram reaches optimum.
items.quote: And once Bikram Coal Block comes on field, once that achieved the optimum level of production, it should go up to around 30% -- between 30%, 32% of our total.

items.statement: Bikram coal to reach optimum in FY27.
items.quote: I think next year , it will not reach optimum level. Optimum level will be reached in the next financial year, that is '26-'27.

items.statement: Marki-Barka coal to meet 55-60% of total coal requirements.
items.quote: Marki-Barka once that comes, it will be around 55% -- between 55% and 60% of our total requirements.

items.statement: Green power target 35% in 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: So our aim is to reach to the level of 35%. But it will take -- as you rightly said, it will take another 1 year to 1.5 years.

items.statement: Pet coke price expected to range $100-110.
items.quote: And we expect this to range between $100 to $110 pet coke prices.

items.statement: Net debt around INR3,000 crores as of Q3.
items.quote: Our net debt as of the third quarter is around INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Closing incentive balance INR435 crores as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: As our closing balance is about INR435 crores as of 31 December '24, this is excluding the West Bengal incentive which is under litigation.

items.statement: Received INR187 crores cash subsidy this financial year.
items.quote: INR187 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: FY25 industry growth expected around 4-5%.
items.quote: Going forward, what we at JK Lakshmi see is that this year the growth is going to be around 4 % to 5%, somewhere around that, and next year FY26 may be around 6 % to 7%.

items.statement: Udaipur capacity utilization expected around 65% in FY26.
items.quote: So, we will achieve somewhere around 65% of capacity utilization in FY26 for Udaipur, right?

items.statement: CAPEX expected about 1,000 crores in FY26 and 1,500 crores in FY27.
items.value: 1,000 crores in FY26 and 1,500 crores in FY27
items.quote: Yes, CAPEX we expect Next year to be about, as I mentioned in my last call also , this year in nine months, we already done about 250 crores , another 100 crores may come in the current quarter and then thereafter about 1,000 in the next FY26 and about 1,500 in FY27.

items.statement: Q4 volume growth estimated at 7-8%.
items.quote: Fourth quarter, our estimation is likely to grow at about 7% to 8% and we are going to be in alignment with that, right, 8% I would say.

items.statement: Brand rejuvenation expected to improve price positioning by Rs.80-100 per ton.
items.quote: So, the brand recognition, the idea is to improve price positioning and perhaps I think that is going to give some good benefit in terms of at least improving our price positioning by Rs.80 to Rs.100 a ton.

items.statement: Premium share expected to return to previous levels in coming quarter.
items.quote: But perhaps I think in coming quarter, we are going to go back to the same level because what we have done is in East also we have done some kind of brand restructuring, just to let you, we have Pro+ as a premium product here in this part of India, there we have the base product.

items.statement: Sirohi limestone auction due in 2030; company plans to retain mine.
items.quote: Yes. So, I think auction is due in the year 2030 and this is the case for Sirohi and this is the case for some other locations for other companies as well, right? So, we definitely want to retain this during re-auction also for sure.

items.statement: Udaipur merger expected to complete in about eight to nine months.
items.quote: Yes, for m erger, we already have the stock exchange, SEBI approval, we have approv al from the NCLT and that might take about eight, nine months.

items.statement: Demand good in operating markets and prices improving.
items.quote: So, last quarter from December, demand has started improving , demand is good in our operating markets and so is the prices also are improving.

items.statement: Prices in core markets higher by Rs.75-100 vs Q3 average.
items.quote: I would say definitely about Rs.75 to Rs.100.

items.statement: Company expects to grow better than industry due to Udaipur and Surat.
items.quote: I think we are going to do better because I think we have now Udaipur and Surat also in place. So, our growth is going to be better than industry.

items.statement: Blended cement at 65%, trade proportion at 58% in Q3.
items.quote: Blended cement was at 65%, trade proportion was 58%.

items.statement: Premium sale at 11% of total volume in Q3.
items.quote: Premium sale on an overall volume basis, total trade, non-trade put together was at 11% and fuel was at 1.57 for 1,000 Kms.

items.statement: Renewable energy at 48% of energy requirements in last quarter.
items.quote: In the last quarter it was at 48%.

items.statement: Surat phase 1 commissioning by Feb end or March, phase 2 by June 2025.
items.quote: First phase is going to get commissioned in the month of March itself or February end, which is about half of the capacity about 0.8 million tons, and another rest of 0.6 million tons during around June 2025.

items.statement: Aims to achieve 5% EBIT margin by end of FY2026.
items.quote: Now the 5% margin is something that we hope to achieve by the end of FY 2026.

items.statement: Guides 12-15% growth for overall travel segment.
items.quote: We've said 12% to 15% growth is our guidance on the travel segment.

items.statement: Expects to close FY25 with healthy double-digit growth.
items.quote: On a look ahead, we expect to close FY '25 with a healthy double-digit growth and with continuing to build our base on business for FY '26.

items.statement: Expects 2025 to be a fairly strong year for DEI.
items.quote: With that forward-looking, we see 2025 to be a fairly strong year for us to get back to where we were -- where we have left it in the past.

items.statement: Bagged National Games Uttarakhand business of about INR 120 crores.
items.quote: We are actually doing the National Games in Uttarakhand, which the total size of that business is roughly about INR 120 crores, which will now reflect in the current operating quarter.

items.statement: Forward bookings show 20%+ volume growth and 35% value growth.
items.quote: But despite that, from a volume perspective, we are actually seeing close to about 20 -plus percent growth in terms of volumes. And in terms of value, we are saying close to about 35% growth.

items.statement: Expects 2,000 passengers for Kumbh Mela by season end.
items.quote: And we expect by the time this season ends or the Kumbh Mela ends, we would have roughly close to about 2,000 passengers who would have travelled through us.

items.statement: Japan bookings at 85-90% of last year's volumes; expects positive contribution.
items.quote: And as we speak, we are already close to about 85% to 90% of the volumes that we did last year. So I expect the Japan to contribute very positively in the quarter to come.

items.statement: Non-air business grew to 8% of portfolio in 2024 from 5% in 2023.
items.quote: In 2023, non -air business was about 5% of our portfolio. In 2024, we ended at about 8%.

items.statement: Travel vertical EBIT margin at 3.9% for 9 months; adjusted would be 4.1-4.2%.
items.quote: And if you look at our EBIT margin on the travel vertical, we are holding at 3.9%. Now if you look at FY '24 and compare that to FY '25 for the 9-month period, the 3.9% is despite the one -offs that we have seen in the curren t quarter. If I was to adjust for those, you will actually see the margins actually going closer to the 4.1%, 4.2%

items.statement: Sterling Q3 EBITDA margin exceeded threshold at 38.8%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for Q3 FY '25 has exceeded our intended threshold of 30% to 35% to close at 38.8%.

items.statement: Increased prices for Kumbh Mela due to demand outpacing supply.
items.quote: Just to give a case, I mean, look at kumbh, the kind of demand we have seen, where we see an opportunity to put the price up. We've actually done that because the demand was outpacing the supply in some form.

items.statement: Currency fluctuations impacted profitability by INR 60 million in Q3.
items.quote: So that impacted our business and the impact of that was roughly about INR 60 million on our profitability.

items.statement: East Africa sales dropped 30% due to customer bankruptcy.
items.quote: And therefore, their sales have dropped by about 30%.

items.statement: Expansion focus on asset-right model with limited or no capex.
items.quote: Our expansion focus shall continue to be on an asset -right model with limited or no capex investments only to sweat our existing assets for scale.

items.statement: Expects to be back to normal in the coming quarter.
items.quote: So, my expectation is that we will be back to normal in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Expects Q4 tractor industry growth over 15%, full year over 7%.
items.quote: We expect the industry in the Quarter 4 to grow by over 15%, which will take the full year growth to possibly over 7%.

items.quote: it gives us confidence that irrespective of the price points that we are at, we should be able to do a starting initial volume of about 5,000 a month for both the products together.

items.quote: So, we're going to see two things and we'll start bringing this out from Quarter 4, which will be populated numbers. The Auto standalone number will have two components to it and we'll show them to you separately.

items.statement: EV percentage margin will be lower than ICE, but variable margin per unit similar over time.
items.quote: The percentage margin here is going to be lesser than ICE, which you know we've been repeating every time, because the denominator effect. Over a period of time we do expect the variable margin to be in absolute terms similar twice.

items.statement: EV pricing applicable at time of delivery, allowing flexibility to increase prices if costs rise.
items.quote: So, right now it's basically price applicable at the time of delivery, which means that we have the flexibility to take a price up literally when we want.

items.statement: Auto price hikes: 0.7% YTD December, additional 0.8% in January.
items.quote: Price hikes, basically, Auto YTD December, which was about 0.7, and then we have taken another 0.8 in January.

items.statement: 3XO capacity to increase by 1,500-2,000 units within 3-4 months.
items.quote: So, basically, we have a maximum upside of 1500 -2000 on each of these within the current infrastructure.

items.statement: Will not trade off quality for volume; may sell 3,000 instead of 5,000 if needed.
items.quote: So, if we have a doubt and if we don't sell 5000 and we sell 3000, that's fine. We will not trade off the number for the quality.

items.statement: Evaluating international farm operations, completion expected in Q4.
items.quote: We expect to complete that exercise in the 4th Quarter.

items.statement: PLI for MEAL to be booked in MEAL books, timeline depends on milestones.
items.quote: It will be booked finally in MEAL books.

items.statement: No firm timeline for MEAL PLI benefits due to audit and supplier certifications.
items.quote: So, there's no firm timeline because it will depend on us being able to. And most of just to be sure it's not very vague, there is a specific audit that needs to happen for us to be able to feel good that the PLI benefit is accruable.

items.statement: EV bookings open on 14th February at 250+ dealership outlets.
items.quote: So basically, bookings are opening up in 250 plus dealership outlets on 14th February.

items.statement: EVs and ICE to be sold from same showrooms to give customers choice.
items.quote: We want the customer to have a choice between whether they buy our ICE or our EV, which is why consciously we are keeping the showrooms, selling the EVs and the ICE the same.

items.statement: All critical integrating software including BMS owned by MEAL.
items.quote: No, all critical integrating software is owned by us. So, the BMS software is ours, all the zonal architecture, ECU software, all of that is owned by us.

items.statement: CAFE 3 norms may be delayed due to lack of consensus.
items.quote: Theoretically, yes, because there's so much discussion yet and there is no consensus on what exactly it should be.

items.statement: Total price increase taken is about INR100 crores in Q3, progressively going up to 4-4.5% by year-end.
items.quote: So our total price increase that we've taken currently is approximately about INR100 crores in quarter 3, so -- which would -- in percentage terms, Venkat, would be... N. Venkataraman: 2%. Varun Berry: It's about 2%, but it's progressively going up. By the end of the year, we will be at about 4%, 4.5% price increase

items.statement: Cumulative price increase of 6-6.5% planned: 2% in Q3, 2.5% in Q4, 1.5% in Q1 next year.
items.quote: No, there's no hesitation. It is a necessity today. And you're right, exactly right, there will be a 6% price increase. We've already taken in Q3 2%. In Q4, it's going to be another 2.5%. And then in Q1, which is going to be the Q1 of next year, it's going to be another 1.5%. So cumulatively, it's going to be 6%, 6.5% price increase.

items.statement: Cost savings target of 2.5% of revenue for next year, potentially more.
items.quote: We are also doubling down on our cost efficienc ies, as I said. We are planning to make sure, and as I keep repeating every time, these cost efficiencies and cost savings, they start with 0 on the 1st of April, and whatever has been achieved ends with the year, and there are new cost savings that come up every year. So we are again looking at 2.5% for next year, and hopefully even more than that

items.statement: Capex for next year expected at INR150-200 crores, lower than current year.
items.quote: are going to take the capex break, so to say. We have put up plants and we will try and keep it as low as possible. It will still be -- what, Venkat, about INR200 crores? N. Venkataraman: For the next year? Varun Berry: Yes. N. Venkataraman: Should be even lower. Varun Berry: Even lower. So INR150 crores to INR200 crores is what we'll keep it at, unless there is a volume increase

items.statement: Margins expected to stay in current range, no forward-looking forecast given.
items.quote: So we will stay in the current range, I would say. That would be the range that we would look at, although we don't give any forward-looking forecast, but I would say current range is what we would target.

items.statement: Commodity inflation at 11% requires 6.5% price increase to balance absolute profitability.
items.quote: And yes, the 11% inflation that we spoke about in commodities equates itself to 6.5%, it requires to be balanced, it requires 6.5% price increase.

items.statement: Volume growth may be impacted by price increases, but last quarter volume growth was 6.4%.
items.quote: Well, volumes do take a beating when there is a price increase. There is an arbitrage between volumes and revenues. So -- but we've been growing -- actually, if you look at last quarter, we grew at almost 6.4%, it's almost the same as our revenue growth. S o our volume growths were pretty good. Yes, there will be a little bit of arbitrage which will come through, but that's fine. You've got to do

items.statement: Croissant business to cross INR200 crores next year; milk shakes already crossed INR200 crores.
items.quote: I think it's important that we develop these categories and that's what we are seeing. So if you want to look at it, today, our croissant business is -- next year will cross INR200 crores, right. Our milk shakes business has already crossed INR200 crores, right.

items.statement: Employee cost growth to be 0.75 times top line growth.
items.quote: So we focus on making sure that our top line growths, which I must confess that we've not been able to do in the last 2 years, but we -- our principle is that our -- if our top line growth is X, our fixed cost growth or our people cost growth should be 0.75X. And that's what we will keep with, so that we are leveraging our top line growths.

items.statement: Other operating income from incentives expected to be similar to current year.
items.quote: So we estimate that for the coming years, the incentives that we should be able to get, subject to our fulfilling certain conditions that are prescribed under PLI for that, we expect it to be on similar lines as current year.

items.statement: No concern from new large players like Amul or Reliance in biscuits currently.
items.quote: Not really, Abneesh. We haven't seen any signs of worry at this point in time. And if we do see something, we will obviously react at that point in time. But no, at this time -- the brands are also very important, Abneesh. It's very difficult to just come in and work on one element, which is price and get away with it.

items.statement: Focus states contribute 15% of revenue and growing at 1.3-1.4x, driving rural growth.
items.quote: Yes, so Tejash, Vipin this side. So these states basically contributes about 15-odd percent to our overall revenue. And they have been growing at about 1.3 to 1.4x, which means that over a period of time from 12%, 13%, they've moved to 15%, 16%.

items.statement: E-commerce contribution: biscuits 4%, croissant 17%, cake 9%, dairy 11%.
items.quote: So for example, biscuits is 4% as far as e-com is concerned or slightly lower than 4%. But let's say, I'm just giving you 1 or 2 numbers so that you get an idea. For croissant, it's 17%; for cake, it's 9%, right; for dairy, it's 11%.

items.statement: Cost savings expected to beat full-year targets.
items.quote: No, cost savings are going very well for us. In fact, we probably will beat our targets that we've set for ourselves for the full year.

items.statement: Commodity inflation at 11%, would have been 2-4% higher without forward buying.
items.quote: Sugar is flat. Cocoa is at 103% inflation. Laminates is nominal at 3% and corrugated boxes are at 15%. So our inflation for our products that we buy is about 11%. This would have been at least 2% to 4% higher had we not done the forward buying, and we hadn't had that advantage of that forward buying.

items.statement: Capex benefits from new plants and PLI incentives to continue for longer period.
items.quote: No. So capex, most of the capex gains that we get or the benefits that we get are for a much longer period of time. Yes, there are some plants which exhaust their incentives, but there are other plants we've recently put up 3 large facilities, Ranjangaon, UP and in TN, also in Bihar, Bihta, and we've expanded our Orissa facility as well. So there are big incentives there as well.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to trend in the zone of 15.5% to 17.5% going forward.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect our EBITDA margins to remain strong and trend in the zone of 15.5% to 17.5% on the back of continued investments in A&SP.

items.statement: Guides EBITDA margin range of 15.5% to 17.5% with slight bias towards higher end.
items.quote: The guidance that we are giving is in the range of 15.5% to 17.5% with a slight bias towards the higher end of the range.

items.statement: Expects mid to high teens revenue growth.
items.quote: We are looking at mid to high teens kind of growth in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of Rs.15-20 crore; exploring Rs.35-50 crore for Andhra unit expansion.
items.value: Rs.15 to 20 crore; Rs.35 to 50 crore
items.quote: In terms of our CAPEX plans, while maintenance CAPEX will range between Rs.15 to 20 crore, we are exploring making an investment amounting to around Rs.35 to 50 crore for the expansion of our own unit in Andhra Pradesh, housed in our wholly-owned subsidiary, Prag Distillery Private Limited.

items.statement: Maintenance capex approximately Rs.20 crore next year; potential Rs.50 crore for Prag expansion.
items.quote: In terms of the maintenance CAPEX, I have already guided for a maintenance CAPEX for approximately Rs. 20 crore for the next year. There might be a potential investment which we are exploring of around Rs. 50 crore for the expansion of our own unit in Andhra Pradesh, which is Prag Distillery, which would entail expanding our capacity from 6 lakh cases to 36 lakh cases per annum.

items.statement: Took a price correction in Andhra Pradesh to maintain competitive position.
items.quote: On the NSR Front, we had to take a price correction in Andhra Pradesh in order to maintain our competitive position in the state.

items.statement: Blended price correction in Andhra Pradesh around Rs.200 reduction.
items.quote: The price correction in Andhra blended level on a state basis would be around Rs. 200, reduction.

items.statement: Primary volumes grew 14% in January 2025 YoY; expects to continue growth momentum.
items.quote: We believe that this period of transition in Andhra is over and is reflected by the fact that we have started Q4 on a very strong note, having grown primary volumes by 14% in January 2025 on a YoY basis. We now expect to continue this growth momentum going forward.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin stood at 17.7%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q3 FY25 stood at 17.7%.

items.statement: Launched Monarch Legacy Edition luxury brandy; expanding to Goa, Karnataka, Puducherry.
items.quote: A key highlight of the quarter was the successful launch of Monarch Legacy Edition, our first luxury brandy. Monarch blends French grape spirits aged up to 8 years in French oak casks with premium Indian grape spirit from Maharasht ra’s Sahyadri region

items.statement: Expects to kick-start sales of Samsara Gin and Sitara Rum in Q4.
items.quote: We now also expect to kick-start sales of Samsara Gin and Sitara Rum in Q4 on the back of our usership agreement with Spaceman Spirits Lab.

items.statement: Remains vigilant about ENA price trends; overall cost environment favorable.
items.quote: With softening cost pressures on raw materials and packaging, our premiumization strategy is expected to continue to support margins. While we remain vigilant about ENA price trends, the overall cost environment has been favorable, strengthening our profitability outlook.

items.statement: Reduced gross debt by Rs.47 crore; gross debt now Rs.45 crore with net cash Rs.31 crore.
items.value: Rs.47 crore; Rs.45 crore; Rs.31 crore
items.quote: On the debt front, I am happy to share that in Q3, we have reduced our gross debt by Rs.47 crore. This reduction in gross debt was predominantly on account of full repayment of Kotak Bank term loan. Our aggregate gross debt now stands at Rs.45 crore with net cash balance of Rs.31 crore.

items.statement: Expects tax incidence from Q1 next year at normal rate of 25%.
items.quote: I think we had guided for that either, we may have tax incid ence from first quarter of next year which would be at a normal rate of 25

items.statement: Expects further subsidy in Q4; difficult to quantify amount.
items.quote: We do expect further subsidy to be received in Q4, but it will be difficult at this point to quantify the amount.

items.statement: A&SP reinvestment rates range 1% to 1.5-1.7% of net revenue; expects to increase.
items.quote: So, our A&SP reinvestment rates range anywhere between 1% to 1.5-1.7%, depending upon the quarter. We end up doing more A&SP spends during the peak seasons as such.

items.statement: Aims to deliver mid to high teens EBITDA margin.
items.quote: we have –communicated in the road shows which we have done, we aim to be deliver mid to high teens of EBITDA. That is what the team will keep on working to ensure this is what we want to deliver..

items.statement: Aims to maintain gross margin in 35% to 40% range.
items.quote: Our aim is to maintain a gross margin in the range of 35% to 40%. And blended, we are achieving 39.8% in the first 9 months, which is a good performance.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR800 million for FY25-26.
items.quote: I think in last call, Parikshit, we talked about $8 million to $10 million or about roughly INR800 million of capex that we plan.

items.statement: Order backlog of INR107.8 billion as of December 2024, up 72% from March.
items.quote: Our order backlog stood at INR107.8 billion as at December '24 versus INR62.7 billion as at March, up by 72%.

items.quote: Excluding that, we have order book of about INR52 billion in the 9 months which gives almost INR17 billion as a run rate every quarter. So, our endeavour is to maintain that, and we are working towards that.

items.statement: Sees sustained project pipeline over next 12-18 months, including HVDC.

items.statement: Pricing power expected to remain stable for next 12-18 months due to supply chain and raw material costs.
