items.statement: Varietal shift: Dhampur 75% 238, 25% others; Rajpura 65% 238, 35% others.
items.quote: So if I talk about both the plants individually, in Dhampur, we are hoping that 75 will still stay in 238, 25 will go to others, 118 and everything else. Rajpura, it will be about 65 will go to 238 and 35 will be for other seeds.

items.statement: Dividend or buyback options open, to be examined after March.
items.quote: See, as far as that goes, I mean, we all are pretty healthy. Our balance sheet is very, very healthy as of now. There is enough sufficient gap, but we will have to examine it after March is out exactly as to how much we would like to do vis-a-vis dividend or buyback. So both options are open as of now.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth next year.
items.quote: See, this year, Vivek here, this year the guidance we have given for double-digit revenue growth. Looking at our first nine months performance and looking at how this quarter has started, we believe that will be a repeat next year, a double-digit revenue growth for next year.

items.statement: OBD-II Phase-B will cause a marginal price increase of 1-2% across the industry.
items.quote: As far as the price is concerned, there's going to be a marginal price increase of 1% - 2% because of the additional hardware that would be installed in the products and that would be valid across the industry.

items.statement: Industry demand expected to improve from Q4 with wedding season and festivals.
items.quote: As we move into Q4 and with the wedding season that's coming up and the festives that kind of kick in from March onwards, we expect that the industry will just keep on improving from here.

items.statement: Rural demand momentum expected to continue next financial year.
items.quote: We expect the momentum to continue going forward in the next financial year as well.

items.statement: EV portfolio to become PLI compliant next fiscal.
items.quote: And in the next fiscal, you'll see the whole portfolio coming into the PLI compliance.

items.statement: ICE margin contraction due to higher festive marketing spends, expected to reverse.
items.quote: Yes, because this quarter there was higher spends because of the festive, right. So, we had higher support on marketing and advertisement spends on our power brands. And I think that was the reason why there was a contraction.

items.statement: EV market share to improve from February and March after V2 transition.
items.quote: So that will reflect in the market share by the end of Feb and that too by the end of March.

items.statement: NBFCs serving bottom of pyramid seeing uptick in delinquencies.
items.quote: There hasn't been a pullback on the willing ness to lend, but certainly in terms of the collections, I think most of the NBFCs who serve the bottom of the pyramid in some parts of it are having a little bit of uptick on the delinquencies

items.statement: Hero FinCorp credit cost close to 6%.
items.quote: Broadly, I can tell you the credit cost is currently close to 6%, right.

items.statement: Hero FinCorp loan book increased 13% year-on-year.
items.quote: So, first of all on HFCL Q3, the loan book size is ₹55,500 which is an increase of 13% versus last year, right.

items.statement: Interim dividend of ₹100 per share declared.
items.quote: I am happy to share that the Company has declared an interim dividend of ₹100 per share.

items.statement: EBITDA per unit crossed ₹10,000.
items.quote: Our EBITDA per unit remarkably has crossed now ₹10,000 per unit, driven by premiumization, mix and judicious pricing, which aug urs well as we expand our v olume given the operating leverage it will generate

items.statement: Market share expanded by 520 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 32.8%.
items.quote: As per Vahan, our market share for the quarter expanded by 520 basis point s quarter-on-quarter to 32.8

items.statement: EV investment in Q3 was ₹137 crores.
items.quote: During the quarter, after taking into account the investments behind EV business, ₹137 crores, the overall EBITDA margin improved by 50 basis to 14.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Parts, accessories, and merchandise revenue highest ever at ₹1,555 crores.
items.quote: The Company also reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue from parts, accessories and merchandise business at ₹1,555 crores, year-on-year growth of 9%.

items.statement: Next 12 months, produce hot metal of 7 lakh tons and saleable pig iron about 6 lakh or 5,70,000 tons.
items.value: 7 lakh tons hot metal, 6 lakh or 5,70,000 tons saleable pig iron
items.quote: forward, we are looking that next 12 months, we should be able to produce hot metal of 7 lakh tons and saleable pig iron should come to about 6 lakh ton or 5,70,000 tons, so which Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Limited 5 February 2025 will increase, but there have been some headwinds, But otherwise, I see this progress happening in coming

items.statement: Casting volumes expected to reach 1,40,000 tons this year against 1,26,000-1,28,000 last year.
items.quote: As on date, the volumetric growth is 9%. We have sold 1 lakh ton till date, should expect, if we do well, going towards 1,40,000 tons against 1,26,000 or 1,28,000 tons last year.

items.statement: Tube volumes expected to reach 2 lakh metric tons next year, with Baramati 1,50,000 and Ahmednagar 40,000-45,000.
items.value: 2 lakh metric tons total, 1,50,000 Baramati, 40,000-45,000 Ahmednagar
items.quote: And I definitely look forward to producing and selling 1,50,000 ton next year, and Ahmed nagar contributing anywhere between 40,000 to 45,000. So we can look forward to tube volumes of 2 lakh metric ton next year for the whole year.

items.statement: Casting volumes for FY26 expected at 1,70,000-1,75,000 tons, including Oliver 15,000 and existing 1,60,000.
items.quote: I think it could be maybe about 1,75,000, 1,70,000 kind of numbers. We are yet to finalize the plans, but that's the kind of numbers I look forward for the next year.

items.statement: Casting volumes next year expected beyond 1,70,000 tons, with average 14,500-15,000 tons per month.
items.quote: And I think there is a good support, and that's why I am thinking that the next y ear, we should look for volume beyond 1,70,000 for the whole year.

items.statement: Capex for next year expected INR500-600 crores, including INR200 crores for renewable energy.
items.quote: I expect in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores would be the capex, out of which INR200 crores would be the renewable energy.

items.statement: Plan to add 70-80 MW equivalent renewable capacity in next 1 year with capex about INR200 crores.
items.quote: And otherwise, I would say that we are looking forward to add another 70 megawatt equivalent in next 1 year time. So about 25 megawatt of wind will mean 50 megawatt of solar plus 30 megawatt of solar, about another 70 to 80 megawatt equivalent in the next 1-year time.

items.statement: Expect benefit from reduced coking coal prices and increased use of own iron ore in coming months and quarters.
items.quote: One is because of reduced coking coal prices quarter -on-quarter because of the reducing coking coal prices. Typically, we have 3 months inventory, so we get delayed benefit by 3 months. Also, we have started operating Bharat Mines, and we are gradually increasing the consumption or utilization of our own iron ore. That should also benefit in the coming months and quarters.

items.statement: Pig iron prices have bottomed out; no immediate major increase expected.
items.quote: So though we don't see any immediate major increase in the pig iron prices, but we expect to get some benefit of reduced cost coming on account of two things.

items.statement: Improvement seen in almost all sectors from January, February onwards; better demand forecast from casting, tractor, earthmoving, and commercial vehicle.
items.quote: Over to the next quarter, we are seeing some improvement in almost all the sectors from January, February onwards, better demand forecast from the casting, from the tractor industry as well as earthmoving equipment and commercial ve hicle also, schedules are better compared to the last 2 quarters.

items.statement: Expect at least 20% growth in commercial vehicle volumes over next couple of months.
items.quote: I expect, over the next couple of months, growth of at least 20%.

items.statement: Oliver to start giving volumes from Q1 of next financial year; expect 1,000-1,500 tons per month within a quarter or two.
items.quote: And also we have started trial production and sample supplies from Oliver and we expect that from the month of February and March, we should be able to start ramping up of the production and sales and Oliver should start giving us the volumes from quarter 1 of next financial year.

items.statement: Second iron ore mine in Chitradurga not going to become operational due to reserve forest; will take couple of years.
items.quote: And the second iron ore mine, which is in Chitradurga , is not going to come and it will take some more time. That mine has gone into the reserve forest or wildlife reserve forest, and it's not going to become operational.

items.statement: Plan to list KFIL on NSE as early as possible; work in progress.
items.quote: This is the question I just put it to Mr. Srivatsan. It is work in progress. We are focused. We'll try to take it to NSE as early as possible.

items.statement: Expects 10-15% growth, with long-term CAGR of 20%.
items.quote: So, depending on how the markets open up, if China markets stabilize and prices go up, so the growth may be high, but otherwise 10% to 15% is what bare minimum we are expecting.

items.statement: Pharma revenue expected around Rs. 1,150-1,200 crores.
items.quote: So, pharma will be, now we are expecting around Rs 1,150 to Rs. 1,200 crores for the pharma.

items.statement: Medical devices revenue expected around Rs. 470-475 crores.
items.quote: So, maybe we add another Rs. 80- Rs. 85 crore. So, Rs. 470-Rs. 475 crore is what we are expecting for the medical devices to close.

items.statement: Exports expected to cross Rs. 650-700 crores.
items.quote: So, this itself is the highest ever in the Morepen history that in nine months you have done Rs. 500 crores, we will be easily crossing Rs. 650 to Rs. 700 crore exports.

items.statement: Formulation and OTC business expected to grow at least 25%.
items.quote: Formulation business, formulation and OTC taken together is around Rs. 300 crores. So, we are seeing at least a growth of 25% there.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected between 11-12%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin I would say is between 10 to 11 because now it is 10.72 for 9 months. So, I would say 11 to 12.

items.statement: Medical device facility civil work complete; screen printing plant started; BP and glucose capacity expanded.
items.quote: So, I am happy to share that all the civil work of the medical device facility is complete and we are shared the photographs in the presentation.

items.statement: Share of medical devices in overall revenue increased to 29% and expected to keep increasing.
items.quote: Last year it was 26%. Now it has become 29% for the nine months. And we hope that it will keep on increasing as we go forward, because the rate of growth of medical devices may be higher than the rate of growth on the API business or the Pharma Generic Business.

items.statement: Chinese raw material prices have started increasing, which may lead to higher selling prices after a transition quarter.
items.quote: And now they have started raising the prices, which is a healthy sign that, there is a shortage of raw materials now. And of course, the market has not responded as yet. It may be one quarter transition that we may get an upside in the selling prices also, but that's a good sign that, okay, we do not see much price drop anymore.

items.statement: US market slow, European market up 55%, Chinese prices stabilizing.
items.quote: So, those are the two main updates that US market is slow, European market is up and Chinese prices are stabilizing.

items.statement: Margin decline due to raw material price increases not yet passed on to finished product prices.
items.quote: The broader level is that the prices of the raw materials have started increasing and the prices of the finished product have not increased. So, the margin has temporarily been reduced because the market has not responded to an increase in the prices.

items.statement: Launched weight management products under LightLife brand; response to be updated next quarter.
items.quote: We had launched a product, LightLife, which is for weight management. And it's a big category, $23 billion category. We have launched two products here.

items.statement: Launched two new Rx products: Ticaspan and UdoFix.
items.quote: Then coming to the Rx products, we have launched two more products in Rx. Ticaspan which is ticagrelor, which is antiplatelet like blood thinners that is used at the time of heart attack and strokes is used mostly in the hospitals. And UDCA which is our brand name is UdoFix.

items.statement: Promoters to contribute to new subsidiary; Morepen share cannot be reduced.
items.quote: When you say 80:20 basically, the company has been incorporated in a way that, okay, promoters and the both have to contribute equally. So, if promoters do not contribute, their share will go down. If companies do not contribute, company share will go down. But we have put up a condition in the shareholder agreement that Morepen share cannot be reduced.

items.statement: Full-year steel pipe volume expected around 8.8-8.9 lakh tons.
items.quote: Till now, we have done 6.2 lakh tons net and in Q4, it is expected that we will do 2.65 lakh tons. So, we will not cross 9 lakhs tons. We will do around 8.8 lakh to 8.9 lakh tons in the entire year.

items.statement: FY26 steel pipe volume target 12 lakh tons.
items.quote: So, we should not face much difficulty in making 12 lakh tons for next year.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton target ₹7,000 over next 2 years.
items.quote: Yes. Yes, after all this, as you said earlier, our EBITDA per ton target is ₹7,000 over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA expected around ₹590-600 crores.
items.quote: And we will do EBITDA of around ₹590-₹600 crores for the full fiscal year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA expected around ₹200 crores.
items.quote: To do this, I think in Q4, we will do EBITDA of ₹200 crores as a whole.

items.statement: Lighting division to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin.
items.quote: In the lighting division, there will be a double digit EBITDA margin, it will be 10% plus.

items.statement: Lighting full-year revenue to grow double-digit.
items.quote: Looking forward, we remain optimistic about the business roadmap and we are confident in delivering double-digit revenue growth for the full fiscal year in lighting.

items.statement: Investing ₹25 crores in domestic wire business at Gwalior.
items.quote: And also, we are investing ₹25 crores at our Gwalior facility in lighting division to set up a state-of-art domestic wire business unit of specified size and categories.

items.statement: Hindupur capex increased from ₹75 crores to ₹125 crores.
items.quote: At our Hindupur facility, we are increasing capex from ₹75 crores to ₹125 crores to expand production by almost 200,000 ton s per annum, focusing on large diameter (8 to 20 inch), DFT Mill and coated pipes for water line projects and infrastructure projects as well

items.statement: Steel pipe order book about ₹600 crores.
items.quote: We currently have order book of about ₹600 crores in hand for oil and gas sector, water sector and export business.

items.statement: JJM extended to 2028, providing 3-3.5 years of demand.

items.statement: Steel prices at 5-year low, further declines unlikely.
items.quote: Steel prices are at almost 5 years level low and further declines are unlikely, providing a stable cost environment.

items.statement: Value-added products contributed 45% of steel revenue.
items.quote: Value-added product s (API, spiral and galvanized pipes ) contributed almost 45% of total revenue for both Q3 FY '25 and Nine-month FY '25

items.statement: US tariff policies prevented potential double-digit export growth.
items.quote: Export sales remained unchanged year-on-year, but globally trade uncertainties and reservations around US tariff policies prevented a potential double-digit growth.

items.statement: Expects health loss ratio around 72, not returning to 65-66.
items.quote: No, given the employer-employee group L, so one can reasonably expect it to be around 72 or so, but I don't see that going back to about 65 or 66.

items.statement: Expects to continue to do well over ensuing quarters.
items.quote: We expect to continue to do well over the ensuing quarters.

items.statement: Motor composition reduced to 64% YTD from 65.9% previous year.
items.quote: As of December, YTD, the composition of motor in the overall premium has reduced to about 64% as against 65.9% in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Within motor, composition: 41.2% cars, 42.9% CVs, 15.8% two-wheelers.
items.quote: Within motor, now the company has a composition of 41.2% in cars, 42.9% in CVs, and 15.8% in two-wheelers.

items.statement: 28% of total motor premium from new vehicles.
items.quote: The company gets about 28% of its total motor premium from new vehicles.

items.statement: Entered two large OEM car programs in current quarter.
items.quote: In the current quarter, the company entered two large OEM car programs and businesses commenced in these programs.

items.statement: EOM higher due to 1/n method and product mix changes.
items.quote: The EOM for Chola MS in Q3 was rendered higher because of the 1 /n method change and product mix changes.

items.statement: Committed to Board-approved glide path presented to regulator.
items.quote: The company stays committed to stick to the glide path approved by the Board and presented to the regulator.

items.statement: Technology spend Rs. 92 crores in 9M FY25 vs Rs. 70 crores prior period.
items.quote: In the nine months ended December 24, the company expended Rs. 92 crores towards technology spend as against Rs. 70 crores in the corresponding period, which also had marginal influence on the EOM ratio.

items.statement: Claims ratio 72.6 vs 74.5 in Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Fengal Cyclone impacted company in quarter.

items.statement: Natcat events impacted 9M claims ratio by 0.7%.
items.quote: The combined effect of Natcat events on the claims ratio for the nine months ended December is about 0.7%.

items.statement: Combined ratio 111.7% in Q3; without 1/n effect 108.9% vs 110.3% prior year.
items.quote: The combined ratio for the quarter was 111.7%. If one were to look at it without the 1/n effect, it was 108.9% and compares well with 110.3% of corresponding quarter.

items.statement: YTD combined ratio without 1/n effect 109.4% vs 110.4% prior period.
items.quote: Likewise, the YTDC combined ratio without 1 /n effect was 109.4 % as against 110.4 % in corresponding period.

items.statement: Price increase in one health product from October, another from January 2025.
items.quote: Some of our products, we had a price increase in one of the products coming in from October and in one of the products, we have the division is coming in from January 2025.

items.statement: May take cautious call on high-cost channels/products for EOM compliance.
items.quote: From a company's point of view, if there are certain high-cost channels at this point in time are high -cost products, however profitable they may be, we may need to take a more cautious call keeping the EOM compliance in mind.

items.statement: Cost reduction target of approximately INR200 crores over 18 months, with significant savings in first 12 months.
items.quote: And the cost down thing that we are working on is a pretty large target of approximately INR200 crores over a 18-month period with significant savings coming within the first 12 months.

items.statement: AC cost down to kick in fully by March.
items.quote: Yes, sir, it will kick in fully by March.

items.statement: Refrigerator plant expected to reach 35,000-40,000 units per month by April and PBT breakeven by June.
items.quote: And hopefully, by April, we should be at about 35,000 to 40,000 a month. And hopefully, by June, we should be close to PBT breakeven.

items.statement: Up to Q2 FY26, 15-30% of cost reduction to come; 100% realization by end of FY26.
items.quote: Yes. Sir, up to quarter 2 of financial year '26, 15% to 30% reduction will come and 100% realization will happen by end of FY '26. But the annualized impact will come only after that.

items.statement: If all cost reduction measures implemented, close to INR200 crores will come.
items.quote: Yes. If we implement everything, then close to INR200 crores will come.

items.statement: Margin drop primarily due to fall in washer sales; if washer sales met target, margin would have been better.
items.quote: If you see the margin drop, the margin drop is -- primarily the main reason for the margin drop is washer sales. If washer sales stayed as per target, the margin would have been better.

items.statement: Washer sales should be back on track; January was not good, but hope February and March will be good.
items.quote: Now we believe that washer sales should be back on track, but January was not back on track. January was not good. But we hope February and March will be good.

items.statement: AC capacity of about 500,000 a year should be sold; considering capacity enhancement for next year.
items.quote: Now our capacity is about 500,000 a year. And if we are close to that, therefore, next year, we have to think.

items.statement: Top load market much bigger than front load; internal assessment suggests potential to do 50,000-60,000 units per month vs current 30,000-32,000.
items.quote: So if you look at that, our internal assessment tells us there is no reason why we should not do 50,000, 60,000 a month versus today's present about 30,000 a month -- 30,000, 32,000 a month.

items.statement: Material cost reduction of about INR140 crores; logistics cost about INR20 crores; total breakup of INR200 crores with INR160-170 crores identified.
items.value: INR140 crores, INR20 crores, INR160 crores to INR170 crores
items.quote: The material cost will be about INR140 crores. On that, the weight reduction and then the electronics sourcing and then the benchmarking with other competition and taking ideas from that should reduce the material cost by INR140 crores. The logistics cost about [INR20 crores 0:23:24] so we have got a clear breakup of INR200 crores. Out of INR200 crores, we have got about INR160 crores to INR170 cr

items.statement: Industrial washing machine margin over 18% in December and January, but sales fallen.
items.quote: But in industrial, our margin has gone up, but the sales has also fallen. But the margin has gone to over 18% in the month of December and January.

items.statement: Brand and product campaign for washer, AC, and refrigerators to launch in next 2 weeks, pan-India with focus on top 10 states.
items.quote: We are going to come out with the brand and the product campaign maybe in the next 2 weeks, both for washer and for AC and for refrigerators.

items.statement: Refrigerator plant capacity about 1.1 million per year; PBT breakeven at 50% utilization.
items.quote: About 1 million. About 1 million per year. Yes. 1.1 million...

items.statement: AC volumes for FY25 will be below earlier guidance of 4-5 lakh units.
items.quote: And looking at February, March, we will be below our overall thing that we had given earlier.

items.statement: From now till June, AC capacity will be near full.

items.statement: Next year, AC segment EBIT margins could be near 4-5%.
items.quote: Yes, we could be near that.

items.statement: Company is trying to take AC prices up and will not pass on cost reductions.

items.statement: Compressor supply covered till May-June; no shortage foreseen.
items.quote: Compressors from China, there are some issues to some manufacturers in India. But I think we are covered up till May and June. We have already placed the orders.

items.statement: Company is selling more 2-tonne inverter ACs.
items.quote: And we are trying to take prices up and sell more of 2-tonne inverter and all of that.

items.statement: Stuck with washer inventory due to sudden slowdown; may launch customer schemes in select markets.
items.quote: We are looking into that, yes. We may do that. Again, that to in select markets, not across the board.

items.quote: So it's 300 and 180, let's say.

items.quote: If it's done by us, it comes to around INR20-odd lakhs approximately.

items.statement: Restructuring to consolidate roles; E&Y finance transformation to conclude in 2 weeks.
items.quote: So I think we will restructure this. We are using E&Y for a finance transformation thing and we will come up with this within the next 2 weeks.

items.statement: CEO search for Home Appliances division ongoing; hope to close soon.
items.quote: And that is taking some time, but I hope to close it soon.

items.statement: Launched 4-year warranty on refrigerators, first in market.
items.quote: We are the first ones to offer a 4-year warranty on refrigerator. And that has created a noise in the market.

items.statement: AC business is EBITDA positive, moved from negative.
items.quote: Yes, it's EBITDA positive. From negative, we have moved to EBITDA positive in...

items.statement: Depreciation increased by INR6 crores due to lease and fixed asset additions.
items.quote: Depreciation cost for the quarter has increased by INR6 crores as compared to corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Expects 15% YoY export growth, with orders in hand to execute.
items.quote: As mentioned in my earlier quarter speeches also in exports front, on a year-on-year, we are still expecting growth of 15%. Fortunately, we already have orders in hand, which we have to execute.

items.statement: Indiannica revenue projected between Rs.65 crores and Rs.70 crores.
items.quote: So this year, the revenue projection that we have for Indiannica is between Rs.65 crores to Rs.70 crores business.

items.statement: Indiannica PAT guidance of Rs.2 crores to Rs.3 crores.
items.quote: So PAT is about negative Rs.27 crores. And guidance is about, I think, Rs.2 crores to Rs.3 crores we will make in PAT.

items.statement: Publication margins expected at 27% to 28% for full year.
items.quote: So as far as publication business is concerned, our margins will end at around 27% to 28% for the full year.

items.statement: Publication margins expected around 30-odd percentages next year.
items.quote: And next year, because we are expecting better revenue growth, that margin should be around 30-odd percentages.

items.statement: Stationery overall margin expected 10% to 11% this year.
items.quote: As far as the stationery business overall is concerned, our margin this year may come to around between 10% and 11%.

items.statement: Stationery margins expected to return to 13% to 14% next year.
items.quote: But next year, when we see domestic also doing quite well in terms of revenue, that time we should come back to our original margins of stationery between 13% and 14%.

items.statement: Plans to spend around Rs.150 crores in stationery business over next 3 years.
items.quote: Of this year, I would have guided that in next 3 years, we shall be spending around Rs.150 crores in the business.

items.statement: Anticipates gradual recovery in Q4 FY25 for domestic stationery as distributors restock.
items.quote: However, with paper prices stabilizing rather a little bit on upward movement, we anticipate a gradual recovery in Q4 '25 as distributors and retailers have already regained confidence in restocking the inventory.

items.statement: Confident of 15% volume growth in domestic stationery for Q4, with additional Rs.25-30 crores business.

items.statement: Publication business expected to grow at least 12% YoY next year.
items.quote: In publication business, we are very sure of at least growing by 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Paper prices stabilized, may increase up to April; stable prices help industry.

items.statement: Plans to introduce newer stationery categories in domestic market in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: So I assure you that in next 2 to 3 quarters, you will also start seeing newer category being introduced in domestic market.

items.statement: US antidumping duty may benefit short-term but not long-term due to adjustments.
items.quote: So there would be short-term benefit, but there can't be long-term benefit because of this decision of the US.

items.statement: Launched Navneet AI for teachers, expected to enhance demand for physical books and digital content.
