items.statement: Expects results from long-term partnerships either this quarter or the next.
items.quote: I wouldn’t say 2, 3, or 4 quarters—I would be expecting results either this quarter or the next.

items.statement: AUM growth trend expected to continue in coming quarters.
items.quote: As a result, despite regulatory interventions, our AUM continues to grow, and we expect this trend to continue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Focus on scaling with sensible unit economics and tech efficiency over next 12-18 months.
items.quote: So I think these are the two big themes that you should expect for us, you know, at least over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: AI-driven code expected to rise to 70-75% in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect this number to rise to 70 -75% in the coming quarters, allowing us to move even faster while keeping our team compact.

items.statement: Secured sanctions worth close to ₹81 crores, drawn down approximately ₹27.5 crores so far.
items.quote: We have successfully secured sanctions worth close to ₹81 crores, of which we have drawn down approximately ₹27.5 crores so far.

items.statement: Anticipates further drawdowns in coming quarters.
items.quote: Of course, we anticipate further drawdowns in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Capital not a constraint; focus on right investors and price to maintain positive ROE.
items.quote: As you pointed out in the presentation, fortunately for us, capital doesn't seem to be a constraint at this stage. The biggest thing we want to solve for right now is ensuring that we take capital from the right set of people at the right price.

items.statement: Focus on unsecured lending for ticket sizes below ₹2 lakhs.
items.quote: Our focus is definitely in the unsecured lending space, specifically for ticket sizes below ₹2 lakhs.

items.statement: Will not chase growth if lack confidence; prioritize high-quality long-term loan book.
items.quote: Our primary objective is to build a high-quality, long-term loan book. We will never push for growth if we lack confidence in a particular area.

items.statement: Provisioning this quarter was high due to maturing loan portfolio.
items.quote: One of the things you'll see is that from a provisioning standpoint, the provisioning done in this quarter is quite high. The reason for thi s is that the loan portfolio is maturing as well.

items.statement: Impairment increased because AUM increased, requiring more provisioning.
items.quote: So, see, our loan book has also increased, right? So that's one prime reason why you'll see an increase in our impairment as a function of the absolute amount.

items.statement: Expanded AUM through term loans rather than direct personal loans.
items.quote: We have expanded our AUM through term loans rather than issuing large-scale personal loans directly to end customers.

items.statement: Goal to establish deeper co-lending and BC partnerships with NBFCs.
items.quote: Our ultimate goal is to establish deeper DC and co-lending partnerships with NBFCs.

items.statement: AUM stands at ₹85 crores, nearly double same quarter last year.
items.quote: In fact, this quarter, our AUM stands at ₹85 crores, which is nearly double what it was in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: About 55% of code is AI-driven currently.
items.quote: Currently, about 55% of the code that goes into our system is AI -driven.

items.statement: Team of 30 people expected to remain same for near future.
items.quote: As you can see, we’ve always done all this with a compac t team of just 30 people, and we expect that to remain the same for the near future.

items.statement: Guided EBITDA margin range of 11% plus minus 50 basis points for this year, factoring in startup costs.
items.quote: So, those costs are baked into our assumptions and this year we have guided for our EBITDA margin range of 11% plus minus 50 basis points and those guidance factors in that startup cost as well.

items.statement: Board approved CAPEX of Rs. 72 crores for aluminum die casting plant expansion in Hosur from 11,000 to 15,000 metric tons per annum.
items.quote: Consequently, the Board has approved a CAPEX of Rs. 72 crores for the expansion of the aluminum die casting plant in Hosur from 11,000 tons per annum to 15,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Expanding four-wheel alloy wheel facility in Bawal by additional 30K capacity, commissioning in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: We are expanding our four-wheel alloy wheel facility in Bawal by additional 30K capacity scheduled for commissioning in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Construction of new Greenfield plant at IMT Kharkhoda with capacity of 120K wheels per month and 2 million alloy wheel plant at Supa, Maharashtra progressing as planned.
items.value: 120 K wheels per month and 2 million
items.quote: Additionally, the construction of a new Greenfield plant at IMT Kharkhoda with a capacity of 120 K wheels per month and a 2 million alloy wheel plant for the two-wheeler segment at Supa, Maharashtra is progressing as planned.

items.statement: Expansion project in Indonesia to be commissioned in phases starting from Q4 FY26.
items.quote: As announced last quarter, the implementation of our expansion project in Indonesia has begun and is expected to be commissioned in phases starting from Q4 FY26

items.statement: Consolidation of four-wheeler switch plant from Manesar to Farukhnagar expected to be completed by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: The consolidation of our four-wheeler switch plant from Manesar to Farukhnagar is progressing as planned and is expected to be completed by Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Enhanced capacity at Hosur expected to commence in phases from Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The enhanced capacity is expected to commence in phases from Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Optimistic on medium to long term outlook of domestic auto industry.
items.quote: We remain very optimistic on medium to long term outlook of domestic auto industry.

items.statement: Expect positive impact on two-wheeler and PV segment from budget tax savings.
items.quote: So, considering all those aspect, we do hope and expect that this Rs. 1 lakh crore of annual money which is coming in people’s hands, good quantum should come to the automotive industry and hence should have positive friction on the two-wheeler and PV segment both.

items.statement: Expect to get out of 11% margin range in next couple of years as projects stabilize.
items.quote: So, we do expect to get out of this 11% range in next couple of years because we still have a lot of products as you spoke a lot of projects, almost 12 projects which are under construction and they will ••iilt•)i MINDA I -----.::>-•- ·~ - "T" l-<I - .... . vv-- operational in next 12-18 months and they do tend to dilute the margins for initial couple of

items.statement: Expect margin improvement in medium term as startup costs are behind.
items.quote: But to your point, whether should we have 50-100 basis point margin improvement in next in the medium term, absolutely why not and that has been our endeavor and we just spoke about once we will commission all these operating plants under construction, it should help in terms of improving our margins because a lot of this startup cost, which we are expecting in next year or two should be behind us

items.statement: Secured new export order for seating with peak annual value of Rs. 70 crores.
items.quote: Moving to seating business about quantification of this business, the business is roughly around Rs. 70 crores of peak annual value in terms of sales.

items.statement: Expect growth in seating business from new OEM customer with 4 model launches and e-two-wheeler volumes.
items.quote: As you progress into subsequent quarter, we anticipate boosting revenues from a ramp up of volumes of a newly added OEM customer driven by 4 new model launches by them, increased volume from e-two-wheeler OEMs and the commencement of supply of pneumatic suspended seat.

items.statement: European market headwinds impacting seating exports, down 18% year-on-year.
items.quote: While domestic business demonstrated steady growth, the export segment faced headwinds due to a downtrend in the European market, particularly impacting one of our key customers. Overall export for seating year-on-year is lower by around 18%.

items.statement: European auto industry downturn adversely impacting Clarton Horn acoustics business.
items.quote: While India acoustic business remains stable, our European subsidiary, Clarton Horn was adversely impacted by downward trend in the European auto industry.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of 0.75 per share, 37.5% of face value.
items.quote: Happy to inform, the board has also approved and declared interim dividend of 0.75 per share which is 37.5% of face value reflecting a commitment from the Company to return value to shareholders on a consistent basis.

items.statement: Aiming to reach at least last financial year's presales; may do better if additional Bangalore launches occur.
items.quote: And hence, because of that, I think we ’ll be, we are currently aiming at reaching at least what we have done last financial year in terms of presales. And if we can do that, that would be a good outcome for us.

items.statement: Expects to recognize remaining revenue over next 3 to 4 years, roughly ₹1,000 crores per quarter.
items.quote: That would be roughly about ₹1,000 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Steady-state PBT margin expected at 15% to 18% after corporate overhead, interest, and depreciation.
items.quote: So Kunal, if corporate overhead plus interest plus depreciation, will be removed , so with the PBT level, we should be within range of 15% to 18% steady state going forward.

items.statement: Margins should start improving from Q4 and be far better next financial year.
items.quote: So from Q4, we should start looking at slightly better margin. And also from next financial year, it should be far better.

items.statement: Revenue yet to be recognized has 28% PBT margin at project level.
items.quote: And if we are able to do that and, which I was mentioning, it’s about 28% of PBT at the project level.

items.statement: Incurred ₹1,241 million capex in 9M FY25, up 46.54% YoY.
items.quote: We have incurred ₹1,241 million under capex during 9 months, which is 46.54% more compared to same period last year to support increased area under construction on back of the new launches.

items.statement: Spent ₹6.33 billion net land outflow in 9M FY25, more than 2x YoY.
items.quote: In 9 months, we spent ₹6.33 billion in net land outflow, which is more than 2x of same period last year, in line with our commitment of deploying growth capital.

items.statement: Projected margin cash flow from ongoing and forthcoming residential projects is ₹171.13 billion.
items.quote: As on 31st December, we have unsold inventory of 8.92 million square feet and under forthcoming project s at 21.22 million square feet, the projected margin cash flow from ongoing and forthcoming residential projects stands at ₹ 171.13 billion.

items.statement: Revenue yet to be recognized from sold units is about ₹15,000 crores.
items.quote: On the visibility to our revenue and profitability, the real estate revenue yet to be recognized from already sold units stands at about ₹15,000 crores.

items.statement: Demand strong in cities; sweet spot ticket size ₹2-3 crores in Bangalore, ₹5-6 crores in Gurgaon.
items.quote: Like, for example, in Bangalore, the sweet spot is between ₹2-₹3 crores, and if it’s in Gurgaon, it is about ₹5-₹6 crores. If we are able to be within that range, probably our sale velocity can be really good.

items.statement: NRI demand typically 8% to 10% and unchanged in recent quarters.
items.quote: So, and typically, our NRI demand has been in the range of about 8% to 10%. And largely, that remains unchanged in the last few quarters.

items.statement: Average realization increased from ₹7,500 to nearly ₹14,000 per sq ft due to pricing and mix shift.
items.quote: The price on an average, if you look at, yes, it’s, right from about 5 to 6 years ago, where we were at about ₹ 7,500, now we are almost reaching ₹ 14,000.

items.statement: Descoped civil and glazing contracts caused one-time losses, reducing margins this quarter.
items.quote: As I had mentioned in my previous calls, we are reducing our emphasis on the civil contracts and some of the other contracts related to glazing and in fact, descoped some of the projects this quarter. Hence, we had to account for additional expenses towards the same and that reflects in our lower margins this quarter.

items.statement: Planning to reduce debt by close to ₹900 crores from rights issue proceeds.
items.quote: From the proceeds of the rights issue, we are planning to reduce debt of close to ₹900 crores.

items.statement: Comfortable with absolute debt between ₹1,200 crores to ₹1,500 crores in medium term.
items.quote: Well, it’s not about debt to equity, Puneet. What we currently in the near, or, let’s say, medium term, what we are comfortable is between ₹1,200 crores to ₹1,500 crores.

items.statement: Contracts and manufacturing segment may stabilize at ₹450-500 crores yearly revenue with over 15% gross margins.
items.quote: Our c ontracts and manufacturing segment had a revenue of about ₹160 crores in this quarter, and we might stabilize at a cumulative revenue of about ₹450 crores to ₹500 crores on a yearly basis with gross margins of over net 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain in 2.3% to 2.5% range in future.
items.quote: Okay. So, we had been talking about an EBITDA between 2.3% to 2.5%. We still feel that can be the trend as we move into the future.

items.statement: Steady-state working capital range should be 35 to 40 days.
items.quote: We still feel, Nitin, the working capital range on a steady-state basis, we should consider between 35 to 40 days.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to be 25% to 26% from next year.
items.quote: So, I think a steady-state range should be between 25% to 26% from next year.

items.statement: Optimistic on Q4 due to fiscal year-end, backlog, and momentum in Cloud and TSG.
items.quote: For Q4, with the fiscal year-end for India for many corporates and government with the budget spend, backlog of deals we have carried over from Q3 as well as momentum in both the Cloud and the Technology Solutions Group, we are optimistic on Q4.

items.statement: Bullish on Saudi from new fiscal year starting April 1.
items.quote: But into the new fiscal year, starting April 1, we are bullish on Saudi.

items.statement: Bullish across all verticals in CY25.
items.quote: So, CY '25, we definitely see bullishness across all the verticals.

items.statement: Gross margin may trend down due to higher component of big deals.
items.quote: We do see big deals coming in the next few quarters as well. So, as the component of big deals versus the run rate business goes up, we might see a little bit of trending in that direction.

items.statement: Factoring costs in Q3 expected to continue in Q4.
items.quote: As far as factoring is concerned, I think what you had seen in Q3 is something that should continue in Q4, subject to, as Hari said, we are waiting very eagerly for the Paynet closure.

items.statement: Possible demand slowness in Middle East and Turkey in March due to festive month.
items.quote: March being a festive month in many parts of Middle East and Turkey, we could see some slowness in demand in that part of the world.

items.statement: Paynet divestment expected to close this quarter, subject to regulatory approvals.
items.quote: We are keeping our fingers crossed. We also wish it will get done by this quarter. We are very confident. Let's see. See, since these are regulatory things, Nikunj, we can't answer this with certainty, but our expectation is this quarter.

items.statement: OPEX growth to align with revenue and gross margin growth next year.
items.quote: But we will see growth now and OPEX growth keeping in line with revenue and gross margin growth, because we do need to invest in the business in all the growth markets.

items.statement: Solar business model adjusted; optimistic for next fiscal year.
items.quote: We are actually quite optimistic about this. It will take some time to change the business model from an imported to a local and going into this franchisee model. But as we get into the next fiscal year, we do see our ability to play again in this market w ith a new business model quite strong

items.statement: Oil production expected around 3.48 MMT for FY25, targeting 3.5 MMT.
items.quote: The production actually is expected to be finally around 3.48 with respect to -- this thing, for 2025. Although we targeted 3.6 around, but because of a number of reasons, we had some of the areas where -- this is Director (operation) by the way [Inaudible 17:04]. So we are expecting around 3.5. We will be trying very hard to reach 3.5.

items.statement: Gas production target 3,300 MMSCM for FY25.
items.quote: 3,300 for gas. That is our target now.

items.statement: Target to become 4 MMT crude oil and 5 BCM gas company, reaching 4 MMT by 2027.
items.quote: Our target is to become a 4 million ton crude oil and a 5 BCM company, so that's our target. So we are inching towards that. This year possibly, even though the target is 3.5, we may still reach that target. I'm not writing off that possibility. However, as you have seen that there are huge challenges. Our fields are all depleting fields. Still -- I mean most of the peer companies, they are suffer

items.statement: For FY26, production expected to be maintained, possibly reaching 3.6-3.7 MMT.
items.quote: So '26, you can expect that we'll maintain it. And most probably, we are going to drill in some of the high potential areas this year, like Barekuri. So we are targeting those areas. Once we enter there, I think our production will pick up. And maybe we'll be reaching at least 3.6, 3.7 -- 3.65.

items.statement: Gas production for FY26 expected close to 3.8-4 BCM.
items.quote: It will be close to 3.8 BCM, 4 BCM.

items.statement: 5 BCM gas production targeted in FY27-FY28.
items.quote: 5 BCM is targeted in the year '27, '28.

items.statement: NRL petrochemical project capex INR7,200 crores, completion by December 2028.
items.quote: As far as petrochemical project is concerned, that is a project of about INR7,200 crores of capex. And until now the company has -- NRL has already spent about -- almost INR950 crores to INR990 crores on this project. And the expected completion is maybe after 3 years by December 2028.

items.statement: NRL refinery expansion 3 to 9 MMTPA, 70% complete, INR23,000 crores spent, commissioning by end of year.
items.quote: 3 to 9 MMTPA capacity expansion of the NRL is concerned, that has already achieved about 70% -- more than 70% complete and physical progress has been made. And already around INR23,000 crores of capex has already been spent on this project till now.

items.statement: DNPL pipeline expansion capex INR433 crores, first phase by March 2025, second by March 2026.
items.quote: So that particular project is undergoing under DNPL own window. And it is having a capex of about INR433 crores. And the first phase is expected to be completed by March 31, 25. And second phase is expected to be completed by March 2026, so that it gets matched with the completion of our refinery expansion.

items.statement: Oil India acquired 40,000 sq km acreage in no-go zones, awaiting government notification.
items.quote: But since the release of this no-go zone areas, Oil India Limited has taken a very aggressive and very calculated step in acquiring around 40,000 square kilometers of acreage just as an operator, which is yet to be notified by the Government of India, but we know that we are the lead bidder, and these basins are Mahanadi, KG.

items.statement: NRL GRM for 9M FY25 was $3.61/bbl, with inventory adjustments and excise benefits.
items.quote: Yes, GRM has falling compared to last 9 months -- last 9 months, GRM was about $13.12/bbl, whereas this end, the GRM is $ 3.61/bbl, okay? So there are several reasons actually in which you -- even if you look at pan-India GRM, the GRMs not as impressive as the corresponding period last year for pan -India also. That is the first thing. Second thing is, there are some inventory exemptions, which ta

items.statement: New well gas premium pricing expected to coincide with DNPL augmentation and NRL expansion.
items.quote: So we are now – since you would understand this requires an allocation from the ministry, from our side, Oil India has already given some numbers. Once those numbers are vetted by the ministry, and we are expecting it to come through and it would -- and we expect it to coincide with the DNPL augmentation and NRL refining capacity coming up, those 2 events should ideally coincide.

items.statement: Expect to scale up gas production once IGGL commissioned and CGD network integrated.
items.quote: But our expectation is that once the IGGL is commissioned, we'll scale up our production. We have plenty of gas there. The current situation doesn't quite prompt us to scale up our production, the moment the IGGL happens and the CGD -- I mean, blocks that have already been awarded and those companies are all doing their back-end work, so this integration of their network will help us to send gas t

items.statement: New fertilizer plant in Namrup may increase gas consumption from 1.1 to 2.3 MMSCMD.
items.quote: If I may add, sir, there is a development coming up where a new fertilizer plant has been planned in Namrup. So that also may probably become a source of gas consumption, which would be -- currently, they are consuming around 1.1 MMSCMD, which might go up to 2.3 MMSCMD.

items.statement: Flaring reduced from 8% to 4%, targeting near zero with 11 new compressors.
items.quote: See, in percentage term, it has come down from 8% to 4%. The preceding 9 months, that is FY '23, our flaring percentage was 8. Now in the current 9 months ended 31st December, this has come down to 4.

items.statement: NRL refinery expansion mechanical completion by December 2025, gradual ramp-up thereafter.
items.quote: We are completing -- mechanical completion will be by December 2025. There will be some commissioning exercise that will be there, so it will take some time. After that, it started like what he already said is that accordingly, this will start produce -- like the production will be getting augmented. It will be a step by step process.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance maintained at INR 12.75 billion.
items.quote: Guidance for this year, FY '25 will continue to be INR 12.75 billion and initial guidance for FY '26 will be INR 15 billion with an upside potential based on the current order inflow rates.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected between 17% and 18% for this financial year.
items.quote: I would to put a cap on the EBITDA margin. So I would say factoring something like 17.5% or taking to say between 17% and 18%, I think, would be where we're going to be for this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 17.5% for next year.
items.quote: No. As I said, I just spoke to Anand and said that you can please expect something between 17% to 18% EBITDA margin, 17.5% would be realistic to put in for next year, considering all the costs that we're going to have, considering the ramp-up, considering the product mix and everything.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR 400 crores per quarter expected as new normal for next few quarters.
items.quote: We can certainly say that would be the new normal of the average order inflow for the next few quarters. In some quarters, we could have greater than INR 400 crores.

items.statement: New plant capacity of INR 18 billion to be ready by end of H1 next year.
items.quote: So we have capacity which is INR 18 billion, which we put up should be ready by end of H1. And then we have given initial guidance for INR 15.

items.statement: Demand from gas engine and gas turbine business extremely high for next 18 to 24 months.
items.quote: The gas engine and gas turbine business continues to be driven by demand from CHP, that is combined heat and power plants, AI, server farms and data centers, grid stabilization units and Ukraine. Demand is extremely high.

items.statement: If tariffs come, short term costs passed on to market.
items.quote: If there is a tariff coming in, then for the short term, that will have to be passed on to the market. It will have to get passed on to the market.

items.statement: Steam and gas segments to dominate, followed by hydro.
items.quote: In the coming years, I think steam and gas segment are going to be the dominating segment followed by hydro segment.

items.statement: U.S. exports 8% of turnover; tariffs may impact but customers committed.
items.quote: Our exports to the U.S. will be something like 8% of our overall turnover. And the products that we are exporting to the U.S. to our OE to the gas turbine manufacturers over there have a 2-year qualification, which is required for any other generator manufacturer to, let's say, replace us in the event that duties do come in.

items.statement: Committed to 20% compounded growth year-on-year.
items.quote: We have projected something like a compounded 20% growth. And we will upgrade the performance as and when we see the -- once we come closer to those dates. But right now, we will commit that we can do a definite 20% compounded growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Investment of INR 1 billion to be spent, mostly next year.
items.quote: And we still have the majority of the money is going to be spent, I would say, INR 1 billion is going to be spent starting from, let's say, part of it is going to be this year, let's say, 0.2 to 0.8 are going to go to next year.

items.statement: Domestic demand holding up for FY26, exports main backbone.
items.quote: So we are confident of domestic demand holding up for FY '26, although for TDPS it is exports that is the main backbone of the business.

items.statement: Motors business to grow to INR 6-7 billion in 3-4 years.
items.quote: I gave a number, something I mean I said that we're going to grow it to INR 6 billion, INR 7 billion in the next 3, 4 years' time.

items.statement: Stable raw material environment expected for next financial year.
items.quote: So we see a stable raw material environment for us for next financial year. And if the prices go up or down, then we will have to then see the situation for the following year.

items.statement: New suspension control arm order with annual business USD 4 million and lifetime USD 22 million, SOP from Q3 FY26 at new Pune plant.
items.value: USD 4 million annual, USD 22 million lifetime
items.quote: We are excited to announce a new order win for our lightweighting vehicle vertical. The order is for suspension control arm product with annual business of USD $4 million and lifetime business of USD $22 million. The SOP is expected from Q3 FY26 from our new plant in Pune.

items.statement: Expects to outperform industry in FY26 due to CEV norms, new plant, new order, export business, and LCV/PV launches.
items.quote: So, we should be able to outperform the industry with these additions.

items.statement: Anticipates gross capex around Rs. 50-60 crores, possibly higher this year and early next year due to new plant.
items.quote: So, from the CAPEX perspective, we anticipate on a gross level to be around Rs. 60 crores, Rs. 50-Rs. 60 crores and might be going a little bit higher this year and early next year because of our new plant, b ut generally we will maintain a very similar r un date and of course if there is any inorganic opportunity that comes that is additional or any substantial order when that comes in the lightw

items.statement: Export order for CV emission components with annual business ~$7 million and lifetime ~$40 million, production starts Jan 2026 for US market.
items.quote: That is something that will start production in January, 26 and that is going to be for the US market. The ir annual business is roughly 7 million and lifetime business is about $40 million

items.statement: Hopes for similar margin profile for new products but too early to call.
items.quote: We are hoping for a similar margin profile, and though it is too early to yet take a call on that.

items.statement: Optimistic about PV industry revival, budget good, festive sales good, hopes next year better.
items.quote: I think the PV industry; the budget was very good and hopefully that now really drives consumption and higher demand for PVs. However, given the global environment right now, it is hard to really focus the next year. But we are quite optimistic about the industry reviving.

items.statement: Uses indexing mechanism with all customers to pass through raw material price fluctuations, no hedging.
items.quote: With all our customers, we have a mechanism called indexing, right? So, it is index based on fluctuation. So, sometimes raw material goes down, sometimes it goes up right and it is volatile.

items.statement: Focus on powertrain agnostic products, strengthening lightweighting vertical through M&A and organic investments.
items.quote: Powertrain agnostic products, anything that is powertrain agnostic and first focus is things that can strengthen our lightweighting vertical.

items.statement: TREM-V implementation date notified as April 1, 2026, but government may adjust; orders awarded.
items.quote: So, the government has notified the date for 1st April 26. Th ere is always possibility of time adjustment from the government side. However, the govern ment has not changed the date

items.statement: Plans to use cash for M&A in lightweighting and powertrain agnostic products, no fixed timeline; dividend policy 10-30%.
items.quote: So, our first preference is to utilize this for augmenting our lightweighting vertical through M&A and through of course organic investments as well, second to do M&A in the powertrain agnostic products where we can have a JV, TA or acquire a Company to add content to cars, trucks, tractors and so on.

items.statement: New Pune plant for control arms will have capacity slightly less than 300,000 units.
items.quote: Yes, that is going to be substantial. That plant alone will have about slightly less than 300,000 capacity.

items.statement: Exhaust systems capacity utilization at about 80% plus, can augment easily.
items.quote: We are at about 80% plus, but we don't share utilization numbers just because we can augment it very quickly.

items.statement: Exports currently 1-2% of revenues, significant growth expected.
items.quote: Right now, the contribution from the international markets is very less. In terms of exports, it would be like 1%-2% only.

items.statement: Lightweighting vertical currently 7-8% of revenues, aims to increase significantly.
items.quote: So, sir, my question was on the suspension and lightweighting segment, which right now would be roughly around 7%-8% of our revenues. So, going ahead, what is the aim here like, do you have any internal targets here to reach?

items.statement: Maintain EBITDA margin band of 12% to 14% for Q4 and Q1 next year.
items.quote: We will definitely be maintaining our guided band of EBITDA, which is 12% to 14%, going forward as well, at least for Q4 and Q1 of the next year, which is what we currently estimate.

items.statement: Aim to grow volumes at 2x to 3x market growth rate annually.
items.quote: Our objective has always been to grow 2x to 3x the market. Without being specific, we want to mention that we would like to continue our trajectory of 2 x to 3x the market growth rate on an annual basis

items.statement: Tirex aims to double revenues every year for next few years.
items.quote: If you refer our previous calls, we said that we would like to double the revenues every year for the next few years, and we want to highlight that we are on course for that.

items.statement: Capex estimated at INR 30-40 crore annually.
items.quote: Our trajectory of capex has been around INR 30 crore annually. Going forward, we estimate to have a capex of around INR 30 crore to INR 40 crore.

items.statement: Aspire to move to higher EBITDA margin band over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: we obviously aspire to move to the higher trajectory over a period of next 2-3 years. Every 2-3 years, we would like to move to the higher band.

items.statement: Will take pricing actions to neutralize input cost increase from rupee depreciation.
items.quote: if rupee continues to behave the way it has, definitely pricing actions and/or scheme related adjustments will come in, which will neutralize part of the impact of this input cost increase.

items.statement: Seeing early signs of demand recovery in B2B and B2C.
items.quote: We have definitely started seeing some early signs of demand recovery because it has been slightly challenging in the last few quarters.

items.statement: Focus on premiumization, aiming premium products to grow at least twice overall growth.
items.quote: suppose we are growing 7% overall, we would like to have the premium products growing at least twice that, and the percentage varies of that across segments, and that is what our focus is towards.

items.statement: AdBlue segment expected to grow 10-15%.
items.quote: You'll see, we have been looking at 10% to 15% growth in the segment. I think that is where we see it.

items.statement: Battery business quarterly revenues around INR 20-25 crore, turned EBITDA positive.
items.quote: Battery business, as we have been highlighting, is crossing around INR 20 crore quarterly revenues, INR 20 crore to INR 25 crore range and have turned EBITDA positive during the current year.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of INR 20 per share.
items.quote: we have declared a very good return to our shareholders in terms of an interim dividend of INR 20 per share, which is 1,000% on the face value of INR 2.

items.statement: Expects to grow 1.5x the industry, with industry growth 6-7% next financial year.
items.quote: So I just explained this in the previous question, but we would definitely want to grow 1.5x the industry. So while the industry is expected to grow about 6% to 7% over the next financial year, we are in position in order to achieve our goals and targets.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to be stable and then grow.
items.quote: So while we are very happy to share that we have done an all -time high percentage, we expect this to be stable and then grow in the times to come.

items.statement: Highest capex in die-casting and electronics divisions.
items.quote: So in our portfolio, the highest capex comes primarily from the die -casting division. And that is where the highest investment is probably expected. Also in the areas of Electronics, which is, again, across various segments, or across various verticals because everything is becoming more electronics per se.

items.statement: Lifetime order wins in Q3 exceeded INR 1,250 crores, with EV platforms over 25%.
items.quote: Key recent developments include order wins in Q3, and lifetime order wins exceeding INR 1,250 crores with EV platforms contributing over 25% of these wins.

items.statement: Order book surpassed INR 6,000 crores in first nine months.
items.quote: For the first nine months of the year, our order book surpassed INR 6,000 crores, reflecting an expanding product portfolio, product premiumization, and rising demand for both ICE and EV products across customers and across segments.

items.statement: CV industry expected to bounce back with single-digit growth in next few quarters.
items.quote: So, we believe that the CV industry should bounce back in the next recent quarters to come. But of course, we are expecting a single-digit growth in the next few quarters.

items.statement: 4-wheeler segment expected to grow modestly, reaching 7-8 million vehicles by 2030.
items.quote: And all the reports show that the 4-wheeler is expected to be about 7 million to 8 million vehicles by 2030. So, a modest growth is expected over the next few years.

items.statement: Smart keys are 7-8% of Vehicle Access revenue, expected to grow.
items.quote: So Raghu, in terms of the smart keys, this continues to be about 7% to 8% of our revenue of our Vehicle Access division. And in the next quarters to come, this is expected to grow on a consistent basis, while there are new launches, product launches as well as more penetration increases in the ICE as well as EV vehicles.

items.statement: TFT clusters are 8-10% of Minda Instruments revenue, expected to increase penetration in 4-wheelers.
items.quote: Currently, in our Minda Instruments portfolio, this also continues to be about close to 8% to 10% of our revenue when it comes to the new or next -generation clusters with this TFT in the various sizes, which are connected and other electronics in the driver information system space. Going forward, they will be h aving a larger penetration in the 4 -wheeler segment on the TFT side.

items.statement: Kit value for 2-wheeler portfolio is INR 30,000-35,000, expected to grow with integration.
items.quote: So the current kit value being offered, which is already in mass production and supplied to various customers is in the range of INR 30,000 to INR 35,000 per 2-wheeler. Of course, this is expected to grow when there is more integration and where there are more advanced products, which are coming in terms of a system solution and kit value offering by combining the products of Minda Corporation and

items.statement: Synergies with Flash expected to reach INR 500-600 crores by 2030.
items.quote: So, we expect by 2030, this number is in the range of about INR 500 crores to INR 600 crores.

items.statement: Flash Electronics growing at 17-18%, expected to continue similar growth.
items.quote: So Flash Electronics has been growing at a constant rate of about 17% to 18%, and we expect them to grow in a simila r range in the next few quarters to come.

items.statement: R&D spend at 4% of sales, expected to continue in FY26.
items.quote: Now as an opex and capex put together, we are investing close to about 4% or north of 4% in the R&D. And this year, of course, in the FY26 also, we expect to continue in a similar range.

items.statement: Exports target to increase to 15% of revenue in midterm to long run.
items.quote: Currently, we are about 8% to 10% of our revenue. And as an organization, we would like to grow this much higher than t he domestic growth. So while we have the order book, we would like to take it to about 15% in the midterm to long run for our overall revenue side.

items.statement: Geopolitical concerns may create challenges in American market.
items.quote: But of course, with the new geopolitical concerns, it is in somewhere opening us opportunities. But of course, somewhere they could become challenged in terms of the American market, however, the future comes up with.

items.statement: Targets 12-15% value growth and 10-12% volume growth for FY26.
items.quote: So you rightly said, so we've taken a target wise to grow in value-wise in the range of 12% to 15%. Volume wise, we will grow like double-digit at least 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Plans capex of around Rs. 110 crores next year.
items.quote: But next year, we have very clear visibility for the Capex of around Rs. 110 crores.

items.statement: Aims for 20-22% revenue share from Multimodal Logistics in 2-3 years.
items.quote: The contribution from Multimodal Services is steadily increasing, and we are planning to achieve a 20% to 22% revenue share from Multimodal Logistics in the next two to three years.

items.statement: Expects 1% overall price hike this quarter from big customers.
items.quote: So hopefully, I think in this whole quarter, we will be able to take the 1% price hikes overall basis because 50% is out.

items.statement: Margin erosion of 300 basis points is sustainable, no further erosion expected.
items.quote: So maybe like margin is already like eroded on a 300 basis points. So we've not seen any further erosion on that. This is like sustainable margin, whatever we did that.

items.statement: January saw growth restart, but uncertainty remains for March.
items.quote: Honestly speaking, this January is fantastic or you can say the re started a growth. But again, we are also worrisome because all the time we've seen in last three quarters where good month is not performing well.

items.statement: SME customers hit by inflation and high interest costs, unable to support price hikes.
items.quote: But this time, SME customer is already facing the challenges due to high inflation, high interest costs. They are not able to support us on this time because again, volumes are very less and they also have the like impact of muted growth.

items.statement: Invests $7.5 million in Singapore subsidiary over two years for freight forwarding.
items.quote: Well, so first, this new capital requirement is not for this year, it is for like '25-'26 and '26-'27 for the two year. So overall cash flow will not be more than like in the range of 10% to 15% each year.

items.statement: Plans to open 50-75 branches next year and 75-100 in FY27.
items.quote: So next year, again, we will be planning to open a branch in the range of 50 to 75. And in '26 '27, again, in the range of 75 to 100 that surely we will be open that branches.

items.statement: Automation in two centers reduced costs by 30-50 basis points.
items.quote: So ultimately, we reduced the cost by like 30 to 50 basis points put together in these 2 centres in overall basis.

items.statement: B2C revenue share shrunk to 2.5-3% from 4% last year.
items.quote: Earlier, we have the e-commerce share in overall revenue is 4%. Now it is also shrunk to 2.5% to 3% only because as you are aware, our focus is not on a B2C.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 82%, down 2% from peak.
items.quote: Our strong customer mix, extensive network and market positioning enabled us to maintain stable capacity utilization at 82%.

items.statement: Volume in Q3 was 242,000 tonnes, down 3%.
items.quote: Yeah, Q3, we have achieved a volume of 242,000 tonnes, we have taken in our volume in Q3.

items.statement: Capex for nine months was Rs. 20 crores, including Rs. 9.38 crores in Q3.
items.quote: During nine months '25, we incurred a Capex of Rs. 20 crores, including Rs. 9.38 crores in Q3 '25, primarily directed towards expanding our branch network, constructing sorting centers and ramping up IT infrastructure.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share recommended.
items.quote: Furthering our commitment to shareholder value, the Board has recommended an interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share, reinforcing our confidence in the company's financial stability and growth prospects.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations was Rs. 40 crores in nine months.
items.quote: Our debt-free balance sheet and disciplined financial management have resulted in a strong cash flow generation with Rs. 40 crores cash flow from operations during the period.

items.statement: Expects Matchmaking billing to grow QoQ in Q4, but revenue to decline due to muted Q3 billing.
items.quote: On the billing and revenue output for quarter 4, we expect a growth in Matchmaking billing in quarter 4 on a quarter -over-quarter basis. However, the revenue is expected to decline are due to the muted billing growth in quarter 3.

items.statement: Marriage Services expected to be at similar level as Q3.
items.quote: Marriage Services are expected to be at similar level of that of quarter 3.

items.statement: Expects PAT to be lower than Q3 due to subdued business momentum.
items.quote: However, we expect the PAT to be lower than the levels of Q3 due to the subdued business momentum.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve once revival happens, likely in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect to impro ve margins once the revival happens. We expect the revival sometime probably in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Sees potential for PAT margin to reach 20% or higher and EBITDA margin beyond 25%.
items.quote: Today, we're operating at 12% PAT margin. It can even go to 20% or higher.

items.statement: EBITDA margin can comfortably go beyond 25%.
items.quote: And EBITDA level definitely can easily comfortably go beyond 25% also.

items.statement: Plans to optimize costs, likely in Q1.
items.quote: We are also taking steps to optimize our costs and that may happen sometime in quarter 1.

items.statement: Sees scope to reduce marketing spend from INR47 crores to INR35 crores or INR30 crores per quarter if competition decreases.
items.quote: If you look at what is our marketing spend, I think it can be even easily instead of say INR47 crores, probably you can even even INR35 crores if the competition goes down . So that's the kind of volumes and that's kind of money on market or even INR30 crores per quarter is good enough.

items.statement: Industry saw 8% drop in search queries, affecting member registrations and monetization.
items.quote: As per Google report on the matrimony industry, the whole industry has seen an 8% drop in search queries for the first ever time. All the players, including long -time players, have seen a similar drop and it is a broader industry trend.

items.statement: Expects personal services to have double-digit growth.
items.quote: And we also expect personal services to have a double-digit growth on account of steps that we are taking to convert more members to go for personalised services.

items.statement: Launching new version of community matrimony apps this month.
items.quote: We are launching a new version of community matrimony apps sometime this month.

items.statement: Launching vernacular-based app; already available in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam.
items.quote: However, we are taking new initiatives to drive the profile acquisition growth, including we are launching a vernacular -based app. We already have our apps available in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam.

items.statement: Revenue was muted in Q3 despite hopes of revival due to marriage season and campaign.
items.quote: During the last call, we were hopeful of revival in quarter 3 due to the marriage season and also due to the launch of our Great India Matchmaking Fest campaign. However the revenue was muted.

items.statement: New initiatives burn rate expected to be in similar range as before.
items.quote: At this point of time, we can think that it will be a similar range, but it is not a lot of experience happening, but definitely some of the initiatives are very encouraging.

items.statement: Plans to monetize many jobs after reaching 5 million resumes and 10,000+ employers.
items.quote: We intend to monetize once we reach our 5 million resumes, once we reach probably 10,000 plus employers.

items.statement: Revised revenue guidance to INR7,200 crores by FY27, up from INR6,300 crores.
items.quote: Yes, already we were at INR6,300 crores. Now we are guiding at INR7,300 crores as we are already reaching out of INR3,300 crores, we have already done INR2,500 crores. So we have changed our guidance to INR7,200 crores because these are clients we have not counted in our guidance of INR6,300 crores.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 is INR5,700 crores.
items.quote: Yes. So already we have given the guidance of INR5,700 -- we have revised the guidance to INR5,700 crores for the FY '26 and INR7,200 crores for '27.

items.statement: Annual revenue target for FY25 is INR3,300 crores.
items.quote: We have delivered a strong performance in the first 9 months for the financial year and remain on track to achieve our annual revenue target of INR3,300 crores driven by new client acquisition opera tion efficiencies and enhanced management capabilities.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin of 3.5% to 4% on INR7,300 crores business.
items.quote: So we are expecting from 3.5% to 4%, 3.5% to 4% in between that.

items.statement: Expects gross margin 7%, EBITDA margin 5.5%, PAT margin 3.5% in FY27.
items.quote: So gross margins, we are expecting to be at 7%, EBITDA at 5.5% and 3.5% PAT.

items.statement: Plans to build new facility to reach 4 ton per month capacity after FY27 March.
items.quote: We want to make a 4 ton capacity facility, including all lab-grown, natural, 18-carat and all. So let's see, we are planning for that arrangement and we'll look at the Board and we'll in form you but we have a mind that we should have a capacity of 4 ton per month.

items.statement: Expects to add 50 kg per month from CaratLane and 50 kg from Aditya Birla starting April quarter.
items.quote: So now we are making monthly 450 kg per month with the subsidiaries. We are expecting 10% of revenue more growth from CaratLane and Aditya Birla. So we are expecting monthly 50 -50 kg from both CaratLane and Aditya. This will add 100 kg extra production from our regular guidance.

items.statement: Wedding season demand is good; retail impact of 10-15% for short term due to gold prices.
items.quote: So wedding season is good. As a manufacturer, we are backed by order every month because there is every wedding season , then Akshaya Tritiya comes in the April . For example, March orders will come for Akshaya Tritiya. Now we are making for wedding season. At retail level, there is 10%, 15% of impact is there for a short term of 10 to 15 days.

items.statement: 18 carat revenue increased to 5% from 3%; diamond carats doubled to 883 carats.
items.quote: Yes. So 18 carat, we were at 3% last quarter and now we have done 5% of this revenue in 18 carat. So last quarter, we sold diamond of around 400 carat, and this quarter we have done 800 carat.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond prices falling; company procures only against fixed orders to mitigate risk.
items.quote: Sure. So I will throw a light on that because lab-grown is a devaluating asset every time -- every quarter rates are falling. Earlier, it was falling drastically. Now it ’s falling in a limited -- but as a manufacturer, all the industry works on that model, we also procure that only order to the lab growing companies, that quantity only, which we get the fixed order of that.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to IND A-/Stable, expected to reduce cost of funds and collateral requirements.
items.quote: We are pleased to announce an update on Sky Gold's credit rating from India Rating, a subsidiary of Fitch globally, which has assigned an ‘IND A-/ Stable’rating to the company bank loans. The fund-based working capital limit and proposed fund-based working capital limit have been rated ‘IND A- / Stable / IND A2+’.

items.statement: Expects to be cash flow positive by FY27.
items.quote: By FY '27, we'll be cash flow positive.

items.statement: Plans to convert 70-80% of debt to gold metal loans by FY26, reducing finance cost by 0.5%.
items.quote: We want to go up to 80%, 75% to 80% and already it will help because we have already a rating of A- from Fitch Rating. We were at BB stable. Now we are at A -. So there is a good sign that we have got a good rating, which will help us to reduce our finance cost in CC limit also in GML also and reduce our collateral part also.

items.statement: Expects 30-40% of business from clients providing raw material in next 2 years.
items.quote: So in next 2 years, we are expecting 3 0% to 40% from this client. We will grow 1,000 kg, at least 300 to 350 kg we get from this advance ,650 maybe from our inventory.

items.statement: Exports to grow to 13-15% of revenue by FY27 from current 7-8%.
items.quote: So already, we are at 8% this quarter, 8% -- sorry, 7% this quarter, INR71 crores export we have done. And we were at 1%, 2% year before. And in 2 years, we are expecting it to take it to 13%, 14% or 15%.

items.statement: Volume guidance for FY26 is 650-700 kg per month.
items.quote: So we are expecting to 650 kg approximately, 650 to 700 kg. So as we told that we'll update new PPT guidance also in this 7 days and in our actions also. So I think we are expecting to 650 kg.

items.statement: Aspiration of 12% to 15% revenue growth stays, hopeful improved consumption with tax cuts will aid efforts.
items.quote: Our aspiration of 12% to 15% revenue growth stays, and we are hopeful that an improved consumption scenario with recent tax cuts will aid our efforts.

items.statement: Guidance to continue growing EBITDA by at least 100 basis points going forward.
items.quote: our guidance is that we will continue to grow by at least 100 basis points going forward.

items.statement: Guiding around 5% to 7% like-to-like in full price growth.
items.quote: we are guiding that we are looking at around 5% to 7% like-to-like in full price growth.

items.statement: Guidance on square foot expansion is around 15% net addition, around 1.5 lakh net square foot addition every year.
items.quote: So our guidance on square foot expansion is around 15% net addition. We are at around 1.15 million square foot as on date, and our guidance is to grow that at a 15%, so around 1.5 lakh net square foot addition every year.

items.statement: Wholesale channels expected to grow at 8% to 10% in near term.
items.quote: both the other wholesale channels should grow immediately at 8% to 10% in the near future.

items.statement: B2C will become two-third and B2B one-third of online business in next 6 months.
items.quote: And if I look at the next 6 months, B2C will be a bigger business, maybe two-third and B2B will become one-third.

items.statement: Online business expected to grow more than 10%.
items.quote: we are now seeing that online business will grow more than 10%.

items.statement: Direct channels share reached nearly 55% this year, medium-term vision to take to two-thirds.
items.quote: There's a nearly a 4% increase in the share of the revenue mix for direct channels, and their share has reached nearly 55% this year. This is in line with our medium -term vision of taking this number to maybe two-thirds of our business.

items.statement: Expect Arrow and Flying Machine EBITDA growth higher than 100 basis points.
items.quote: if the overall company has to grow at 100 basis points, the Arrow and Flying Machine growth -- EBITDA growth has to be higher than 100 basis points.

items.statement: Footwear business impacted by BIS implementation, but worst is behind us.
items.quote: Footwear growth has got impacted because of BIS implementation, which has impacted inventory levels and assortment.

items.statement: Adjacent categories growing between 15% to 20%, double the company growth rate.
items.quote: And that business is growing between 15% to 20% , much higher or almost double the growth rate of the company.

items.statement: Retail channel growth mid-teen likely to sustain and may improve further.
items.quote: The support engines for retail of like -to-like growth, square foot addition, and renovations of stores have reached the momentum where this mid -teen growth of retail is very likely to sustain and may even improve further.

items.statement: Q3 GP went up by 160 basis points to 55%.
items.quote: With lower discounting and richer channel mix in favor of direct channels, retail and online B2C, Q3 GP went up by 160 basis points to 55%.

items.statement: EBITDA in Q3 grew by more than 110 basis points and reached 14.5% of NSV.
items.quote: the EBITDA in Q3 grew by more than 110 basis points and reached 14.5% of NSV in Q3.

items.statement: Return on capital employed crossed 19%, confidence to take beyond 20% in medium term.
items.quote: another highlight this quarter is a strong improvement in our return on capital employed, which has now crossed 19%, a significa nt shift in the last two years. This gives us confidence to now take it beyond 20% in the medium term, a target which we had set for us last year.

items.statement: Expects to return to 14-15% margin range by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: In terms of overall margins, yes, we expect by quarter one, we should be back in the range of 14, 15, which has be en our guidance and which has been what we haven't delivered.

items.statement: Full impact of cost and pricing actions to neutralize input cost inflation by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We will see the full impact coming to us in the 1st Quarter. By March, we would have taken all the actions to neutralize.

items.statement: Biscuits price increase of 4-5% through price hikes and de-grammage.
items.quote: So, in terms of, Harit in terms of price increase, which we are kind of taking, would anything range between approximately as of now what looks like is go to 4% to 5% kind of price increase as of now, because it's a mix of price increase, it's a mix of de -grammage and some part of the cost element.

items.statement: Bread price increase of 3-4%, mainly in North India.
items.quote: Bread, yes. Bread, if I remember right, is around 3% to 4% kind of price increase. We have taken and the price increase is 3 to 4, I am saying, is more primarily on the North India side and it is much lesser on the West and the South side.

items.statement: Cost efficiency program to add 0.5% to margins over next 12 months.
items.quote: In terms of saying that what would be the impact of these cost efficiency programs in terms of on the margin side, I would say that over the next 12 months, our target should be kind of have an impact of close to half a percent on an annualized basis on our margins through this cost efficiency program.

items.statement: Dhar plant commissioning scheduled for April 2025.
items.quote: The commissioning of our new Biscuits facility at Dhar, Madhya Pradesh is scheduled for April 2025 while our state- of-art facility in Khopoli is expected to be operational by the 2nd Quarter of the next financial year.

items.statement: Kolkata plant to commence operations in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Additionally, our Kolkata plant is set to commence operations in the 1st Quarter of the financial year 2025-26.

items.statement: Domestic biscuits volume growth recovery expected to continue in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: But only the good signs which we are seeing now, at least in our part of the business is that from Quarter 3 of this financial year, we have seen for us the revenue growth, the volume growth has started looking up and we expect a similar trend to continue in the Quarter 4 of the financial year.

items.statement: Export growth expected to mellow down but continue in mid-teens.
items.quote: Yes, so export which has been kind of growing very, very aggressively over the last 2-2.5 years, obviously we can't expect a similar growth to come in export because they're sitting on a very, very high base. And so that kind of growth we expect to kind of mellow down but continue to grow well in mid -teens.

items.statement: Annual revenue growth guidance maintained at mid-teens.
items.quote: And our guidance has always b een, we will maintain on an annualized basis, a growth of around mid-teen

items.statement: Frozen B2C products to be introduced in Q1 FY26 under English Oven.
items.quote: So, by quarter one of the coming financial year, we will start introducing some of those product lines in our B2C segment, which is English Oven and start kind of building that.

items.statement: Red Sea impact on freight costs expected to persist with no immediate change.
items.quote: The Red Sea or the higher freight cost on account of exports, which is higher that I am not expecting any immediate change there, right? We haven't seen that change over the last 12 months.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 margins expected to improve sequentially from Q3 FY25.
items.quote: So, Samanta, we definitely, as we briefed you about the action we have taken, both in the cost and the pricing side, we definitely expect Quarter 4 to be better than Quarter 3 in terms of our margins.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 3 per equity share declared.
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have declared an interim dividend of INR 3 per equity share.

items.statement: Expects about 20% growth in Agrochemical segment next financial year.
items.quote: So we expect about 20% growth in the next financial year, in Agrochemical segment.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin in the range of 14% to 16% in the next few quarters.
items.quote: So I think going forward in the next few quarters, I think we will be somewhere in the range of 14% to 16% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: No big capex planned for next 1 or 2 years in any segment.
items.quote: So Keshav, first of all, I would like to mention in between that from the debt point of view, we will not be doing any big capex for the next 1 or 2 years' time. in Agrochemical segment as well as in other segments also.

items.statement: Multipurpose plant has potential to generate revenue of more than INR 1,000 crore.
items.quote: So the multipurpose plant where we have invested close to INR 400 crore, it has got potential to generate revenue of more than INR1,000 crore.

items.statement: Multipurpose plant to take 2 to 3 years to reach INR 1,000 crore revenue level.
items.quote: Yes, definitely. So I think it will take nearly 2 to 3 years to reach at nearly INR 1,000 crore level -- better utilization point of view.

items.statement: Expects TiO2 revenue of INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore next year.
items.quote: So after that, so we will be ramping up the capacity. So as Ankit said, next year, we are expecting 250 crore to INR 300 crore of top line.

items.statement: Pigment business revenue to be between INR 550 crore to INR 650 crore yearly.
items.quote: Yes. But overall, as the pigment business, the revenue would be on a yearly basis between INR 550 crore to INR 650 crore.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on TiO2 from China expected by March 2025.
items.quote: So as India, we initiated antidumping duty last year. So we believe that the outcome, the antidumping should come by -- tentative by March 2025, in the next 2 months' time.

items.statement: Demand recovery in agrochemicals expected to continue.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect the demand will remain -- continue in a similar mode.

items.statement: New products launched have started contributing to revenue.
items.quote: Now the new products, whatever we launched, those new products have also started giving the results in revenue. So because of the new product mix, there is an improvement in the revenue mix.

items.statement: Plan to demerge segments to unlock value once reasonable growth achieved.
items.quote: So we wanted to showcase the next 1 year, the growth trajectory in all the segments. Once we reach at a reasonable level, then yes, there is a plan to demerge the segment to unlock the value.

items.statement: Long-term debt on consolidated basis around INR 474 crore; standalone debt free by FY26-27.
items.quote: Okay. As far as debt is concerned, so we have long-term debt of consolidated basis at around INR474 crore. On standalone basis, we see in the next FY26-27, we will be debt free.

items.statement: Nano urea plant running at very low capacity, not even 10%.
items.quote: From the utilization point of view, our capacity is significantly large. So it is running at very, very low capacity, not even 10%.

items.statement: Anticipates major ramp-up in Q4 and confident of 20-25% revenue growth for FY25 with EBITDA margins 35-40%.
items.quote: We anticipate a major ramp-up in the quarter 4 and remain confident of achieving 20% to 25% revenue growth by FY '25 while maintaining strong EBITDA margins at 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Targets INR20-30 billion in new orders over next 18 months.
items.quote: With a robust bidding pipeline, we target INR20 billion to INR30 billion in new orders over the next 18 months.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,095 crores as of December 31, with development and production contributing 47% each.
items.quote: As of December 31, our order book stands at INR1,095 crores, with growth observed across all verticals where development and production contribute 47% each.

items.statement: Order book of INR1,184 crores including orders worth INR89 crores in negotiated till date.
items.quote: In Q3, as highlighted in our earnings release, we maintained an order book of INR1,184 crores, including orders worth INR89 crores in negotiated till date.

items.statement: Order inflows stood at INR240 crores for the quarter, with 9-month total at INR324 crores.
