items.quote: Margin, yes, I think, operational leverage can give us better margins, but it is very difficult to say because at the same time you have to also prepare for higher turnovers and more sales going forward.

items.statement: Most prices are fixed; 30-40% of projects have variable pricing if stretched over 8-10 months.
items.quote: Yes, most of the prices are fixed. When there is a longer-term project, we do take variable pricing. So, I think today would be maybe 30%-40% of our projects would have variable pricing if the project stretches over 8-10 months

items.statement: Export margins slightly better than local, but freight costs high; looking at higher volume from exports for simpler buildings.
items.quote: So, we are looking at higher volume from there for simpler buildings and utilize more of our production capacity and execute those orders. But overall, I think the margin is only slightly better.

items.statement: Collaboration with JSPL for heavy structures and joint marketing of high-rise buildings, data centers, commercial buildings, malls.
items.quote: So, we are going to use them for the heavier structure production and joint marketing of other building like high rise buildings and data centers and commercial building, malls. There we are going to do joint marketing, joint bidding and our engineering and design strength their production and they also have a good history with their work on a lot of these projects.

items.statement: Land was a major issue for new plants; company now booking land earlier.
items.quote: And yes, we have found that land was a major issue, when we want to set up a new plant land was the biggest hurdle that took time. So, we have started booking the land earlier keeping it which we are not doing earlier.

items.statement: Working capital cycle to be held at 20-21 days; cash reserves nearly Rs. 300 crores.
items.quote: So, I think that we will be able to hold our working capital cycle to 20 -21 days and I don't think that working capital cycle if I am not mistaken doesn't include our cash reserve. I think it is debtor s, the customer, advances, suppliers and the stocks

items.statement: Top 10 customers can contribute 40%-50% of revenue.
items.quote: So, our top 10 customers would be very different in FY24 than in FY25 than in FY19, but if you were to ask me that whatever the top 10 customers will be, so top 10 customers could be, let us say, for FY25, it will be Reliance, Tata Projects, and let us say 4-5 more, next year it could be Aditya Birla and somebody else.

items.statement: Warehousing sector is about 23% of revenue.
items.quote: I think what we are showing is infrastructure is primarily that warehousing sector. So, about, say 23%, we have shown that as the warehousing, what we show as infrastructure is primarily the warehousing sector, “A” grade.

items.statement: Capacity utilization to reach about 90% of utilizable capacity in next one year.
items.quote: So, going forward, we do feel that we should be able to raise our capacity utilization of already utilizable capacity percentage by at least 3-4% and we should reach to about 90% of the utilizable capacity in next one year.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 15% with similar margins.
items.quote: I think Mr. Nanda had already mentioned about 15% during this call itself in the top line and margins being similar.

items.statement: After FY26, growth could be 20-25% to achieve doubling turnover in four years.
items.quote: All these capacities once they come on stream and we utilize them fully, our growth going forward in the years after FY26 could be greater than 15% to be able to achieve that doubling the turnover in four years as we had said, so it could also be 20-25% in those year.

items.statement: Gujarat plant capacity: 40,000 tons, Rs. 500 crores building sale.
items.quote: Gujarat will also be about Rs. 500 crores with 40,000 tons of buildings manufactured there.

items.statement: Gujarat plant production expected in Q1 FY27, 9 months after September start.
items.quote: Normally, it takes about 9 months. So, if you start in September, sometime by 1st Quarter, May-June next year, June-July, we should be able to have it in production.

items.statement: Upgradation at Pantnagar and Tamil Nadu to increase efficiency by 2-3%.
items.quote: I would say that they can increase 2-3% efficiency inside the plant.

items.statement: Average order value increased to Rs. 12 crores from Rs. 4 crores three years ago.
items.quote: The fact of the matter is that 3 years ago it used to be Rs. 4 crores. It moved up to Rs. 6.5 crores to Rs. 9 crores and now it is Rs. 12 crores.

items.statement: Order book may pick up from March with increased capacity in April and May.
items.quote: I don't see much change, maybe from March onwards it might start picking up, the order book because we will have increased capacity coming in place in April and May.

items.statement: Operational leverage expected to improve margins.
items.quote: I think operational leverage will kick in and make it better.

items.statement: Gross margins improved by 100 basis points sequentially and Y-o-Y.
items.quote: Gross margin have actually improved by 100 basis points sequentially as well as Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Small and medium orders are critical for pre-engineered building business.
items.quote: See in pre-engineered building, another thing I would like to point out is that the small and medium orders in numbers are very critical because they are the biggest beneficiaries of pre-engineered building.

items.statement: Skilled labor shortage may impact operations.
items.quote: But I think highly skilled people will always have a shortage going forward.

items.statement: Working capital requirement approximately 30 days of sales, Rs. 150 crores.
items.quote: So, right now, sir, we are operating at about 28 days and our requirement is going to be approximately 30 days of working capital, sir, 30 days of the sales will be our networking capital requirement.

items.statement: Fixed cost around 9.2% of sales, Rs. 12-13 crores per month.
items.quote: Right now, there are about 9.2%. Arvind Nanda: I think if we look at a figure I would probably about Rs. 12-13 crores a month

items.statement: Aims for revenue CAGR of around 15-20% over next four to five years.
items.quote: For the next four to five years, we aim for a revenue CAGR of around 15 to 20%.

items.statement: Aspires to reach EBITDA margin range of 28-30% in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: I think the 28-30% steady state that we are saying, we will get there in the next 2 to 3 years. That's our stated objective.

items.statement: Expects to add another 100 to 125 crores in current quarter.
items.quote: We probably expect to add another 100 to 125 crores in this current quarter.

items.statement: Added 100 KL manufacturing capacity in November; expects another 100 KL in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: The Company added 100 KL to its manufacturing capacity in November and expects to add another 100 KL in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Continues to grow pricing at 2-3% annually for most customers, not dropping pricing.
items.quote: In fact, we continue to grow at the 2-3% increase annually for most customers, and we are sticking to our pricing at this point.

items.statement: Sees strong demand across CDMO business due to cost efficiency and supply chain diversification.
items.quote: Additionally, we see strong demand across our CDMO business, as pharma and biotech companies seek cost-efficient, high-quality manufacturing solutions and supply chain diversification.

items.statement: Sees more Phase 1 to Phase 3 assets moving to India earlier than post-COVID.
items.quote: But what we are seeing is that now today we are seeing both late phase, which are coming from China, but we are seeing a lot more of the Phase 1 to Phase 3 assets coming in, which are moving much earlier than they did post-COVID.

items.statement: New company formation in biotech has slowed down; timing of recovery uncertain.
items.quote: But the new Company creation definitely has slowed down. Time frame is hard to judge. It's your guess as good as mine in terms of when new Company formation is going to start.

items.statement: Aims for ROCE of mid to high teens over 3-4 years.
items.quote: I think our aspiration on the ROCE side, I am looking at more return on capital employed, is probably a mid to high teens over a 3-4 year period. That's really what we aspire to get to.

items.statement: Expects Q4 to be strongest quarter, H2 stronger than H1.
items.quote: I think Quarter 4 has generally been the strongest quarter that we have had. And Quarter 3 and Quarter 4 relatively, H2 is generally stronger than H1, which is, you know, it's the case with most of the CDMO business across, and we also believe that it will be the same way.

items.statement: Expects reduction in interest cost in current quarter after debt repayment.
items.quote: The remaining debt was repaid in January and we expect a reduction in interest cost in the current quarter.

items.statement: Plans significant capacity increase across discovery, CMC, and development based on demand.
items.quote: We expect we will have significant investment, not investment, but increase in capacity across all three areas based on the demand we are seeing right now from our customers.

items.statement: Sees traction in peptides, amidites, ADCs, and conjugation technologies.
items.quote: One is peptides, which we are having reasonable traction with. Another one is Amidites, which we are part of several commercial products on Amidites. Another is ADCs, and the next one would be basically any kind of conjugation technologies going for peptide conjugation, prototype conjugation.

items.statement: Expects 3-4 molecules to commercialize over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: We have a few other molecules, Rahul, but I am saying, you know, from an overall perspective, there is at least three, four molecules that we are seeing that will get commercialized over the next 2-3 year period.

items.statement: Expects growth much faster than 12% TAM growth over next 10-15 years.
items.quote: So, I have maintained through the roadshows, and I will still maintain that the opportunity that we have created for ourselves is to execute far faster than the 12% TAM growth over the next 10, 15 years, not just over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Aims to reach steady-state EBITDA margin in mid-30s within a year.
items.quote: And I think as long as we stay on that path, maybe we get to the steady-state margins towards the mid-30s instead of the next two years within a year.

items.statement: Deals to ramp through Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26, full effect over next two quarters.
items.quote: As it relates to your specific question about when these deals will ramp, all of these three deals actually have gone live as we talk and they will ramp through Q4 of Fiscal ‘25 and Q1 of Fiscal ‘26.

items.statement: Expects to be debt free next fiscal if no other capital uses.
items.quote: So, all things remaining equal, we should be able to get debt free sometime next fiscal.

items.statement: Plans to reveal three to four new features over next 12-18 months.
items.quote: I would not be surprised if we would reveal three to four new features over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Contracts have COLA clauses indexed to U.S. inflation.
items.quote: Having said that, I think a reflection of the strength of our platform has been that we have cost of living adjustment clauses in our contracts with most of our customers that are indexed to U.S. inflation.

items.statement: Large deal defined as contributing over $10 million in annual contract value.
items.quote: But I will say that in today's world, a large deal for IKS still is one that is able to contribute north of $10 million in annual contract value per year.

items.statement: Full manifest of platform could generate nearly $100 million per year per customer.
items.quote: Typically, the 500-odd customers that we are really going to focus on, at the full manifest of IKS, should all be able to generate nearly $100 million a year of revenue to IKS.

items.statement: AQuity margin transformation not yet halfway, significant runway ahead.
items.quote: I will say that we are probably not even at the halfway mark yet.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 are seasonally weaker due to holidays and winter weather.
items.quote: For example, Q3 and Q4 are traditionally weaker quarters than Q1 and Q2 because of the seasonality that sets in patient volumes due to the holiday season in Q3 and due to the severe winter weather in Q4.

items.statement: GenAI could lead to 20-35% automation, up to 70-85% in clinical documentation.
items.quote: So, one way to think about it is, while cognitive RPA maybe leads to 5% to 15% automation, GenAI could lead to 20% to 35% automation; and in some cases, like clinical documentation, even 70% to 85% automation.

items.statement: Palomar deal includes $16.5 million upfront guarantee, first $16.5 million of net economic value to IKS.
items.quote: And in a unique arrangement, the way this will happen is, as those upsides start accruing now that we have gone live with Palomar, up to the $16.5 million will accrue directly to IKS.

items.statement: Radiology Partners deal could improve radiologists' productivity by 25-30%.
items.quote: Partnering with them, we are creating a very unique virtual radiology assistant model that through a combination of technology and global human capital has the potential to improve radiologists' productivity on the same fixed cost by as much as 25% to 30%.

items.statement: For every human replaced, about $20,000 additional gross margin per year.
items.quote: One of the math that I would share with many people in the roadshows was that, for every human that we are able to transform or replace through a combination of our technology and some supervision through a global human capital, we are able to create about, give or take, $20,000 a year of additional gross margin through every human that we replace.

items.statement: PLA project cost revised to Rs. 2,850 crore gross, Rs. 1,750 crore net, with expected capital subsidy of Rs. 1,100 crore.
items.value: Rs. 2,850 crore gross or Rs. 1,750 crore net
items.quote: Now, based on a complete capex and opex review, our project cost stands at Rs. 2,850 crore gross or Rs. 1,750 crore net, with an expected capital subsidy of around Rs. 1,100 crore.

items.statement: PLA project commissioning on track for October 2026.
items.quote: The commissioning schedule remains on track for October 2026.

items.statement: At full capacity, PLA project expected to generate ~Rs. 2,000 crore revenue with EBITDA margins targeting 35% plus.
items.quote: At full capacity, the project is expected to generate ~Rs. 2,000 crore in revenue, with EBITDA margins, though it's still early, we are targeting 35% plus.

items.statement: PLA project funded through long-term debt of Rs. 1,650 crore and Rs. 1,200 crore from internal accruals.
items.value: Rs. 1,650 crore debt, Rs. 1,200 crore internal accruals
items.quote: The project cost is expected to be funded through long -term debt of Rs. 1,650 crore and Rs. 1,200 crore from internal accruals.

items.statement: Crushing expected to be 3% lower and recovery loss 0.40% for the season.
items.quote: So, crushing number would be 3% lower – is our estimate. And yes, 0.4 0% loss in recovery.

items.statement: Distillery margin will be muted compared to last year due to higher raw material cost and no increase in realization.
items.quote: Distillery margin will surely be muted in comparison to last year for previous years because of the continuous increase in the raw material cost and no increase in the realization.

items.statement: Converted two units from B-heavy to C-heavy after zero ethanol price increase; will make more sugar.
items.quote: So, how we have reacted, we have converted two of our units from B-heavy to C-heavy, immediately, after the zero increase. And post the export, sugar production will become attractive.

items.statement: Current sugar price in UP and our mills prevailing upwards of Rs. 41/kg.
items.quote: The current expected price in UP and in our mills are prevailing upwards of Rs. 41/kg.

items.statement: Export quota of around 31,000 tonnes traded; domestic release to be received over five months from March.
items.quote: So, our export quota was around 31,000 tonnes. We have traded our export quota, and we retain our domestic release, so we will be getting the domestic release of this 31,000 tonnes over a period of five months beginning from March, so there is an upside in the domestic.

items.statement: Sugar production for the season expected around 9.4 to 9.5 lakh tonnes.
items.quote: As far as the sugar production is concerned, for this year the sugar season looks like we will be doing around 9.4 lakh tonnes to 9.5 lakh tonnes.

items.statement: Alcohol volume for FY25 expected around 21.5 to 22.5 crore liters including ENA.
items.quote: Yes. For FY25 it looks like alcohol volume will be in the region of around 21.5 crore to 22.5 crore, including ENA and everything.

items.statement: Target around 4 crore liters ethanol from grain route for the ethanol year.
items.quote: And our target is around 4 crore liter during this ethanol year.

items.statement: Ethanol price unchanged is disappointing and could put government's program in jeopardy.
items.quote: However, the recent decision to keep the price unchanged or without any hike has been very disappointing. This is a deviation from the past practice of linking ethanol prices to the hike in FRP.

items.statement: Overall sugar availability seems sufficient with closing stock expected around 62 lakh tonnes.
items.quote: Despite this decline in production, overall sugar availability seems to be sufficient. We began with an opening stock of 80 lakh tonnes.

items.statement: PLA project capacity enhanced from 75,000 to 80,000 tons.
items.quote: This higher investment will lead to an enhancement of capacity from 75,000 to 80,000 tons and a much lower conversion cost than envisaged.

items.statement: PLA project expected to have lowest capex per ton globally and competitive opex.
items.quote: When we benchmark globally, our capex per ton will be the lowest by far.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain EBITDA margin range of 13% to 14%.
items.quote: So margins, in fact, that has been our endeavor. That is what we have been maintaining that our endeavor is to maintain the range of 13% to 14%. We stay with that.

items.statement: Foresees gradual recovery in demand.
items.quote: And I do foresee that gradually -- I do foresee a gradual recovery in the demand. How much it will go, whether it will go back to the earlier stage, we still need to wait and watch, but I see a gradual recovery.

items.statement: Foresees higher single-digit growth for the industry over 5 years.
items.quote: I foresee a higher single -digit growth for the industry over a period of 5 years.

items.statement: Putty pricing is a challenge; no change seen.
items.quote: So as of now, we don't see much change in the putty scenario.

items.statement: Putty margins are very low, risk of losses.
items.quote: Margins are very low, maybe I don't know whether there are margins or not margins, but very, very low.

items.statement: Paint+ salience in double digit.
items.quote: And the salience of Paint+ product is in double digit now. So that's the first milestone which we wanted to achieve, and it is in the double digit now.

items.statement: New products contribution in double digit.
items.quote: And our overall contribution of new products is also in the double digit. So that's a good sign.

items.statement: New business salience crossing double digit.
items.quote: And even for new business, the salience is now crossing double digit. So that's, again, the milestone which we wanted to achieve critical mass, and we are on track.

items.statement: Services business reached critical mass around 5%.
items.quote: So there also, we have kept a milestone a critical mass, which is around, say, 5% and I'm happy to share that we are now in that particular range.

items.statement: Present in more than 80 towns in project business.
items.quote: Today, we are present in more than 80 towns now and our growth continues to be better that even if you compare with the industry.

items.statement: More than 300 shoppes and shop-in-shop in over 100 towns.
items.quote: In terms of retail experience, the total number of shoppes and shop -in-shop concept, we have more than 300 plus now in almost, you can say, more than 100 towns that we have the representation of Shoppe, which is a good experience centre and the customer can have a good touch and feel experience in these stores.

items.statement: Distribution expansion on target with double-digit increase.
items.quote: So we have been targeting double -digit increase in the distribution expansion, which we are plus/minus 1%. But even in this year, we are on target.

items.statement: Tinting machine penetration closer to 75%.
items.quote: And our -- this penetration of the machine is closer to 75%. So tha t's the penetration which we are maintaining.

items.statement: Rural share of decorative business around 30-35%.
items.quote: It is -- depend on how the rural is defined, but whatever way we define, it could be around 35% -- 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Putty contribution higher single-digit to business.
items.quote: The second is on the putty business, putty contribution may be higher single -digit contribution to the business.

items.statement: New competition may have taken 3-4% market share.
items.quote: So as of now, just a rough estimate. I may not be very strong on the numbers, but 3% to 4% of redistribution would have happened.

items.statement: Expects domestic tractor industry to grow around 6-7% for full year FY25.
items.quote: For FY '25 full year, we expect the domestic tractor industry to continue its growth trajectory with a growth of around 6% to 7% for the full year.

items.statement: Expects 14-15% growth in Q4 and decent growth in Q1 for tractor industry.
items.quote: So, Vijay, we're looking at about 14% to 15% of growth in quarter 4. So, this quarter is going to be a robust quarter. So, we're looking at a growth of about 14%, 15%. And for quarter 1 also, we are looking at a pretty decent good growth in industry.

items.statement: Anticipates temporary volume impact in construction equipment due to BS-V transition.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate a temporary volume impact due to price escalation within Construction Equipment industry due to transition to BS -V standards.

items.statement: Increased prices in line with contribution margin on increased RMC; aims to recover cost in 3-4 months.
items.quote: So, we have increased in line with what is our contribution margin on the increased RMC. And we will see that in the next 3, 4 months, we will try to recover it, but, however, given the condition that we are also approaching monsoon in Q1, so it might take a little longer.

items.statement: Cost increase for BS-V transition: 10% or more for BS-III to BS-V, 5-6% for BS-IV to BS-V.
items.value: 10% or so or slightly more than that; 5% to 6%
items.quote: So, there are certain products which are moving from BS -III straightaway to BS-V, where the cost increase for the customer is to the tune of 10% or so or slightly more than that. And products which are moving from BS-IV to BS -V, which is about 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Expects flattish year for construction equipment in FY26, with cost recovery leading to slightly positive to flattish profitability growth.
items.quote: So, we are not expecting a decline, it will be a flattish year. But, in terms of cost it varies from product-to-product. So, there are certain products which are moving from BS -III straightaway to BS-V, where the cost increase for the customer is to the tune of 10% or so or slightly more than that. And products which are moving from BS-IV to BS -V, which is about 5% to 6%. So, it's quite a steep

items.statement: Expects gradual margin improvement next year, no significant jump unless operating leverage from volumes.
items.quote: So, this similar trend will continue even in next year. So, you will see the gradual improvement will be there. But we don't see a significant jump certainly on the margin front. So, unless you see a major operating leverage playing out and the volumes start picking up, otherwise at the normal level the kind of inflation which is there and the kind of commodity price we have, we expect will have m

items.statement: Expects export tractor volume to grow 20-25% next year due to low base and European market pickup.
items.quote: So, we expect the next year we should see double digit growth and for high double-digit growth could be anywhere between 20% plus, 20%, 25% sort of growth should be there. One, because the base is also very low this year. We're not going to do much numbers. I think overall export will be close to 5,000 -odd numbers.

items.statement: Non-tractor revenue 21% of Agri Machinery; spare parts and engine 8%, Agri solution 12-13%.
items.quote: So out of the 21% sales, spare parts and engine gave about 8% and balance really comes from - 12% to 13% comes from the Agri solution, which includes harvesters, transplanters, and other implements.

items.statement: Agri business margin dipped due to harvester imports; localization to improve margins later.
items.quote: Yes. So that's the reason you're seeing there's a dip in the Agri business margin even though the top line has grown and in the harvester business has done very well in this quarter and have seen almost 30% plus growth, but since it’s a traded item right now and we are importing, so the margins are not similar as you do in the manufactured component or manufactured product in India.

items.statement: Railway division order book over INR 890 crores, excluding BMBS orders of INR 380 crores on hold.
items.quote: Order book for the division at the end of December 2024 stand at more than INR 890 crores. This order book however excludes BMBS orders for trade variance for approximately INR 380 crores, supply for which have temporarily been hold by RDSO.

items.statement: Greenfield plant in UP delayed; waiting for government land acquisition.
items.quote: But since there has been some delay in the acquisition process, so it's still going on. I think once they complete the acquisition, they will ask us to complete the balance formalities . So, we're waiting for government to revert when they complete the acquisition of the land.

items.statement: Board approved sale of land to Sona Comstar for INR 110 crores; will relocate spare part division.
items.quote: The Board has approved the sales and transfer of approximately 33,000 plus square yards of the land adjacent to Railway Equipment Business Division to Sona Comstar for a total of INR 110 crores. This industrial plot is currently being used for a spare part business division of the company. We will relocate the spare part division to a new location before finalizing the sale.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR 10 per equity share (100%).
items.quote: Board declared interim dividend at 100%, i.e., INR 10 per equity share.

items.statement: Captive finance pilot initiated; full impact expected in second half of next fiscal.
items.quote: As regards to the captive finance, it has been initiated in some states. Pilot is going on. We've identified certain dealerships and certain districts where it has got started. But the due impact of the captive finance will actually come into play in the second half of next fiscal.

items.statement: Launched Promaxx series under Farmtrac brand in 30-50 HP; expects market share improvement over next few quarters.
items.quote: So, you heard in the opening comments, Gunjan, that we have very recently launched a new product range in Farmtrac, which is known as the Promaxx series. So Promaxx series is primarily for the western market, that is Gujarat, Maharashtra, and certain markets where we are not present currently.

items.statement: Expected volume growth of at least 8% to 10% for current fiscal and similar level next year.
items.quote: So we have given some kind of an indication also in the investor presentation in terms of the expected volume growth, which is expected to be at least in the 8% to 10% range. And we hope to keep at the same level going into the next year also.

items.statement: Announced Rs.250 crores capex for capacity expansion in existing products, with debottlenecking first.
items.quote: So while we had also mentioned that the capacity which we mentioned is just for a basket of products, yes, and the basket of products are at different utilization levels. So while we have mentioned that for some of the products, there still the utilization level has some way to go and we will take time to fill it up. Some of the products are already at 95%, 100%, 90%, that range.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin was 8% in Q3 FY25 and 10% in 9M FY25.
items.quote: operating EBITDA, operating EBITDA for Q3 FY25 stood at Rs.24 crores as against Rs.38 crores in Q2 FY25 with EBITDA margins at 8% in Q3 FY25. For the 9 months ended December N O C IL '24, the operating EBITDA stood at Rs.103 crores as against Rs.150 crores compared to the 9 months of previous year. Margin standing at 10% in 9MFY '25

items.statement: Intense pricing pressure and product dumping from Chinese, Korean, Thailand and EU players impacted domestic prices.
items.quote: We have continued to experience intense pricing pressure and product dumping from Chinese, Korean,Thailand and EU rubber chemical players, which has had a significant impact on domestic rubber chemical prices.

items.statement: Lower production at customers and aggressive priced imports caused 10% volume de-growth sequentially; expect demand to pick up in next few months.
items.quote: Volume saw a 10% de-growth compared to the previous quarter due to lower demand from customers on account of lower production at their end, coupled with some aggressive priced imports as compared to the previous quarter. We see this lower production as transitionary and expect demand to pick up in the next few months.

items.statement: Prices moved in tandem with raw material prices; adjusted selling prices to maintain value addition per kg.
items.quote: Our prices for the quarter have moved in tandem with raw material prices. We have continued to experience intense pricing pressure and product dumping from Chinese, Korean,Thailand and EU rubber chemical players, which has had a significant impact on domestic rubber chemical prices.

items.statement: Tire industry replacement and export demand positive, but OEM demand slowdown; infrastructure spending expected to drive commercial vehicle demand.
items.quote: Coming to our largest and key customer segment, the tire industry. The replacement and export demand for the tire industry in India is on a positive trend, but there seems to be a slowdown with OEM demand.

items.statement: Antidumping duty investigations initiated for a couple of products; outcome expected in 9-12 months.
items.quote: We have also moved on the antidumping duty front. And we have got the investigations initiated for a couple of products and then that's quite a bit underway now.

items.statement: R&D working on value-added products to launch soon.
items.quote: On the innovation front, our R&D and application teams are working to innovate value-added products for our customers that we look forward to launching soon.

items.statement: Utilization at 65% to 70% for April to Dec 24; sub-optimal operating leverage.
items.quote: I think today, we are at about 65% to 70% utilization for the period April to Dec 24

items.statement: China Plus One playing out; product approvals and commercial lots underway with customers.
items.quote: So yes, the China Plus One is playing out. It's not limited only to Japanese. I think you could broad base it a bit more. And that traction is happening in terms of what I mentioned in terms of product site approvals, samples, commercial lots and then larger bulk lots going.

items.statement: Actively looking at diversification beyond rubber chemicals into adjacencies.
items.quote: But also we are actively looking at what other areas to look at beyond rubber. So there are some adjacencies that we can look at based on similar chemistries or the expertise that we can take into other industries that we have in quite a few areas.

items.statement: Cost control initiatives underway; conversion cost growth 5.5% on 9M basis.
items.quote: But what is more important, on the other part, we are trying to control the cost. So overall, if you see on a 9 months basis, if I take the other expenditure and aggregate the employee cost, the overall growth is about 5.5% or thereabouts.

items.statement: Inventory build-up due to higher production than sales; Rs.21 crores credit in P&L.
items.quote: And therefore, this has resulted in a higher inventory. So the inventory build-up is there. And you can see it from the stock change in the P&L account, which has Rs.21 crores credit.

items.statement: Margins per kg marginally better than China Sunsine.
