items.quote: So I think it will be a year from now where we will have the plant ready and operational.

items.statement: New plywood plant capacity about 50,000 per day for 25 working days.
items.quote: So it would be about per day capacity about 50,000 into 25 working days.

items.statement: Plywood capacity at full utilization about 80,000 CBM; expansion in West and other factories about 15,000 to 20,000 CBM.
items.quote: So the capacity at full utilization would be about 80,000 CBM. And as far as the expansion in our West and some other factories, it's about 15,000 to 20,000 CBM.

items.statement: Laminate to break even by Q2 next year.
items.quote: Here next year, by Q2, we should be looking at breaking even only as far as laminate is concerned.

items.statement: Particle board to break even at EBITDA and PAT in FY27.
items.quote: Yes, that's what you would aim for.

items.statement: Attempt to maintain similar margins for MDF.
items.quote: Yes. Our attempt will be to maintain similar margins.

items.statement: MDF prices increased by 3% to 4% blended pan-India.
items.quote: For MDF, we have taken close to 3% to 4% blended increase pan-India as far as prices are concerned.

items.statement: No price increases taken for laminate and plywood in last quarter.
items.quote: For laminate and for plywood, I don't think we have taken any increases as far as last quarter is concerned.

items.statement: Plywood industry to grow 5% to 7% year-on-year.
items.quote: Plywood as an industry will continue to grow at 5% to 7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect H1 next year to be much better than current.
items.quote: I certainly believe that the H1 of the next year will be much better than what we have today.

items.statement: MDF capacity created should be absorbed within about a year.
items.quote: So I expect that within next about a year's time, whatever capacity has been created should be absorbed.

items.statement: MDF South to reach similar value-added product mix as Hoshiarpur by H2 next year.
items.quote: But I think next year, towards H2 you will see us reach somewhere close to the same figures that we have in Hoshiarpur in the Badvel unit.

items.statement: Export obligation from MDF unit not currently on track due to high raw material prices; aim to meet within 6 years.
items.quote: Yes, we do have an export obligation from the MDF unit. And currently, we are not in line to meet the same because the raw material prices have shot up drastically, but we are working on all available options, and we are sure that within the 6-year time horizon, we'll be able to meet our export obligations.

items.statement: Plywood market share goal to reach 15% in next 4 to 5 years.
items.quote: And our goal is ultimately in the next 4 to 5 years to reach 15% market share.

items.statement: Company expects to open about 100 to 110 new screens for the whole year.
items.quote: For the whole year, the Company expects to open about 100 to 110 new screens.

items.statement: Current financial year total CAPEX will be sub Rs. 400 crores.
items.quote: For the current financial year, we will be sub Rs. 400 crores in terms of our total CAPEX expenditure versus Rs. 625 that we did last financial year.

items.statement: Next year CAPEX spends will be in the range of Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores.
items.quote: But overall, CAPEX spends will be somewhere in the range of Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Signed 100 screens under new capital-light growth model.
items.quote: We have signed 100 screens under the new capital-light growth model.

items.statement: F&B price increase of 5% to 7% on certain product items for coming year.
items.quote: We are going to be taking a 5% to 7% increase on certain product items.

items.statement: Pre-COVID at 32% occupancy business delivered 18% margin; Q3 this year at 25% occupancy delivered 15% margins.
items.value: 18% margin at 32% occupancy; 15% margins at 25% occupancy
items.quote: Just to give you some directional sense, pre-COVID at a 32% occupancy the business used to deliver 18% margin. However, in quarter 3 itself this year after 25% occupancy, the business has delivered 15% margins.

items.statement: On track to open 110 new screens this year and similar number next year.
items.quote: we are on track to open 110 new screens this year and a similar number of screens next year.

items.statement: Incrementally new screen additions will be roughly 35% to 40% in South India.
items.quote: I think, just to give you a ballpark, incrementally new screen additions will be roughly about 35% to 40% in South India.

items.statement: Management fee for FOCO model is 6% to 10% of net GST revenues.
items.quote: And we are eligible to enjoy a management fee anywhere between 6% to 10% of the net of GST revenues that get generated from the property.

items.statement: In asset-light model, occupancy cost is 15% to 20% and developer yield is 7% to 12%.
items.quote: So, in terms of the revenue, should think about it that anywhere between 15 % to 20%, 15% to 20% is the occupancy cost, which the developer would end up enjoying for giving the property. For the balance CAPEX that he has given, he becomes eligible for a fixed yield. A yield which could be anywhere between 7% to 12%.

items.statement: Rationalized about Rs. 50 crores of rental from contracted rental up till December.
items.quote: So, up till December we have rationalized about Rs. 50 crores of rental from the contracte d rental.

items.statement: 4700BC on course to cross Rs. 100 crores revenues this financial year.
items.quote: It is on its course to cross Rs. 100 crores revenues in this financial year.

items.statement: Distribution commission is 6% to 9% of total box office collections.
items.quote: So, the commission is anywhere between 6 % to 9% of the total box office collections.

items.statement: Re-releases contributed over 4% of total footfall since April.
items.quote: In fact, since April till now, close to 4.3% of the total admissions have come in through re-releases, which is the bulk which is 90% and about 10% through events.

items.statement: SCREENIT has done close to about 100 odd shows.
items.quote: So, these are early days for screen adds the only one thing that I can share with you that we have currently done close to about 100 odd shows under SCREENIT.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth from Q4 FY25 onwards.
items.quote: Now our production schedules have been streamlined and bel ieve that from Q4 FY '25, we should see a double-digit growth going forward.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth and EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY26.
items.quote: We feel that, okay, the growth will be there and we will be close to around double-digit growth. And EBITDA margins would be around 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR 30-35 crores over next 2 years for manufacturing and retail.
items.quote: Other than the requirement for our office development, there will be a capex requirement of around INR 30 crores to INR 35 crores for next 2 years, which will be primarily enhanced our manufacturing capability as well as expansion of our retail business, including some EBOs.

items.statement: Capex of INR 35 crores split 50-50 between manufacturing and retail.
items.quote: Capex, I said is around INR 35 crores, which we said it will be for the manufacturing as well as retail capability. Bifurcation should be around 50-50.

items.statement: Kraus EBITDA margin for Q3 FY25 was 20%, sustainable at 18-20%.
items.quote: The EBITDA numbers have also increased and it's around 20% for Q3 of FY '25 for the Kraus particular brand. On a sustainable basis, EBITDA margin should be in the range of around 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Will maintain EBITDA margin range of 18-20%.
items.quote: We will continue on our EBITDA margin range of 18% to 20% and will keep continuing it.

items.statement: Unable to get price increment and discounting increased due to poor winter wear sales.
items.quote: We were not definitely able to get the price increment in terms of realization. And the discounting has also increased because this current quarter is related to winter wear and winter wear was not as expected.

items.statement: Tertiary sales at EBO level grew 14% in current quarter.
items.quote: I would say on a tertiary level, okay, on our retail EBO, SSG for the current quarter was close to around 14%.

items.statement: Plans to open 50-60 Killer EBOs and 40-50 Lawman EBOs next year.
items.value: 50 to 60 stores of Killer EBOs and 40 to 50 stores of Lawman EBOs
items.quote: So we feel that okay, close to around 50 to 60 stores of Killer EBOs and 40 to 50 stores of Lawman EBOs. That would be our planning for the next year.

items.statement: Lawman stores to be COCO driven, targeting 40-50 stores next year.
items.quote: And we are planning to open close to around 40 - 50 stores in the next year itself. And the strategy for retail stores would be more COCO driven for Lawman.

items.statement: Just-in-time production strategy failed, not pursuing for at least a year.
items.period: at least for a year period
items.quote: We tried to get just -in-time productivity but we have failed in that. Because of that, my business also got hampered. We had orders in our hands but we couldn't supply that. So, what happened, as such, we will not do such a big experiment for the time being.

items.statement: Marketing spend estimated at 5-7% of overall number.
items.quote: For that, marketing activity, Deepak, we have not yet pipelined it, okay? But we estimate that on the overall number, it should be around 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Kraus staggered payment outflows of INR 50 crores over next 3 years.
items.quote: So the deal was done on a staggered payment. There will be outflows for next 3 yea rs, okay? But -- it will be INR 50 crores for the next 3 years.

items.statement: Other income to normalize at INR 8-9 crores per quarter.
items.quote: INR 8 crores to INR 9 crores is what we actually get as a realized gain on the other income.

items.statement: ROE expected around 20% for Lawman stores.
items.quote: We feel that, okay, ROE would be around 20% on the overall investment structure, should be around 20%, okay.

items.statement: Reiterates around 16%-plus growth in Cranes, Material Handling and Construction Equipment segment for current year.
items.quote: Also, we would like to reiterate our guidance of around 16% -plus growth in Cranes, Material Handling and Construction Equipment segment for the current year and expect Agri segment to remain flattish during this year.

items.statement: Overall growth around 15%-plus with stable EBITDA margins at current levels.
items.quote: On the whole, we are looking at a growth of around 15% -plus with a stability in EBITDA margins at current levels.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance to double FY23 top line by FY26 is intact.
items.quote: So we said that whatever we had achieved in FY '23, we are going to do uble that by FY '26. More or less, that's the medium-term guidance, and we are sticking to that as of now.

items.statement: EBITDA margins to remain stable at current Q3 levels.
items.quote: So we would like to have a little bit of stability in the current EBITD A margins. Of course, there is a scope because of operating leverage and pricing actions. There is a scope of a little bit of expansion also, but as of now, we would like to guide that the EBITDA margins will remain stable at the current levels.

items.statement: Capex of INR90-95 crores in 9M FY25; capacity to reach INR5,000-5,100 crores by end of Q4.
items.quote: Yes. So in 9 months FY '25, we have done a capex of close to INR90 crores to INR95 crores. And with this, we are expected to reach a capacity of INR5,000 crores to INR5,100 crores.

items.statement: CEV 5 products expected to increase realization by around 8% to 15%.
items.quote: So it totally depends upon the equipment. But genera lly, what we expect is around 8% to 15%, let's say, in that range.

items.statement: Expects anti-dumping duty on Chinese heavy cranes by March end or mid-April.
items.quote: We're expecting a favorable reply somewhere in the, you can say, probably March end or mid of April, in which we expect the government will be putting an antidumping duty on those products.

items.statement: Demand scenario remains healthy on infra side and private capex revival expected.
items.quote: So the whole urban infra space is getting revamped. And the demand scenario remains healthy on the infra side. But most importantly, apart from infra, the kind of products that we make a re also very widely used in manufacturing industry.

items.statement: Exports and defence target 15-20% of overall business in medium to long term.
items.quote: But from a medium - to long-term perspective, I think 15% to 20% coming from defence and exports seems very much on track for us.

items.statement: KATO JV production to start Q3 or Q4 FY26, full steam in FY27.
items.quote: Here, Mudit, I would like to just add a little bit that we intend to start the production in this JV by, let's say, Q3 FY '26 or maybe Q4 FY '26. So somewhere those lines, these time lines are similar to what we had mentioned in the last con -call. So things are on track with respect to that. The full steam production will happen in FY '27.

items.statement: Expects one of biggest defence orders within this quarter, revenue from next financial year.
items.quote: Yes. So we are expecting one of our biggest defence orders. It should have come by now, but it is just held up with some paper works and should be here, I believe, within this quarter.

items.statement: Plans calibrated price approach in next 2-3 quarters, focus on stabilizing margins.
items.quote: So I believe in the next 2, 3 quarters, we will start to take a price calibrated approach. But as of now, the thing that is on the top of our mind is to stabilize the margin profile of the company where we stand and if possible, it can expand a little bit from here.

items.statement: Agri segment expected to remain flattish this year due to base effect.
items.quote: And hopefully, we can grow in agri, but for the time being, we are saying that we w ould remain flattish. That time will tell if we can grow in agri, yes.

items.statement: Electric cranes ready, awaiting CMVR guidelines; few units sold in unregistered areas.
items.quote: Yes. So as you are aware that we are already ready w ith the product and we are awaiting the CMVR guidelines, which is pending some final paperwork. So once that is through, I think we'll be able to take our machines to the markets for that.

items.statement: Land deal: 22 acres done, agreements ongoing for balance 60 acres.
items.quote: So in that 82 acres, somewhere around 22 acres is already there, done. It is there in the books. And for the balance 60 acres the agreements are going on.

items.statement: Expects positive demand from February onwards.
items.quote: But going forward, from February onwards, we see some positive vibes in the market.

items.statement: Expects to commence production from Palghar plant in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: And we are expecting to commence the production from Q4 '26.

items.statement: Expects Orissa plant production in Q4 FY28.
items.quote: So there, our expectation in Orissa is Q4 FY '28.

items.statement: No reduction in raw material costs expected due to rupee devaluation.
items.quote: I don't see any reduction in the fiber -- in the raw material cost going forward on account of the rupee devaluation.

items.statement: Price increases will happen gradually over next 5-6 months.
items.quote: Definitely, the price increase will happen. And it will be gradually the price increase will happen over the next 5 to 6 months.

items.statement: Demand expected to be positive in Q4 and Q1 next year.
items.quote: So we are very positive in Q4 as well as Q1 next quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin improved by 180 bps to 43.7% in 9M FY25.
items.quote: However, we are witnessing stabilization in raw material prices, which has led to a 180 bps improvement in our gross margin, reaching 43.7% in 9-month FY '25.

items.statement: Forex impact expected in Q4 FY25 due to rupee depreciation.
items.quote: Having said that, we might witness some forex impact in Q4 FY '25 as rupee has depreciated compared to USD and as you are aware, we import one of key raw materials, asbestos from Kazakhstan

items.statement: Value-added product share was 12% in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Q3 is lower but, I think it is at 12%.

items.statement: Ocean freight costs have started reducing from January.
items.quote: Now it is already started reducing. It went, if you talk about the Dubai sea freight from JNPT, it went to $700, now it is $75 to $100.

items.statement: Demand was not up to the mark till January.
items.quote: As I said till January, the demand was not up to the mark.

items.statement: Could not increase prices due to low demand.
items.quote: Yes, we could not increase the prices because the demand is not upward. Demand was at the lowest end.

items.statement: Land acquisition for Palghar expected to resolve in 3-6 months.
items.quote: And hopefully, within next 3 to 6 months, that will be resolved.

items.statement: Targets minimum 20% growth in premium products (Maharatna and Focus Maharatna) year-on-year.
items.quote: So you can say it’s a continuous target that we have to increase minimum 20% product sale in B2C segment every year.

items.statement: Targets gross margin of 30-35% and EBITDA margin of 12-13% in next 1-2 years.
items.quote: the target of the gross margin in next 1 to 2 years of time, you can say 30% to 35% with the EBITDA of about 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Aims to increase premium products share to 65% of B2C sales in 1-2 years.
items.quote: the vision is that Maharatna numbers or premium product numbers should cross 65% very soon. So we can say in 1 to 2 years of time.

items.statement: Plans INR125 crores capex over next 2 years, majority in next fiscal.
items.quote: Capex is like we have not -- I can say about INR125 crores is going to go in the next 2 years. This year and next year, the majority of which is going to go in the next year from here, because now we are going to order some of the plant parts, but they will be coming in tranches.

items.statement: Sotanala plant to start manufacturing in 2026; first full year at 70% capacity to generate INR500 crores.
items.quote: So it will take one year. So 2026 is the target to start the manufacturing in the Sotanala site. So, these are the two which are employed. And in the subsidiaries of course, there will be some work in Kaeros and IIL Biologicals also.

items.statement: Expects double-digit EBITDA margin for the full year.
items.quote: This year, the closing should be good with the double -digit margins. We are able to maintain already 11.7% of EBITDA margin in 9 months. And I believe that the closing should be a decent double-digit margin in this entire year.

items.statement: Expects all three businesses (B2B, IBD, B2C) to grow in Q4.
items.quote: So I can say the international business, the B2B business and the B2C business, all three will be rising in this fourth quarter.

items.statement: Sees price stability and northward movement in international and Indian markets, positive for B2B and IBD.
items.quote: So we see the favourable tailwinds. There is stability in price, the monsoons have been quite good. So the water availability in the reservoirs is there. And if you look at the price in particular, I can say that it is not only stable, but we have also started seeing the northward movements in the prices in the internationa l market, which is now also visible in the Indian market

items.statement: Plans to launch new Nissan herbicide Altair for kharif season in April-May.
items.quote: And there will be a new addition from the stable of Nissan also this year, a new like herbicide, which we are going to add to our range, which will be known as Altair and which will be available for the kharif seas on in this year especially April, May, it will be launched into the market.

items.statement: Plans more than half a dozen new product launches next fiscal, including four insecticides, one herbicide, one fungicide.
items.quote: So there are four insecticides which are coming and there is one herbicide and one fungicide. So precisely, there are at least 6 products which are clearly visible now and there can be further additions because we are looking at certain more biological products also and some other segments also.

items.statement: Plans to improve working capital cycle by 20-25 days next year.
items.quote: In next year, we are again working to improve our working capital cycle by at least 20 to 25 days.

items.statement: Expects Kaeros to generate INR100 crores plus business with double-digit margin.
items.quote: But I can just give you the assurance that the net business is going to be IN R100 crores plus with a margin with a double -digit margin. That is what I can say.

items.statement: Plans to increase distributor network by 4-5% and retailer network higher.
items.quote: So broadly, you can say that in my total network, there might be about a 5% increase in the number of distributors, maybe 4%, 4% to 5%. In the number of retailers, there may be a little higher increase because, at the moment, the retailers are not covered by our ERP system.

items.statement: Expects seaweed product to cross 1 lakh liters sales in FY26.
items.quote: But in next fiscal, I believe that we should be able to cross at least 1 lakh liters of sales in the next full year, '26.

items.statement: Expects Centran to achieve 500-600 tons sales this year, qualifying for Focus Maharatna next year.
items.quote: So this year it will do 500-600 tons. 500-600 tons will mean INR79 crores of sales. So yes, whenever we get the full year of operation, then we can say that it will start making good sense actually.

items.statement: Revising EBITDA margin guidance to INR4.5 to INR5.5 per SCM due to APM gas reduction.
items.quote: No. We will be revising it to INR4.5 to INR5.5, especially in light of the APM gas reduction.

items.statement: Planning capex of around INR1,000 crores for FY26.
items.quote: Yes, we are planning close to INR1,000 crores, not less than INR1,000 crores. The budget process is going on. So we are estimating around INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Capex for this year expected around INR800 crores to INR850 crores.
items.quote: Yes, this year also it will be same. This year, we'll be having around close to INR800 crores to INR850 crores of capex would be there.

items.statement: Anticipating Morbi volumes around 3 mmscmd in this quarter due to increased propane price differential.
items.quote: So we are anticipating 3 mmscmd presently, in this quarter, we did close to 3.35 mmscmd from Morbi. Hence, it will be around 3 mmscmd now going forward because of the price differential, which has increased, the offtake has reduced now.

items.statement: Anticipating Morbi volume range of 2.75 to 3 mmscmd due to propane price difference.
items.quote: So basically, we are looking at a volume maybe of 2.75 to 3 mmscmd. That's the range, which we are anticipating.

items.statement: Increased industrial prices by approximately INR2 per SCM due to significant increase in LNG prices.
items.quote: During the quarter, we had to increase the industrial prices by approximately INR 2 per SCM. The increase was mainly on account of significant increase in LNG prices.

items.statement: Increased CNG and domestic prices by INR3 in December and January.
items.quote: No, I think we have increased the prices by INR3. In December, we increased by INR1.5 and in January , we increased by INR1.5.

items.statement: Natural gas price in Q4 expected to remain high due to geopolitical factors, may adversely impact competitiveness.
items.quote: The natural gas price during the Q4 are expected to remain high, mainly on account of geopolitical factors. The same may result in adverse impact in the competitiveness of natural gas vis-à-vis alternate fuel.

items.statement: CNG sales growing at close to 12% and domestic at 5-6%, sustaining growth.
items.quote: So for the rest of the areas, that is the CNG and the domestic customers, the CNG has been growing at close to 12%, and we see that growth coming in. And the domestic is also moving at close to 5 to 6 percentage.

items.statement: Future portfolio will include combination of Brent and Henry Hub for new agreements.
items.quote: So going forward, we will have our portfolio will have a combination of Brent as well as Henry Hub going forward. That's how we are looking at new agreements also.

items.statement: Signed more than 50 dealer agreements under FDODO scheme, targeting to cross 100 this quarter.
items.quote: We have already signed more than 50 dealers agreement with the FDODO under the FDODO scheme with a condition is that you have to build your stations within the year 1 year from signing of the agreement. So I think the clock has started ticking.

items.statement: FDODO commission rates: INR8 per kg for online stations, INR10 per kg for daughter booster stations.
items.value: INR8 per kg, INR10 per kg
items.quote: For online stations, the commission will be in the range of INR8 per kg, while for daughter booster station, it will be in the range of INR10 per kg.

items.statement: Completed hydrogen blending pilot at 8%, seeking regulatory approval to increase to 15%.
items.quote: We have completed blending and testing at 8%. We originally started with 5%, then we have increased to 8%. 8% model has also been successfully proved. So now we are gearing up our system to increase it to 15%.

items.statement: In process of signing at least 6 more CBG suppliers agreements; presently 3 suppliers.
items.quote: CBG, I think, we are the first company to have CBG connected to our network and we are recently in the process of signing at least 6 more CBG suppliers agreement. Presently, there are 3 CBG suppliers with whom either we are taking compressed biogas or we are taking gas into our network.

items.statement: Received more than 150 customer responses for propane-linked gas sales agreement, waiting for right time.
items.quote: And for your -- that propane linked GSA, gas sales agreement, we have received more than 150 customers response . We are just waiting for the right time, right moment to get into that.

items.statement: Looking at inorganic growth opportunities after transaction completion.
items.quote: Yes. With respect to your second question, yes, we are looking forward to that. Once the transaction is completed, we'll be pursuing that.

items.statement: Targets Rs. 1,000 crores revenue by FY29-FY30 and consolidated breakeven by FY27-FY28.
items.quote: We are still holding on to our ambition, aspiration of crossing, of reaching Rs. 1,000 cross by FY29-FY30 in that range and by FY27-FY28 will be breakeven on a consol idated basis

items.statement: AGEasy to become Rs. 500 crores business before 5 years.
items.quote: Absolutely, the it will be Rs. 500 crores before 5 years actually.

items.statement: AGEasy gross margin target 55-60% next year, 60%+ in two years.
items.quote: So, I think on a gross margin business, that is the first, we should look at about 55%-60% range next year, right, and a two-year timeframe, 60% plus, right? That is what we should look at.

items.statement: AGEasy to be CM2 positive in two years.
items.quote: And CM2 positive, we want to be in two years, we should be CM2 positive as well, which is including all your direct spend.

items.statement: Assisted Care capex about Rs. 10 lakhs per bed, asset light lease model.
items.quote: See, Assisted Care, t he model is capital light. We only take facilities on lease and the only CAPEX spend is about Rs 8 lakhs or Rs 9 lakhs on a bed and about Rs 2 lakhs, let us say on the operating losses with breakeven, so let us say Rs. 10 lakhs per bed is the kind of investment

items.statement: AGEasy channel mix to evolve to 55:45 marketplace:D2C, eventually 50:40:10 with offline.
items.quote: Eventually, we should end up with a 55-45, 60-40 marketplaces versus D2C. And we have been advised to cede the offline channel right now because after 2-3 years, both marketplaces and our D2C website will tend to plateau and that also we have done, so in the short term, we are focusing on 60-40 and then eventually it will become 50, 40, 10 offline kind of scenario in the next 3 years.

items.statement: AGEasy marketplace to D2C and offline ratio potentially 55:45.
items.quote: The way we see the marketplace is to D2C and offline ratio is potentially 55:45 in times to come.

items.statement: Gurgaon Phase-1 sold 82% inventory, 240 of 292 units.
items.quote: Q2 FY25 has been a phenomenal response where within the few months we have been able to sell 82% of the inventory, so roughly 240 of the 292 units have been sold.

items.statement: Noida Phase-2 prices will be much higher than Phase-1.
items.quote: While there will be a delay in Phase-2, the silver lining in the market continues to be quite buoyant and compared to the price point, we had sold Noida Phase-1, the Noida Phase-2 will be much higher.

items.statement: Committed to create 1.5 million sq ft every year; pipeline includes Noida, Chandigarh, Gurgaon.
items.quote: We are actively pursuing the Chandigarh opportunity with a stage of definitive agreement negotiation now, so our commitment to create 1.5 million square feet every year quite remains.

items.statement: 234 beds added in Care Homes this financial year, capacity now 300 beds.
items.quote: On Antara Assisted Care, we have added 234 new beds in Care Homes in the current financial year. Our bed capacity is now increased to 300.

items.statement: Close to 200 beds to go live in Q4 from Chennai and Bangalore.
items.quote: We will get live in quarter 4, which is again close to 200 beds.

items.statement: Sourcing from China to improve gross margins by about 20%.
items.quote: We have initiated our sourcing for China to improve our gross margins, already placed order worth Rs. 5 crores for 20 products which will improve our margin by about 20% and once we are able to stabilize this supply chain, will look at more sourcing from China.

items.statement: Mature Care Home to hit annual revenue of Rs. 5-6 crores.
items.quote: In the mature steady state, we will hit the annual revenue of Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 6 crores as we were saying in each Care Home.

items.statement: Noida OC application in abeyance due to sector 150 issues awaiting government direction.
items.quote: The application for OC has been kept in abeyance by Noida as some of you are aware, there is a sector 150 issues being sorted out and the Noida authority is waiting for direction from the Government.

items.statement: Rights issue at Hold co level, next $10-$12 million at subsidiary level, no hurry 6-9 months.
items.quote: As I said, the rights issue will happen at the Hold co. level, which is the first branch of funding in the next $10-$12 million will happen at the subsidiary level perhaps. Whether it happens in AGEasy or AACS we don't know.

items.statement: Sustainable margin for this industry is 12% to 15% at PBT level.
items.quote: The order profile is changing, and a normal margin for this kind of industry would be in the range of 12% to 15%. So we have always given this kind of a projection that a sustainable margin would be something around 12% to 15%.

items.statement: P-75(I) order expected next financial year if process proceeds normally.
items.quote: We are quite hopeful that if the process goes as per the normal pace, next financial year the order should be in place.

items.statement: Additional submarines order expected before 31st March this year.
items.quote: Additional submarines, we are quite hopeful that we are confident that it can be done before 31st March this year.

items.statement: Floating dry dock CAPEX of around Rs. 500 crores, with Rs. 350 crores realized next financial year.
items.quote: It is around Rs. 500 crores CAPEX is there, approximately. So that balance will get realized completely in the next financial year. Rs. 350 crores will get realized at that time.

items.statement: No decline in revenues expected next year; marginal growth possible.
items.quote: We are not saying that next year growth is not projected at 20%. We are saying that there would not be a decline in next year revenues. Growth numbers have not been worked out. There could be a marginal growth.

items.statement: Next financial year margins expected healthy, not 12-15%.
items.quote: Next financial year is primarily the existing orders where the margins are comparatively higher, better. So next financial year would be not 12% to 15%, but at the same time difficult to assign any kind of a number. But we expect healthy margins next financial year also.

items.statement: AIP order for approximately Rs. 1768 crores received in December.
items.quote: AIP order for approximately Rs. 1768 crores we have already received in the month of December.

items.statement: Refit order decision expected next financial year.
items.quote: As far as the refit order is concerned, it is still with Navy to decide. So we expect next financial year, there should be a decision.

items.statement: Submarine deliveries: first after six years from order, then one per year.
items.quote: Six years from the date of placement or receipt of order and then subsequent submarines each one year, additional one year for each submarine.

items.statement: P-75(I) deliveries: first after seven years from contract, then one per year.
items.quote: Seven years on signing of the contract for the first one and one year subsequent for the remaining submarines.

items.statement: Existing order book executable over approximately 2-2.5 years.
items.quote: Approximately 2-2.5 years.

items.statement: No deliveries expected in current financial year; next year one or two.
items.quote: In this financial year, no deliveries are expected. We are not expecting any further delivery in this financial year. Next financial year, one is definite, could be two.

items.statement: Next Generation Corvette price bid opening expected next financial year.
items.quote: Right now Navy has not indicated. So we don't see anything happening this financial year. Navy will take time for the bids to be technically evaluated, then all the deficiency documents has to be collected, and then later on the price bid has to be opened. Next financial year only it will happen.

items.statement: Follow-on projects 17 Bravo and next generation destroyers expected in 2-3 years.
items.quote: Large order is not there, but discussion is there with regard to 17, follow on of 17 Alpha, that is 17 Bravo, and with respect to next generation destroyers. So a firming up at the Naval end has not taken place, but we expect between 2 to 3 years from now, these two projects should be fructifying.

items.statement: Indigenization not expected to significantly impact margins.
items.quote: Indigenization is not likely to have an impact on the overall margins because initially there is an investment required. Some opportunities would be there, so we expect to counter both the factors with each other. So we don't see any significant impact neither on the negative side nor on the positive side with regard to indigenization because these would be the first projects where the indigenizat

items.statement: No budgetary constraints for defense orders; proposals will convert to orders.
items.quote: As far as the budgetary allocation is concerned for the CAPEX, there is an increase of around 5% on an overall basis, considering all the three wings. But our experience states that whatever is the requirement, whatever proposals are firmed up, there is no dearth of funding or none of the proposals have been stalled by the government. So as and when the proposals get firmed up, we are quite confid

items.statement: Expects high single-digit growth in Q4 FY25, possibly small double-digit.
items.quote: I think it will be a gradual recovery, month -on-month basis, and we'll be happy if we do high single -digit growth in this quarter. If we are lucky, we may end up doing small double -digit growth as far as this quarter is concerned, but we have to wait and watch.

items.statement: Water-based paint plant at Jodhpur expected commissioning by Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Due to minor delays in civil construction, the water-based paint plant is now expected to be commissioned by Q3 of FY '26, while the solvent-based plant is expected to be up and running by Q1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of putty plant at Jodhpur to be completed by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: The brownfield expansion at Jodhpur of the putty plant will also be completed by Q1 of FY '26. This minor delay is not expected to cause any adverse impact as we have enough capacity to cater to the existing demand.

items.statement: Expects Apple Chemie margins to improve in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: However, the margins have improved sequentially from Q2, and we expect it to improve by a good measure in Q4 which has always been a seasonally strong quarter for Apple Chemie.

items.statement: Incremental employee cost impact on EBITDA to disappear when demand normalizes.
items.quote: We expect this impact to disappear once normal demand pattern returns.

items.statement: Gross margins declined due to price cuts and product mix change.
items.quote: The gross margins were slightly muted compared to the corresponding period of the previous year when it was 48.4%, partially due to the price cuts taken by the industry in Q4 of last year and somewhat due to the change in product mixes which happened.

items.statement: January showed significant improvement over previous three months.
items.quote: Starting with your first question about January, all I can say is that January has been significantly better for us than any of the preceding 3 months of October, November and December in terms of Y -on-Y growth.

items.statement: Trade inventory low; expects dealers to stock up as sentiment changes.
items.quote: So, at the moment, I would say that the trade level inventory, at least as far as Indigo is concerned, is fairly low. And as the sentiment changes, we would expect the dealers to start stocking up.

items.statement: Premium emulsion segment growing fastest, bucking trend.
items.quote: As I said, the fastest growing segment for us has been the premium emulsion segment at the retail level. And that has happened because we have focused for the last 1.5 years with absolute steadfast conviction on the contractors, the painting contractors in metros, Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 towns, wherever they exist.

items.statement: New entrant impact on Indigo sales less than 2.5%, likely 1%.
items.quote: As far as Indigo is concerned, I would say that we have been even impacted to a lesser extent by Birla Opus. I don't think that with our differentiated products and with the kind of distribution network that we have, I don't see -- I mean, I won't say that the effect is 0, but I would say that the impact on our sales has probably not even been 2.5%, it would probably be maybe 1% or something.

items.statement: A&P spends as percentage of revenue expected to decline for full fiscal.
items.quote: The overall increase in A&P spends will be less than the expected top-line growth in revenues. Hence, A&P spends as a percentage of revenue is still expected to decline for the full fiscal.

items.statement: Treasury investments about INR196 crores as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: But yes, I mean, if you want, I can tell you that at -- about -- our treasury balance is about INR196 crores as on 31st December. And this is after all the internal funding that is happening for the capex.

items.statement: Active dealers about 18,600 and tinting machines about 10,800 as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: As of 31st December 2024, our count of active dealers was about 18,600 and our tinting machine population was about 10,800.

items.statement: Aims to increase tinting machine ratio to 70% in 1.5-2 years.
items.quote: And we just would like to take this ratio of 60% of our active dealers having a tinting machine to maybe 70% in the next 1.5 years, 2 years. That's pretty much what we hope to do.

name: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd

items.statement: Nashik will break even by Q2 or Q3 of next year.
items.quote: But that should get rectified by Q2, Q3, given that Nashik will break even by then.

items.statement: Thane and two Bangalore hospitals to commence in Q2 FY26, maybe early Q1.
items.quote: So, that is the reason that we may able to start full-fledged in quarter 2 all the 3 projects in Thane and Bangalore, 2 hospitals, quarter 2 of '26, maybe early in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Loss funding for Thane and two Bangalore hospitals in FY26: INR 10-15 crores each.
items.quote: But for '26 for each of these facilities, we have factored around INR 10 crores to INR 15 crores.

items.statement: No loss funding expected for FY27.
items.quote: So, I don't think we should have loss funding for '27.

items.statement: AP cluster margins to reach 30% in 2-3 years after oncology facilities operational.
items.quote: With Oncology and Mother and Child coming in most hospitals in this financial, in FY '26 and FY '27, maybe 3 years from there we should get to a 30% kind of a margin.

items.statement: International patient revenue to grow to INR 100-150 crores over time from Telangana cluster.
items.quote: We are hoping that it will go up to INR 100 crores, INR 150 crores over a period of time, just from the Telangana cluster.

items.statement: CAPEX guidance remains unchanged.
items.quote: As far as the guidance as to the CAPEX, nothing changes. It remains the same.

items.statement: Nashik incurred a loss of INR 5 crores for the quarter.
items.quote: As far as Nashik is concerned, we have incurred a loss of INR 5 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: One-time expenditure of INR 8-9 crores due to provisions and write-offs.
items.quote: And there has been a one-time expenditure towards the tune of INR 8 crores to INR 9 crores, largely due because of provisions of PBDD and general dues write-off.

items.statement: Sunshine EBITDA was INR 40 crores in Q3 vs INR 48 crores in Q2.
items.quote: And EBITDA has been INR 40 crores versus INR 48 crores of Q2.

items.statement: ARPOB growth in Telangana and Andhra to continue at same rate; ALOS to reduce to 3.3-3.4.
items.quote: That will continue to grow at the same growth rate. And there will be more efforts in trying to reduce the ALOS from the current 3.5 to probably 3.3, 3.4.

items.statement: Nashik occupancy in January was 25 beds, ~10%; revenue INR 3.5-4 crores.
items.value: 25 beds, 10%, INR 3.5 crores to INR 4 crores
items.quote: In the month of Jan, the occupancy has been around 25 beds, so that's around 10% occupancy and revenue of INR 3.5 crores to INR 4 crores in the month of Jan.

items.statement: Specialty mix: cardiac ~17-18%, others 9-10% each; perceived as multi-specialty.
items.quote: Cardiac is around 17%, 18%. Rest of the specialties like renal, neuro, orthopedics, oncology, gastro are around 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Write-offs in Nagpur mostly done; INR 50 lakh to 1 crore expected in Q4.
items.quote: In Q4 of this financial year, you will see about some INR 50 lakh, INR 1 crore kind of write-off. But over and above that, I think most part of it is done in Nagpur.

items.statement: Kollam hospital to commence operations from April.
items.quote: Kollam, which should commence operations from April onwards.

items.statement: Beauty business will continue to invest in customer acquisition, funded by its profitability.
items.quote: So, I think we'll continue to invest in the Beauty business. It's a business that has the profitability to support its customer growth plans.

items.statement: Losses in B2B and Fashion should reduce from here.
items.quote: So, we believe that trend will continue. So, losses will reduce in B2B. And in Fashion, I think as growth picks up once again for the overall Fashion industry, you'll see a lot of operating leverage in that business, too.

items.statement: Launched 6 flagship stores, with more to come in the coming months.
items.quote: As a result, we have launched 6 flagship stores across I ndia. These are large format stores, 3,000 square feet plus and many more to

items.statement: Beauty vertical EBITDA margin increased despite higher marketing investment.
items.quote: Just to add to what Anchit mentioned, as we can see from the numbers, while given the focus on new customer acquisition, et c, there is higher investment in marketing, in spite of that, the EBITDA margin for the Beauty vertical has actually gone up.

items.statement: Fashion gross margin improved to 51% from 44% year-on-year.
items.quote: seen a more than 700 basis points improvement in gross margin, which is a significant move from 44% last year, same quarter to 51% this year

items.statement: eB2B gross margin improved by 250 bps and contribution margin by over 500 bps.
items.quote: And this really helps us to improve our profitability, where you can see that in gross margin alone, we have improved by almost 250 bps, which is driven a lot by ad income.

items.statement: Marketing expenses are controllable and will align with annual strategy.
items.quote: But yes, I think it is something that can easily be controlled. It's a marketing expenses considered available expense and totally controllable.

items.statement: Beauty category has low penetration and per capita consumption, requiring category expansion.
items.quote: Again, as we've said in the past few quarters, the Beauty businesses has quite a healthy profitability, but because the penetration of the category and the per capita consumption for the category is so low, there is a lot of category expansion work that needs to be done.

items.statement: Fashion owned brands focus on five brands and shift to Nykaa channels.
items.quote: We had a handful more brands, but we've actually now decided to just focus on five and those five are listed here. We feel that the tail was not adding enough value and also obviously drawing attention and investment, whereas we feel that we want to just double down on what really are the big brands in our portfolio.

items.statement: Shein's entry is not expected to significantly impact Nykaa Fashion due to market breadth.
items.quote: I think the market is very wide, and no one brand can dominate it. So, I think that's what I do believe that it should not have a much of an impact.

items.statement: Beauty business funds expansion of new businesses through cash accruals.
items.quote: And in terms of supporting other businesses within Ny kaa, as Ganesh said, we continue to fund all of our expansion in new businesses through the cash accruals of the Beauty business. So that will continue

items.statement: B2B contribution margin improvement of 500 basis points; trend will continue, losses will reduce.
items.quote: So, we believe that trend will continue. So, losses will reduce in B2B.

items.statement: Fashion losses should reduce even more from here, improving overall profitability.
items.quote: So, we're quite optimistic that we'll continue to fund growth for all of our businesses, new and old, but that the losses should be reducing even more from here for both fashion and B2B, which should be good news for the overall profitability as well.

items.statement: Marketing income trend reversing; brands redeploying promo budgets to advertising, expected to continue.
items.quote: So, we're optimistic. We're seeing early shoots of it improving, and we don't think it's a Q3 phenomenon. We think it should continue into coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Working capital days reduction is representative of ongoing basis.
items.quote: So directionally, as you would see over the last few quarters, the working capital days have been consistently coming down. So, in that sense, the reduction which you are seeing, you can take it as a representative of an ongoing basis.

items.statement: eB2B EBITDA loss will go down over time.
items.quote: We have a positive momentum because we think that the EBITDA loss in eB2B will go down over time.

items.statement: Fashion could have had EBITDA breakeven this quarter if marketing expense had stayed under control.
items.quote: Well, we remain comfortable because if you look at it, like if our marketing expense, which became adverse from 24.6% to 30.5%, if that had stayed under control, we could have possibly had EBITDA margin breakeven this quarter.

items.statement: eB2B covers 1,100 cities; added 250 cities last year; will keep adding coverage without worsening unit economics.
items.quote: I think like we already cover 1,100 cities, which is very wide. And like you saw last year, we increased by 250 cities.

items.statement: 70% plus of orders across 110 cities are same day or next day delivery.
items.quote: And today, as we've said before, 70% plus of orders across 110 cities are sitting at same day or next day delivery.

items.statement: Beauty gross profit margin improved from 42.2% a year ago to 43.4% now.
items.quote: We have had some improvement in gross profit margin in overall in Beauty business, like it's moved up from 42.2% a year ago to 43.4% now.

items.statement: Beauty marketing expense increased from 9.5% to 10.1%; conscious investment to accelerate growth.
items.quote: And I think marketing, which is also a direct cost item, we have chosen to invest a little bit more than, say , a year ago when it was at 9.5% for Beauty and now it's at 10.1%.

items.statement: Other expenses at 12.5% now vs 12.6% a year ago; aim to control and improve EBITDA margin.
items.quote: I think the next line that we need to really work on is other expenses, which have been 12.6% a year ago and only 12.5% now. There could be some improvement in controlling those expenses and we would like to do that.

items.statement: Fashion acquired about 7 million customers ever, of which about 3 million are annual transacting users.
items.quote: So, I think today, Fashion businesses where we have acquired about 7 million customers, I'm giving rough numbers, ever acquired 7 million, of which about 3 million are annual transacting users.

items.statement: Fashion own brands contribute about 10% to 12% of GMV.
items.quote: We think our own brands on our platform is not a very large contributor. I mean we've always announced it that it's about 10% to 12%, but that was always -- we had said the GMV of our own brands to a GMV of our fashion omni -channel business.

items.statement: GCC rollout slower than expected; e-commerce pending technology stack adoption.
items.quote: However, the rollout of the stores has been slower than expected and e -com rollout is also pen ding adoption of the technology stack over time.

items.statement: KFC store expansion pace of 70-80 stores per year to continue.
items.quote: While we have doubled the store count in 3 years from Decem ber 2021, going forward, we believe that we should be able to continue our current pace of expansion, about 70- 80 stores per year

items.statement: Pizza Hut store expansion cautious, 20-25 stores.
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, again, we'll be cautious, perhaps 20-25 is what we are looking at.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin floor around 18% with flat to positive SSSG.
items.quote: And the current level, the floor is around 18%. So if you're able to get an SSSG of flat to positive, I think that should be the range.

items.statement: KFC margins stable around 18% if 5% SSSG achieved next year.
items.quote: On KFC, I would say if we are currently trending at 18% margin, if we are able to drive a 5% growth from here, let's say next year, then it will take care of the inflation. So at that level of SSSG, our margins should remain stable.

items.statement: Pizza Hut margins depend on ADS: INR47-48k gives 5%, INR50k high single digit, INR55k double digit.
items.quote: If it's in the range of INR 47,000-48,000, you are at where you are, that 5% range, which include additional marketing spends as well by the way. If you fall below that, you go towards that breakeven or even loss making. And you move towards INR 50,000, maybe you are high single digit. You need to move towards that INR 55,000 mark to go towards double digit.

items.statement: Sri Lanka medium to long term revenue CAGR target at least 15%.
items.quote: So again, we have called out our medium-term to long-term ambition. So, I think we should be at least aiming for a 15% revenue CAGR over there.

items.statement: KFC SSSG trajectory improved but consumer sentiment remains soft; no material change expected soon.
items.quote: But we would still say the overall consumer sentiment remains soft. While from an SSSG point of view, because of the base effect, you may see that it will still improve further as we move into Q4. But we don't see the environment changing materially any sooner.

items.statement: KFC expected to turn positive SSSG over next 2 quarters due to base effect.
items.quote: So hopefully, the brand will get into positive territory over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Q4 consumer demand environment challenging for KFC, no big pickup expected.
items.quote: When we enter into Q4, we still see the consumer demand environment being challenging. So, we don't see a big pickup from a demand perspective on KFC.

items.statement: KFC capex per store around INR 2 crores; Pizza Hut INR 1.35-1.4 crores per store.
items.quote: But yes, we have called out previously that KFC continues to be in the range of INR 2 odd crores per store, and Pizza Hut is in the range of INR 1.35-1.4 crores per store.

items.statement: No further room for Pizza Hut capex reduction without compromising consumer experience.
items.quote: Cutting down it any further would mean that you are then compromising on the consumer experience. So I don't see there is any much room left from a capex reduction point of view.

items.statement: KFC requires 5% SSSG to cover inflation.
items.quote: Over a longer period, we require a 5% SSSG just to take care of the inflation.

items.statement: KFC strategy focuses on core products and value offers to drive transactions.
items.quote: Our strategy of focusing on value offers on core products is enabling us to get TG momentum.

items.statement: No tangible change in competitive intensity; capacity not being added.
items.quote: We are not seeing tangibly any major difference in reduction, or tangible reduction, in competitive intensity at least for now. I'm not too sure, but I don't think capacity is being added also.

items.statement: Budget giveback of INR 1 lakh crores to middle class seen as positive for consumption.
items.quote: And the fact that there is INR1 lakh crores that has been given back to middle class consumers is only a positive. We are hoping and wondering as to how soon we will see that reflect in consumption, but that can only be a positive.

items.statement: New KFC stores open at 75-80% of brand average ADS; existing stores need 5-6% growth to neutralize impact.
items.quote: Because the new stores would come at anywhere between 75-80% of the brand average ADS. The existing stores, if they grow by 5-6%, it neutralizes the impact of the new stores, which helps you to maintain the ADS level.

items.statement: Full year revenue expected in the range of $100 million to $105 million.
items.quote: Overall, I would like to end by saying that as we had outlined during our Analyst Day in the last quarter, we had given a revenue outlook, which was in the range of $100 million to $105 million. Our current performance is definitely tracking towards that number.

items.statement: Next quarter revenue growth guidance of 2% to 3% on a sequential basis.
items.quote: Some of these projects, for instance, while we did execute, we also have to understand that some of them will go from a development phase to a maintenance phase in the coming quarters, which would mean that the revenue growth guidance that we can at this point in time give for the next quarter will be between 2% to 3%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance in the 18% to 20% range.
items.quote: We would like to be a bit conservative and then put out a guidance more in the 18%to 20% kind of a range in terms of what we see.

items.statement: Long-term revenue target of $200 million to $220 million over the next 3 years.
items.quote: And as we speak, we are also in the process of putting together a strategic plan for us to deliver the $200 million to $220 million that we had outlined over the next 3 years that we had outlined during our Analyst Day.

items.statement: Next quarter EBITDA margin expected in the range of 24% to 25%.
items.quote: On the EBITDA side, our expectation is that the margin in this particular quarter was impacted by this forex loss that we had, but we don't expect a similar sort of a charge in the following quarters, which means that at least on the EBITDA side, we will be in the range of 24% to 25% for the subsequent quarter.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 20% to 25%, aiming for the higher end.
items.quote: But long term, the intent would be to stay between that 20% to 25%, if possible, towards the higher end of that guidance, but we will continue to invest for growth is the guidance that I would like to give.

items.statement: Reinvestment of 1% to 2% of revenue into the business for GenAI capabilities.
items.quote: And some of this would need some level of, I would say, reinvestment back into the business, and that could be between 1% to 2%.

items.statement: Order book expected to be 35% higher at the end of this year compared to last year.
items.quote: Now with that context in mind, if I look at what were the order book number at the end of quarter 4 last year versus where we expect to be at the end of this year, there will be a good 35% kind of a jump in terms of the order book.

items.statement: Historically, price revisions contributed 3% to 4% year-on-year benefit.
items.quote: Typically, in the past, we have seen year-on-year about 3% to 4% kind of benefit coming in from price revisions.

items.statement: CPG practice targeting 40% to 50% growth aspirationally.
items.quote: And at this point in time, aspirationally, we are still targeting 40% to 50% growth, right, in terms of the combined CPG practice that we have.

items.statement: Generative AI work is about 10% of current fiscal work and 20% of pipeline conversations for next year.
items.quote: The Generative AI pipeline is pretty strong. I mean, even in this fiscal, about 10% of the work that we are doing is around Generative AI. If I look at the pipeline for the next year, almost 20% of the conversations that we are having are all around Generative AI.

items.statement: CPG space facing headwinds due to market conditions and client cost cutting.
items.quote: We do see some headwinds in terms of the general market conditions for CPG companies, which has resulted in their own subdued performance. And also impact in terms of their market capitalization and appetite to spend on initiatives, as a result of which there is some amount of consolidation and cost cutting that is going on.

items.statement: Forex loss of INR 6.8 crore impacted reported earnings this quarter.
items.quote: And there was a sharp movement in the INR versus the GBP and euro, which meant that for this particular quarter, the total loss that we had to book on account of the forex movement was close to about INR 6.8 crore.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to be 20% in the long term.
items.quote: If you take that out, realistically, the business should continue to deliver a 20% PAT number in the long-term.

items.statement: Cash balance stood at over INR 1,000 crore.
items.quote: Our cash balance again stood at in excess of about INR 1,000 crore as at the end of the last quarter, which reflects the strong cash generation capability of the business.

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA margins to remain in 17-20% range.
items.quote: I think for the Express Parcel business, service EBITDA margins will remain in the 17% to 20% range.

items.statement: PTL business to grow 25-30% in next financial year.
items.quote: Our own ambition internally is certainly to grow the business overall at nearly 25% to 30% in the next financial year.

items.statement: CapEx as percentage of revenue to be 5.6% or lower this year.
items.quote: I think this year we will end up with CapEx as a percentage of revenue being 5.6

items.statement: Long-term CapEx expected to settle at 3.5-4% of revenue.
items.quote: We've indicated that over the long term we expect CapEx to settle at between 3.5% and 4% of revenue, which is largely going to be maintenance CapEx, upgrade CapEx as we need.

items.statement: PTL margins to improve faster than Express.
items.quote: No, I think PTL margins actually will improve at a faster rate.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin improved to 3.8%, highest in 11 quarters.
items.quote: The Part Truckload business' service EBITDA margin has improved from 2.9% to 3.8%, which is the highest service EBITDA margin that this business has generated in the last 11 quarters, sequential improvement will continue.

items.statement: Fleet costs increased due to higher demand for intra-city vehicles during festive season.
items.quote: And as a consequence of that, supply was limited and overall pricing of the fleet went up compared to what we'd expected.

items.statement: Will sign more long-term contracts with fleet partners to lock in rates for next year.
items.quote: And our decision is that we will sign more long-term contracts with our fleet partners, locking in these rates for next year a lot better.

items.statement: E-commerce growth has moderated this financial year.
items.quote: I think overall e-commerce growth has certainly moderated, Aditya. There's no question in this financial year.

items.statement: D2C business grew ~30% YoY and SME business grew over 50% YoY.
items.quote: The heartening sort of piece of our volumes has been that our direct-to-consumer business has grown close to about 30% YoY, and our SME business has actually grown over 50% YoY, so we continue to have a pretty compelling proposition to that group of customers.

items.statement: Rapid commerce business expected to add Rs. 80-100 crores revenue through the financial year.
items.quote: I expect that this business will add maybe somewhere between Rs. 80 crores and Rs. 100 crores of revenue to Delhivery through the financial year and the margin structure will broadly be similar to the Express Parcel business as a whole.

items.statement: Rapid commerce pricing is Rs. 80-100 per order, with 50 dark stores planned.
items.quote: It's a per delivery fee and there's also a warehousing fee included in this typical pricing is in the range of between Rs. 80 and Rs. 100 per order that is serviced. We expect to set up 50 dark stores in the top eight cities.

items.statement: Incremental capital flow into industry will be severely constrained.
items.quote: I think the reality is that incremental capital flow into this industry is now going to be severely constrained.

items.statement: Corporate overheads glide path down towards 6% of revenues continues.
items.quote: They are currently at Rs. 211 crores, which represents 8.9% of total revenue versus 10.2% at the start of the year, and the broad glide path down towards 6% of revenues continues.

items.statement: Targets volume growth of 13%-14% over next three to four years.
