items.statement: US steel/aluminum tariff impact unknown; awaiting clarity on HSM codes and calculation base
items.quote: So, we do not know that yet as I told you, we do not know what the tariffs are how they will be calculated. What is the base? What exactly are the HSM codes? We do not know that yet.

items.statement: US emission regulation uncertainty; California standards to continue but represent small market share; federal green push rethink expected
items.quote: So, those will go ahead no matter what. But that represents only a small percentage of the overall US automotive market. So, I think in general, there is going to be a rethink on the whole green push in the US, that is what we are hearing from the President.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiaries review underway; European losses ~Rs 90 crores PBT/quarter may persist for 2-3 quarters; decision on footprint in 6 months
items.quote: Right now, there is a lot of uncertainty about policy, about what is going to be the way forward, is it a glo bal world, is it a regional world? So, like I said, we are undertaking a thorough review of our manufacturing footprint. And within six months, we will have a concrete way forward

items.statement: EV-to-ICE transition rethink in Europe; OEMs spending €1B+ to retool for hybrid/ICE platforms; temporary issue per management
items.quote: You may have seen announcements by two European OEMs in this week, t hat they will each spend upwards of €1 billion to retool their planned new ICE platforms for hybrid and also full ICE platforms going forward

items.statement: Consolidated 9M ROCE 16.5%; standalone ROCE net of cash ~19%; net debt/equity improved to 0.36x after QIP debt repayment
items.quote: The consolidated balance sheet continues to remain robust with ROCE of 16.5% as of December '24. More importantly, leverage has gone down as QIP funds were deployed to pay down the debt. The resultant gearing position has improved with net debt to equity improving to 0.36x as of 31 December, '24.

items.statement: Defense 9M revenue Rs 1,488 crores, up 49% YoY; Q3 revenue ~Rs 337 crores
items.quote: As of nine months this year, the revenue was Rs. 1,488 crores, translating in a Y-o-Y growth of 49%.

items.statement: Signed long-term agreement with European company to collaborate on manufacturing facility for landing gear and aerospace components for global OEMs
items.quote: we have signed a long -term agreement with a European Company to collabo rate to set up a manufacturing facility to manufacture cutting edge landing gear and other aerospace components for global OEM requirements

items.statement: L3Harris MOU for C4I defense electronics and systems; new sector entry for India
items.quote: Yes, that is a sector called C4I. L3Harris is one of the largest companies in the whole imaging and electronics that are used in defense. And this is a very large Company, L3Harris. And these are new sectors that we are getting into related to defense, electronics and systems for India.

items.statement: Semiconductor entry too early to discuss in detail; will address later
items.quote: I think it's too early to talk about that in detail. So, I think we will talk about that at some later point in time.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance maintained at INR2,500 crores
items.quote: So the guidance given for FY '26 was INR2,500 crores. That -- we maintain the same guidance. I mean, we definitely meet that.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR2,000-plus crores maintained
items.quote: And into -- if you see the 9-month results, we are on course to cross like I won't mention the number, but the INR2,000 crore plus guidance was more or less given. So that we are going to achieve.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25% plus/minus 3%
items.quote: And we'll meet the guidance of INR2,000-plus crores and on top line and bottom line. So we are on track. And as I said, it will be a good growth, more than what you are saying, it will be stronger than that.

items.statement: Board approved INR118 crore TPU extrusion line at Waluj plant
items.quote: Furthermore, we are pleased to announce that the Board of Directors have approved an investment of INR118 crores, which is a first-of-its-kind TPU extrusion line at our Waluj plant.

items.statement: Fourth PPF line capex on track for completion by September 2025
items.quote: The fourth capex of additional PPF line is on track and is expected to be completed by September '25.

items.statement: New TPU line planned capacity of 360 LSF per annum, production to start by end of October 2026
items.quote: The new TPU is expected to be completed within 18 months with a planned capacity of 360 LSF, lakh square feet, per annum. Production from this line is set to commence by the en d of October '26

items.statement: Second PPF line to be utilized 50-75% conservatively for first 6 months after September 2025 commissioning
items.quote: So you can say it will be utilized 50% to 75% conservatively for 6 months. But it will in terms of technicality and all, it will be very -- I mean, it will be up and running very fast.

items.statement: 9-month FY25 EBITDA margin at 24% on annualized basis
items.quote: We have completed and delivered 3 Capex since 2018, which has helped us to build a portfolio of newer products, which has significantly increased our revenues by approximately 2.5x and EBITDA margins at 24% based on the 9 months FY '25 on an annualized basis.

items.statement: TPU backward integration expected to improve operating margins by 1.5-2%
items.quote: We expect around 1.5% to 2% improvement in the gross margin -- operating margins.

items.statement: TPU line expected to yield INR4-5 crores annualized savings
items.quote: So the last -- to answer your last question is, yes, you are in the right direction. We will say INR4 crores, INR5 crores here and there, but you are bang on the numbers, right?

items.statement: Q3 FY25 seasonally soft due to lower IR film sales; Q4 expected to be strong
items.quote: Following an outstanding performance in the first half of the year, our performance has demonstrated a stable year-over-year growth trajectory despite the anticipated seasonal softness which traditionally impacts this quarter.

items.statement: Sun Control Films grew 15% YoY in Q3 FY25 driven by architectural business expansion
items.quote: On SCF business, we experienced 15% year-on-year growth in revenues. This growth is attributed to the expansion of our architectural business.

items.statement: IPD segment grew 24% YoY in Q3 FY25 driven by specialty films demand
items.quote: The IPD segment has grown by 24% Y-o-Y basis, supported by strong demand for specialty films such as lidding films, PCR and shrink films.

items.statement: Value-added products comprise 85% of product mix
items.quote: Exports continue to be a strong contributor, comprising approximately 74% to our performance with value-added products comprising 85% of our product mix and playing a key role in our global expansion.

items.statement: Launched Coloured PPF and Headlight/Taillight Glass Protection at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025
items.quote: We recently introduced 2 advanced PPF product variants at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025 in Delhi. The first is Colo ured PPF, which is a game changer for Indian auto enthusiast, offering vibrant color options to personalize and protect vehicles like never before. The second is Headlight and Taillight Glass Protection, providing advanced solutions to safeguard the brilliance of car lighting

items.statement: Added sales resources in Latin America and US architectural business to expand market reach
items.quote: So we have hired another resource in that area to fuel the growth for South American market, Latin America. So we are very cognizant of the fact that we need to grow continuously.

items.statement: Domestic architectural business grew 2x in 9 months FY25 with new dedicated team
items.quote: And I'm happy to announce that this team has performed so well because we made an entire new team with a new team leader. So it has performed in the architectural domestic market 2x growth as compared to last year.

items.statement: Coloured PPF priced 20-25% higher than transparent PPF
items.quote: See, coloured PPF, definitely, I can give you like in a percentage terms, it is roughly 25% on transparent PPF and a ballpark figure because this pricing and all those is decided based on the market situation, competition and all those things. But in a like comparative between our products, it is 20% to 25% at a higher price because it has got a value addition in it.

items.statement: US tariffs on China at 35% vs India at 6.6% provides competitive advantage
items.quote: And I would like to reinforce one thing that the duty on the -- our neighbours China is around 35% now, vis-a-vis our duty stands at 6.6%. So we have a lot of headroom available in US market and we are treating it as an opportunity for us.

items.statement: Cash surplus of INR572 crores as of Dec 31, 2024; zero net debt
items.quote: Our financial position remains strong and we are pleased to report that we have a cash surplus of INR572 crores as of 31st December, 2024. We continue to remain net debt -- zero net debt, positioning us well to advance our strategic projects.

items.statement: TPU capex to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: And given our strong cash flows, we will fund this expansion through internal accruals.

items.statement: Added sales, marketing and R&D headcount globally including US and Latin America
items.quote: Yes, yes. See, what we are doing is, like I said, we are deploying employees, I mean, overseas and making a new team. And what we have seen, like we feel a strong need of growth in countries where we can further grow.

items.statement: Worst-case reciprocal tariff impact estimated at 2-3% margin impact
items.quote: In the worst phase, if I say, like worst-case scenario, there can be a counter reciprocal tariff which does not affect much because it's hardly 2% to 3% difference.

items.statement: FY25 pipe & fittings volume growth expected to be single-digit, not double-digit as earlier estimated
items.quote: we will be, I think, closing the year definitely with a growth, but more likely a single -digit growth than a double -digit growth.

items.statement: FY26 pipe & fittings volume growth expected to be double-digit
items.quote: And next year, we are hopeful, I would say, quite confident of a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 pipe & fittings volume growth expected at 5-10%
items.quote: For the quarter, definitely. For the quarter, definitely.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY26; no absolute number given
items.quote: So yes, I wouldn't put a number to it. But yes, we see improvement in margins going ahead.

items.statement: PVC resin prices dropped INR3 last week; pipe & fitting prices may see some correction
items.quote: PVC Resin prices dropped by INR3 last week. And obviously, although we haven't dropped as yet, there would be some correction on the Pipes & Fittings prices also

items.statement: 50,000 MT brownfield expansion: ~25,000 MT in Q4 FY25, remaining ~25,000 MT in Q1 FY26; greenfield on hold, no announcement in next 6 months
items.quote: Out of this 50,000 tons expansion at the current locations, about 45% of that, the machines have already arrived, but we won't complete the entire 50,000 by Q4 '25. So about 25,000 tons roughly will come in this quarter, Q4 FY '25 and the remaining 25,000 will go into Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Current pipe capacity 420,000 MT, fittings 50,000 MT; post-expansion pipe capacity 470,000 MT, total 520,000 MT
items.quote: our revised, post all this expansion, our revised pipe capacity will become 470,000 and the fitting capacity will remain at 50,000 levels. So overall basis, we will be at from 470,000 to 520,000.

items.statement: Non-agri mix improving: Q3 FY25 67:33 agri:non-agri vs 68:32 YoY; 9M FY25 66:34 vs 63:32 YoY; target 50:50 in 3-4 years
items.quote: for agri, during the current quarter, our mix is 67 -33, whereas the corresponding quarter of the last year, it was 68 versus 32 on a quarter-on-quarter basis. And on a 9-month basis, current 9 months is 66-34 and whereas in the last year's 9 months, it was 63 versus 32

items.statement: Net cash surplus INR2,300 cr as of 31 Dec 2024 vs INR1,570 cr YoY
items.quote: The company continues to have a strong balance sheet with a net cash surplus of around INR2,300 crores as on 31st December '24 as compared to INR1,570 crores in the corresponding previous year quarter.

items.statement: Board to decide on returning cash surplus to shareholders; one of the possibilities
items.quote: That is for our Board to decide at the end of the year, Shravan. So, I really can't comment on that. But yes, that is one of the possibilities.

items.statement: Land bank sale: 10 acres left out of ~70; FY25 gain INR417 cr; cumulative gain ~INR900 cr; no immediate plan to sell remaining
items.quote: This year, we have a gain of INR417 crores and odd. And overall, I think... Chandan Verma: Around INR900 crores. Saurabh Dhanorkar: Yes. Overall, we made about INR900 crores from sale of land. So, we still have about 15% of the land bank with us, but there is no immediate

items.statement: PVC/EDC spread Q3 avg $517/MT, current $482; PVC/VCM spread Q3 avg $167/MT, current $165
items.quote: PVC/EDC spread during the quarter average it was around $517. And PVC/VCM split is $167 per metric ton. And as of now, speaking on today's date, the PVC/EDC spread is $482 and PVC/VCM spread is $165.

items.statement: No inventory loss expected in Q4 despite PVC price drop; channel inventory at low levels
items.quote: No, we are not expecting any kind of inventory loss also. So too early to say, but we are not expecting any inventory loss for Q4.

items.statement: Industry-wide discounting in Q3 via quarterly schemes (ended Dec 31); competitive intensity has now come down
items.quote: the competitive intensity, which I think prevailed for some time in November and early December, that has now come down because I think people are comfortable with whatever they are carrying.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028; Swamih affordable housing scheme and Dhan-Dhanya Mission for 1.7 cr farmers announced in budget
items.quote: we are enthused by the recent schemes announced by the Government of India in the last budget, the Swamih scheme for affordable housing, Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028, Dhan-Dhanya Mission which will benefit more than 1.7 crores farmers.

items.statement: Demand pickup expected in 5-6 months as liquidity improves; next couple of quarters challenging
items.quote: I think another at least another five to six months and I think the demand should start moving in the right direction again. That would be my estimation. I think next couple of quarters, it is going to be a little challenging, but that's my take on this.

items.statement: Timber costs up 8-10% in last 8-9 months; inflationary pressure to continue for at least another year, possibly two more years
items.period: next two more years or at least another year
items.quote: The timber cost this year we have seen a significant jump of about 8% to 10% on the raw material side in the last 8 to 9 months. We've been able to pass on some of it to our customers, but not the entire part of it. Going forward, I do not see a slowdown in the inflationary pressure on the raw material coming anytime soon.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin 34.2% vs 35.6% Q2 FY25 and 33.9% Q3 FY24; EBITDA margin 4.9% vs 4.5% Q2 FY25 and 4.1% Q3 FY24
items.quote: Our gross margin saw a drop from the second quarter. We ended at 34.2% for Q3 FY25 as compared to 35.6% in Q2 FY25. Gross margin in Q3 last year stood at 33.9%.

items.statement: Nine-month FY25 gross margin 34.7% vs 33.9% nine-month FY24; EBITDA margin 4.7% vs 4.8% nine-month FY24
items.quote: Our gross margins saw an improvement for the year ending at 34.7% as compared to 33.9% in the nine-month FY24. EBITDA stood at 12.5 crores, up by 9.4%, however, EBITDA margin is a percentage of sales is at 4.7% of sales, down from 4.8% for the same period last year.

items.statement: Duro premium segment grew 5% YoY but declined 7% QoQ; Tower economical segment grew 50% YoY and 30% QoQ in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The Duro segment for Q3, FY25, saw growth of only 5% on year-on-year basis, but a decline of 7% on quarter-on-quarter basis. Our economical offering segment under the brand name Tower showed a robust growth of 50% on a year-on-year basis for this quarter and a 30% growth on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Able to pass on some but not all of the 8-10% timber cost increase to customers
items.quote: We've been able to pass on some of it to our customers, but not the entire part of it.

items.statement: Employee expense at 11.3% for Q3 FY25 as company hires aggressively to build sales and operations team
items.quote: The company employee expense stood at 11.3% for the quarter as we continue to hire aggressively to build our sales and operations team.

items.statement: Rapidly increasing sales team and investing in infrastructure across the country
items.quote: We are rapidly increasing our sales team and investing in our infrastructure across the country and we expect stronger growth numbers in the coming future.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue Rs 89.82 crores, up 12.5% YoY, down 1.1% QoQ; PBT Rs 1.2 crores, up 127% YoY, up 5% QoQ
items.quote: Despite these challenges during Q3 FY25, Duroply reported a revenue of 89.82 crores which is an increase of 12.5% from the same period last year, though we are down 1.1% from Q2 FY25. The business reported a profit before tax of ₹1.2 crores, a 127% increase on a year-on-year basis and a 5% increase on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Nine-month FY25 revenue Rs 265.5 crores, up 11.1% YoY; PBT Rs 3.61 crores, up 10.4% YoY
items.quote: For the nine-month revenue, we closed the nine-month period at 265.5 crores up by 11.1% from the same period last year. Profit before tax stood at 3.61 crores for the period ended up by 10.4% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Inhouse manufacturing revenue Q3 FY25 Rs 54.4 crores, up 16% YoY, down 3% QoQ; contract manufacturing Rs 35.5 crores, up 7.5% YoY, up 2.5% QoQ
items.quote: For the quarter, revenue from our inhouse manufacturing plant in Rajkot stood at 54.4 crores up by 16% year-on-year. However, down by 3% quarter-on-quarter basis. Revenue from our contract manufacturing stood at 35.5 crores, a growth of 7½% for the year and up at 2.5% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Nine-month FY25 inhouse manufacturing revenue Rs 160.3 crores, up 11.5% YoY; contract manufacturing Rs 105.2 crores, up 10.4% YoY
items.quote: Revenue from inhouse manufacturing stood at 160.3 crores, a growth of 11.5% and revenue from a contract manufacturing stood at 105.2 crores growth of 10.4%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA Rs 4.37 crores, up 32% YoY, up 6.3% QoQ; EBITDA margin 4.9% vs 4.1% YoY, up from 4.5% QoQ
items.quote: Despite the lower gross profit margins, we saw an improvement in our EBITDA margins for Q3 FY25 EBITDA stood at 4.37 crores up by 32% year-on-year and 6.3% quarter-on-quarter basis. EBITDA as a percentage stood at 4.9% of sales as compared to 4.1% in the same period last financial year, up from 4.5% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Marketing spend moderated at 3.7% for Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our marketing spend for the quarter stood at a moderated 3.7%.

items.statement: Construction ban across NCR due to high pollution post Diwali impacted premium segment demand in Q3
items.quote: The slowdown in the premium segment is largely consistent with the challenges that we normally face in third quarter, which is driven by work disruptions related to festivities and also the construction ban across NCR area due to the high pollution levels post Diwali.

items.statement: Confident of a very strong fourth quarter.
items.quote: And we hope and we are very conﬁdent that we will have a very strong fourth quarter.

items.statement: Steady-state domestic growth 9-10%, plus 3-4 percentage points from new products.
items.quote: On a steady state basis we should be able to in the current circumstances, current market condi Ɵons, anywhere between 9 to 10% growth is possible with the introduc Ɵon of our stabilizer technology and the low end market product. I think adding another 3, 4 percentage points to that growth is not unrealisƟc.

items.statement: US operations to just break even this year.
items.quote: No, we will probably just break even.

items.statement: No price increases; prices kept constant.
items.quote: Yeah, we have not increased our prices, we have kept our prices constant.

items.statement: Indian market showing signs of slowing down, customers delaying decisions.
items.quote: So, the Indian market deﬁnitely is exhibiƟng signs of slowing down. There is no doubt about that. But it's not something that I would get worried about. It's not like a signiﬁcant. But there are signs of customers delaying decisions.

items.statement: New low-cost compressor range to launch next financial year, targeting Chinese-dominated low-end market.
items.quote: We have developed a range of machines and in the next ﬁnancial year we will be launching them. They are far more reliable than the Chinese machines and extremely compe ƟƟve from a cost point of view and far be Ʃer in performance in terms of eﬃciency.

items.statement: Stabilizer technology launched; products to market within a month in India, six months globally.
items.quote: We hope the products will start coming out to the market within the month India and within the next six months globally.

items.statement: US tariffs not expected to impact compressors; even if imposed, manageable.
items.quote: Even during the earlier regime, Trump regime, when there were duƟes imposed, compressors were not in that category. So, we don't expect it. So even if it comes, those are business challenges. Those are not going to be game changers, yeah.

items.statement: GST portal downtime caused revenue loss of about Rs 15 crore, shifted to January.
items.quote: It has lost about, I think about 150 million. 15 crores.

items.statement: One-time costs: transport about Rs 5 crore, warranty about Rs 2 crore.
items.quote: It is what Transport is about 5 crores and warranty is about 2 crores. Yeah.

items.statement: Europe growth expected low double digit, potentially more with new products.
items.quote: In terms of growth, I would say low double digit is what is possible. But with these new products that we have we could realis Ɵcally expect a lot more.

items.statement: FY25 group revenue guidance ₹450-500 crore; FY26 group revenue guidance ₹650-700 crore
items.quote: Given the cleared orders, which were on hold by customers in the previous two quarters and some revenue spillover into the next financial year, we expect the current fiscal year to have a turnover of between ₹450 crores to ₹500 crores.

items.statement: FY25 group EBITDA margin guidance 20%+
items.quote: We remain confident of maintaining a margin of 20% for the current fiscal year at group level, thanks to a diversified order book and strong project pipeline.

items.statement: Group order book ₹409 crore as of Dec 31 (Kilburn ₹368 crore, M.E. Energy ₹41 crore); plus ₹35 crore new orders in Q4 so far
items.quote: As on December 31, Kilburn's order book stands at ₹368 crores with M.E. Energy at ₹41 crores, bringing the group total to ₹409 crores. In addition, we have also bagged orders over ₹35 crores at group level in the current quarter so far.

items.statement: Enquiry pipeline over ₹2,000 crore (Kilburn ~₹1,400 crore, M.E. Energy ~₹600 crore)
items.quote: We continue to see strong interest in our offerings with a current enquiry pipeline of over ₹2,000 crores, which includes ₹1,400-odd crores for Kilburn and ₹600 for M.E. Energy across different verticals.

items.statement: Target FY25 group order intake ₹500 crore+
items.quote: Well, I would say at the group level, we expect that we will close the order intake at ₹500 crores plus.

items.statement: M.E. Energy Phase 2 expansion capex ~₹5-10 crore; Kilburn capacity enhancement plans to be finalised next quarter; no immediate capex for Monga
items.quote: Our current CapEx, which is expected would be for M.E. Energy, this is the second phase of expansion, okay? That could be maybe around ₹5 crores to ₹10 crores, let's see.

items.statement: Ambernath plant (Monga) 50% utilised, targeting 100% by June 2025; Saravali plant 70-80% utilised; M.E. Energy 100% utilised (driving Phase 2); Monga plants 85-90% utilised
items.quote: Ambernath currently as on date is 50% utilised, and I expect it to be 100% utilised by June, which I mentioned in my opening statements. The Saravali factory also is around 70% to 80% occupied in terms of the existing orders.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield revenue FY25 ~₹10-15 crore; FY26 ~₹90-100 crore
items.quote: But next financial year, Monga Strayfield should contribute anywhere between ₹90 crores to ₹100 crores of revenue. So that is straightaway ₹100 crores added to this year's top line.

items.statement: M.E. Energy revenue FY25 ₹100-110 crore (vs ₹70 crore full year FY24)
items.quote: Against that, M.E. Energy should cross the ₹100 crore mark. So we are looking at between ₹100 crores to ₹110 crores in the current fiscal.

items.statement: Kilburn standalone revenue FY25 revised to ₹300-350 crore (from earlier ₹380 crore) due to held orders
items.quote: We may not reach that figure of ₹380 crores, but somewhere we are looking at, let's say, between ₹300 crores and ₹350 crores, we should be able to achieve that.

items.statement: Kilburn standalone revenue FY26 target ₹450-500 crore
items.quote: We expect to close the order book for Kilburn in the range of, I would say, ₹375 crores to ₹400 crores. And there would be more orders coming in the next 45 days plus in the next two quarters.

items.statement: No broad slowdown seen; enquiry pipeline robust; growth in nuclear, soda ash, fertiliser, metal recovery offsetting any carbon black softness
items.quote: Well, not really. In fact, we are seeing a good inflow of the enquiries. And it has really kept us busy. Our marketing and sales team have been busy submitting offers to all our customers.

items.statement: Export order from JESA for OCP Morocco ($15 million) - largest single order; working with OCP on more opportunities; bidding with L&T for nuclear projects
items.quote: As also mentioned in our previous calls, Kilburn was awarded an export order by JESA in Q3 for the supply of rotary dryers to be installed at OCP Morocco, the largest producer of rock phosphate. This marks the single largest order ever awarded to Kilburn, establishing a strong global footprint. The value of the order is $15 million.

items.statement: Export share currently 15-20%; expected to rise to 25-30% in FY26 with Morocco, Birla Carbon Thailand orders and Monga's 80-90% export-oriented sheet metal business
items.quote: Presently it is around 15%, 20%. But with all this new orders from Morocco and other orders from Birla Carbon, Thailand and all coming and the revenue coming going ahead, this percentage is definitely going to increase.

items.statement: Raw material imports only 6-8%; rupee depreciation on dollar orders gives positive impact; no significant input cost pressure
items.quote: No not on the input cost side, but well, if there is rupee depreciation and if some orders are in dollars, then you see a positive side of it. But most of our raw material comes from within India. I think as of now, hardly 6% to 8% we import as and when required.

items.statement: Nuclear opportunity: 2-3 qualified players; order sizes ₹30-50 crore initially; vapour recovery units and coolers for nuclear plants
items.quote: Well, I would say there would be two to three players who would qualify for these kind of businesses. And as of now, in the recent past, we haven't done. We have references from the past for vapour recovery units and coolers for the nuclear power plants. So order sizes can be anything from ₹30 crores to ₹50 crores.

items.statement: M.E. Energy cement waste heat recovery boiler market ₹5,000 crore; targeting entry by FY27 with orders ₹70-80 crore each
items.quote: But the larger waste heat recovery boiler system, which is a ₹5,000 crore industry, I think that will take some time. Hopefully by FY '27, we should be able to at least get one or two large orders. Typically, those are ₹70 crores to ₹80 crores each.

items.statement: Pharma/granules project first order won; project sizes ₹40-50 crore (rotary kilns); metal recycling orders in advanced discussions
items.quote: So we are currently doing a project for granules, which is informed to you earlier. And that is the first project that we have bagged recently. So once that gets completed, I think we'll have good reference and the project sizes could be anything from ₹40 crores to ₹50 crores.

items.statement: Kilburn executing mix of rotary dryers, paddle dryers, rotary kilns; mostly with balance of plant; Monga adds RF dryers for food/textile; M.E. Energy adds waste heat recovery boilers, baking ovens
items.quote: It's a combination of all. We have new orders for paddle dryers. We have existing orders for rotary dryers. We have for rotary kilns. So it's a combination. Most of them are rotary dryers and most of them are not standalone equipment. They are along with the balance of plant.

items.statement: Mr. Joshipura (ex-Praj) appointed Independent Director; based in Pune near subsidiaries; will guide growth strategy and talent acquisition
items.quote: So we are very honoured that Mr. Joshipura has agreed to join the Kilburn Board. His experience and expertise will add immense value, especially to Kilburn Engineering's Board in terms of giving guidance to the management team on steering its part on making the company into a larger enterprise.

items.statement: Warrant conversion in FY26 to bring ₹120-140 crore; usage pre-approved: long-term working capital, capex, general corporate purposes (including acquisitions), long-term debt repayment
items.quote: So whenever any inflow will come in due to the equity raise, which has happened, it will be used as per what has been approved by the Board that has already been pre-decided as long-term working capital, some part as CapEx, some part will go for general corporate purpose, which could be any further acquisition and some part as repayment of long-term debt.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty: too early to assess; wait-and-watch approach; currently not impacting business focus
items.quote: It's too early to say. We'll wait for things to stabilise. I think the tariffs that have been spoken about for different countries, they have declared on day 1 then they're taking back on the other day. So we'll wait and watch.

items.statement: Open to further acquisitions that complement business; no specific targets currently
items.quote: Yes, we will keep looking out for opportunities.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline 3-4 years for large projects
items.quote: These projects are bigger in size. Generally, they are being executed in 3 to 4 years. Unless there is some short job, which may be completed in 1 year or so. Generally, bigger projects are completed 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: IOCL Paradip PMC-1 awarded, PMC-2 (~INR 700 crores) expected in weeks
items.quote: The PM package 1 on has been awarded to us recently, I think last week, it has been awarded to us. And package number two is expected to be awarded in next couple of weeks.

items.statement: BPCL Andhra petrochemical complex initial studies underway, major tender next FY
items.quote: Initially, it would be initial studies, pre-project activities and all those things activities will be there. Later on, it would be the major tender would come, but not in this quarter itself. It should come somewhere in the next financial year or towards the end of this quarter.

items.statement: CPCL Nagapattinam expansion on hold due to land issues
items.quote: It's -- I think the project is kind of on hold because of the land issues. So, we are yet to hear from them further decision on the project from the IOCL side and CPCL side.

items.statement: Consultancy order book target INR 8,000-8,500 crores, currently INR 5,554 crores
items.quote: In the previous conference call, you had said that the order book in Consultancy segment is expected to reach about INR8,000 crores to INR8,500 crores.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue recognition: 5-7% year 1, ~35% years 2-3
items.quote: Around 36 to 40 months. So, during the first year, the revenue recognition 5% to 7% and in the second and third year, the revenue recognition is around 35%.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi office doing well with ADNOC assignments, targeting Middle East growth
items.quote: But definitely, with respect to the overseas business like our Abu Dhabi office is doing pretty well. They are doing a lot of assignments, engineering assignments. They have been getting a lot of projects, engineering -- midsized consultancy projects from the ADNOC group of companies in the Offshore segment and the Onshore oil and gas segment in the refinery and petrochemical segment.

items.statement: International consultancy order inflow ~INR 40-50 crores per project, multiple midsized projects
items.quote: Around INR40 crores, INR 50 crores each. So, there will be many such projects accumulated many such projects. It will be midsized projects, totally accumulated and they add to the book business for -- apart from that, there are certain projects, major projects are also EPCM projects are also in the bidding phase.

items.statement: Expanding beyond hydrocarbons into infrastructure (44% of segment), metallurgy, coal gasification, green hydrogen, data centers
items.quote: You must have seen the infrastructure has grown from earlier 25% to 44% in this segment. So, we're getting a lot of assignments in the infrastructure segment also. So, all the segments would be contributing in these efforts.

items.statement: Government approved incentives for coal gasification projects, bidding underway
items.quote: We are bidding for the upcoming coal gasification projects wherein the government has given some -- approved the incentives for the upcoming coal gasification projects, which are there on the anvil. So, we'll be targeting those.

items.statement: West Coast Refinery future uncertain, may not proceed or split into two refineries
items.quote: West Coast Refinery, we do not know the future of it because we have been hearing like it's always published in the paper that may not come. They might decide to go for two refineries at two different locations. So, we don't see any future at this point of time for this refinery.

items.statement: Cash on books ~INR 1,000 crores at end of Q3
items.quote: Cash is around INR1000 crores.

items.statement: Expect substantial turnover increase in FY26, FY27 from strong order book execution
items.quote: So going forward in the financial year '26, '27, there will be a substantial increase in the turnover. We are expecting an increase in the turnover.

items.statement: 9M FY25 order inflow ~INR 7,000 crores, ~130% growth vs 9M FY24
items.quote: First question on the order inflow, which we have received during the 9 months is close to INR 7,000 crores compared to -- which is almost 130% growth compared to 9-month period of last year.

items.statement: Bina and Kochi refinery expansions expected within 1 year
items.quote: There are two refineries who are sort of thinking of expanding -- thinking of going for the expansion in the times to come. So that would definitely happen within 1 year time. The Bina refinery and the Kochi refinery, both of them would be expanding.

items.statement: Oil-to-chemical projects: 4-5 feasibility studies ongoing, 2-3 expected to materialize in a year
items.quote: There are 4, 5 such kind of projects and studies are on. At least 2 or 3 should realize, and 2 or 3 should be materialized in the times to come in a years' time.

items.statement: Successfully winning competitive bids despite being a Government of India company
items.quote: We are very much competitive. We are bidding very -- despite being the -- facing various challenges being the Government of India -- company, but still, we are getting the jobs on competition basis and very successfully getting those assignments.

items.statement: Focus on employee productivity improvement and brand visibility enhancement
items.quote: Management has put in a lot of focus on the new sectors, new areas, improvement of efficiency of the working productivity of the employees. All these segments, we have been focusing not only on the business, all the fronts, new technology initiatives, visibility of company as a brand in the market.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target over 6% for FY25 and 7-8% for FY26
items.quote: We see from this year, as we begin the quarter Q4, Jan to March, the impact of GPI which will start coming in, which is already rolled out, and we see the EBITDA margin ending in the year over 6%.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 8-10% from FY25 onwards, 10% above market growth
items.quote: We see ourselves growing it in the range of 8 to 10% from this year onwards. If you see FY '25 onwards, we see ourselves growing at 8-10%.

items.statement: Gross margin target 27% for FY25 and 29% by FY27
items.quote: So, we are right now at 26.2 for 9 months. So, we, for the current year itself, we are looking at 27. So, as you said, 29% for '27 is very much in sight and very much doable.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 11 crore spent so far in FY25, budget of Rs 15 crore for FY25 and Rs 20 crore for FY26
items.quote: So, we had done a CAPEX of 11 crores so far. There is small CAPEX which could complete the 15 crore budget for the current year. Next year also we are keeping a budget of 20 crore CAPEX.

items.statement: Opened new surface transshipment center in Vijayawada; plan to open 8 new hubs by end of FY26
items.quote: On the infrastructure front, I am pleased to share that during the quarter, we have opened our new surface transshipment center in Vijaywada, and we plan to open eight new hubs by the end of Financial Year 2026.

items.statement: 8 of 21 large STCs renovated; 6-7 more to be upgraded in next 12 months
items.quote: And we have now renovated of the 21 large Surface Transshipment Centers we have across the country, 8 have been renovated with the upgradation of infrastructure, newer sites, more cross docking bays, dock levelers, MHE machines. And in the next 12 months, we have identified 6 to 7 such STCs to further upgrade them.

items.statement: General Price Increase (GPI) rolled out; single-digit realization so far, improving month-on-month through March and into June
items.quote: As of today, we have realized a single-digit GPI realization, and that will improve month-on-month into March, and as I said, month-on-month into June.

items.statement: Express business gross margin improved 340 bps YoY to 25% in Q3 FY25; 9-month gross margin 26.2% vs 24% YoY
items.quote: Corresponding gross margin has improved by over 340 bps year-on-year and stands at 25% for Q3 FY '25 as compared to 21.7% for the quarter ended December 2023.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 4.8% in Q3 FY25 vs 1.6% YoY; 9-month Express EBITDA margin 5.4% vs 3.5% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q3 FY '25 stood at 4.8% as against 1.6% during Q3 FY '24 on consolidated basis.

items.statement: Highest ever volume in Q3 FY25; Express tonnage 331,000 MT in Q3 FY25 vs 319,000 MT YoY and 313,000 MT QoQ
items.quote: Another milestone that I would like to highlight here is that Allcargo Gati has registered its highest ever volume in the quarter ended of December 2024.

items.statement: Average DSO reduced to 68 days in Q3 FY25, lowest since Q1 FY24, down from 74 days YoY
items.quote: We are able to reduce our average DSO to 68 days in Q3 FY '25 which is lowest in since Q1 FY '24. For the last quarter of the similar corresponding year, our DSO was 74 days.

items.statement: Sold one fuel pump in Belagavi for Rs 3 crore; process underway to sell remaining two
items.quote: In line with our strategy to exit non-core businesses during the quarter, we have announced the sale of one of our fuel pumps in Belagavi for a realization of 3 crores. We are in the process of selling the remaining two fuel pumps.

items.statement: Quick commerce B2B business growing very strongly with three large players; FMCG only single-digit contributor
items.quote: Yes, very good growth. We are growing much higher than the growth of the market. We operate with the large three quick commerce players who deliver shipments to your homes. So, that business is growing very, very strongly.

items.statement: MSME and retail client mix improvement delayed due to MSME stress; cautious approach until macro improves
items.quote: You will also be very, very cognizant of the fact that MSMEs are under a lot o f stress because of the, you know, environment that we have on the front and because of that stress, we are kind of approaching them with a little bit of caution and sensitivity

items.statement: Organized sector gaining share from unorganized due to formalization (e-way bill, GST); no real dent from unorganized sector
items.quote: So, we are seeing that swing happening from unorganized to the organized market. So, we are very happy that that is the situation we are currently in. So, no real competition or impact or dent from the unorganized sector on the organized.

items.statement: Express logistics market expected to grow at 11% CAGR to 2029; company targets 8-10% growth
items.quote: So, 2-3 years, the market is expected, this Express business market I think is slated to grow at 11% from current year onwards to, let's say, 2029, if you see.

items.statement: Oracle Fusion ERP live; full modules go-live from July 1, 2025
items.quote: Another milestone we achieved on the ERP front where our Oracle Fusion ERP is up and live and which will finally go live from 1st July from all the modules point out.

items.statement: MSME stress and inflation impacting retail/MSME acquisition pace; GPI tail extends to June due to RFQ cycles
items.quote: MSMEs are under a lot o f stress because of the, you know, environment that we have on the front and because of that stress, we are kind of approaching them with a little bit of caution and sensitivity

items.statement: Capex for current year will be lower than FY2024 and continue to unwind in FY2026
items.quote: We believe that our capex for the current year will be lower than FY2024, and this will continue to unwind in FY2026.

items.statement: Q3 capex was Rs 6,860 crore; rolled out 5,214 sites and 13,950 route km of fiber
items.quote: Capex for the quarter was 6860 Crores. We rolled out 5214 network sites and over 13,950 route kilometers of fiber in the quarter.

items.statement: Radio capex has decelerated significantly and will continue to decelerate next year; transport, homes, B2B and data centers remain key capex areas
items.quote: Radio, which has been a substantial part of our capex. This one has decelerated very, very significantly, and we expect it to continue to decelerate next year.

items.statement: Planning to transfer ~16,100 towers (12,700 from Airtel, 3,400 from Hexacom) to Indus Towers
items.quote: we are planning to transfer about 16,100 telecom towers, approximately 12,700 from Bharti Airtel and about 3400 from Bharti Hexacom to Indus Towers.

items.statement: Hexacom EBITDA margin 53% (+300 bps QoQ); EBITDAaL margin 46.3%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs.1194 Crores with EBITDA margin of 53% improving by almost 300 bps. EBITDAaL, which is the new terminology that we have introduced, and the right one to monitor the organization’s performance, for the quarter was 1042 Crores with a margin of 46.3

items.statement: Airtel Business revenue ~Rs 5,650 crore, up 8.7% YoY
items.quote: Airtel Business we delivered revenue of just under 5650 Crores. This is a growth of 8.7% over the same period last year.

items.statement: ARPU rose to Rs 245 from Rs 233 QoQ; drivers: feature-to-smartphone, prepaid-to-postpaid, data monetization, international roaming
items.quote: ARPU came in at Rs.245 compared to 233 last quarter; another quarter of industry leading growth. ARPU drivers on an underlying basis remain intact; these are basically feature phone to smartphone upgrades, prepaid to postpaid upgrades, data monetization, and growth of international roaming.

items.statement: Hexacom ARPU grew 5.7% QoQ to Rs 241
items.quote: The company delivered another quarter of industry leading ARPU growth of 5.7% to reach 241.

items.statement: 5G base reached 120M; 5G handsets >80% of smartphone shipments
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a 5G base of 120 million, 5G shipments continue to grow now contributing over 80% of overall smartphone shipments and we continue to get our fair share from growing 5G handset adoption.

items.statement: Airtel Finance: 1M+ customers served, Rs 4,600 crore disbursed, AUM Rs 2,500 crore; Payments Bank: 87M monthly transacting users, ARR ~Rs 2,800 crore (+50% YoY), deposits Rs 3,300 crore (+42% YoY)
items.quote: Airtel Finance has served over a million customers till date across various financial products with over 4600 Crores of total disbursement and a current AUM of 2500 Crores. On the Payments Bank, the monthly transacting users stood at 87 million, annualized revenue run rate now is about 2800 Crores, growing at 50% year-on-year. Deposits remain robust at over 3300 Crores growing by 42% year-on-year.

items.statement: Partnered with Bajaj Finance to create large digital financial services platform; Airtel to offer Bajaj's 27 product lines on Thanks App and stores
items.quote: To increase supply, we partnered with Bajaj Finance to create one of India's largest digital platforms for financial services. The partnership combines Airtel's digital platforms and omni-channel capabilities with Bajaj Finance portfolio of 27 product lines and strong underwriting strength.

items.statement: Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) Rs 9,440 crore in Q3
items.quote: We delivered strong operating free cash flow; this is really EBITDAaL minus capex of 9440 Crores.

items.statement: Free cash flow to be used for deleveraging, step-up in dividend, and selective prudent M&A/bolt-on acquisitions
items.quote: Opportunities for free cash flow, I think, will be some amount of deleveraging, which will continue as you also pointed out. There will be a step-up of dividend for sure and that is a second area of free cash flow and the third, we will be selective and very prudent in any investments we make.

items.statement: ARPU still lowest globally; further tariff repair needed for industry financial stability
items.quote: Finally, I want to underscore that ARPU in India continues to be the lowest globally. Tariff repair is needed some more for the industry to be financially stable and deliver reasonable returns on a sustained basis.

items.statement: Exceptional charge of Rs 1,400 crore in Hexacom from periodic asset/liability review; provision for regulatory dues; one-time, no cash payout
items.quote: Well as any other organization, there is a periodic review of the carrying value of various assets and liabilities, so in that review, it was felt that there is a provision which has to be taken. There were also some reversals on account of the recent court judgement on passive infrastructure, it is a combination of this. There is no cash payout or anything of that sort.

items.statement: FWA ready on SA architecture; can launch immediately; currently on NSA; thousands of customers tested for 3-4 months
items.quote: we have already tested fully the SA solution for FWA, we have proven it, and given the empty network, we are not seeing any uplink differentiation. Secondly, we are fully ready to launch FWA, like if it can be done tomorrow morning, we can do it tomorrow morning if we want to and so, we will do it at the point that we need to.

items.statement: Transport blueprint accelerated over last 2 years; using fiber nodes, FTTH, and E-band microwave; now largely caught up with blueprint
items.quote: about two years back, we created a five year transport blueprint and all we are doing is trying to accelerate that blueprint. For the last two years the only effort has been to say do more, do more, do more so that that blueprint is actually met. We are not yet in line with exactly where that blueprint is, but every month in the last eight quarters, every quarter we have made progress and we are n

items.statement: EBITDAaL introduced as key metric: Q3 consolidated EBITDAaL Rs 16,306 crore at 49.3% margin; Hexacom EBITDAaL Rs 1,042 crore at 46.3% margin
items.quote: We are now reporting EBITDAaL, which is EBITDA after lease obligations. We believe this is a true reflection of our underlying margin and leverage. As a management team, this is a metric we track so as to drive the right behavior about the underlying health of the business. EBITDAaL for the quarter stood at 16,306 Crores with a margin of 49.3%.

items.statement: Gaana expected to break even in next 4 to 5 quarters
items.quote: As Gaana revenues continue to scale, losses are narrowing, reinforcing our expectation that the business will likely break even in the next 4 to 5 quarters.

items.statement: Full impact of Gaana price revision to reflect from FY26
items.quote: Since our pricing plans follow our annual subscription model, we expect the full impact of the price revision to reflect from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Radio volumes down 3% YoY due to shorter festive season and weak economy
items.quote: The volumes have gone down by about 3% over last year. And that comes from a point of view, that there was a shorter festive season.

items.statement: Overall ad sales muted across media; shift to experiential marketing
items.quote: If you look at the market factors also, there is a shift in media, which is moving towards more experiential marketing rather than advertising sales.

items.statement: EBITDA excluding digital at INR38.8 crores with 28% margin
items.quote: EBITDA excluding digital stood at INR38.8 crores with EBITDA margins at a healthy 28%.

items.statement: Margin pressure due to product mix shift from radio to events
items.quote: It's a product mix change. If you do more events and less radio , , radio is more profitable than any other business.

items.statement: Concerts have lower margins than managed events
items.quote: If you look at the media business or the experiential business, the concerts will generally have a less margin compared to managed events.

items.statement: Non-FCT segment grew 21% YoY to INR50 crores driven by events
items.quote: On the other hand, the non -FCT segment witnessed strong momentum, growing 21% year -on-year to INR50 crores.

items.statement: Digital revenue INR15.4 crores, up 151% YoY; Gaana revenue INR12.6 crores
items.quote: Our digital business continued to deliver exceptional growth with revenue reaching INR15.4 crores, up by 151% year-on-year, largely fuelled by the strong performance of Gaana.

items.statement: Gaana annual pack price increased from INR299 to INR599 in July 2024
items.quote: As you may recall, we launched an updated version of Gaana in July 2024 with a revised pricing moving from INR299 to INR599 for our annual pack pricing.

items.statement: Radio yields flat QoQ but 25% below pre-COVID levels
items.quote: So, on overall radio yield on quarter-on-quarter, we're almost about flat. But pre-COVID level, as I said, it's about 25% down.

items.statement: Radio revenue at 75-80% of pre-COVID levels
items.quote: So, if I just compare radio to radio, it could be about 75% to 80% of pre-COVID levels.

items.statement: Invested INR10.5 crores in digital during quarter, down 26% from Q1
items.quote: We remain committed to strengthening our digital offerings, investing INR10.5 crores during the quarter, which is almost 26% down over Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Gaana cash burn INR10 crores in Q3, 25% less than Q1
items.quote: So, this quarter, we burned about INR10-odd crores, which is almost 25% less than what we spent in Q1.

items.statement: Radio utilization 71% (11 minutes/hour inventory); significant headroom
items.quote: It's about 71% the way we count, but at an inventory level, it's about 11 minutes an hour. So, there's a lot of volume available on that for us.

items.statement: Radio 63% of total revenue YTD vs 71% last year; digital 26% of radio revenue
items.quote: At YTD levels, radio contributes to 63% of our total revenues compared to almost 71% last year.

items.statement: Auto, jewellery, health/pharma performed well; real estate, consumer durables, apparel weak
items.quote: I would say auto has done well relatively because of last year impact. Last year, auto was not doing so well. So, from a base point of view, automobile and health and pharma has done reasonably well plus the jewellery section.

items.statement: Radio maintains 27% market share; Gaana competes with Spotify in paid market
items.quote: However, pricing remained stable, and we continue to maintain our revenue leadership position in the segment with a healthy 27% market share.

items.statement: Gaana paid subscriber growth ~15% YTD; blended ARPU ~INR300
items.quote: At YTD levels, our paid subscriber growth has been healthy and in the range of approximately 15%.

items.statement: Gaana paid market share increasing quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Our paid market share is also increasing quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance INR344 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a cash balance of INR344 crores as of December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Consistent dividend policy; will evaluate payout now that Gaana stabilizing
items.quote: The way we look at it is, for us, we have been consistent on the dividend policy from day 1 for every year-on-year.

items.statement: Ad sales model in transition across media; vanilla advertising muted
items.quote: The overall ad sales business is going through a shift, it is in a transition phase, and we'll have to weather that storm.

items.statement: Management expects next financial year to be better than current year
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic that the positive cycle for the textile sector may start in the next financial year.

items.statement: Spinning capacity utilization at 97% for 9 months FY25 vs 91% last year
items.quote: Our spinning capacity used in current 9 months was 97% against 91% in the corresponding period.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 42% in Q3 FY25, up 4% YoY; EBITDA INR7 cr vs -INR1 cr YoY
items.quote: For Q3 '25, our consolidated total income came in at INR658 crores. Gross margin was at 42%, which was higher by 4% on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA is at INR7 crores from minus INR1 crore for the corresponding period.

items.statement: EBITDA margins low due to demand-supply mismatch; expected to improve when demand emerges
items.quote: And that should keep on improving going forward. But the demand has to emerge and for which we are optimistic.

items.statement: Shifting mix from apparel to non-apparel; adding value-added products like lycra twisted and core spin yarns
items.quote: We are changing product mix to some extent like from apparel to non-apparel, we are increasing. We are going in value-added products like lycra twisted yarn and lycra core spin yarn.

items.statement: Spent INR50 cr this year on automation and modernization in dyed yarn
items.quote: This year also we have spent INR50 crores for different types of automation and other things which can be possible and something like that.

items.statement: Recycled fiber unit running at 110% capacity (130 t/day vs 120 t/day); Q3 production 12,000 tons
items.quote: 120 tonnes/day, whereas we have produced 130 tonnes/day. But the point here is that basically this unit was set up for captive consumption to have the better quality of yarn because otherwise, when we used to purchase from outside, there used to be variation in the supply of the fiber. So that was basically meant for our own fiber. But having said so, there has been an increase in the PET bottle p

items.statement: PET bottle-fiber price delta narrowed by INR3-4/kg vs last year, pressuring recycled fiber margins
items.quote: It is basically the delta between the PET bottle and the fiber price. So the last year delta used to be higher by INR3 to INR4 per kg. And this year, in this quarter, particularly, delta has been lower by that much amount.

items.statement: Tightened credit to domestic wholesalers in home textiles due to payment issues; exports to Middle East suffered
items.quote: Secondly, we intentionally reduced our domestic sales to some extent, particularly to the wholesalers because we find that the payment issue is coming there. So we have tightened our credit to the domestic wholesalers, not for other things.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation helps margins on US exports but competing currencies depreciated more; limited benefit overall
items.quote: Depreciation of rupee will definitely improve the margin, but in products which we export to USA. If you talk to other countries like South Korea or any other country, the depreciation in their currency has been much more than our currency. So there, we don't get benefit. So it is the competing countries currency, we say it's rupee versus dollar. So wherever it is and whatever we are exporting to

items.statement: Government imposed 20% or INR115/kg customs duty on imported knitted fabrics to restrict China imports
items.quote: Another step taken by government is the imposition of custom duty of flat 20% or INR115 per kg, whichever is higher on imported knitted fabrics. This will restrict such imports from China and is a very positive step for domestic yarn manufacturing.

items.statement: Employee cost at 15% of turnover vs peers at 10%; workforce optimization and automation underway; expects improvement in FY26
items.quote: If you will see the next year, say FY25-26, I am hopeful that the percentage will come down.

items.statement: Domestic demand muted due to geopolitical uncertainty; expects improvement from budget measures, lower rates, better crops
items.quote: We are optimistic about the prospects and the Indian domestic market is expected to boost up on the benefits given in the budget, but the situation at present remains muted due to wait-and-watch approach regarding the geopolitical landscape, post Trump administration's uncertainties and its implications for the trade.

items.statement: Value-added yarn share normally 15-20% but currently lower due to recessionary demand for cheapest yarn
items.quote: Normally, we used to have about 20% of the value-added yarn, but it is fluctuating now. Because in such recession times when the demand is low, people want the cheapest type of yarn. They don't need those type of yarn except for specific application. So demand of those type yarn is a little lower at this point of time. But we hope that as the things improve going forward, the demand will again com

items.statement: Chinese currency depreciated more than rupee; new import duty will curb knitted fabric imports from China
items.quote: s currency is depreciated much more than us. So suppose China is exporting to USA, and we are exporting to USA, we are in the same boat. And if China is exporting to some other sum Laxl:ins and industries limited Sutlej Textiles and Industries Limited February 1 0, 2025 country, we are also exporting to same country, we are almost in the same boat. But where Indian market is concerned, it's a diff

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio maintained below 1, currently at 0.85; focus on strengthening balance sheet
items.quote: We have consistently maintained our debt-equity ratio below 1. Presently, it is at 0.85.

items.statement: No volume growth in yarn as all spindles operating; home textile export volumes flat, domestic volumes intentionally reduced
items.quote: As I mentioned to you, if you compare Q2, Q3, since we have operated all the spindles in Q2 as well as in Q3, there has not been any volume growth because until unless the demand pattern changes, volume growth cannot happen. If you talk of the home textile, in exports, our volume growth has been the same. And in domestic, of course, intentionally, we have reduced our volume there.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, Red Sea crisis, Trump policy uncertainty, and competing country currency depreciation are key risks
items.quote: Positioning of key countries like Turkey has been worsening due to continuous increase in the interest rates, and consequent negative impact on the demand of the dyed yarn. Further, the positioning of tariff may take some more time to stabilize. The fourth quarter will be of particular importance as it will set the tone for the next financial year.

items.statement: Hospital margin guidance for FY25 is around 20.5%
items.quote: Yes. So we are maintaining our margin guidelines where we have said for the current financial year, we should be for Hospital business around 20.5% and for the Diagnostic bu siness around 21%, 22

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is around INR 900 crore including INR 600 crore expansion and INR 300 crore maintenance
items.quote: So, capex for all the brownfield projects that we are moving forward and there is a capex requirement for normal maintenance also. So , total capex need for a year is around INR 900 crore, which includes expansion -related need of around INR 600 crore and INR 300 crore is basically maintenance capex.

items.statement: Hospital revenue growth guidance medium-term around 14% year-on-year
items.quote: I will say ARPOB growth will be in the range of 5% to 6% going forward. And I'm first talking of the Hospital business, and our revenue growth should be somewhere around 14% year -on-year.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guidance going forward 5-6%
items.quote: I will say ARPOB growth will be in the range of 5% to 6% going forward.

items.statement: Diagnostics growth expected to reach industry levels of 8-10% by Q2 FY26
items.quote: And we are hopeful that by the second quarter of next year, we would be able to reach industry levels of growth.

items.statement: Brownfield bed additions estimated at 350-400 beds per year including FY26 and beyond
items.quote: Yes. So we are estimating around this number, 350 to 400 type of number year -on-year. It all depends how quickly we can operationalize our brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Manesar greenfield facility started with 53 beds, another 50 beds to open, targeting breakeven at INR 9 crore monthly revenue by Q1 FY26
items.quote: You are right. So currently, the hospital is functional. We have opened only 53 beds right now. Maybe another 50 beds, we will be opening by

items.statement: Hospital occupancy improved to 67% in Q3 FY25 from 64% in Q3 FY24, occupied beds up 6.2% to 2,790
items.quote: Hospital occupancy improved to 67% compared to 64% in Q3 of financial year '24. This translated into occupied beds increased by 6.2% to 2,790 beds compared to 2,627 beds in Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin 19.4% in Q3 FY25 vs 16.9% in Q3 FY24, up 250 bps
items.quote: Our consolidated operating EBITDA increased 32% to INR 375 crores, delivering a margin of 19.4% versus 16.9% in Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Hospital operating EBITDA margin 20% in Q3 FY25 vs 18% in Q3 FY24, up 200 bps

items.statement: Aims to become 1,000-bed hospital chain within next 2 to 3 years.
