items.statement: Planning to raise up to ₹600 crores through QIP.
items.quote: To support our strategic expansion plans, we are planning to raise up to ₹600 crores through the QIP route.

items.statement: QIP proceeds to open company-owned stores.
items.quote: The proceeds from the QIP will be utilized to open company-owned stores.

items.statement: Majority of QIP funds for inventory, smaller portion for CAPEX including store development.
items.quote: Right, we are raising fund ₹600 crores. The majority of the funds will be allocated to inventory, with a smaller portion used for CAPEX, including store development.

items.statement: Aiming to double stores within next 2-3 years, opening 10 more stores.
items.quote: Right. We are undertaking a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) to significantly boost our store expansion, aiming to double them within the next 2-3 years. Additionally, we are planning to open a few franchises as part of our growth strategy, pursuing both avenues to achieve our goals.

items.statement: Plan to open 2-3 franchises within next 2 years.
items.quote: We plan to open 2 -3 franchises within the next 2 years, with further expansion to follow. Initially, our focus is on establishing these first few franchises.

items.statement: Aiming to improve current margins, targeting an increase of 20%-25% with focus on wedding, collection, diamond, studded, and Polki jewelry.
items.quote: We are definitely aiming to improve our current margins, targeting an increase of 20%-25% with continued focus on wedding jewelry, collection jewelry, diamond jewelry, studded jewelry, and Polki jewelry.

items.statement: 50%-55% of revenue from wedding jewelry.
items.quote: So, almost like the 50%-55% is coming from the wedding jewelry.

items.statement: White gold and rose gold jewelry contribution is 10% to 15%.
items.quote: So, the White Gold and Rose Gold jewelry contribution is nothing very much, but yeah, 10% to 15% is the total contribution.

items.statement: Inventory price is 8%-10% lower than market, naturally hedged if market falls.
items.quote: So, we are doing the weighted average method. So, our inventory price and market price is different. So, as of now our inventory price is lower than the market around like 8% -10% lower than the market. If market goes down so we are already hedged.

items.statement: Expect organized sector's market share to increase to 50% by FY29.
items.quote: Mandatory hallmarking and rising compliance costs are further steering consumers towards organized jewelry retailers, and we expect the organized sector’s market share to increase to 50% by FY29.

items.statement: New showroom in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, spans 7,700 sq. ft. with Ground+3 layout.
items.quote: As per the guidance for FY25 strategic expansion, we launched a new showroom in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, during Q3 FY25. This showroom spans a super built-up area of 7,700 sq. ft. with a modern Ground+3 layout, located just 150 kilometers from our registered and administrative office in Ratlam.

items.statement: Second showroom in Ratlam to have carpet area of 12,000 sq. ft., expected launch by end of FY25.
items.quote: Additionally, the construction of our second showroom in Ratlam is progressing well. This showroom will have a carpet area of 12,000 sq. ft., with 8,000 sq. ft. dedicated to retail and the remainder for back-office operations. We expect to launch this showroom by the end of FY25.

items.statement: CAPEX for new stores approx ₹1-2.5 crores; inventory held ₹55-60 crores.
items.quote: This is approx. ₹ 1-2.5 crores capex and inventory which is held at the store is ₹55 cores- ₹60 crores.

items.statement: Stores expected to reach breakeven in around 6 to 9 months.
items.quote: Around 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Capex for current year will be lower than FY2024 and continue to unwind in FY2026.
items.quote: We believe that our capex for the current year will be lower than FY2024, and this will continue to unwind in FY2026.

items.statement: Capex moderation expected even in FY2026, with capex as percentage of revenues trending downwards.
items.quote: I would say at headline, you should see moderation of capex even in FY2026, and with the revenue growths that we are seeing, the capex as a percentage of revenues will continue to trend downwards and soon be at the levels of global peers.

items.statement: Transferring about 16,100 telecom towers to Indus Towers.
items.quote: we are planning to transfer about 16,100 telecom towers, approximately 12,700 from Bharti Airtel and about 3400 from Bharti Hexacom to Indus Towers.

items.statement: Launching comprehensive cloud solution in next few months.
items.quote: We will be launching a comprehensive cloud solution in the next few months.

items.statement: Postpaid opportunity to reach upwards of 50 million over next few years from 80 million base.
items.quote: There is no reason why we should not get upwards of 50 million over the next few years on postpaid, because there is an 80 million base that is ready to actually get onto postpaid.

items.statement: FWA EBITDA margins similar to home services.
items.quote: Yeah, It will be in that same ballpark.

items.statement: Hexacom addressable market for broadband about 3 to 4 million.
items.quote: In terms of addressable market, I would say this would be about 3 to 4 million.

items.statement: Hexacom has about 2 million home passes currently.
items.quote: About 2 million home passes we have, currently at Bharti Hexacom

items.statement: Hexacom capex directionally same, could marginally increase due to FWA rollout.
items.quote: So, directionally same could be marginal increase, it all depends on FWA rollout.

items.statement: Hexacom dividend payout to be considered positively.
items.quote: Dividend payout is something which will be certainly looked at with a positive angle.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.4% in Q3 FY25 from 5.6% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: 5.6% improving to 6.4% in Q3 FY25, which is a jump of 30% year on year.

items.statement: India multi-channel adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 11.2% in Q3 FY25 from 10.7% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: We continue to improve our adjusted EBITDA from 10.7% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this by 50 bps to 11.2%, which is a n increase of 20% year on year for Q3

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin for nine months FY25 was 5.1%, up from 4% in nine months FY24.
items.quote: And the 4% consol. EBITDA in nine months FY24 has increased to 5.1% for the nine months FY25, which is a n increase of 54% year on

items.statement: Gross margin for Q3 FY25 was 37%, up from 34.5% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: From 34.5% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this to 37% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Gross margin for nine months FY25 was 37.3%, up from 35.4% in nine months FY24.
items.quote: Similarly, for the nine months, the gros s margins has improved to 37.3% compared to 35.4% in nine months FY24

items.statement: International business adjusted EBITDA improved to -15% in Q3 FY25 from -16% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: From 16% negative EBITDA in Q3’FY24, end of December, we have improved this to minus 15%.

items.statement: Globalbees adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.4% in Q3 FY25 from 0.6% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: From 0.6% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this to 1.4% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Education business adjusted EBITDA for nine months FY25 was around 23%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the nine months is around 23% EBITDA, for Q3 is around 22%.

items.statement: Annual unique transacting customers grew 17% for period ending Dec 2024 vs Dec 2023.
items.quote: Annual unique transacting customers in India and Middle East, 17% increase for the period ending Dec ’24 vis-a-vis period ending Dec’23, annual unique transacting customers.

items.statement: GMV grew 17% for nine months FY25 over nine months FY24.
items.quote: Likewise, our GMV grew for nine months over last nine months by 17% and the net revenue from operation s increased by 19% to INR 5,729 Cr

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew 54% to INR 293 Cr for nine months FY25.
items.quote: And consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew by 54% for nine months ending Dec’24 vs nine months ending Dec’23 to INR 293 Cr and India multi- channel as well grew by 26% for the same nine month period resulting into overall cash profit after tax of 47% increa se for the similar nine months to INR 139.7

items.statement: GMV increased 13% in Q3 FY25 over Q3 FY24.
items.quote: GMV increase in Q3 is 13%.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% revenue growth over next 3 years.
items.quote: So, next 3 years, we are looking at the growth rate of around 15% to 20%. Although, we will target to achieve more, but 15% to 20% definitely we will be able to achieve and EBITDA margins, we expect the EBITDA margins to be at the same, similar lines across the product.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain similar across products.
items.quote: and EBITDA margins, we expect the EBITDA margins to be at the same, similar lines across the product.

items.statement: Chennai plant phase 1 capacity ~55-60 crores, phase 2 total ~100-110 crores.
items.quote: Basically, we are going to put a CAPEX at Chennai plant in phase 1 and phase 2 and in phase 1, approximately, in value term, the capacity will be approximately 55 to 60 crores and phase 2, which will be happening in next year, we will be touching the overall capacity in Chennai in value term approximately 100 and 110 crores.

items.statement: Chennai plant commissioning expected by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We expect that this plant would be commissioned by Q1 of FY’25-26.

items.statement: Investing 11 crore in Wada plant for various machines.
items.quote: So, we will be investing this CAPEX of 11 crore in different machines, in the Disc Spring, Coil Spring, and Fastener as well.

items.statement: Strong order book and pipeline support growth momentum.
items.quote: We have a strong order book and pipeline, which gives us confidence of continuing our growth momentum.

items.statement: Offers 15-18% price saving vs German producers in export market.
items.quote: Yes, so basically when we compete with German producers in the export market, we are able to offer about 15% to 18% price saving as compared to the German prices and in terms of India of course, we are the market leaders in our products, particularly for spring.

items.statement: In India fastener category, offers 3-4% saving vs local suppliers.
items.quote: In fastener category in India, we are able to offer 3 to 4% saving because customers are looking more technical solutions, more customized suppliers rather than only price saving as compared to their local suppliers.

items.statement: Renewable and industrial to drive growth 30-40%, mobility 20-25%.
items.quote: I think, broadly, renewable and industrial will be the major drivers of the growth that will be about 30 to 40% and mobility will be about 20-25%.

items.statement: Export and domestic mix to remain 35-40% exports, 60% domestic.
items.quote: So, broadly the export and domestic mix will remain same which is about 35 to 40% exports and about 60% will be domestic even going forward.

items.statement: No major impact expected in next 1 year from US renewable uncertainty.
items.quote: But based on the discussion with customers of course in last couple of weeks we do not see any major impact in next 1 year because most of the projects are allotted.

items.statement: Wada plant max revenue potential 325-350 crore.
items.quote: Going forward with some incremental CAPEX we will be able to achieve around 325-350 crore from Wada itself.

items.statement: Fastener segment growth expected higher than other product groups.
items.quote: So, I think company level we are looking at about 15 to 20% growth CAGR for next 3-4 years and of course fastener being a much smaller base and we just started adding more and more customers more and more segment. So, growth in fasteners will be higher than the other product groups category.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stabilize at 15-18%.
items.quote: Post COVID in fact year on year we are able to improve our EBITDA if you see our last 4 year performance and going forward we are thinking we should be stabilizing this EBITDA level 15-18-17 something and so there will be quarter-on-quarter there will be some plus and minus but because of the various reason or product mix or some one time cost and all.

items.statement: 68 crores of IPO funds unutilized, to be used for Chennai and Wada capex.
items.quote: Major portion of the 78 crores 68 crores is actually unutilized IPO funds which has been kept in fixed deposit which will get utilized for the Chennai and Wada CAPEX over the period of next 6 months to 1 year.

items.statement: Expects at least 15%-20% growth next year with new products.
items.quote: So, if everything goes well, then we are looking at growth of at least 15%-20% for the next year with these new products coming in pipeline.

items.statement: Seamless tube project capex approximately INR170 odd crores, starting Q4, majority in FY26.
items.quote: We would be starting our investments in quarter 4 for the seamless tube plant. And the majority of it would be done in FY26. The total value of the capex on the seamless tube project is approximately INR170 odd crores.

items.statement: Seamless tube project completion targeted mid-FY27, orders for imported equipment by end of FY25.
items.quote: We anticipate the completion of this project within 18 months, targeting mid-FY27.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of approximately INR70 crores allocated to capex, in line with plan.
items.quote: But we had basically, from the proceeds of the IPO, we had set out approximately INR70 crores on our capex. This is mainly on the enhancement of our forging capabilities and our new line in the foundry and as well as new machines for us to equip us to ramp up on our production of our exports.

items.statement: February order book approximately 4,000 axles.
items.quote: However, we've seen good growth in the month of January and our order book of February is approximately of 4,000 axles.

items.statement: Expects better EBITDA margins in Q4 and ahead, especially with exports.
items.quote: But within Q4 and going ahead, we will see better EBITDA margins coming in. And especially with the exports going up, we would deliver better EBITDA margins and profitability as well.

items.statement: Export business could run at 20% to 22% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: The margins, fortunately, are much better. I mean, if we are to draw our balance sheets only based on export business, we would be running with an EBITDA of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Backward integration into seamless tubes to reduce cost by 3% to 4%.
items.quote: Now, the effect of it will be about 3% to 4% on the cost of the product. If we go in for our own backward integration and use the tubes which we manufacture ourselves, they will cost about 3% to 4% lesser than our existing route.

items.statement: Q4 demand from trailer business is good and strong.
items.quote: And more importantly, we see Q4, the demand from the trailer business is quite good, quite strong.

items.statement: Component business improving, OEM volumes getting better.
items.quote: The component business is getting better. Volumes at OEMs are getting better.

items.statement: Launched 18-ton axle and two mechanical suspensions; car carrier axle and suspension launching this quarter.
items.quote: What we are going to get into in this quarter will be the launch of the car carrier axle and suspension. This product aims at trailers, which are specifically designed to carry cars and bikes from the OEM to the various dealers and everything.

items.statement: Extrusion plant to increase capacity to 7,500 units per month from 5,000.
items.quote: This advanced technology will increase our capacity to 7,500 units per month, up from our current 5,000 trailer capacity for axles and suspension assemblies.

items.statement: Employee cost increase was one-off, will revert to previous percentages from coming quarters.
items.quote: But this is, you could say, it is a one-off case in this quarter. It's going to be back at our previous percentages from the coming quarters.

items.statement: Exports to reach 15% of revenue in next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: 15% of our revenue coming in from exports in the next 2 to 3 years. That's what I was explaining.

items.statement: Exports expected at 5% of revenue this year, around INR25 crores-INR28 crores.
items.quote: So, we are looking at 5%, around INR25 crores-INR28 crores revenue coming in this year from the export front.

items.statement: Seamless tube investment of INR167 crores funded through debt and internal accruals.
items.quote: This will involve an investment of INR167 crores and this will be funded through a mixture of debt and our internal accruals.

items.statement: Anticipates double-digit growth in Q4 on a year-to-year basis.
items.quote: We feel that the situation has now improved quite a lot and we are anticipating double-digit growth in Q4 on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Secured INR1,089 crores order from Vedanta Limited, a four-year contract till 2028.
items.quote: your company was able to secure a landmark INR1,089 crores order from Vedanta Limited, which we feel is one of the largest orders in Indian multimodal and supply chain solutions. This four-year contract which will go on till 2028, covers the entire gamut of transportation and logistics of their several products such as aluminium ingots, billets, wire rods, pig iron and EXIM shipments from their pl

items.statement: Received INR170 crores order from Hindustan Zinc Limited for logistics of finished goods for four years.
items.quote: We also received about a month ago an order of INR170 crores from the world's largest and India's only integrated zinc, lead and silver Western Carriers ( producer, which is Hindustan Zinc Limited. This is also for logistics of their finished goods, which includes zinc and lead ingots for a period of four

items.statement: Materials handling contract from Vedanta for import and domestic EXIM operations at Jharsuguda, value INR139 crores.
items.quote: Another contract that we have which is corollary to the INR1,089 from Vedanta is the materials handling contract from them for both their import and domestic, EXIM operations, again at the Jharsuguda plant. And the order value of that is INR139 crores.

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 24%, offsetting 15% decline in EXIM container volumes for 9M FY25.
items.quote: The domestic volumes at the same time have shown a growth of 24% which has successfully offset this about 15% decline in EXIM container volumes for the first 9 months.

items.statement: Margin improvement too early to say, but should happen in the long term.
items.quote: So margin improvement it's too early to say, sir, because all of these new projects and work is in progress, but margin improvement should happen in the long term for sure, sir.

items.statement: International supply chain constraints caused dip in quarterly profits due to higher costs.
items.quote: So, that is the reason why we have seen a dip in our quarterly profits this time. It is really nothing to do with our own efficiencies, but more to do with the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Detention and demurrage charges not fully pass-through to customers, depends on contract terms.
items.quote: So, it is not a straight pass through Western Carriers ( to the customers. It depends on your order booking and the terms of your contract. So, not everything can be passed on to the customer

items.statement: Product mix shifted with domestic business surging 24% and EXIM shrinking 15%.
items.quote: So, domestic businesses actually surged 24%, but the EXIM volumes because of the geopolitical reasons has shrunk by about 15% and I'm giving you approximate numbers. Now, what happens is the product mix completely change and what happens is because we are in bed with our customers, what happens is that volume gets shifted for us,

items.statement: Revenue booking for Vedanta order has started and will ramp up further.
items.quote: Sir, already revenue booking has started in this, and it will ramp up further as we go ahead.

items.statement: Confident to give revenue growth this year.
items.quote: Yes, sir. I am very, very confident that we will be able to give revenue growth this year, sir.

items.statement: Total outstanding debt as on 31st December is INR164 crores.
items.quote: As on 31st December, the total outstanding debt is INR164 crores.

items.statement: Receivables slightly higher due to new orders; benefit of reduction visible from next year.
items.quote: So, since we've had a lot of new orders that have come in, the receivables are slightly higher. We are working very hard on actually reducing its quarter-on-quarter. And I think the benefit of that will be visible from next year more than this year, sir.

items.statement: Expects robust growth in Vedanta plant volumes in next three to four years.
items.quote: I would like to say that in the next three to four years, Vedanta expects very robust growth year on year in this plant.

items.statement: Working on large proposals in pharma and FMCG, hopeful to fructify in next quarter.
items.quote: We are working on some large proposals which hopefully we should be able to fructify in the next quarter or so, sir.

items.statement: Targets 15% revenue growth and 100 bps margin expansion every year.
items.value: 15% revenue growth, 100 basis points margin expansion
items.quote: And ma'am, for future years, obviously, last quarter conference call, you did mention, that you are targeting revenue growth of 15%. And obviously, it's a 100-basis point of margin expansion every year. So, this kind of a guidance stays? So, that was my first question. Ritu Mittal: Yes, it stays.

items.statement: Annual capex budget is INR70 crores, with 5-7% for maintenance and rest for expansion.
items.quote: So, our capex outlet that we have budgeted is around INR70 crores per year. Out of this, maintenance would be to the tune of 5% to 7% every year and the rest is all expansion.

items.statement: Plans to reach 100 centers in next 3 years.
items.quote: So, for 3 years, we definitely want to reach a number of 100 in the next 3 years. And then we would definitely plan to focus on the businesses from these centers, stabilize all the centers, all the 100 centers, and then go ahead with the next centers that we want to plan.

items.statement: Plans to add 12 to 15 new centers each year.
items.quote: Our commitment to expansion remains strong, with plans to add 12 to 15 new centers each year.

items.statement: No price hike yet; annual increase of 3-4% at financial year end.
items.quote: Sir, we have not raised prices as yet. We actually go for a 3% to 4% hike, at the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Old centers target EBITDA margins of 40-41% in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: And the old centers which we have, which is like around 40, maybe 40 plus old centers, what sort of EBITDA margins are we targeting in the next 2, 3 years? Can we go to 40%, 41%? Ritu Mittal: Yes, it is at around 40, 41%.

items.statement: Small and medium centers become EBITDA positive in 3-4 months; big centers in 6-7 months.
items.quote: So, typically a small centre and a medium centre becomes EBITDA positive in 3 to 4 months and a big centre takes around 6 to 7 months to become EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Plans to open 6 centers in Q4 FY25: 2 PPPs, 2 big, 2 small.
items.quote: Yes, so out of the six there are two PPPs that we open. There will be two big centres and two small centres.

items.statement: Added 5 new centers till Dec 2024, 1 in Jan 2025, and adding 6-8 in Feb-Mar 2025.
items.quote: So, in FY25 till December ‘25***, we have opened 5 new centres and one centre has been added in January and are in process of adding another 6 to 8 centres in February and March.

items.statement: Targets 3% market share in East.
items.quote: So, the market share that we think of getting in the East is around 3%, which is also very similar to the leaders, the regional leaders in the diagnostic plane in their core geographies.

items.statement: Plans to sustain 20-30% pricing premium due to lack of availability.
items.quote: Sakshi Trivedi: Okay, ma'am. So, my next question would be, would you be able to sustain the 20-30 percent pricing premium if we expand the current ways? Ritu Mittal: Yes, we would because, like we mentioned, East India is the least penetrated market as far as quality diagnostics is concerned. And therefore, the premium remains because of lack of availability.

items.statement: Revenue mix: pathology 56%, radiology 44%.
items.quote: So, our pathology is 56% and our radiology is 44%.

items.statement: Volume mix: pathology 75%, radiology 25%.
items.quote: Yes, volume. Just give me a minute. So, it will be around 75% will be pathology and 25% will be radiology. Volume mix.

items.statement: Revenue mix from radiology and pathology stable at ~54% pathology and ~45% radiology for last 2-3 years.
items.quote: In terms of revenue mix from radiology and pathology, in general it is around 54% from pathology and 45% from radiology. And it is being observed that since last 2-3 years, the mix is more or less the same.

items.statement: AIIR subsidiary is EBITDA positive and profitable; Suraksha Radiology not yet breakeven.
items.quote: In terms of subsidiaries, AIIR is already a EBITDA positive and is earning profits. AIIR has started in May’24 only and by December’24, it has already started doing profits. In fact, the profit before tax in the quarter of December’24 was 11.87 lakhs. And in terms of Suraksha Radiology, which is another subsidiary, this is started. Basically, two PPP models have been started under this and this is

items.statement: PPP center NRS Medical College operates at 30% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Two of them have opened about a month back. So, it is just getting familiar. But if you take as an average, we have one PPP in NRS Medical College for a long time. That works on a 30% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Mining capacity expansion approval for Ari Dongri mines from 2.35 to 6 million ton expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: The approval for mining capacity expansion of Ari Dongri's mines from 2.35 million to 6 million ton is expected to be in place by Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Boria Tibu iron ore captive mines with 0.7 million ton per annum capacity restarted
items.quote: GPL has also restarted mining operation at Boria Tibu iron ore captive mines having a capacity of 0.7 million ton per annum.

items.statement: 0.6 million ton iron ore beneficiation plant for BMQ at Ari Dongri mines started out of proposed 6 million ton capacity
items.quote: 0.6 million ton iron ore benefaction plan for B&Q out of proposed 6 million ton capacity situated at Ari Dongri mines has also started.

items.statement: Pellet plant capacity increase from 2.7 to 4.7 million ton expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY26
items.quote: The increase in pellet plant capacity from 2.7 million to 4.7 million ton is expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Greenfield integrated steel plant of 2 million ton dropped; evaluating smaller capacity alternatives with lower capex
items.quote: The plan to set up a greenfield integrated steel plant with a capacity of 2 million ton has been dropped. Company is evaluating different alternative projects with lower capacity and lower capex for which announcement will be made once the project is finalized.

items.statement: OPVC pipe manufacturing project dropped; INR125 crore capex planned, only INR14 crore spent on equipment order
items.quote: The plan to venture into OPVC pipe manufacturing has been dropped due to changed market scenario.

items.statement: 70MW solar power plant planned for additional pellet capacity; additional 25MW solar plant for new beneficiation plant at Ari Dongri mines
items.quote: In addition to 70MW solar power plant that is planned to be set up for additional capacity of pellet plant, an additional 25MW solar power plant is also decided to be set up for additional power requirement of new verification plant at Ari Dongri mines.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of 49% stake in Jammu Pigments Limited on fully diluted basis as on 31st December 2024
items.quote: GPL has completed acquisition of 49% stake in share capital of Jammu Pigments Limited on a fully diluted basis as on 31st December '24.

items.statement: Entered agreement with GAIL for supply of electrified natural gas for upcoming pellet plant for 7 years
items.quote: The company has entered into an agreement with GAIL for supply of electrified natural gas for GPLI's upcoming pellet plant for a period of 7 years.

items.statement: Eligible to supply steel blades to all manufacturers of galvanized steel structures for Power Grid Corporation transmission projects
items.quote: The company is eligible to supply steel blades to all manufacturers of galvanized steel structures for the transmission projects of Power Grid Corporation of India Limited.

items.statement: Production guidance achievement for FY25: iron ore mining 69%, iron ore pellets 73%, sponge iron 84%, ferro alloys 96%
items.quote: Of the production guidance set for FY '25 for iron ore mining, iron ore pellets, sponge iron and ferro alloys, the company has already achieved 69%, 73%, 84% and 96%, respectively.

items.statement: Pellet sales decreased YoY in Q3 due to shifting of export consignment to Q4; sponge iron, steel billets, MS rounds decreased due to increased HB wire production
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, sales of iron ore pellet decreased on Y-o-Y basis due to shifting of export consignment from Q3 to Q4 FY '25. Sponge iron steel billets and MS round decreased on Y-o-Y basis due to increase in production of HB wires.

items.statement: HB wires and ferro alloys sales increased significantly on both quarterly and 9-month basis
items.quote: Sales of HB wires and ferro alloys increased significantly on both quarterly and 9-month basis.

items.statement: Pellet realization increased 2% on 9-month basis to INR10,387 per ton; other product realizations down 3-8%
items.quote: Pellet realization increased by 2% on a 9-month basis to INR10,387 a ton, whereas realization for other products were down in the range of 3% to 8%.

items.statement: Consolidated 9M FY25 revenue flat at Rs 3,908 crores; EBITDA and PAT down due to lower realizations; EBITDA margin 22%, PAT margin 15%
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, the company achieved flat revenue of Rs 3,908 crores. EBITDA and PAT was down on account of lower realization of finished products. Despite the challenges, EBITDA margin and PAT margin stood strong at 22% and 15%, respectively.

items.statement: Company has healthy balance sheet with net cash balance of INR725 crores
items.quote: The company has a healthy balance sheet with net cash balance of INR725 crores.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand projected to grow 8-9% in 2025 driven by construction in housing and infrastructure
items.quote: India's steel demand is projected to grow by 8% to 9% in 2025, driven by increased construction in housing and infrastructure sector.

items.statement: Government restricted coke imports to merchant cokeries, forcing company to include coke oven in steel plant capex adding ~INR5,000 crores
items.quote: Government of India has restricted the import of coke into India to merchant cokeries in India, right? So merchant cokeries have been -- to help them support them by imposing certain duties. So what Indian government has done is they have limited the quota of imports from respective countries for a period of 6 months.

items.statement: Steel plant capex revised from INR5,000-6,000 crores to over INR8,000 crores due to higher intra cost (60% vs 40% estimated)
items.quote: The capex we envisage initially, we got it wrong. So usually what happens, we thought 60% is equipment cost and 40% will be the intra cost. But what has happened is it is opposite. So 40% is your equipment cost 60% is your intra cost, so the entire capex which is about INR5,000 crores to INR6,000 crores 2 million plant will probably cross INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: Evaluating smaller steel capacity of 0.8-1 million ton with capex of INR3,500-4,000 crores; major expansion from FY27
items.quote: For example, if we do a 0.8 million capacity or 1 million capacity, the figure be somewhere about INR300 crores to INR400 crores. If you even consider INR400 crores to INR 450 crores per 1 lakh ton of steel. So 0.8 million, INR3,500 crores for 1 million, probably INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Remaining pellet plant capex of INR432 crores to be spent over next 4 months (Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26); trial production by early Q2 FY26
items.quote: So between Q4, which is already going halfway. So next 4 months, the entire remaining INR432 crores will be spent. And we are confident we can start the trial production of the new pellet plant in FY '26, Q2.

items.statement: New pellet plant ramp-up to full utilization expected in 3-6 months; full volumes from Q4 FY26 worst case
items.quote: See, 3 to 6 months maximum. So end of probably Q3 or mid of Q3, we can expect full production.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR1,000-1,100 crores for mining, beneficiation, pellet plant, solar; FY27 capex depends on revised steel plan
items.quote: So roughly capex of about, say, INR1,000 crores to INR100 crores will be spent in FY '26. And FY '27, hopefully, we are able to come up with a concrete plan for the revised steel capacity.

items.statement: FY26 pellet production guidance: 3-3.25 million tons (2.5M current + 0.5-0.7M new plant); FY27 full capacity 4.5 million tons
items.quote: So FY '26, we'll do about 3 million to 3.25 million tons of pellet. But FY '27, we should do about 4.5 million tons of pellets.

items.statement: Export pellet realization currently INR1,000 less per ton net vs domestic market; not exporting currently due to domestic demand pickup
items.quote: Okay. So if you export right now, the realization will be about INR1,000 less compared to domestic market.

items.statement: Beneficiation cost: delivered cost to plant currently INR2,200 per ton after beneficiation; royalty on 65 grade concentrate ~INR750 per ton
items.quote: So my delivered cost to my plant currently, which we are beneficiating is about INR2,200 after beneficiation.

items.statement: BMQ beneficiation yield ~50%; high-grade iron ore (60-61) beneficiation yield 80-85% annually
items.quote: So on the BMQ side because it's low grade, we do about 50%. And on the plant side, so the yield is about 80%, 85% on an annual basis.

items.statement: Iron ore inventory was ~1 lakh tons in Q3; exported one vessel; inventory now below 20,000 tons; all carryforward inventory to be sold in Q4
items.quote: We were carrying an inventory of more than about 53,000 tons, which never happened happens. So on the inventory, we've exported a vessel. And the end of December, the market picked up, and we have a healthy order

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA target: bare minimum INR500-800 crores additional from pellet expansion; current market scenario suggests ~INR600 crores additional EBITDA
items.quote: To be honest, 4.5 million capacity of pellet and plus addition everything bare minimum is about INR50 crores to INR800 crores of EBITDA FY '27. But of course, it's a very -- I would say, it's a very assumption-based because you don't know where the market is going to be in next 15 months being a commodity market.

items.statement: ~8 million tons of additional pellet capacity (excl. Godawari) to be commissioned in next 6-8 months in Chhattisgarh/Maharashtra; India installed capacity ~150M tons at 80% utilization
items.quote: So apart from Godawari, about 8 million tons of pellet plant is being commissioned in the next 6 to 8 months, which is a good capacity.

items.statement: Top 3 pellet buyers: Prakash Industry, Real Ispat Group, Kanukripa; all domestic long-term buyers
items.quote: The top 3 buyers for GPL. So Prakash Industry, which is in has been a big buyer, plus there are a couple of local guys. One is a group called Real Ispat Group is a big buyer and another group called Kanukripa.

items.statement: Pellet margin ~INR4,000/ton (cost INR6,000, selling price INR10,000); steel value-add margin additional INR5-7/ton from sponge to finished
items.quote: So our pellet cost is about INR6,000 per ton and the average selling price is about INR10,000. So we make a margin of about INR4,000 on pellets on ex plant basis. And we sell finished, which is wire rod and HB wire. So if you see from sponge because sponge is captive. So from sponge to a finished sale and with all the infra and the power cost, we make about INR5 to INR7 there.

items.statement: Currently purchase ~50,000 tons iron ore fines per quarter (6 lakh tons annually) for 25-30% of requirement; will become zero once mine expansion complete
items.quote: So see, roughly, our current mines capacity gives us about 70%, 75% of the requirement. So we purchased about 50,000 tons of iron ore from the market, 50,000. So about 6 lakh tons annually we purchase from the market currently

items.statement: Public hearing for mining EC expected post-Holi (end March); EC expected by Q1 FY26 after center approval received 2 months ago
items.quote: So expecting the public hearing to be announced probably in the next couple of weeks. So we expect the public hearing to happen Godawari Power & somewhere in post Holi end of March. And once that is done, so in a couple of months, we'll get the EC

items.statement: High-grade pellet production currently 35%; will increase to ~80% with new capacity; open to domestic or export sales for maximum value realization
items.quote: See, currently, our high-grade production is about 65%, 35% is the high grade, right? And the new capacity, which will be coming up will be totally high grade. So going forward, our high grade will be close to about 80% and 20% will be the commercial grade, which is in the domestic market.

items.statement: New pellet plant to switch from producer gas to natural gas via GAIL agreement; no commercial benefit expected but keeps options open for CBAM compliance from Jan 2026
items.quote: For the new pellet plant, we will switch to natural gas. And depending on the commercials and how the plant performs, given the situation, we might convert the entire on the 3 pellet plants to natural gas. It depends on the scenario going forward.

items.statement: FY25 crude steel production target around 18.5 mt
items.quote: For next year, we are still in the proces s of finalizing our business plan. We cannot exactly comment. But this time it is around 18.5 mt crude

items.quote: In FY25, our total CAPEX target is 5,700, out of which 3,900 we have already incurred by December, so the remaining you can say 1,800 in the next three months, that is January, February and March.

items.statement: FY26 CAPEX expected around Rs 7,500 crore as expansion CAPEX starts
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the range of 7,500 roughly you can say because the expansion CAPEX will also start happening in FY26.

items.statement: FY25 sales volume target around 17.5 mt with 1.57 mt achieved up to January
items.quote: Up to January, we have achieved the sales target of 1.57 m t and our total target is around 17.5 mt for the whole year

items.statement: Debt expected to return to March 2024 level of ~Rs 30,500 crore by end of FY25
items.quote: we are expecting that by the end of this particul ar financial year, our debt will be in the similar range as it was in 31st March 2024

items.statement: 9M FY25 CAPEX incurred Rs 3,900 crore
items.quote: Nine months CAPEX is around Rs.3,900 crores.

items.statement: Phase-III expansion of 7.5 mt across Rourkela, Bokaro, Durgapur estimated at Rs 55,000-56,000 crore by 2031
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the range of around 55,000 to 56,000 crores.

items.quote: Roughly, if you say , thumb rule figure that it would be in the range of 1,10,000 to 1,20,00 0 crores of 15 mt. As far as the funding is concerned, we are maintaining 1:1, that is the debt-equity ratio

items.statement: Phase-III expansion adds 7.5 mt across three plants with Stage-I approval; total 15 mt by 2031
items.quote: So, it will be roughly 7.5 mt all the three plants together.

items.quote: Yes, we have a plan to bring down this 1 mt TMT mill and also on B U basis 0.4 m t TMT mill. So , the plan is to utilize the s emis as much as possible

items.quote: Overall, if you see that both flat and long, in Q2 it was around 50,500, which has come down to 49,700 or you can say roughly 800.

items.quote: The blend cost in last quarter was around 20,600, which has come down to 19,200. So, you can say overall there has been reduction as far the coal cost is concerned.

items.statement: Coal blend 85% imported, 15% domestic; domestic prices have import parity with caps so fall less than imported
items.quote: We are using a blend of you can say almost 85% of the imported coal and 15% of the domestic coal at SAIL as a whole.

items.quote: Mainly the increase in the consumer sector, that is infrastructure sector where the increase has happened.

items.quote: But at the peak sometimes it might go up to 1.2 but not beyond that whatever the projection we have made.

items.quote: So, total inventory of finish ed and semi-finished goods is 2.98 m t and the value of this is around 12,000, 13,000 crores

items.quote: As far as safeguard duty is concerned, as you are aware, that we have given all our input to the ministry, whatever was required and there was a demand of 25% of the safeguard duty. The issue is still pending with the finance ministry.

items.quote: For conversion of that into the p elletization, we are yet to get this first stage approval from the board. We are in the process of forming of the board note and if we put to the board and once the approval is given, we'll go ahead

items.statement: Decarbonization Phase-I cut specific CO2 ~20%; targeting further 12% reduction to 2.19 t/tcs by 2031

items.quote: when we look at our outlook, right, for, let's say, FY '26 and beyond, we are absolutely aiming for double digit growth in this business, okay?

items.quote: it is revenue growth. And therefore, it has a volume, have mix because we have clearly said that B&C will grow faster than Oral Care. So, there's a mix, right? And there is some pricing depending on how commodities move, okay?

items.quote: We have initiated capacity expansion in Brazil to cater to better -than-expected Beauty & Cosmetics demand, and this new capacity will go online by Q1 FY '26.

items.quote: we are confident of bringing these back by about 150 basis points over next few quarters. And those actions have alre ady been implemented in the business.

items.quote: EBITDA margin reached 20.3%, delivering an improvement of 152 basis points year- on-year.

items.quote: are multiple initiatives which are still under play. The Europe and America initiatives that we have taken are still being played out, and hence, there is a little -- some juice there. items.quote: long- term, I think our tax rate guidance has always been between 20% to 22%, and that should remain.

items.quote: helped reduce our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to 0.76x and the ROCE further improved to 16.9%.

items.quote: what we are expecting is that once we reach steady state, we should do EBITDA margins upwards of 80% to 85%.

items.quote: I can see the profit of around INR18 crores to INR20 crores in the Chemical segment.

items.statement: Targets Chemical capacity utilization of 85% from current 75%
items.quote: our target is to reach the capacity of 85% from the existing 75%.

items.quote: we procured the raw material in bulk at a discounted prices. So that resulted in direct adding to my PAT. And secondly, the market which we are catering to this U.S., which temporary there is a problem. So we cater this in domestic market. So we got the better realization.

items.quote: we don't need to raise any further funds for this. Because actually, the way we have enough internal accruals and reserves in our cash to suffice for both the LPG and the Morgan case.

items.quote: If I recall correctly, 2 or 3 parties have settled. So it's definitely more than one now. items.quote: you are seeing in last 9 months, there is a cumulative profit of almost INR12 crores to INR13 crores in Chemical segment as compared to just INR6 crores in previous 9 months.

items.quote: As far as the debt EBITDA levels are concerned, as explained earlier, we will continue to have a guidance of not exceeding 3x to 3.5x of net debt to EBITDA.

items.quote: With commencement of commercial production at Chamarajanagar in November '24 and Mahad expected in this quarter, that is Q4 FY '25, Birla Opus would be the second largest player by installed capacity in the Indian decorative paints market.

items.quote: Demand across all sectors, that is individual house builder, infrastructure sector and urban housing growth has been improving and domestic gray cement volume grew by 11% Y-o-Y in the quarter gone by.

items.quote: While both U.S. and Europe are looking at tariffs on epoxy resins, there are other jurisdictions such as Korea and China, which are likely to be more severely impacted if you look at what type of a grant filing has been done.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin contracted 309 bps QoQ to 9.1% due to sluggish OEM demand and higher natural rubber costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins during the quarter were recorded at 9.1% vis-à-vis 12.2% in the previous quarter, which has contracted by 309 basis points due to sluggish demand in OEM and the higher raw material costs, primarily driven by a significant rise in natural rubber prices.

items.statement: Average raw material basket increased 2% QoQ; natural rubber prices rose sharply due to seasonal and climatic factors in Southeast Asia
items.quote: the average raw material prices have increased 2% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and here I would say that the natural rubber prices have actually played little havoc and the reason of which is actually because of the season changing and the climatic impact in this availability of natural rubber plus labor availability as well in the Southeast Asian belt.

items.statement: Strategic raw material inventory built in Q1-Q2 depleted in Q3, causing full impact of higher costs; most high-cost inventory consumed in Q3
items.quote: in Q1 and Q2, we had taken some strategic stocking of the material which helped us to evade some of the cost in Q2. But then that strategic inventory had depleted and Q3 saw the full impact of the raw material.

items.quote: the good thing is that most of the inventory has already been consumed in Q3, so in Q4, we can expect some improvement in margins unless there is again some increase in raw material prices going forward.

items.statement: Year-to-date capex spend of Rs.600 crores against annual outlay of Rs.800 crores for first three quarters
items.quote: the outlay is about Rs.800 crores in these three quarters period. We have already spent about Rs.600 crores.

items.statement: PCR capacity utilization close to 90%

items.statement: North America accounts for ~5% of JK Tornel exports; majority to Brazil and Latin America; expanding to USA with higher rim sizes
items.quote: North America, about 5% of the total export because we are exporting more to Brazil and to Latin America. But we are now increasing our exports to USA with the higher rim sizes

items.quote: Net Debt of the company as on 31 st Dec'24 was Rs.4,317 crores which is net of the cash available with the company and the $100 million loan which we have tied up with IFC is for the expansions which are under implementation at this point in time and partly this loan will be used for replacing the high-cost debt in Cavendish Industries Limited.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduction on schedule; short-term working capital borrowings increased for strategic inventory, to normalize in 1-2 quarters; finance cost expected to decrease next fiscal year
items.quote: Debt reduction on the long-term borrowing spaces, we have been going ahead as per schedule and as we envisaged earlier. It's only in the short term the working capital borrowings have gone up in the last nine months period and this is to maintain the strategic inventory and also some finished goods inventory were accumulated but this is going to get corrected in next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Long-term industry EBITDA margin range 12-15%; FY26 margin target depends on raw material volatility and passing on FY25 under-recovery; sharper guidance next quarter
items.quote: generally, as we had earlier also said that in the longer term the industry is somewhere between that 12% to 15% range. So, let's see we will have to kind of keep it like that as of now, but maybe in the next quarter, we will be able to give you a sharper number on that.

items.statement: Capex for new kiln completed in December-January; switchover to new kiln planned for end of February or first week of March, taking 20-25 days

items.statement: Naked cement price Q3FY25 Rs.3,302 vs Rs.3,762 in Q3FY24 (down ~8%); industry down 10-12%; Q4 prices flat but volumes improving; expect price discipline and recovery in FY26 as consolidation completes
items.quote: So, in Q3 of FY24, what I generally use the word naked cement rate is because it excludes logistics, it excludes the tax, everything. So naked cement price of Q3FY24 is Rs. 3,761. Now it is Q3FY25 is Rs. 3,302. So, if you look at your realization standpoint, it has reduced by 8%.

items.statement: Q1-Q2 FY25 weak due to elections and monsoons; Q3 volumes began stabilizing; Q4 showing strong offtake across all plants; expect sustained demand from government infrastructure spend
items.quote: Q1-Q2 was extremely bad mainly because of election and then the monsoons. The fag end of Q3 showed some kind of an improvement and Q4 has shown the very good offtake for all the cement plants in the country.

items.statement: Cement dispatches grew 12.6% QoQ in Q3FY25; Q3FY25 volume 58,960 tons vs 68,610 tons in Q3FY24 (down 14%); 9M FY25 volume ~173,600 tons vs ~174,000 tons in 9M FY24
items.quote: So, the volumes of Q3FY24 was 68,610 tons and Q3FY25 was 58,960 tons. So, there's a dip of around 14% . So, for nine months FY24 is around 1,74,000 and similarly almost 1,73,600 for nine months FY25.

Whereas the cost of power outside even by DISCOMs is upwards of Rs. 7.

items.quote: So, 9 months FY24 industry generated Rs. 1,064 EBITDA per t on. items.statement: Karnataka renewable energy policy remains positive; no specific company-level incentives currently; scope to add more solar capacity under existing policies
items.quote: So, as such, I would say even today the policy of Karnataka government regarding renewable power is still positive. And I see that is going to be a good vertical to be started into. So, company will look into these things and then continue to grow. Even with these current policies, there is a scope for the company to add more capacity.

items.statement: Cement revenue ~76% in Q3FY25; solar revenue ~15%; solar share to decline as captive consumption rises to 90-95% with new kiln; solar EBITDA benefit retained via internal power cost <Rs.1.50/unit
items.quote: So solar as we start with a new plant and 50 %-60% or even 70% of the generation, we reach 70% to 80% of our cement plant utilization lev els. Then of course there won't be any solar revenues coming into picture. But it does not mean that we would lose out on those EBITDA because even the figures, what I am speaking today is excluding the benefits of solar.

items.statement: Board discussing additional solar capacity expansion; no decision finalized; may have update by next quarter
items.quote: Regarding expansion, yes, the board and company is thinking of adding more solar capacity. But as such as of now nothing has been finalized. Maybe by next quarter we will have some answer to our plans and expanding on renewable power.

items.statement: No acquisition plans in cement; open to renewable power acquisitions if opportunity arises but none currently
items.quote: No, currently we don't have any acquisition planned in the cement sectors. Not that we're looking at new renewable power either. But if there is some sc ope, if we see that there is someone who wants to sell in renewable sector, management will be keen to look at it.

items.quote: Now what has happened is suddenly there is a huge increase in dispatches from January. And once we start doing the switchover, it might take about 25 days Shri Keshav Cement & for us to shut down the kiln. So, we will not have any production of the clinker during that period

items.statement: EBITDA per ton: South peers Rs.422 (Q3) / Rs.463 (9M FY25); national top 18 Rs.620 (Q2) / Rs.719 (Q3) / Rs.800 (9M FY25); SKCIL <Rs.50 currently; target at par with South plus solar benefit

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected to be lower single-digit, not high single-digit as previously projected
items.quote: No, we will not be ending FY25 with high single-digit growth. It will be more in the range of lower single-digit growth.

items.statement: Target Rs 2,900 crore revenue by March 2027 contingent on market recovery
items.quote: we are optimistic and committed in terms of meeting our projected target, what we have set i.e Rs. 2,900 crore by March 2027.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to 16-17% range in next one or two quarters
items.quote: we are quite confident that we are going to achieve this 16 % to 17% in the next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 demand remained challenging with persistent headwinds suppressing growth
items.quote: In Q3 FY25, while we initially witnessed early signs of demand improvement, market conditions remained challenging as persistent head winds continued to suppress growth.

items.statement: January and February 2025 better year-on-year but still expecting lower single-digit growth for FY25
items.quote: January and February so far have been better compared to last year on a year-on-year basis. But still, we do not anticipate achieving high single-digit growth as projected earlier.

items.statement: Shell & Tube Heat Exchanger target 200 units/month by Q3 FY26

items.statement: Order book strong with high visibility for coming quarters

items.statement: IPP Global orders: 3.5 million in hand, discussing another 3.5 million, expect 7-8 million by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, that is there. They already we are ordering I think 3.5 million orders we have in the hand from IPPs. Another 3.5 million orders we are discussing with IPPs. And this is going to next year, maybe 7 million, 8 million second quarter that we are expecting from IPP orders.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 20.1% in 9M FY25 driven by export contribution
items.quote: Nine months, 25 revenue, INR455 crores, 33% year -on-year growth. EBITDA INR 91 crores, 42% year-on-year growth, with margins improved 20.1 % EBITDA.

items.statement: Export margins higher than domestic margins
items.quote: No domestic is very tight situation. Export is high margin we said.

items.statement: Pharma contributes 82% of 9M FY25 revenue
items.quote: We are still very strong in pharma. I think these 9 months, if you look into it, 82% is business coming from pharma.

items.statement: Launching Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers, conductivity glass, high corrosion resistant glass for semiconductors
items.quote: We are launching Shell & Tube heat exchangers. That is, I explained to you earlier also, AGI Inc., Japan, it's a licensing agreement. This is -- India, every year that business is approximately, we are estimating INR 2,000 crores, and globally 2 billion business opportunities available.

items.statement: 18 new products under development, total 72 products currently
items.quote: We manufacture 72 types of products with 18 more under development.

Except in India, Japan, Indonesia, the Middle East and Russia, this will significantly boost our export sales.

items.statement: AGI Inc. Japan partnership for technology and licensing (4% domestic, 7% export royalty)
items.quote: And this licensing purpose, we are going to pay AGI Inc., Japan to 4% domestic sales royalty and 7% royalty on exports we are going to pay AGI, Japan.

items.statement: Q3 exports low due to SCOMET license delays, Q4 exports to increase
items.quote: Exports, some license delays happened. That's the reason the third quarter's export is late. We Standard Glass Lining Technology Limited February 12, 2025 got licenses now and the export is going to increase in the fourth

items.statement: SCOMET license delays impacted Q3 exports, now resolved
items.quote: Third quarter, very less export, and fourth quarter is going to, I mean, again, because of some Scomet license, we are not able to get the all types.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved from -INR65 crores to +INR6 crores in 9M YoY
items.quote: Correct, sir. That is correct, sir. Earlier, I think, last year, same period, we have m inus INR65 crores cash flow. And today, we have—bring plus INR6 crores cash flow

items.statement: INR130 crores IPO proceeds used for working capital loan repayment
items.quote: So out of INR210 crores, INR130 crores as mentioned in the prospectus, INR130 crores we are going to utilize it for the working capital loan repayment, which we have done it already.

items.statement: 9M FY25 revenue INR455 crores (33% YoY), EBITDA INR91 crores (42% YoY), PAT INR52 crores (45% YoY)
items.quote: Nine months, 25 revenue, INR455 crores, 33% year -on-year growth. EBITDA INR 91 crores, 42% year-on-year growth, with margins improved 20.1 % EBITDA. PAT INR52 crores, 45% year-on-year growth, with margins at 11.5%.

items.statement: Client capex slowdown in pharma/chemical for last 2-3 years, but new large capex discussions underway
items.quote: Last 2 years, 3 years, pharma, our client's capex is very less. But still, we are going 20%-22% growth. And last 1 or 2 months, I'm discussing with many clients. Many clients have started big, big, very, very big capex. And they want to start some more facilities. And the coming years, 2-3 years, is very exciting, really.

items.statement: MAT credit of approximately 22-23 crores will be fully utilized by March 2025
items.quote: The MAT credit that was available to the Company will get fully utilized by March 2025. Because we are in the old tax regime, we are able to carry forward the MAT and that MAT is getting utilized. It is utilized on an annual basis, so we can't give you the number for utilization up to December.

items.statement: Decision on tax regime change will be taken in next couple of months for FY26
items.quote: The Company is analyzing that in a lot of detail and will be in a position to take a decision in the next month or two in this regard.

items.statement: Average occupancy rate at 99.5% for Q3 FY25 with 15,000 sq ft vacant at NKP and 6,200 sq ft at Nirlon House
items.quote: On the operational front, the average occupancy rate for the Company as a whole, that is NKP and Nirlon House combined, was at 99.5% for the 3rd quarter of the Financial Year 2025 and as on 31st December 2024. Approximately 15000 square feet at NKP and 6200 square feet at the Nirlon house was vacant.

items.statement: Morgan Stanley vacating 449,000 sq ft in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26; 230,000 sq ft already re-licensed to BNP Paribas, EY, ICICI Prudential and Globeop SS&C
items.quote: Morgan Stanley has given notices to vacate approximately 449,000 square feet of space with the last notices for about 176,000 square feet received in December 2024. These spaces will largely be vacated in Quarter 4 of FY 2025 and Quarter 1 of FY 2026. Of this, around 230,000 square feet has already been re-licensed to BNP Paribas, EY, ICICI Prudential and Globeop SS&C with discussions going on for

items.statement: BNP Paribas renewed 156,000 sq ft at NKP; terms finalized for re-licensing 60,000 sq ft coming up for renewal in FY25
