items.quote: Now Clean Energy segment looks a very comfo rtable number, whereby the Santa Cruz boxes have been streamlined. We're adding more wallet share into the system with the customer as well. So we're looking at almost close to about INR500 crores plus in terms of sales that we will be doing with respect to Clean Energy for the next year. Vipraw Srivastava: Okay. So in terms of hot boxes, how much it wil

items.statement: MNC Aerospace revenue target INR125 crores FY26 (mix of first articles and batch production), major volume breakthrough FY27
items.quote: Yes. So Aerospace and Defence would really drastically improve. Like, for example, next year, we'll be doing around -- only in MNC aerospace itself, we'll be doing about INR125 crores next year, which is a phenomenal growth, right? And that's a combination of first articles and volume production and then FY '27 will be much larger than that.

items.statement: Target FY2026 revenue mix: 75% flights, 25% non-air (currently 86% flights)
items.quote: So, our target is that in FY2026, we should be able to say 75% of our business came from flight and 25% business came from all other sectors, which right now is at 86%.

items.statement: Q3 FY2025 GBR grew 7% YoY; discount reduced from 3.8% to 3% QoQ
items.quote: We did grow about 7% in this particular quarter. But again, we also agree that growth would have been much better had we increased our discount. From last quarter, we reduced from 3.8% to 3%.

items.statement: Q3 FY2025 EBITDA INR 51 cr, margin 33.2%; PAT INR 34 cr, margin 22.1%
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR 51 crores, growing quarter-on-quarter at 20.7% which translates to a margin of 33.2%. PAT for the quarter stood at INR 34 crores, growing quarter-on-quarter at 30% with a margin of 22.1%.

items.statement: Hotel nights booked 2.5 lakh in Q3 FY2025, up 172% YoY, 11.1% of GBR
items.quote: This quarter, total nights booked stood at 2.5 lakhs, reflecting a significant 172% year-on-year growth and contributing 11.1% to the gross booking revenue.

items.statement: EV bus manufacturing underway, will take a few more quarters to complete
items.quote: So, the EV buses, what we started off in the manufacturing mix , that is going to take more few quarters' time to completely come in shape.

items.statement: Franchise stores opened in Raipur, Srikalahasti, Bangalore, Jabalpur, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad; new Mumbai office inaugurated
items.quote: We have accelerated the rollout of our franchisee model, opening new stores in Raipur, Srikalahasti, Bangalore, Jabalpur, Bhubaneswar and Hyderabad. Additionally, our new Mumbai office has been inaugurated to enhance corporate and my travel solutions.

items.statement: Private competitors burning cash to grow airline share; EaseMyTrip prioritizes profitability over discount-led growth
items.quote: There are efforts by newly listed players who are trying their level best to capture the market. At EaseMyTrip, we are very, very caution able in growing ourselves while remaining profitable

items.statement: Received IATA GoGlobal accreditation, enhancing credibility with global airline partners
items.quote: This quarter, we were hono ured to receive the prestigious GoGlobal accreditation from IATA, which is a testament to our expanding international presence and credibility amongst global airlines partners

items.statement: Dubai GBR INR 170 cr in Q3 FY2025, up 227% YoY; management sees sustainable long-term growth
items.quote: Our Dubai operations have also shown remarkable progress, showing a year-on-year growth of 227% and the gross booking revenue stood at INR 170 crores in Q3 FY2025.

items.statement: Acquired Planet Education Australia to enter study tourism sector
items.quote: Furthering our expansion into specialized travel services, we have entered the study tourism sector with the acquisition of Planet Education Australia.

items.statement: Promoters commit no share sales for this year; bonus issue decisions are Board-driven, management took investor feedback
items.quote: And the public commitment is made that for this particular year, we will not be selling any shares. So, we would abide by that.

items.statement: Competitor discounting pressure may suppress near-term GBR growth; promoter stake sale and leadership changes create perception risk
items.quote: Had we increased our -- or had we kept our discount to 3.8%, we would have seen at least 15% to 20% increase in our GBR. But ag ain, as a company which has been bootstrapped ever since. Only, last year ago, we raised some capital. We really, really care about profitability

items.statement: Non-air share of GBR rising: hotels 11.1%, trains/buses/other 2% in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: Total nights booked stood at 2.5 lakhs, reflecting a significant 172% year-on-year growth and contributing 11.1% to the gross booking revenue. Bookings in the train, buses and the other category grew by 31.9% year-on-year to 3.6 lakh contributing 2% to GBR.

items.statement: Strategic partnerships with OLX (35M MAU) and CARS24 for distribution and engagement
items.quote: Our strategic partnership with OLX India has expanded our digital footprint, integrating our dedicated travel booking section within their platform, providing seamless access to flights, hotels and holiday packages for its 35 million plus monthly users.

items.statement: Sustainability partnership with BNZ Green for real-time carbon footprint tracking and blockchain-based carbon offsets
items.quote: In line with our commitment to sustainability, we have partnered with BNZ Green to introduce real-time carbon footprint tracking and also blockchain based carbon offset program.

items.statement: Management declined to provide revenue or margin guidance for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: But as I mentioned, we are not giving the guidance so request that we stay like that.

items.statement: Plant-6 brownfield expansion underway to reach INR1,000 crores oral solids capacity; capex details to be shared by end of March
items.quote: I think that one upcoming capex will be primarily for Plant-6 bringing up which is the oral solid expansion and we are in the layout and machinery identification selection process. So I request that I be allowed to comment on this query by end of March call.

items.statement: Plant-2 extension fully operational; oral solids capacity sufficient for ~INR800 crores revenue; Plant-6 to add capacity for INR1,000 crores target
items.quote: So we have sufficient capacity for our oral solids and oral liquids business to reach across about INR800 crores. This is aside of injectables. So that much capacity with plan 2 expansion is in place now.

items.statement: Injectables facility GMP certified in Dec 2024; large customer audits scheduled in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Jan 2025, the injectables facility received Good Manufacturing Practices GMP certification from the Food Safety & Drugs Administration Authority of Uttarakhand following an inspection in December 2024 confirming compliance with WHO's TRS guidelines in all five plants now of the company. Accordingly, large customers have scheduled audits of our injectable facility in Q4 of FY '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.3% for 9M FY25 and 12.6% for Q3 FY25 despite injectable facility depreciation increase of INR9.7 crores (9M) and INR3.6 crores (Q3)
items.quote: EBITDA surged by 22% Y-o-Y to INR68.6 crores, 12.3% margin for 9-month FY '25 and by 21% Y-o-Y to INR24.6 crores, 12.6% margin for Q3 FY '25. Despite increase in depreciation by INR9.7 crores for 9 months FY '25 and INR3.6 crores for Q3 FY '25 almost entirely due to injectable facility, PAT stood at INR44.7 crores, up 9% for 9-month FY '25 Y-o-Y and INR15.6 crores, up 3% Y-o-Y for Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Some order book exists for injectables from stability batches; commercialization progressing as audits scheduled
items.quote: There might be more in Q1 of FY '25. So we'll have to -- having said that, there is already some order book in place for our existing production happening and products getting ready for commercialization and out of stability batches.

items.statement: API price reductions impacted CDMO conversion due to cost-plus model; long-term impact neutralized
items.quote: API prices have fallen down and there has been obviously some effect on conversion. But having said that, there has also been increase in past and so API prices tend to have some impact because ours is a cost plus model. In the long run it gets pacified for plus as well as minus in API prices.

items.statement: IP ownership (99%) enables selling same formulation to multiple customers; not just job work; drives EBITDA margins
items.quote: When you actually have IP, then you have the ability to use that IP and sell the same formulation maybe with a different color tablet or with different packing material to multiple customers. Then essentially you're not selling capacity. You have developed the product and you are able to take it to multiple customers and grow and that's what we are doing.

items.statement: Net cash position includes mutual funds >INR200 crores, FDs ~INR15-16 crores, cash in bank minus CC utilization
items.quote: So we have money lying in mutual funds upwards of INR200 crores. There is some -- mutual funds includes liquid funds, debt funds. There is also fixed deposits of about INR15 crores - INR16 crores. Some money lying in cash in bank and minus CC utilization that keeps happening and keeps changing that's broadly.

items.statement: Injectables facility investment ~INR75 crores; depreciation on WDV method
items.quote: Investment in injectables about INR75 crores.

items.statement: No break-even guidance for injectables; management refuses to disclose injectable opex due to cost-plus competitive sensitivity
items.quote: So we have not given any kind of guidance. Of course the goal of the entire management is to achieve the break-even milestone as soon as possible. But we have not given any guidance and we would request you to let us stay in that.

items.statement: Working capital days and net cash not disclosed; stated to be within typical range
items.quote: So again Neelam, since those are not part of LR, we are not sort of disclosing those numbers. But we are still within range of what we have been typically.

items.statement: Targeting KFC brand contribution margin of 19-20% at about 100,000 ADS over a few quarters
items.quote: we are targeting KFC to get to 19 to 20% margin at about 100,000 ADS , and we are tracking on that . It will take us a few quarters to be able to get there

items.statement: Plan to add 20-25 stores in Thailand (8-9% growth) and target 3-4% SSSG for 11-12% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We plan to add about 20 to 25 stores, which is 8 to 9% of the stores that we have. And then on top , we are targeting a SSSG of about 3 to 4% which should give us about 11 to 12% revenue growth.

items.statement: Will moderate Pizza Hut expansion further versus current pace; expansion dependent on brand performance
items.quote: Going forward, as we have spoken in the past, we will be moderating Pizza Hut expansion, and you will see even further lower numbers versus what we have done so far.

items.statement: Three new QSR brands planned for launch from Q1 FY26 (April onwards)
items.quote: Yes, we are on track from Quarter 1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Focus on small format stores which are highly capital efficient and offer stronger payback potential
items.quote: A key driver of this has been our focus on small format stores over the past few years which are highly capital efficient and offer stronger payback potential.

items.statement: Added 111 net new stores in Q3 FY25, total store count 2,032 as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: In Quarter 3, we added 111 net new stores, bringing our total store count to 2 ,032 as of December 31st, 2024.

items.statement: Core brands KFC, Pizza Hut, Costa added 107 stores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our core brands KFC, Pizza Hut and Costa added 107 stores in Quarter 3, thereby further strengthening our brand performance.

items.statement: KFC India added 44 stores in Q3 FY25, total 689 stores
items.quote: KFC in India added 44 new stores in Q3 FY25. With this, the total store count for KFC in India stands at 689 stores at the end of Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India added 51 stores in Q3 FY25, total 644 stores
items.quote: During the quarter, Pizza Hut added 51 new stores, reaching a total count of 644 stores in India.

items.statement: Costa Coffee added 2 stores in Q3 FY25, total 209 stores
items.quote: Costa Coffee added two new stores during the quarter, reaching a cumulative store count of 209 stores.

items.statement: International stores total 374 with 9 KFC stores added in Thailand and 1 Pizza Hut store in Nepal in Q3
items.quote: Total number of international stores was 374 with the addition of 9 new KFC stores in Thailand and 1 Pizza Hut store in Nepal in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment remained subdued but green shoots of recovery seen in metro and large cities during festive season
items.quote: While the overall consumer sentiment remained a little subdued , during the festive season our QSR in general and DIL witnessed some green shoots of recovery in the metro and large cities.

items.statement: KFC and Pizza Hut clocked highest-ever sales on big festival days driven by value menu items and discounts
items.quote: With both brands experiencing recovery in demand by clocking highest -ever sales of big festival days.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 68.7%, down 60 bps QoQ due to food inflation in oil, chicken, cheese, coffee beans
items.quote: The gross margin for the consolidated business was 68.7%, a drop of 60 basis points versus the previous quarter. The impact on gross margins was primarily due to food inflation that we have seen in core brands, driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing.

items.statement: Consolidated brand contribution 14.3%, up 70 bps QoQ on sales leverage and cost optimization in India and Nigeria
items.quote: The brand contribution for Q3 FY25 stood at 14.3%, higher by 70 basis points versus the previous quarter. Improvement in brand contribution was mainly on account of sales leverage and fresh measures on cost optimization in the Indian and Nigerian operations.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution 17.2%, up 60 bps QoQ on better sales leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The brand contribution margin at 17.2% for the current quarter saw an improvement of 60 basis points because of better sales leverage and cost optimization measures.

items.statement: Pizza Hut brand contribution 2.1% (Rs 4 crore); margins lower but expected to improve from next quarter on marketing cost optimization
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 76.2%, and brand contribution for the quarter was Rs. 4 crore with the margin at 2.1%.

items.statement: Costa Coffee brand contribution 16.9%, gross margin 75.5% up 50 bps QoQ
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 75.5%, an improvement of 50 basis points over the previous quarter. Brand contribution in Q3 saw an improvement and stood at 16.9%.

items.statement: International brand contribution 16.6%, up 60 bps QoQ; reported EBITDA 14.9% vs 13.4% in Q2
items.quote: Brand contribution margin at 16.6% saw an improvement of 60 basis points versus Q2 FY25. The reported EBITDA was 14.9% during the quarter versus 13.4% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Expect Pizza Hut margin improvement from next quarter due to marketing cost optimization and fresh cost measures
items.quote: we will see margin improvement coming from next quarter because we are optimizing the marketing cost in Pizza Hut versus what we have done in the last 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Fresh cost optimization measures in KFC and Pizza Hut (labor, electricity) to yield results from January
items.quote: At the same time, we have taken some fresh cost optimization measures also in Pizza Hut as well as KFC, which will start to yield the results from January onwards.

items.statement: Food inflation driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing impacted gross margins
items.quote: The impact on gross margins was primarily due to food inflation that we have seen in core brands, driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing.

items.statement: Value menu items (KFC Roll Variants, Snackers, Epic Savers) and Pizza Hut discounts drove volumes during festive season
items.quote: For the budget conscious consumers, Value Menu Items such as KFC Roll Variants and Snackers were major attractions during the festive season. KFC Epic Savers and Pizza Hut discounts offered help in driving volumes.

items.statement: Vaango SSSG strong due to older airport locations; new stores in food courts/high streets start lower and mature over time
items.quote: Vaango is doing well on SSSG because of the older locations, because that is how the SSSG gets calculated , the formula is one -year-old stores . During the period ended 9 months we have added 31 new stores in Vaango. The new stores typically start the journey at a lower rate and then they mature over a period of time .

items.statement: KFC performance impacted in Kerala, Assam, West Bengal due to geopolitical situation; improvement seen as situation stabilizes
items.quote: We have primarily seen the KFC numbers getting impacted in Kerala, Assam and West Bengal, which are very highly concentrated because of geopolitical situation. However there also we have seen an improvement and a turnaround happening.

items.statement: Sister franchise partner has higher metro share where recovery is better; DIL sees similar trends in metros but not big divergence
items.quote: As you know, our sister franchise partner is predominantly present in the large metros because if you look at the country, they have a higher share of metro cities. And we have seen a better recovery in metros versus smaller ones.

items.statement: Union Budget 2025 new personal tax regime expected to enhance purchasing power and improve consumer spending for QSR industry
items.quote: We are optimistic that the recently presented Union Budget 2025, particularly the new personal tax regime, will bring much needed cheer for the middle class in the country. In our view , the Budget should enhance purchasing power leading to improved consumer spending.

items.statement: Nigerian currency showing signs of stabilization, broke continuous weakening trend in Q3
items.quote: The Nigerian currency is showing signs of stabilization and broke its continuous weakening trend in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Thailand currency impact caused 100 bps drop in international gross margin due to closing inventory valuation
items.quote: The gross margin was 64.1%, a drop of 100 basis points versus the previous quarter because of Thailand currency impact on closing inventory valuation.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation impact minimal on operations; only key equipment capex affected; international consolidation is translation effect
items.quote: we don't have a lot of imports except for, we only get a little bit impacted by, key equipments on the capex side. But as far as operations are concerned, the impact will eventually come in depreciation. But otherwise, on the raw material side, packing material side, our import structure is very small.

items.statement: No change in aggregator agreements yet; discussions ongoing but managed to hold against pressure
items.quote: No, not yet. So the discussions are on, because there has been a pressure from the aggregators, but so far we have managed to hold.

items.statement: PBT improved to Rs 9 crore from loss of Rs 4 crore QoQ on better EBITDA
items.quote: The PBT for Q3 FY25 on a consolidated basis was Rs . 9 crore versus a loss of Rs. 4 crore for the previous quarter. The improvement in PBT is primarily on account of better EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 1,294 crore, up 53.5% YoY (includes Thailand acquired Jan 2024)
items.quote: DIL's consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,294 crore, reflecting a 53.5% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: India business revenue Rs 873 crore, up 9.6% YoY mainly due to store expansion; up 4.4% QoQ
items.quote: The Indian business witnessed a growth of 9.6% year-on-year mainly due to store expansion. Revenue was Rs . 873 crore with growth of 4.4% versus the previous quarter.

items.statement: International revenue Rs 430 crore, up 9% QoQ
items.quote: The international revenue for the quarter was Rs. 430 crore with growth of 9% versus Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Consolidated pre-IndAS EBITDA Rs 131 crore (10.1% margin) vs Rs 114 crore previous quarter; post-IndAS EBITDA margin 16.9% vs 16.3%
items.quote: Consolidated operating EBITDA on a pre-IndAS basis was Rs. 131 crore vs Rs. 114 crore in the previous quarter. The pre-IndAS margins for the quarter for the consolidated business were 10.1% , an improvement of 70 basis points versus the previous quarter. The Consolidated reported EBITDA on a post -IndAS basis was 16.9% versus 16.3% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Aggressive expansion during downturn is conscious strategy; missing real estate opportunities is irreversible; cannot open 400 stores in one year later
items.quote: If we were to say that there's a downturn of three years and we will be able to open 400 stores together in the fourth year, it's physically not possible. So, it's a very different nature of business , and that's the reason we are kind of at it because eventually, if we all believe in the India story and we all believe that India will grow, the economy will grow , and the consumer sentiment will i

items.statement: Pizza Hut expansion moderated due to brand performance; DA commitments forced some openings but flexibility exists
items.quote: If you look at our openings on Pizza Hut this year are lower versus the previous year. And therefore, there is flexibility available. But again, at the same time, we are very cautious that we should not be defaulting on our agreements, and the DA works from January to December period. So, therefore, we will be recalibrating Pizza Hut as we go along.

items.statement: Opened first food court under JV with PVR INOX at Kota (51% economic interest); entity to be consolidated per AS-28
items.quote: We opened our first food court under the strategic tie-up with PVR INOX at Kota. DIL has an economic interest of 51% in the new Company. Please note that this entity shall be consolidated in accordance with Accounting Standards 28.

items.statement: Experimenting with KFC Coffee in some outlets but strategy focuses on smaller formats for payback efficiency, not large formats like McCafe
items.quote: we have introduced, and we have experimented with KFC Coffee in some of the outlets. Now, this is a different strategy versus what McDonald's is doing by way of McCafe or what Burger King is doing by way of BK Café because they operate large stores, and whereas our strategy is to bring the formats down to focus on the core, to make it more efficient on the paybacks and the margins.

items.statement: In discussions with aggregators on 10-minute delivery; KFC ready-to-eat model can participate; Pizza Hut preparation time 7-9 minutes
items.quote: we are also in discussions with one or two players in terms of how we can participate and experiment. Just to give you as to how the dynamics work, take the example of Pizza Hut, the pizza is prepared after you get the order and the preparation time itself is about 7 to 8 minutes. Depending on the pizza, it could be 9 minutes also. And then you have the delivery time. Whereas if you look at a bran

items.statement: Full-year FY25 sales volume guidance trimmed to 4.6-4.8 million sq ft and sales value to INR 2,400-2,700 crores
items.quote: Based on our sustainable sales expectation for Q4 and contribution from the 2 launches that are expected this quarter, we are constrained to trim our full year number to about 4.6 - 4.8 million square feet. Sales values go down to some extent.

items.statement: Q4 handover target of 1,500 units vs 1,300 units last year
items.quote: We are setting ourselves with a targeted Q4 handovers of about 1,500 units as compared to 1,300 units that we did last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin (excl. other income) guided at 22-25% annually; PBT margin 9-11%; PAT margin 8-10%
items.quote: We believe EBITDA without other income can reasonably stabilize between 22% - 25% at any point of time on an annual basis. Quarter-to-quarter fluctuations will always be there because of base effect.

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration to nearly triple annual revenue by FY28 from ~INR 1,000 crores base
items.quote: On a medium-term basis, as we have said, we are looking at more than nearly tripling our revenues on an annual revenue recognition by FY '28, which is a 3 years plan that we have articulated publicly.

items.statement: Robust demand with customer activity reviving post festive season from late October 2024
items.quote: Customer activities have revived post the beginning of festive season, midway through October-November 2024. We have seen a remarkable bounce back in customer activity; therefore, we remain positive about the underlying market conditions.

items.statement: Q3 sales volume 1.26 msf (+22% QoQ, +14% YoY); sales value INR 670 cr (+18% QoQ, +14% YoY)
items.quote: Firstly, I'm pleased to announce that we achieved resilient quarterly sales of 1.26 million square feet, 22% quarter -on-quarter and 14% year -on-year increase. And the sales value of INR 670 crores, which is 18% increase on quarter -on-quarter and 14% increase on year-on-year in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 9-month sales volume ~3 msf; 9-month sales value not explicitly stated but implied ~INR 1,800-1,900 cr
items.quote: Because we had a muted Q2 and a mix trend in Q3, the 9 -month performance remained almost muted or almost same as previous year.

items.statement: Acquired development rights for 3 new projects (Yelahanka, Electronic City, Koyambedu) with 1.1 msf potential and GDV INR 850-1,000 cr
items.quote: Shriram Properties has acquired development rights for 3 new projects in Yelahanka, which is North Bangalore; Electronic City in South Bangalore; and Koyambedu in Chennai with a combined development potential of 1.1 million square feet and a gross development value of about INR 850 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Target to double launch pipeline from 17 msf to 30-35 msf over next 12-24 months
items.quote: As we have set out to achieve our medium-term aspiration, we need to nearly double our pipeline from 17 million square fee t launch pipeline to over 30 million square feet in the next 12 to 18 months, max 24 months

items.statement: Q3 gross margin ~31%, EBITDA margin ~24% (incl. other operating revenue), PBT margin ~8%
items.quote: Overall, margins remained healthy, that clearly shows that the projects that are getting recognized have a healthy margin profile. Gross margins are about 31%. EBITDA margins were about 24%, 8% PBT margins.

items.statement: Portfolio price hike ~5% in FY25 so far; mid-market realization ~INR 6,700/sq ft (70% of portfolio); plot prices up INR 500/sq ft YoY
items.quote: Overall, price remains stable. Our portfolio price hike is in the range of about 5% during the year so far, appreciable modesty in price hikes because we have had very robust price hikes over the last 2 years, 20% growth in our portfolio price averages between FY '23 and '24.

items.statement: 3 definitive launches planned for Q4 (Pune, Bangalore Electronic City, Kolkata contingent); 2 launches high confidence
items.quote: These 3 appear to be the definitive launches for current year. Two of them surely on track. Third one is still contingent on the West Bengal. Final clearances are still awaited.

items.statement: Pune launch delayed ~3 quarters due to elections/regulatory delays; now weeks away from RERA
items.quote: Pune, we have spoken about it a couple of quarters now. I think it's about delayed by almost 3 quarters. Variety of factors beyond our control, central elections, state elections, post-election delay in appointing the regulatory authorities.

items.statement: Gross collections stable at INR 346 cr in Q3 and INR 1,030 cr for 9M FY25; growth impacted by deferred handovers/launches
items.quote: Gross collections remained stable at INR 346 crores for Q3 and INR 1,030 crores for 9 months for FY '25. However, growth was impacted by deferred collections from handovers and new launches.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 470 cr, net debt INR 400 cr (from INR 631 cr gross, INR 440 cr net); further reduction expected in Q4
items.value: Gross INR 470 cr, Net INR 400 cr
items.quote: Today, we've got a gross debt of INR 470 crores, net debt of INR 400 crores. So even on a net basis, we are down from INR 440 crores to INR 400 crores on a gross basis, reflecting these repayments, we have come down substantially from INR 631 crores to INR 470 crores.

items.statement: Bangalore Pristine Estate: favourable court verdict on penal charges; bill approved in assembly, awaiting GO notification for registrations to start next week
items.quote: We got a favourable verdict now in our favour, saying the release orders or the completion certificate should be issued and without the penal charges. And simultaneously government has also moved ahead for the industry as a whole on a voiding such penal charges on plotted development. And therefore, both fronts have moved well, and the bill has been approved in assembly, waiting for the GO to be n

items.statement: Chennai Park 63: OC/CC issues resolved, papers moved, registrations to commence next week
items.quote: Park 63, Chennai, again, got stuck for some time, but I think it's resolved now. Papers have moved. And in both these projects, we have lined up customers for registration. Necessary sale deed preparation, sale deed alignment with customer, everything is progressing well.

items.statement: Revenue recognition potential of INR 500 cr from 2 stuck projects (Pristine Estate, Park 63) expected largely in Q4
items.quote: These 2 projects alone held revenue recognition potential of about INR500 crores, most of it should come through in Q4.

items.statement: Ongoing projects 21 msf (80% sold); Shriram share GDV ~INR 9,500-10,000 cr; net of JV/DM ~INR 6,500 cr to be recognized over 1-3 years
items.quote: Ongoing projects have 21 million square feet. Shriram share of the total 21 million square feet have a gross development value of roughly about INR 9,500-10,000 crores. If I strip off the JVs and DMs and minority interest there, we are still in the INR 6,500-odd crores of GDV that belongs to Shriram Properties these projects have already been ongoing, and they will be completed and handed ov er th

items.statement: Promoter HoldCo restructuring: SEBI approved; Murali's effective ownership in SPL up to 15.2% (from ~7-8%); no royalty payable beyond FY25; brand perpetuity secured
items.quote: The restructuring that we are proposing or working towards is very simple. Promoter holding will not change. The shareholders of promoter holding, which is held through a HoldCo. The shareholding of the HoldCo is only changing between Shriram Group and Mr. Murali. We had to go through a SEBI approval because it's an indirect shareholding change of the promoter group. We secured SEBI approval, and

items.statement: No definitive promoter buyback plans; IR efforts ongoing with mutual funds/FIIs; not yet eligible for index inclusion
items.quote: On the question of promoter buying, there are no definitive plans right now. We'll come back to you if there any plans which is approved by the promoters as well as the shareholders.

items.statement: Kolkata launch contingent on KMDA final approval (equal probability by mid-March); some Q4 handovers may spill to Q1
items.quote: Kolkata is still awaiting couple of final clearances between Urban Development, Ministry and local development authorities. So therefore, I'm betting not 100% on them. Hopeful of getting it, but I will keep my -- bit of reservation there.

items.statement: Royalty provision for Bengal continues conservatively at INR 4 cr/Q3 (INR 12 cr 9M) pending final court/government orders
items.quote: We continue to provide on a conservative basis. When the verdict finally comes in our favour on paper, the actual orders from the court or the government, we will stop accruing this and we'll treat the prior provisioning in an appropriate manner. But for now, we have provided about INR 4 crores against INR 5 crores last year same quarter.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents INR 71 cr end-Q3; INR 143 cr post Chennai land monetization proceeds
items.quote: We ended the quarter with about INR 71 crores of balance, and subsequently, benefit of mall land monetization proceeds we have gone back to about INR 140 crores of cash and cash equivalents as we speak now, INR143 c rores to be precise

items.statement: Expects US subsidiary to reach operating break-even in Q4 FY25 and turn profitable from Q1 FY26
items.quote: this quarter will have break-even at the operating level, it will not be a loss. And going forward from quarter 1 onwards, we see that it turn into the profitable.

items.statement: New factory to be constructed on land opposite existing facility for built-in appliances and potential Quartz expansion
items.quote: A new factory will be constructed on the land opposite to existing facility to support above expansion plans in the built-in appliances. If required, we may use this land for further Quartz expansion business.

items.statement: Quartz sink plant utilization at 65% as of Dec 31, 2024; expects to reach 80% in coming quarters with IKEA SKU approval and Karran USA orders
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, our plant capacity utilization stood at 65%. We are also happy to inform a second breakthrough by the new SKU has been approved by IKEA for their global requirement and will overall improve our capacity utilization to 80% in the coming quarters of FY '25, - '26.

items.statement: Karran USA awarded huge order from major US home retail chain; expects large order flow this quarter requiring new moulds and machinery investment
items.quote: Finally, we are pleased to inform you that our major customer, Karran USA has been awarded a huge order by one of the biggest US home retail chains, and we are expecting a large flow of orders from them by this quarter.

items.statement: IKEA approved second SKU for global requirements; expects 10-15% sales increase from IKEA business
items.quote: IKEA, we have already got the order flow. We are expecting a 10% to 15% rise in sales with the IKEA business.

items.statement: Secured starting order with Kohler India for stainless steel sinks valued at ~$1 million annually
items.quote: The Kohler is a good starting point. The deal value could be about $1 million a year to start with, but it's a good starting point with such a global company.

items.statement: Domestic business flat in Q3 FY25 due to softer market conditions and North India pollution shutdown; expects value-driven growth in coming quarters
items.quote: Our domestic business remained relatively flat quarter 3 FY '25 due to softer market conditions... However, we expect a more value-driven growth in the coming quarters.

items.statement: UK subsidiary maintaining steady healthy growth despite weak economy; gaining market share as German competitors face rising costs
items.quote: UK, yes, the economy is bad. The people are struggling but somewhere we've been able to maintain even if it's not grown very steady growth and healthy growth in UK.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin impacted by US subsidiary operating loss, GBP/INR translation loss (INR2.8 crore), higher freight costs (INR2.1 crore), MMA price increase (INR70 lakh), and strategic marketing spend (INR3 crore)
items.quote: EBITDA, margin for quarter 3 FY '25 was impacted mainly due to reasons like the export freight cost increased from 6.5% in March '24 to 9.3% in December '24 due to Red Sea issues. This has resulted in impact of margin by INR2.1 crore on Q-on-Q basis.

items.statement: MMA raw material price increased from $1.79/kg (Apr 24) to $2.52/kg (Dec 24); expected to decline to $2.02/kg from Mar 25
items.quote: Increase in price for key raw material MMA from $1.79 per kg in April '24 to $2.33 in September '24 to now $2.52 in December '24. However, the current trade shows that this will come down to around $2.02 per kg in March '25 onwards.

items.statement: Invested INR35 crore in new moulds, machinery, utilities for high-margin Quartz sinks, stainless steel sinks, and kitchen faucets in 9M FY25
items.quote: To support the development, we invested over INR35 crores in new moulds, machineries, utilities and new products, reinforcing our commitment to deliver high-quality cutting-edge kitchen solutions.

items.statement: Consolidated borrowings INR255 crore as of Dec 31, 2024: INR95 crore for acquisitions, INR35 crore capex term loan, INR125 crore working capital
items.quote: our consolidated borrowings stand at INR255 crore as compared to INR300 crore as of 31st March 2024. The debt utilization on 31st December '24 is mainly in the areas like we have INR95 crore debt, which is for the acquisition of Carysil Surfaces Limited and United Granite LLC.

items.statement: Raised INR125 crore via QIP for capex, working capital, and general corporate purposes
items.quote: We have raised INR125 crores through QIP for capex, working capital and general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Employee cost benchmark at 10% of sales; carrying skilled workforce for future capacity expansion; new salesforce undergoing training
items.quote: we have cost benchmark like 10% of the sales. If anything in that range, it's all acceptable because number one, we are growing and also we need to have more talented manpower. And second, we have built something more manpower for our future capacity expansion.

items.statement: Focus on women empowerment, talent acquisition, and building young energetic team for domestic expansion
items.quote: We are also focusing on women empowerment very, very strongly. Attracting, developing, and retaining top industry talent, we aim to foster country innovation, enhance operational efficiency, and deliver an exceptional customer experience.

items.statement: BIS standards implementation creating opportunity to manufacture built-in appliances (hoods, hobs, ovens, dishwashers) for domestic market
items.quote: The implementation of the BIS standards has provided a unique opportunity to assemble and manufacture built-in appliances, products like kitchen hoods, hobs, ovens, dishwasher, etc, to capture significant market share.

items.statement: US business expected to grow from ~13-14% to ~25% of total revenue in FY26 driven by Karran USA deal; UK contributes ~40% of revenue
items.quote: This deal that we have got through recently will put up, I think the US business to about around 25%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 sales volume: Quartz sinks 472,193 units (+15% YoY), stainless sinks 109,346 units (+27% YoY), kitchen appliances 41,759 units (marginal decline)
items.quote: sales volume for Quartz sink stood at 472,193 as compared to 4,10,728. This is recording growth of 15% on a Y-on-Y basis. stainless sinks stood at 1,09,346 units as compared to 85,998 in 9MFY25, recording impressive growth of 27%.

items.statement: Distillery segment EBITDA margin expected to return to 10-11% with raw material price correction and edible oil exit
items.quote: I think the Company will go back around to at least 10-11% of EBITDA margin from the distillery segment.

items.statement: Distillery revenue expected at Rs 1,750-1,800 crore; biodiesel at Rs 250 crore at full capacity; Bengal unit at Rs 750-800 crore
items.quote: See, the distillery should give us about 1,750 to 1,800 and the biodiesel once working at 100% capacity utilization should give us anywhere close to 250 crores of revenue.

items.statement: 1,150 KLPD capacity expected to generate approximately Rs 2,800 crore revenue
items.quote: 1,150 would be, I think around, depends on the, it's not price in the future, but, approximately, I think it should be around 2,800 crores.

items.statement: 150 KLPD Bathinda distillery expansion capex ~Rs 116 crore, commissioning within 12 months
items.quote: The total capital expenditure for this project is approximately 116 crores.

items.statement: 75 KLPD biodiesel plant at Bathinda capex ~Rs 120 crore, commissioning in 3-4 months
items.quote: The estimated CAPEX for the project of biodiesel is around 120 crores.

items.statement: Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD ethanol + 20 TPD bio-CNG + paddy straw boiler total capex ~Rs 370 crore
items.period: 18 months for ethanol, 2 years for bio-CNG
items.quote: I think including the bio-CNG, the paddy straw-based power plant and the distillery, I think we are looking at around 370 crores of CAPEX in total.

items.statement: Internal accruals funding current capex; plans to raise Rs 60-70 crore debt for 150 KLPD and biodiesel projects
items.quote: For now it is coming out of internal accrual, but I think the Company will look to raise about, get about 60 to 70 crores in debt for these two projects.

items.statement: Current distillery capacity 700 KLPD; 150 KLPD Bathinda expansion commissioning within 12 months; 250 KLPD Fatehabad in 18 months
items.quote: We have already begun work for the 150 KLPD at our Bathinda capacity and expansion. So, that we are hoping to commission within 12 months.

items.statement: 75 KLPD biodiesel at Bathinda commissioning in 3-4 months; 75 KLPD biodiesel at Kharagpur approved, work not started
items.quote: The Company is also currently setting up a 75 KLPD biodiesel plant in Bathinda, which will support complete vertical integration in ethanol production. This we expect to be commissioned in the next three to four months.

items.statement: 20 TPD bio-CNG plant at Fatehabad using 300 TPD paddy straw, commissioning in ~2 years
items.quote: See, that plant will be commissioned along with the 250 KLPD plant in Fatehabad. And so we are seeing a timeline of about 18 months for the 250 KLPD ethanol plant and at least two years for the bio-CNG plant.

items.statement: Filled tender for 15-17% of ethanol quantity from FCI rice; allocation expected in a day or two
items.quote: We have filled in about 15 to 17% of our quantity to be from FCI rice and on an average throughout the year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 distillery EBITDA Rs 42 crore, down 14.2% YoY; margin pressure from high maize/rice prices
items.quote: The distillery segment demonstrated robust growth with ethanol volumes rising by 26.9% to 48,845 KL. Revenue from the ethanol segment reached 350 crores with a steady 37.8% increase year-on-year, while the distillery segment EBITDA stood at 42 crores, reflecting a 14.2% decrease year-on-year.

items.statement: Maize price corrected from Rs 27.5/kg to Rs 25.5-25.8/kg; FCI rice at Rs 22.5/kg expected to further reduce RM cost
items.quote: Last quarter they were hovering around 27.5 per Kg and this quarter they are somewhere around Rs. 25.5 to Rs. 25.

items.statement: Maize DDGS price improved from Rs 12-13/kg to Rs 15/kg; rice DDGS at Rs 16/kg
items.quote: Currently, I think it's for maize is around Rs. 15 and for rice is around Rs. 16.

items.statement: Ethanol price from maize not expected to increase; biodiesel selling at ~Rs 104/litre
items.quote: I think it's around Rs. 104 rupees a liter.

items.statement: ENA realization stable at Rs 69-70/litre; Rajasthan ENA contract fixed at Rs 77/litre including transport and duty
items.quote: In that pricing is very good including all of transportation and duty and all that we got Rs. 77 a liter.

items.statement: 50% of biodiesel raw material (corn oil) sourced in-house; balance from acid oil, used cooking oil, fatty acid
items.quote: For a complete 75 KLPD plant, around 50%.

items.statement: Wet maize procurement advantage: few buyers, lower price, in-house dryers enable blending without process impact
items.quote: Yes, see wet maize is a crop that very few buyers are there in the market because mostly it's infected maize. Once the maize has been wet for a couple of days, it tends to catch an infection. But what we have done is we have installed our own dryers to help dry out the maize very quickly.

items.statement: Edible oil exit by Q1 FY26 to free up Rs 90 crore working capital; BCL working capital to reduce from Rs 200 crore by Rs 60 crore in next two quarters
items.quote: The exit is expected to be completed by Q1 FY '26, freeing up 90 crores in working capital and significantly reducing the debt on the Company.

items.statement: BCL long-term debt Rs 107 crore (Canara Bank, 4.5% under interest subvention); working capital Rs 200 crore reducing by Rs 60 crore
items.quote: For long-term debt in BCL, there is the one loan that is under interest subvention with Canara Bank, which has about 107 crores outstanding.

items.statement: Svaksha Distillery: long-term debt Rs 105 crore (Rs 65 crore at 4.7% subvention); working capital Rs 55 crore
items.quote: For Svaksha Distillery, we have a working capital of about 55 crores and two term loans, one for the 200 KLPD, which has about 39 crores outstanding and another for the ethanol expansion, which is under interest subvention, about 65 crores.

items.statement: Goyal Distillery acquisition not under interest subvention (deadline passed); purchase via direct share transfer, 100% subsidiary
items.quote: The Goyal Distillery will not be under interest subvention. Although it was approved for interest subvention, the deadline for commissioning has passed.

items.statement: FCI rice policy extended till September 2025 (sugar year end) at Rs 22.5/kg vs Rs 20/kg previously
items.quote: I think the industry will have FCI rice until September end at least. When FCI rice was available in the past, it was available at Rs. 20 a Kg, which is now at Rs. 22.5 a Kg.

items.statement: Bengal imposed Rs 6/litre import duty on ENA, creating level playing field for local distilleries
items.quote: Whereas Bengal has now added about I think Rs. 6 a liter on import into Bengal. So, that is beneficial to the distilleries stationed in Bengal.

items.statement: Phased exit from edible oil (low margin, high volatility) by Q1 FY26; focus on ethanol, biodiesel, bio-CNG, ENA
items.quote: BCL is undergoing a key transition with a phased exit from the edible oil segment to enhance profitability and operational focus.

items.statement: PML segment sold ~13.2 lakh cases in Q3; seasonal demand momentum expected to continue
items.quote: The PML segment delivered strong results supported by seasonal demand with approximately 13,21,223 cases of liquor sold.

items.statement: Grain-based ethanol capacity ranks top 3 in India; high entry barriers in ENA (licenses, environmental clearance) limit new competition
items.quote: I think in the grain-based we would be top 3, I don't know. I think the top 3 are quite close by in terms of capacity.

items.statement: SEBI show cause notice regarding undisclosed promoter entity; settlement application filed, awaiting resolution
items.quote: I think the show cause notice from SEBI, I think it was regarding an entity which they said should be considered as promoter, which was not declared as promoter entity and I think the case has been adjudicated and we will come up with the resolution soon.

items.statement: Expects PAT of Rs 1,800-2,000 crore for FY25 and similar earnings for FY26, but warns of significant drop (>50-60%) in FY27 post Revlimid
items.quote: I mean, we believe that this year we will probably end up with about Rs 1,800 to 2,000 crore PAT. and that's our expectation. We are still hopeful that we will meet that guidance. Even next year, I think our expectation is that we will be able to do that

items.statement: Will receive one-third allocation of Revlimid market for next year starting March quarter
items.quote: I think, as you are aware, we will get almost one-third allocation of the total market as per our settlement and that will start kicking in the next quarter

items.statement: Q3 was soft due to no Revlimid sales and elevated R&D; expects healthy growth in ensuing quarter
items.quote: During the quarter, the contribution from the export formulation business was lower. However, the company expects healthy growth of business in the ensuing quarter

items.statement: Revlimid sales were zero in Q3 as full allocation sold by September; new allocation starts March
items.quote: Basically, all the allocation that we have had, we have sold it off by September end. And we didn't have any further allocation

items.statement: Semaglutide India launch targeted March 2026 subject to regulatory approval; focusing on injectable only
items.quote: India launch, as you are aware, my friend, I think subject to regulatory clearances and other issues, March 26 is the India launch

items.statement: Risdiplam: First-to-File shared with Sun Pharma; litigation early stage; India launch pending Delhi HC verdict
items.quote: We are First-to-File on that, and I think we have shared FTF. I think there are two filers on day one. So, I think this we are, working with Sun Pharma on this one

items.statement: Everolimus launched this quarter with 50-50 share; total market ~$120M; Bosentan launch date confidential
items.quote: This Everolimus product, TFOS got launched and Bosentan the launch date is not announced yet. We will announce close at the time of the launch

items.statement: Pipeline includes Wegovy/Ozempic, Olaparib, Ibrutinib (sole FTF), Erdafitinib (sole FTF), Carfilzomib, Trabectedin, Bosentan
items.quote: But if you want to start with this year, we have Revlimid and then we have Wegovy and Ozempic, whenever that happens, But that's the next big one and then we have Olaparib

items.statement: Kothur site remediation ongoing; key products moved to Vizag; still supplying from Kothur
items.quote: I think a remediation action is ongoing. And so, as of now, we are still supplying. But we have moved a lot of the key products to Vizag

items.statement: R&D spend ~8-10% of annual revenue; quarter appears high due to soft revenue; normal run-rate 7-8% of net sales
items.quote: Basically, what happens is, see, we are spending probably about 8 to 10% of our revenue as R&D. So, when your quarter is soft, basically happens, the expenditure that you start doesn't stop

items.statement: Short-term debt ~Rs 200 crore (bill discounting + advance tax) at ~6% cost vs 8% deposit yield; repaid in 60-90 days
items.quote: It's 200 crores of debt that we have. About 100 crores is what you call foreign bill discounting. 100 crores are tax payments that we make for the advance tax

items.statement: Net cash ~Rs 3,000 crore as of Dec 31 (Rs 3,264 crore cash/investments vs Rs 241 crore debt)
items.quote: As of now, as of December 31st, we have 3,264 crores of cash and shares of liquidity investments and we have about 241 crores of debt. So, net cash would be about 3,000 odd

items.statement: Actively seeking acquisitions to strengthen ROW business and US front-end; may use cash and debt
items.quote: One is we want to strengthen our ROW business. I think that's one acquisition we are looking at. Another one, possibly, is also to strengthen our U.S. front end

items.statement: Holding cash for acquisitions; modest interim dividend (Rs 1.25-1.5); no buyback planned currently
items.quote: We believe that we will do an acquisition. I want to preserve the cash for the acquisition. I don't want to give it up and we are g iving a modest

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences revenue ~Rs 60 crore/year; targeting Rs 120-150 crore next year to approach breakeven
items.quote: We are doing about 60 crores a year right now. Our target is that we should target about 120 to 150 crores next year so that will help us come closer to break even

items.statement: US tariff risk: only mitigation is US front-end manufacturing; evaluating moving some products
items.quote: The only escape is you need to buy a front-end manufacturing in the U.S. That's the only way you can go forward. That's the only solution

items.statement: Business model inherently volatile due to dependence on few large products; investors must accept volatility
items.quote: You have to live with volatility and that's the nature of our model, unless you are willing to accept that, you will always see these highs and lows

items.statement: Semaglutide India: Sun and Dr Reddy's already started clinical trials; Natco awaiting clinical permission after BE study
items.quote: Sun and Reddy's, I think, have already started their clinical. I think we are hoping we will get our clinical permission shortly

items.statement: Q3 consolidated revenue Rs 651.1 crore vs Rs 795.6 crore YoY; net profit Rs 132.4 crore vs Rs 212.7 crore YoY
items.quote: Natco recorded consolidated total revenue of Rs 651.1 crore for the 3rd Quarter of FY '25 that ended 31st December 2024 as against Rs 795.6 crores for the same period last year. Net profit for the period on a consolidated basis was Rs 132.4 crores as against Rs 212.7 crores same period last year

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 10%-12% from existing order book
items.quote: We are on target this year to grow around 10% and we expect to continue the growth momentum in the next year as well where we may again grow at 10%-12%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected above 15% driven by new order inflows
items.quote: See with this order inflow, we see at least more than 15% in for FY27.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 16,396 crore as of Dec 31, 2024 with 64% hydropower, 21% irrigation, 10% tunneling
items.quote: As of December 31st, 2024, our order book stands at Rs. 16,396 crores with 64% coming from hydropower, 21% from irrigation, 10% from tunneling and the remaining from other sectors.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of Rs 30,000 crore under evaluation; another Rs 30,000-40,000 crore expected for bidding soon
items.quote: An update on our bidding activity, we have bid for projects worth more than Rs. 30,000 crores which are currently under evaluation stage and yet to be awarded with more projects worth Rs. 30,000-Rs. 40,000 crores expected to be available for bidding soon.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 10,000-12,000 crore order inflow in next one year (by Dec 2025)
items.quote: So, see, we are targeting at least Rs. 10,000-Rs. 12,000 crores order inflow and accordingly similar inflow may happen in the next year as well

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 13%-14% for FY26
items.quote: Yes, somewhere around that range only, 13%-14%.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced to Rs 1,422 crore from Rs 1,885 crore at Mar-24; debt-equity improved to 0.38 from 0.6
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our debt stands at around Rs. 1,422 crores as compared to Rs. 1,885 crores at the end of the previous year, March 24. Hence the debt has come down significantly by more than Rs. 450 crores in this year. Client advances is at Rs. 713 crores compared to Rs. 760 crores. So, the debt equity ratio has improved to 0.38 compared to 0.6 as of March.

items.statement: Capex requirement of Rs 150-200 crore for expected order inflow
items.quote: CAPEX for order inflow what we expect Rs. 150-Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Net working capital days at ~115 days after adjusting for land claims, borrowings, investments and bank balance
items.quote: Our net working capital days after adjusting for land claims and bank borrowings and investments, and bank balance is at around 115 days.

items.statement: Strong PSP project bid pipeline emerging, especially from private sector; targeting Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from PSP in next year's order inflow
items.quote: So, we have started bidding, as we mentioned, we have already submitted bid for around Rs. 30,000 crores worth of projects, which includes PSP from private sector also. So, we have already started bidding for the project. Eventually, we target to get out of Rs. 10,000, around Rs. 3,000-Rs. 4,000 crores from PSP also.

items.statement: Market share in hydropower execution ~45% of 18,000 MW under execution; traditionally ~25%
items.quote: Traditionally our market share has been around 25% and right now, of the 18,000 MW hydropower projects under execution, we are being doing associated with almost 8000, so which is around 45%.

items.statement: Non-core asset realization (including arbitration) targeted at Rs 200 crore per year for next couple of years
items.quote: So, we expect Rs. 200 crores year-on-year for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Arbitration awards in hand ~Rs 800 crore; claims under arbitration ~Rs 3,000 crore; historical award rate >50% of claim value excluding interest
items.quote: See, we have arbitration awards in our favor of around Rs. 800 crores. And apart from that, there are under arbitration and various stages of claims of around Rs. 3,000 odd crores, all combined.

items.statement: Land monetization potential Rs 200-300 crore over next 3 years
items.quote: So, if we have to look from land monetization, maybe Rs. 200-Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Receivables at Rs 550 crore vs Rs 475 crore earlier, in line with revenue growth; central PSU clients are cash-rich so collections not an issue
items.quote: The receivable cycle, there is no major change in the receivable cycle and we are still having receivables, although the revenues have increased, our current receivable is around Rs. 550 odd crores as compared to Rs. 475 crores earlier which is in line with the increase of revenue and all.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow only Rs 400 crore so far (including L1); bids worth Rs 30,000 crore pending opening
items.quote: This year it has been pretty sluggish, I would say. Including L1, it is almost Rs. 400 crores and we have bided almost Rs. 30,000 crores right now. So, that bid should start opening up.

items.statement: New order inflows take 6-9 months mobilization; revenue growth surge expected from FY27 onwards
items.quote: With new order inflows, this project would take around 6-9 months for mobilization, FY27 onwards, the revenue growth should take a surge.

items.statement: Employee headcount to be maintained at current level for FY26; increase likely in FY27 with new order book of Rs 10,000-15,000 crore
items.quote: At current level we expected to employee level will be maintained. Now, as we are expecting new order book Rs. 10,000-Rs. 15,000 crores in next one year, so based on that, which projects we are getting project to project, we might need to increase.

items.statement: US subsidiary litigation ~$15-20 million; entity already sold, no impact expected on company
items.quote: So, it may be somewhere around $15-$20 million.

items.statement: Tunneling opportunity ~Rs 1 lakh crore; irrigation opportunity >Rs 1 lakh crore (river linking ~20%)
items.quote: So, see in terms of tunneling. So, there are many projects and almost Rs. 1 lakh crore of work is there for tunneling. For irrigation, across it is more than Rs. 1 lakh crores of work out of which river linking projects may be almost 20%.

items.statement: Order book execution profile: >50% substantially progressed, 30-50% at Rs 6,000 crore, <10% at Rs 2,800 crore; book-to-bill ~3.5x
items.quote: See, almost more than 50% is done substantial progress. So, in the presentation we have this thing. So, if you see in the presentation, we are put so more than 50% projects out of this is almost Rs. 4,000 crores, 30%-50% is Rs. 6,000 crores which will start moving in this year and below 10% is only Rs. 2,800 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 execution on track for ~10% full-year growth; Q3 and Q4 are best post-monsoon quarters
items.quote: So, we are in line for growth around 10% this year what we had said and execution is going on at all project sites.

items.statement: Bid success ratio historically ~20%
items.quote: Generally, are success ratio is around 20%, so we should get that.

items.statement: Bid pipeline split: hydro+PSP ~70%, irrigation ~7-8%, balance other segments
items.quote: So, in terms of hydro, irrigation and tunneling, see hydro and PSP combined is almost 70% and rest other segment is balance 30% out of which irrigation is around 7%-8%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 other income Rs 185 crore mainly interest on arbitration awards, tax refunds, sale of shares, scrap
items.quote: For 9 months, right? So, that mostly includes interest income on arbitration awards, some income tax refunds on sale of shares investment, sale of scrap and all.

items.statement: MoU signed with Ircon & RVNL for joint bidding on large projects; bids already started
items.quote: So see, We have signed MoU for bidding large projects together. The biddings have already started, so let us hope how much orders we get.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028 with Rs 67,000 crore FY26 allocation; PMKSY funding increased
items.quote: The extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission till 2028 within allocation of the Rs. 67,000 crores for FY26 and increase funding for Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana will push the irrigation sector supporting our long-term goals.

items.statement: Microfinance sector faces over-leveraging, weakened JLG discipline, rising attrition, and high household indebtedness with limited income growth, straining repayment ability.
items.quote: Over the past few quarters, the microfinance sector has faced several challenges, inc luding over -leveraging, weakening of the center meeting discipline, deterioration of the joint liability group or JLG model and rising employment attrition

items.statement: Consolidated AUM stood at Rs. 2,280 crores as of Dec 31, 2024, down 6.5% YoY.
items.quote: As on 31st December 2024, our consolidated assets under management stood at Rs. 2,280 crores, reflecting a year-on-year decline of 6.5%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 disbursements were Rs. 338 crores; nine-month disbursements were Rs. 1,170 crores, down 28% YoY.
items.quote: for the quarter amounted to Rs. 338 crores, while the nine -month disbursement stood at Rs. 1,170 crores, down 28% from the previous year, of course, due to the r easons mentioned previously

items.statement: Consolidated gross total income for Q3 was Rs. 164 crores, down 2.4% YoY; nine-month income grew 10.9% to Rs. 530 crores.
items.quote: Our gross total income for the quarter was Rs.164 crores, almost Rs.165 crores, down 2.4% year on year, while for nine months it grew by 10.9% to Rs. 530 crores.

items.statement: Pre-provisioning operating profit (PPOP) for Q3 was Rs. 69 crores, down 4.7% YoY; nine-month PPOP grew 13% to Rs. 231.6 crores.
items.quote: Pre-provisioning operating profit, or PPOP, stood at Rs. 69 crores for Q3 down 4.7% year on year, but grew by 13% to Rs. 231.6 crore for the 9 month period.

items.statement: Namra Finance (MFI) AUM Rs. 1,768 crores, down 13.6% YoY; Q3 disbursements Rs. 214 crores vs Rs. 459 crores YoY; Q3 PAT loss Rs. 17.2 crores due to Rs. 67 crores impairment cost.
items.quote: For the microfinance business, our wholly owned subsidiary Namra finance reported an AUM of Rs. 1,768 crores as of December 31, 2024, a decline of 13.6% year on year. Disbursements for Q3FY25 stood at Rs. 214 crores compared to Rs. 459 crores in the same quarter last year. The cautious lending approach along with aggressive provisioning has impacted short-term profitability with Namra's Q3 profit

items.statement: Namra gross NPA 4.4%, net NPA 0.56%; capital adequacy 45.7%.
items.quote: However, despite these headwinds, for Namra finance, we continue to maintain a strong capital adequacy ratio of 45.7%. Our gross NPA for the microfinance business stood at 4.4%, while net NPA was only at 0.56%.

items.statement: MSME/Two-Wheeler/LAP segment AUM grew 30.9% YoY to Rs. 512 crores; Q3 income Rs. 44.9 crores up 32.4% YoY; PAT Rs. 9.9 crores.

items.quote: As of December 31, 20 24, our total broadband site count stood at approximately 460,300, which includes about 74,800 TDD sites, 13,950 Massive MIMO sites, and 12,800 small cells.

items.statement: Plan to increase 4G towers to 215-220k (up ~45k from start of investment cycle); add 13,000 more by mid-Q1 FY26

items.statement: Combined VLR subscriber numbers for Dec and Jan show positive net adds in 11 circles
items.quote: I am pleased to inform all of you that the combined VLR subscriber numbers for December and January are showing positive net adds in 11 circles.

items.statement: Vi ranked best 4G network in India by Opensignal across all six experience categories
items.quote: Vi emerged as the best 4G network in India. Vi led across all six experience categories for 4G users: Best Download Speeds, Best Upload Speeds, Best Video Experience, Best Live Video Experience, Best Games Experience, and Best Voice App Experience.

items.statement: Tariff hike in July 2024 drove ARPU and revenue growth; Customer ARPU ex-M2M up 4.7% QoQ and ~13% vs Q1
items.quote: Customer ARPU excluding M2M has shown a quarter -on-quarter increase of 4.7% and it has increased by almost 13% vis a vis Q1 ARPU.

items.statement: DoT waived bank guarantees for pre-2021 spectrum auctions (~Rs. 247.5B previously required); only 1-year BG for 2015 auction shortfall remains
items.quote: Prior to this reform, BGs aggregating to ~Rs. 247.5 billion were required to be provided by the company for respective spectrum instalments, 13 months prior to each installment falling due. items.statement: Bank debt reduced to Rs. 23.3B (from Rs. 76.2B YoY); cash balance Rs. 120.9B from FPO proceeds for capex

items.statement: Actively engaging lenders for long-term debt funding; BG waiver supported discussions; seeking clarity on AGR liabilities
items.quote: We remain actively engaged with our lenders for tying up debt funding towards the execution of our long term network expansion. The recent support from Government on Bank Guarantee has supported these discussions to move forward.

items.statement: Revenue Rs. 111.2B (+4.2% YoY); EBITDA ex-IndAS116 Rs. 24.5B (+15% YoY), margin 22% (highest since merger)
items.quote: The revenues for the quarter were Rs. 111.2 billion, a YoY growth of 4.2%. The EBITDA excluding IndAS116 for the quarter was Rs. 24.5 billion, improving by 15% on YoY basis. This is the highest quarterly EBITDA since merger and the margin has improved to 22%.

items.statement: Postpaid base growing QoQ and YoY; M2M drives most growth but consumer postpaid also up consistently for 1 year
items.quote: In the postpaid business, we continue to see improving performance. While a larger part of this increase is from M2M segment, we have seen a continuous increase in postpaid consumers over last one year.

items.statement: Launched Super Hero (unlimited data 12hrs) in 12 key markets and Non-Stop Hero (24x7 unlimited) in 10 markets

items.statement: Launched Easy+ for corporate postpaid allowing digital purchase of add-ons (roaming, OTT, data) on Vi App
