items.statement: DyStar equity value bids expected $1.3-1.9B
items.quote: we expect that the bid has come from $1.3 billion to $1.9 billion, much higher than $700 actually for the equity value of DyStar.

items.statement: Copper project technology partner: world's largest copper producer, 40+ years experience
items.quote: they are the world's largest Copper production company, very renowned, well-known and one of the best globally. So, please be rest assured that the technology partner has been selected, has been experienced for more than 40 years in Copper.

items.statement: Targeting 100 bps gross margin improvement in next two to three quarters
items.quote: internally we are targeting the 100 -basis point improvement of gross margin, right, in the next two to three quarters, right, that's what we are planning to do.

items.statement: Domino's India LFL grew 12.5% YoY driven by 24.7% delivery LFL growth
items.quote: LFL sales grew by a strong 12.5% year -over-year, driven by exceptional Delivery LFL growth of 24.7%.

items.statement: Domino's India order growth surged 33.8% YoY with new customer acquisition up 55.4%
items.quote: Revenue surged by 18.3% year -over-year, fuelled by an impressive 33.8% increase in order growth. New Customer Acquisition grew by 55.4%

items.statement: Opened 60 net new Domino's stores in India and entered 19 new cities, total network 2,139 stores across 466 cities
items.quote: We opened 60 net new Domino's stores in India this quarter and entered 19 new cities, ending with a total network of 2,139 stores now serving guests across 466 cities.

items.statement: Total store network comprises 3,260 stores with net addition of 130 stores in Q3 (67 India, 63 international)
items.quote: Our total store network now comprises 3,260 stores, with a net addition of 130 stores during the quarter with 67 net store addition in India and 63 in international markets.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 19.4%, down 145 bps YoY but flat QoQ; pre-Ind-AS-116 EBITDA margin 12.4% up 70 bps QoQ
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA reached Rs. 3.1 billion, up 10.6% year-over-year, with an EBITDA margin of 19.4%, lower by 145 bps year -on-year and flat quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin 75.1%, down 160 bps YoY due to higher food costs, inflation, discounting and delivery fee waiver
items.quote: The Gross Margin came in at 75.1%, lower by 160 bps year -on-year on account of higher food costs for some of our new product launches, inflation, sharper discounting during big-days, and the waiver of delivery charges, not in the base.

items.statement: Free delivery waiver and minimum order value reduced to Rs. 199 from Rs. 350 driving order growth
items.quote: One thing that you must note when we did free delivery, we moved to a minimum order value of about Rs. 200. Rs. 199. Earlier there were higher delivery charges before Rs. 350.

items.statement: Launched Chicken Feast range nationally starting at Rs. 99 with ATL campaign to unlock chicken occasion opportunity
items.quote: We were patiently perfecting customer value proposition in South India and have now launched the Chicken Feast range nationally starting at Rs. 99 along with a ATL campaign.

items.statement: Introduced three new flavours to Cheese Burst range and launched Cheese Volcano pizza
items.quote: During the quarter, we introduced three new flavours to our popular Cheese Burst range, further enhancing our pizza offerings.

items.statement: Domino's India app reached nearly 14 million MAU with 28.6% YoY app install growth to ~12 million
items.quote: Our digital engagement teams continues to grow, quarter on quarter with nearly 14 million monthly active users (MAU) on the Domino's India app. App installs also saw impressive growth of 28.6% year-over-year, reaching around 12 million.

items.statement: December monthly active riders 46,700, up ~50% from last December enabling 20-minute delivery
items.quote: in December, we had 46,700 monthly active riders, which 5 was up by ~50% from last December, helping us meet high consumer demand. This also underscores the power of our digital platform to manage variable peak loads and allowing us to deliver in 20 minutes

items.statement: Popeyes CAPEX materially lower than at start; targeting top 100 locations for expansion
items.quote: CAPEX is actually materially low from where we started. I think getting the location is a one-way road, right. If you get a wrong location then you h ave to like live with it for a long time, and therefore we can open 100 stores as long as we get those 100 locations

items.statement: Domino's Turkey LFL -3.2% on base of 18.9% LFL in Q3 FY24; COFFY LFL -2.6% on base of 27.7%
items.quote: Domino's Turkey LFL growth came in at -3.2% on the base of 18.9% LFL in Q3FY'24. COFFY LFL growth came in at -2.6% on the base of 27.7% LFL in Q3FY'24.

items.statement: DPEU revenue crossed Rs. 5 billion milestone for first time with 9.5% QoQ growth
items.quote: I am excited to share with you that DPEU Revenue crossed the milestone of Rs. 5 billion for the first time registering a strong 9.5% qoq growth.

items.statement: Sri Lanka revenue Rs. 213 million up 65.4% YoY driven by same-store sales growth; Bangladesh revenue Rs. 173 million up 38.6% YoY
items.quote: We've achieved a significant turnaround in Sri Lanka, with record revenue of Rs. 213 million in Q3, up 65.4% year -over-year. This strong performance is entirely driven by same -store sales growth

items.statement: Turkey business reducing debt, interest costs coming down, inventory levels managed to control inflation accounting impact
items.quote: their interest costs are coming down, their debt overall is reducing. So, healthy shape of the business as the economy also recovers there.

items.statement: Turkey inflation reduced from 64.9% to 42.1% leading to lower wage revisions and consumption boost
items.quote: We believe the economy in Turkey is headed in the right direction as the Government has brought down inflation from 64.9% a year back to 42.1%. However, this has also led to lower wage revisions.

items.statement: Delivery cost pressure during festive season due to higher rider payouts to maintain 20-minute service levels
items.quote: Where we are not 15 getting the leverage and there is a higher -than-expected headwind, it is the delivery cost. Because delivery at the channel is growing, which puts more pressure on riders, and therefore to keep the same service level of nearly 20 minutes, we are actually paying more to the riders during the festive season

items.statement: Expanded Popeyes team; put in team to carry business from here to Rs. 1,000 crores
items.quote: We fixed a lot of unit economics in the last three or four months. We expanded the team. I have already put in a team that will carry it from here to Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs. 21.5 billion up 56.1% YoY (organic 19.4%); standalone revenue Rs. 16.1 billion up 18.9% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated revenue came in at Rs. 21.5 billion, up 56.1% year-over-year. The organic growth came in at 19.4% while the rest was on account of DP Eurasia sales not being in the base. Standalone revenue was Rs. 16.1 billion, up 18.9% year-over-year.

items.statement: 9M FY25 consolidated revenue Rs. 60.4 billion up 48.0% YoY; EBITDA Rs. 11.8 billion up 42.1% YoY at 19.6% margin
items.quote: For the nine month of FY25, Consolidated Revenue came in at Rs. 60.4 billion, up by 48.0% with EBITDA of Rs. 11.8 billion, up 42.1% year -over-year translating to an EBITDA margin of 19.6%.

items.statement: Domino's India pre-Ind-AS-116 EBITDA registered mid-teen growth YoY despite free delivery and growth investments
items.quote: While we don't separately disclose brand-wise EBITDA, we would like to mention that Domino's India Pre-Ind-AS-116 EBITDA registered mid-teen growth yoy despite free delivery and growth investments.

items.statement: Q3 revenue declined 8% YoY due to lower demand from Diwali festival season and Maharashtra state elections
items.quote: The performance for the quarter was primarily impacted by lower demand with the festival season in Diwali and the state elections in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin at 10.74%, down from 14.68% for 9M FY25 and 23-24% historically
items.quote: The EBITDA margin stood at around 10.74% for the third quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization at 53% across three running plants; Umargaon Wadi plant at 41% utilization after recent upgrade
items.quote: The consolidated capacity utilization of the three running plants was around 53%, which was lower due to the gradual scale up of Umargaon Wadi plant, which has recently completed its upgradation

items.statement: Completed Phase II of Vada plant expansion, doubling AAC block capacity to 5 lakh cubic meters per annum; Umargaon plant technology accreditation completed Oct 16, 2024
items.quote: We have also completed Phase II of the Vada plant expansion. With this, our AAC block manufacturing capacity doubled to 5 lakh cubic meters per annum at this plant.

items.statement: Secured INR 4.5 crore work order from Tata Projects for 2 lakh sq ft of 100mm AAC panels at Micron semiconductor facility in Sanand, Gujarat
items.quote: I am also happy to inform that the company has secured INR 4.5 crores work order from Tata Project Limited for the supply and installation of 2 lakh square feet of 100 ml AAC panels at Micron, India's semiconduc tor facility in Sanand, Gujarat.

items.statement: Launched Smart Build Wall by Next Bloc panels with IIT and ARAI certifications; only Indian company supplying 20-foot walls; expanding into construction chemicals manufacturing (block jointing mortar, ready mix plaster, tile adhesive)
items.quote: The new product launched by Siam Cement and BigBloc Construction under the brand name Smart Build Wall by Next Bloc have recently received product test certificates from IIT as well as ARAI.

items.statement: Added Tata Projects as new customer; 65-70% sales to commercial/real estate, 15-20% to large infra (Reliance, Adani, L&T), 10% retail
items.quote: So almost 65% to 70% of our material is going into commercial as well as real estate business. Almost 15% to 20% of the material is going into Reliance or Adani, L&T or Prawai, etc. And 10% material is going into retail business sales -- retail sales.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 1.15-1.2:1 as of Dec 31, 2024; target long-term range 1:1 to 1.5:1; no debt repayment target as company plans further expansions including Indore plant
items.quote: So, regarding our debt repayment plan, I think as on 31 December 2024, our debt equity ratio will be in the range of almost 1.15:1 or 1.2:1.

items.statement: Acquired land near Indore for new AAC block plant; targeting capacity increase from 1.3M to 2.3-2.5M cubic meters in next couple of years; also evaluating land in South India
items.value: 1.3 million cubic meters to 2.3 million to 2.5 million cubic meters
items.quote: And in the next couple of years, we'll be looking at increasing our installed capacity from 1.3 million cubic meters to 2.3 million to 2.5 million cubic meters.

items.statement: Realizations lower due to raw material price declines (cement at 4-5 year lows) and competitive pressure; passed pricing benefits to customers
items.quote: to the realization point of view, we have the realization in the current year as Big Bloc Construction Limited Q3 9M FY '25 Earnings Conference Call 17.02.2025 being a little bit on the lower side, because, one, all the raw material costs have also been going down and the cement prices, I think, in the last quarter had been just almost four - or five-year

items.statement: Construction chemicals trading at 10-12% margins; manufacturing expected at 18-22% EBITDA margins; same target market as AAC blocks
items.quote: I think similar margins of almost 18% to 22% is something what we are seeing in the Construction Chemicals space. Since even in the trading division, we have been witnessing almost 10% to 12% margin for the construction chemicals.

items.statement: Fly ash content 60-70% (industry average 65%); lime sourced from Rajasthan; cement from UltraTech, JK Lakshmi, Chettinad, Truco; sand-based blocks 8% of volume at 18% GST vs 12% for fly ash
items.quote: So, I think from my understanding, across the entire AAC block industry, almost entire industry would be using ash in the ratio of 60% to 70%, 65% being the industry average.

items.statement: Grade 1 (4+ MPa) blocks 85-90% of volume; Grade 2 (3+ MPa) 5-10%; Grade 5+ MPa 3-5%; rejection rates 1-1.5% at new plants, 4-5% at StarBloc
items.quote: The other is Grade 1, which is 4 plus 10, which is almost 85% to 90% of the volume that we are totally manufacturing. And the third is the Grade 2 strength, which is the 3 plus 10, which is almost 5% to 10% of the total volumes of our sales.

items.statement: Targeting 65-70% capacity utilization next FY (from 53% currently); expect substantial top-line jump next FY; 5-10% utilization increase from current levels
items.quote: So, I think we should see at least a 5% to 10% jump in our capitalization from the current levels of 53%, but then we intend to be 65% to 70% in the next FY.

items.statement: 16% of power from renewable sources currently; targeting 35-40% with new solar installations (800kW at StarBloc, 1,350kW at JV plant); total solar capacity reaching ~3,475kW
items.quote: During the quarter, of the total power requirement for the company, 16% came from renewable sources of energy. And going ahead, we intend to reach this level to almost 35% to 40%.

items.statement: GST clarification issued Dec 20: fly-ash AAC blocks with >50% fly ash at 12% GST (no rate change); sand-based blocks at 18% GST
items.quote: And recently, the clarification has been issued that the fly-ash base AAC block with the content of more than 50% of fly-ash will be classified as the 12% GST because the DTI, which is the authority from the Government of India, which is evaluating GST rates for different products, has been trying to identify this issue.

items.statement: Organized vs unorganized AAC players ~50-50; organized players command 3-7% premium due to timely supply and volume capability
items.quote: So, I think that would be today at approximately 50-50 ratio sort of.

items.statement: Maharashtra demand picking up post mid-December election results; Mumbai infrastructure projects and Navi Mumbai Airport driving housing demand; Pune IT growth strong
items.quote: And post the election results from mid-December onwards, we have started seeing a decent pickup in Maharashtra. And I think going ahead, the Maharashtra demand will keep on

items.statement: AAC panels targeting industrial segment (data centers, semiconductors, electronics); 4+ hour fire rating vs 90-120 min for sandwich panels; 6m height vs 3-3.2m for alternatives
items.quote: Secondly, the noise installation is also better than those of the desktop panels. And thirdly, these panels, which are the Bison panels or sandwich panels, they have a height restriction of almost 3 to 3.2 meter, whereas we are able to provide single panel with a height of almost six meters.

items.statement: AAC blocks ~10-11% share of walling material vs 80% red bricks; huge conversion opportunity from red bricks to AAC blocks
items.quote: But even after all these years, the share of AAC blocks in the warning material is around 10, 11 percentage, whereas that of Red Brick is still at around 80 percentage.

items.statement: JV plant (Siam Cement JV) loss ~INR 5 crore in Q3 at sub-optimal utilization; breakeven expected at 45-60% utilization with panel sales ramp-up
items.quote: The consolidated capacity utilization of the three running plants was around 53%, which was lower due to the gradual scale up of Umargaon Wadi plant, which has recently completed its upgradation and the lower utilization for the TM cement and BigBloc Construction Technologies private limited plant, which has recently started production, which also resulted in a loss of around INR 5 crores at the s

items.statement: JV company employee benefits provisioning started in current year (auditor observation); impact immaterial as most JV employees are new
items.quote: The JV company considered and started last year, so I believe it is listed out. But in the current year, we will be accounting for the sale as required.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory limited to 4 days due to bulkiness; raw material inventory 8-10 days (increased pre-monsoon for ash and coal)
items.quote: So, this is a bulky production and inventory is a cheaper measuring at our plant in a way that we have to do four days of inventory that are applied for finished goods as well as 8 to 10 days for raw materials.

items.statement: No carbon credits sold in current year; awaiting VERA audit authority issuance; will decide to sell or hold based on market prices
items.quote: So in the current year, so far no carbon credits have been sold. We are waiting for the issuance of carbon credits from the audit authorities of VERA.

items.statement: Industrial sales share at 15-17% (down from 50% historically); expect increase with manufacturing growth in country; panels have better margins in industrial segment
items.quote: Yes, definitely. We are so earlier, if I talk about some of the year, that used to have to be 50% or type of the quarter from industrial sales. It's just one of the almost 15%, 17% in the last couple of quarters.

items.statement: QoQ revenue and utilization growth expected; targeting 70%+ utilization in next 3-4 quarters; no specific revenue/EBITDA guidance for FY26/FY27
items.quote: So going ahead on a QoQ basis, I think our capital utilization and revenue should keep on increasing, and we should be able to reach almost 70% plus utilization hopefully in the next three to four quarters

items.statement: Solar EPC order book reached INR 7,000 crores as of 31st December 2024
items.quote: These order wins have boosted our solar EPC order book to a healthy INR 7,000 crores as of 31st December.

items.statement: Three large solar EPC projects won in Q3 FY25 worth approximately INR 3,000 crores
items.quote: The 3 projects that we have recently won, the projects were for 275-megawatt, 245 megawatt and 225 megawatts, all of which we have won in this quarter, which is approximately close to about INR3,000 crores of order book.

items.statement: EV manufacturing capex of INR 15 crores and EV leasing capex of INR 10-15 crores in 9 months FY25
items.quote: On the EV manufacturing, I think about maybe last quarter, we would have done INR15 crores of capitalization. So very small between the 2 businesses.

items.statement: Gross debt INR 1,150 crores; net debt INR 600 crores after adjusting for Refex deal and cash
items.value: INR 1,150 crores gross, INR 600 crores net
items.quote: Total gross debt is INR1,150 crores. And if you back out the Refex deal debt, which is about INR320 crores, that's going to transfer to Refex, so you get to about INR850 crores. So INR850 crores against the equity of INR600 crores is the gross debt, which is about 1.5x. And if you were to think of it in terms of net debt, then that number is INR600 crores, which is 1:1 ratio to equity.

items.statement: Warrant round of INR 540 crores; INR 140 crores received, INR 400 crores balance due by 31st December 2025
items.quote: So, we have done one warrants round for INR540 crores out of which we have received INR140 crores and INR400 crores is remaining to be received before the end of the last date, I think, for wiring of that money is 31st December 2025.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 582 bps to 23.3% from 17.5% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA increased significantly by 89% to INR 246 crores in these 9 months and the margins expanded by 582 bps from 17.5% to 23.3%, representing a remarkable year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 margin dip due to higher BoS execution; Q4 expected better as turnkey share increases
items.quote: I would say it will be better than the previous quarter. But yes, it will be better because this quarter, we will have some more turnkey projects that we will be executing. So, it will be slightly better than previous quarter.

items.statement: Aim to maintain 42% YoY growth rate seen in 9M FY25; Q4 traditionally strongest quarter
items.quote: So, we have done a very good growth rate in the first 9 months, and that will continue to get maintained and we will be around that range.

items.statement: EV manufacturing capacity 30,000 vehicles/year; slow ramp-up planned starting FY26
items.quote: So, first, our total production capacity is 30,000 vehicles, it's not 12,000 vehicles. Our total production capacity is 30,000. And like I mentioned earlier, we would be going slowly and steadily.

items.statement: 30,000 pre-orders for EZIO and EZIBOT from fleet operators at Bharat Mobility Expo
items.quote: And the market's response has been overwhelming with 30,000 pre-orders from fleet operators.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 250 crores (half free); non-fund-based limits access INR 350-400 crores
items.value: INR 250 crores cash, INR 350-400 crores limits
items.quote: Right. So, the total liquidity in the books is about INR250 crores. And on the working capital, about INR350 crores to INR400 crores access to the limits is what we have.

items.statement: Refex deal to transfer INR 315 crores loan obligation and 2,997 EVs; expected to close Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: As a part of the agreement between Refex eVeelz and Gensol Engineering, INR 315 crores of loan obligation will transfer to Refex eVeelz and which will significantly deleverage our balance sheet.

items.statement: EV leasing business turned profitable in Q2 and Q3 FY25
items.quote: Let me just reconfirm. I think this quarter, we were turned profitable. Last quarter also, we were profitable on the EV leasing business. And this quarter also, we have turned profitable on the EV leasing business.

items.statement: EV leasing AUM reached INR 850 crores as of December 2024
items.quote: With this dynamic landscape, our EV leasing vertical continues to grow and diversify with assets under management reaching approximately INR 850 crores as of December 2024.

items.statement: EV leasing revenue INR 280-300 crores for FY25 (combined Gensol and Let'sEV)
items.quote: INR280 crores to INR300 crores is our overall EV leasing revenue.

items.statement: 80-90% of solar EPC order book from A-rated customers with secured PPAs and financial closure
items.quote: I think maybe 80% of our order book is A-rated customers. So, 80% of our order book is A-rated customers where this is not a problem at all. They have all secured their power purchase agreements and they have all secured their financial closures.

items.statement: 80% of INR 7,000 crores order book is turnkey (higher margin), 20% balance of system
items.quote: And just to give you a guidance, our -- 80% of our INR 7,000 crores order book comes from turnkey and only 20% comes from balance of system.

items.statement: Preferential allotment proceeds: >50% working capital, ~25% EV manufacturing, small portion inorganic
items.quote: If I remember, from INR540 crores approximately, more than half of it was towards working capital, about 25% of it towards EV manufacturing, a small piece we had kept for inorganic acquisition.

items.statement: EV manufacturing slow ramp-up: ~100 cars first batch, then 200, based on customer feedback
items.quote: We are going to maybe make 100 cars in the first batch, use those 100 cars, then give it to our customers. And then based on their feedback, maybe produce another 200 set of cars.

items.statement: Q3 execution impacted by extended rainfall and delayed land handover from customers
items.quote: But I think what has led to a slightly slow growth for the quarter 3 was the reason that we would have had extended rainfall in certain parts of the countries where we were having our projects, so we were not able to execute on ground. And secondly, in some of the large projects that we are executing, the land from the customers have not been able to transfer to us in this quarter.

items.statement: Government allocated INR 27,000 crores to MNRE in recent budget, 54% increase YoY
items.quote: In the recent budget, the allocation of INR27,000 crores to Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, which is a 54% jump from the previous year is substantial.

items.statement: Promoter pledge ~81.7%; Refex deal to release INR 300 crores worth of pledged shares; further reductions via similar transactions
items.quote: So that is going to be a good significant share pledge removal once the Refex transaction gets concluded. Meanwhile, we will also try to do similar kind of transaction like Refex in the coming quarters, which will mean that, one, we will get deleveraged more; and two, the promoter pledge will continue to fall.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% revenue growth in FY26 on standalone basis
items.quote: we expect to grow at a rate of 30% to 35% in FY '26.

items.statement: Guides consolidated EBITDA margin at 26-28% with upward bias
items.quote: I would continue to guide at 26% to 28% EBITDA margin, though I know there is an upward bias

items.statement: Order book stands at INR10,700 crores over 5-6 years; INR3,100 crores commercialized
items.quote: At present, our order book stands at approximately INR10,700 crores, spread across on an average 5 to 6 years. Of this INR10,700 crores, INR3,100 crores worth of order book is already commercialized.

items.statement: Completed INR650 crores of planned INR670 crores capex; all plants on track for commercialization by March 31, 2025
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, we have completed INR650 crores of the planned INR670 crores capex. As Anand-bhai mentioned, all the plants are on track for commercialization by March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Capacity increased from 27,000 to 30,000 tons; expansion across Sachin and Jhagadia units
items.quote: So one in Sachin, one in Jhagadia and another one will come in Jhagadia as we go.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin at 31%, up 389 bps YoY due to favorable product mix and Tanfac
items.quote: EBITDA, including other income, was at INR121 crores in Q3 FY '25 as compared to INR81 crores in Q3 FY '24, up 48% Y -o-Y. This would translate to 31% EBITDA margin in this quarter, up 389 basis points.

items.statement: Agrochemical demand weak especially from Europe; expects improvement in Q4 FY25 and FY26
items.quote: We see strengthening of the Agrochem demand, especially also from Europe. And we anticipate that by -- Q4, you will see a stronger number from the Agrochem , and in FY '26 as well.

items.statement: Targets 180-200 days net working capital in 18-24 months; currently higher due to degrowth and inventory buildup
items.quote: I -- that's what we've been saying that 180 to 200 days is the target that we are focusing, and that is the target we want to continue to focus on.

items.statement: 9.2 MW hybrid power plant commissioned Oct 2024; expected annual energy savings INR15 crores; total green energy savings INR28 crores annually
items.quote: This initiative is expected to generate annual energy cost savings of approximately INR15 crores. Combined with our previous INR68 crores investment in our 17.9-megawatt project, the total savings will amount to INR28 crores annually.

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic opportunities across agrochem, pharma, polymer if value-adding and strategically advantageous
items.quote: we keep looking at any value -adding opportunities that we can have. Like what we did for Tanfac, we keep continuing to look at certain companies, which are across geography.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA target of INR 300 crores maintained
items.quote: At this point of time, we'll stick with our FY27 EBITDA guidelines of INR 300 crores and we believe we are firmly on track to achieve that.

items.statement: No fresh EBITDA guidance increase despite recent acquisitions
items.quote: Well, we obviously make our best effort to beat our prediction. But at this point of time, we're not prepared to give a fresh guidance.

items.statement: Preferential placement of INR 495 crores to Aksana Estates LLP for acquisitions and organic growth
items.quote: To support our continued expansion, we have placed a preferential placement of INR 495 crores to Aksana Estates LLP led by Mr. Arpit Khandelwal and Mr. Mithun Sacheti, founder of CaratLane.

items.statement: Acquired CATS, Crash Arena TurboStars, and King of Thieves IPs directly in Nazara Technologies Limited
items.quote: We have also started acquiring popular gaming IPs. Recently, we announced C ATS, Crash Arena, TurboStars, and King of Thieves. These games are very popular IPs globally, and we have directly acquired them in Nazara Technologies

items.statement: NODWIN acquired Trinity Gaming, AKF Gaming, and StarLadder investing over INR 75 crores
items.quote: NODWIN continued to make strategic acquisitions, including Trinity Gaming (Influencer/Talent Management), AKF Gaming (Content Management and Distribution) and StarLadder (IP and event production portfolio), investing over INR 75 Crores in these assets.

items.statement: Datawrkz acquired 100% stake in Space & Time Media for GBP 4.8 million (~INR 52.3 crores) in October 2024
items.quote: Datawrkz through its subsidiary Datawrkz Operations UK acquired 100% stake in Space & Time Media for an equity value of GBP 4.8 million (~INR 52.3 crores) in October 2024.

items.statement: Smaaash Games acquisition pending NCLT approval, expected to close next quarter
items.quote: However, there are delays at the NCLT approval process and we have been following up on the same. And we hope that in the next quarter or so, we should be able to close and take control of the company.

items.statement: Kiddopia licensing agreements with Mattel for Barbie and Moonbug for Little Angel to drive organic user acquisition
items.quote: Kiddopia has entered into a licensing agreement with Moonbug Entertainment, owner of the popular IP, Little Angel to integrate Little Angel into Kiddopia, and a licensing agreement with Mattel, for integration of Barbie-branded content with Kiddopia.

items.statement: Fusebox signed agreements for Bigg Boss and Big Brother games expected to launch in 2025
items.quote: The studio recently signed agreements to acquire rights to produce new games based on popular reality TV shows "Bigg Boss" and “Big Brother”, and these are expected to launch in 2025.

items.statement: Animal Jam partnership with Slinky signed in Jan'25, new game beta expected in 6-7 months
items.quote: A partnership agreement between Slinky and Animal Jam has been signed in Jan’25. WildWorks continues to explore integration of popular IPs to drive greater organic user acquisition.

items.statement: Gaming segment EBITDA margin 22.2% in Q3FY25
items.quote: Our Gaming segment revenue grew by 52.7% in Q3FY25, with EBITDA margin of 22.2%.

items.statement: eSports segment EBITDA margin 8.4% in Q3FY25
items.quote: Our eSports segment revenues grew by 20.1% in Q3FY25, with EBITDA margin of 8.4%.

items.statement: Datawrkz standalone EBITDA margin 14.1% in Q3FY25
items.quote: Datawrkz on a standalone basis posted revenue growth of 38% YoY with EBITDA margin of 14.1% in Q3FY25 as efforts that were being made in prior quarters to shift towards more profitable business lines in Datawrkz's independent business are bearing fruit

items.statement: NODWIN Q3 EBITDA impacted by NH7 Weekender cancellation, would have been profitable without it

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission renewal pending caused order delays; now extended to 2028 with Rs. 67,000 crore outlay for current financial year
items.quote: see, the Jal Jeevan Mission itself,the renewal was pending. That's the reason all the orders which are linked with the Jal Jeevan Mission, either they have been tendered and the orders have not been allotted, or they are not doing the tender, which has done now, since Jal Jeevan Mission has extended up to 2028

items.statement: NARCL dues of Rs. 700 crore reduced to Rs. 433 crore by FY25 end after Rs. 224 crore paid last year and Rs. 44 crore this year
items.quote: Out of our total NARCL dues Rs. 700 crore, we have already paid roughly around Rs. 224 crore last year. This year, we have further paid roughly around Rs. 13 crore, and this year with the sale of one property for which the agreement has already been executed, we will further pay Rs. 30 crore. By the end of this year, there will be a loan book of roughly around Rs. 433 crore, which we have to pay i

items.statement: Arbitration award of Rs. 625 crore with accumulated interest; targeting Rs. 800 crore recovery in 3-4 years to cover NARCL dues 2x
items.quote: We also have an arbitration award of roughly around Rs. 625 crore with accumulated interest. This accumulated interest keeps on increasing every day, whereas our loan book has been frozen at Rs. 433 crore. Our target is to get the arbitration award in the next three to four years in tranches, like one of the arbitration award at the Supreme Court final hearing level of roughly around Rs. 200 crore

items.statement: Cash balance of roughly Rs. 270 crore as on 31st December; expecting bank guarantee limits at lower margin after rating upgrade
items.quote: We roughly have around Rs. 270 crore cash balance as on 31st December, and we roughly have around Rs. 2,500 crore order book.

items.statement: Actively exploring opportunities in battery energy storage system market with adequate pre-qualification for tenders
items.quote: Before I conclude, I would like to mention that we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage system market considering the huge focus of the government and the incoming business volumes as we have adequately pre-qualified to participate in this tender as well.

items.statement: Government fund deployment reduced substantially in FY25 due to elections and other issues; Q2 and Q3 under pressure
items.quote: As I mentioned in my previous conversations, the deployment of funds by the government has reduced substantially this year because of various factors, including the election and various other issues of the government, and as I told in the first quarter itself, that Q2 and Q3 will remain under pressure, which has

items.statement: Achieved all-time best rank of 14 in GWI world top 50 private water companies list
items.quote: I am also pleased to inform you all that SPML Infra has achieved an all -time best rank of 14 in the latest GWI world top 50 private water companies list. It is an accomplishment for us that we are among the top 15 companies worldwide dealing in water

items.statement: L1 orders at Rs. 2,853 crore across four tenders; Rs. 9,518 crore projects targeted for bidding
items.quote: It is at Rs. 2,853 crore. There are four tenders where we are at L1. That is one, and roughly around Rs. 9,518 crore of projects which we have targeted to bid into going forward, have been already announced and the tenders are going to start soon.

items.statement: Applied for Rs. 2,800 crore orders expecting maximum by March or early April; Rs. 9,800 crore in tender pipeline expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: Now the entire tendering process has started, and we have applied for about Rs. 2,800 crore which is there in our hand. We are expecting , the maximum of these orders in March, or maybe by early April. Orders of Rs. 9,800 crore which is in the tender position are expect ed by the first quarter, from which we should get a substantial portion

items.statement: Q4 FY25 expected to show some betterment but with pressure; normalization from Q1 FY26 with new order revenue
items.quote: In Q4, again, I feel there is some betterment, but there will be some pressure with some betterment from Q3 performance. Going forward, in the next year from Q1 onwards, the performance should be better.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA Rs. 75.7 crore vs Rs. 11.4 crore in 9M FY24; PAT Rs. 37.5 crore vs Rs. 2 crore
items.quote: With regards to our 9M performance, we recorded revenue of Rs. 622.7 crore in 9M FY'25 as compared to Rs. 867 crore in 9M FY '24. Our EBITDA was recorded at Rs. 75.7 crore compared to Rs. 11.4 crore in the same period last year. We recorded PAT of Rs. 37.5 crore in 9M FY'25 as compared to Rs. 2 crore in 9M FY'24.

items.statement: No interest cost except IndAS adjustment; depreciation also not applicable; EBITDA effectively equals PAT
items.quote: We do not have to pay any interest, only the IndAS adjustment we have to pay. Whatever the EBITDA is, that is the PAT because depreciation is also not there for us.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028 for 100% coverage; Rs. 67,000 crore outlay announced in Union Budget
items.quote: It is very admirable to see the continuous emphasis on water infrastructure through Jal Jeevan Mission, which has now been extended till 2028 in order to achieve 100% coverage. The outlay of Rs. 67,000 crore for the current financial has been announced in the Union Budget this year.

items.statement: Prime Minister plans Rs. 40,000 crore river linking project in Rajasthan; Ken-Betwa project foundation laid at Rs. 44,605 crore
items.quote: Apart from these initiatives, our honorable Prime Minister has gone a step further as he plans to dedicate a project worth around Rs. 40,000 crore to link 11 rivers in Rajasthan, which is currently facing a severe water crisis. He also laid the foundation stone of the Ken-Betwa river linking project, which is estimated to cost Rs. 44,605 crore in Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: NARCL dues to be paid over 7 years from arbitration awards; 75% of arbitration proceeds to NARCL, 25% retained for cash flow
items.quote: NARCL total dues have to be paid in seven years, and these dues have to be paid from the arbitration award . Against the Rs. 433 crore dues which we have to pay, we have the arbitration award, which if we take four years, which is our targeted period , we should get roughly around Rs. 800 crore, so we are double covered in arbitration award, during the period, so I do not think there will be any p

items.statement: Industry RevPAR grew 14-16% YoY and 45-46% vs pre-COVID; demand is strong and expected to continue
items.quote: And if you look at versus Pre COVID, the growth is almost 45% to 46%. And our perspective is that the signs are healthy & market is still growing. The demand is pretty strong at this moment. And we foresee a good growth in the coming future.

items.statement: EIH owned and managed hotels RevPAR grew 17% YoY; Oberoi brand 22%, Trident similar to industry 15%
items.quote: If you look at within the Group, within the owned and managed hotels, we have seen a healthy RevPAR growth of 17%. And if we further break that down, we have seen a strong growth in our Oberoi Hotel segment which his around 22% growth. And in Trident, we are almost in the similar pattern as industry.

items.statement: 5-year RevPAR CAGR 13%; RevPAR now ~19,000 vs 10,000 in FY20 (83-85% growth)
items.quote: If we really see versus FY20, which was 10,000, we are running at 19,000 on a RevPAR basis, which is a healthy growth of 83% to 85% in terms of percentages.

items.statement: Q3 standalone revenue +6% (+11% like-for-like ex-Grand), EBITDA +7%, PAT +18%; consolidated PAT +21%
items.quote: So if I look at the Q3 financial statement on a standalone basis, we grew revenue income by around 6%. And just to add here, we had one of the hotel Oberoi Grand in Calcutta, which was shut down for renovation. If I exclude that impact, on a like-to-like basis, we have grown at 11%. EBITDA growing in a healthy range of 7%. And PAT growth was roughly 18% in Q3.

items.statement: Invested ~241 cr in London asset and ~200 cr on new hotel pipeline (Tirupati, Rajgarh, Gandikota, Hebbal) plus renovations
items.quote: The investments which have happened during the last period, we have made, as was announced earlier, was London investment. So, we have invested roughly 241 crores in our London asset and also we have spent on CapEx. The few new hotels in the pipeline, which you see, we have spend around 200 crores.

items.statement: 19 hotels in pipeline (13 Oberoi, 3 Trident, 3 Luxury Boats/Nile Cruiser); 10 domestic, 9 international; 8 owned, 11 managed; some operational in '25, some '26, rest later
items.quote: So overall, if I look at the summary, we're going to add 13 hotels, 3 Trident hotels and will also add 3 Luxury Boats & Nile Cruiser. If we take the split, we are increasing in all geographies, including domestic and international - domestic growth of 10, and 9 international. Out of 19, owned are 8 and managed properties will be 11.

items.statement: Two new management contracts signed (one Oberoi, one Trident, both in India); press release next week
items.quote: And a press release will be coming out next week on two further management contracts that have been signed since our last presentation to you. Both of these hotels, one is a Oberoi, one is a Trident, and they both are in India.

items.statement: Confident of driving ADR further; believes Indian luxury hotels still underpriced vs global peers; will prioritize rate over occupancy
items.quote: So, we continue to drive ADR, and we're confident that we will be able to drive ADR like we've done in the past, and there's no reason for that to change. That position still remains unchanged from previous questions that I've answered along these lines.

items.statement: Willing to sacrifice occupancy for equal or better RevPAR and higher profitability; 10-year data suggests price inelasticity
items.quote: Provided we can increase RevPAR, we will focus on and actually not only just RevPAR but RevPAR plus driving bottom line, we will be happy to sacrifice occupancy for either equal or better RevPAR or increase profitability.

items.statement: International hotels RevPAR +20% YoY; Bali and Marrakech have considerable upside; Middle East crisis stabilizing
items.quote: Our international hotels also have done considerably well versus last year. We have seen a 20% growth in terms of RevPAR, driven by the fact that last year we got badly impacted by the Israel conflict, which is now stabilizing, at least from tourism and travelers' perspective.

items.statement: Flight catering business performed incredibly well with strong topline and EBITDA growth; optimistic due to airline capacity additions
items.quote: All I can say, Yagnam, is that the business has really, really performed incredibly well and we are so happy with the performance of our flight business. We've seen strong growth in topline, we've seen strong growth in EBITDA.

items.statement: Direct booking segment driving revenue growth faster than Leisure and MICE segments
items.quote: If you look at Q3 performance, on a standalone basis, our Q3 was the highest performance, in terms of Revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by occupancy, as well as healthier ARR growth, which is helping the overall financials.

items.statement: No correlation analysis done between stock market declines and hotel demand; last 6 months of market decline hasn't impacted RevPAR growth
items.quote: So my.... first of all, we haven't done that analysis to correlate the stock market movements with our business. But what I can say which is reflected in the numbers is that we have strong RevPAR growth at high occupancy levels. So if that is anything to go by, then the last six months where we've seen a decline hasn't impacted us would be a reasonable assumption to make.

items.statement: Company does not provide revenue guidance; shied away from it historically
items.quote: We don't do guidance. Maybe we should but I don't know, Navin, and maybe we can have a chat separately but we've shied away from guidance.

items.statement: Vineet Kapur joined as new CFO, replacing Kallol
items.quote: Many of you will be meeting Vineet for the first time. So, Vineet joined us as CFO, and it's great to have him on board. Taking on the roles from Kallol, who all of you know.

items.statement: EIH maintains >100% MPI and ARI index vs competition, resulting in sustained RGI >100% except during COVID
items.quote: If you look at both on MPI as well as ARI, we have been able to maintain more than 100% index versus the competition. And that's resulted in a good RGI over a good sustained period of time, except for the blips, which we saw during the COVID era.

items.statement: Strong cash position maintained to support announced and planned expansion
items.quote: This is the cash flow situation. So pretty strong funds position we've been able to maintain. This will help us to support all the expansion plans which we have already announced and are planning to announce in the coming future.

items.statement: Wildflower Hall lease matter - management declines to comment beyond public domain information
items.quote: I really don't want to comment on Wildflower Hall. I think what is available in the public domain is all I would like to restrict my answer to.

items.statement: No fixed occupancy target; pricing strategy varies by hotel, segment, seasonality and competitive set to maximize RevPAR
items.quote: So, I don't, you know, and I take the direct segment. Direct segment; you have great flexibility and a large part of our business, as you can see from the slide, comes from that segment. And that's why we look at our pricing. We're just pricing based on business on books, pick up etc. So, you have the ability to yield either upwards or downwards based on demand.

items.statement: Q4 CY24 EBITDA INR320m vs INR618m YoY; full year EBITDA INR1.5bn vs INR2.1bn (-28%)
items.quote: Full year EBITDA stands at INR1.5 billion compared to INR2.1 billion in 2023, it reflects a decrease of almost 28%.

items.statement: Margin pressure from raw material inflation, adverse sales mix, high freight costs, and one-off items
items.quote: The pressure on margin has arisen due to the cost inflation, which include raw material inflation, sales and unfavorable product mix, high freight costs due to Sea crisis and a couple of one-off items.

items.statement: FMCG demand under inflationary pressure across most segments, impacting consumer spending
items.quote: In the overall ecosystem FMCG sector from which HIL derives bulk of our demand, inflationary pressures are impacting demand across most of the segments, barring a few, and it's affecting consumer spending.

items.statement: Blueloop contribution increased from 25% to 27.5% in CY24 but mainly low-end structures; high-end adoption slower
items.quote: We moved our blueloop contribution from -- sales contribution from 25% to 27% to 27.5% in last year.

items.statement: High-end blueloop structures needed for margin improvement; current low-end structures offer limited differentiation
items.quote: So that's something which is, I would say, work in progress. We have been engaging with a lot many category of our customers. And there is some kind of activation. At the same time, the adaptability -- rate of adaptability is still lower.

items.statement: No major capex planned for CY25; only maintenance capex across 10 plants
items.quote: In 2025, we are not planning for any big capex per se. But obviously, when you have managing 10 plants and always there will be one another capex will be there.

items.statement: Capacity utilization has 15-20% headroom for more production with current capacity
items.quote: But by and far, if you look at, I think we can do more production with the similar capacity. So we do have a room of somewhere between 15% to 20% more production.

items.statement: ECB of ~INR1bn outstanding; 50% repaid in Q3 CY24; no repayment scheduled in CY25, next in CY27
items.quote: End of December 2024, we have only ECB, which is reflected into our books of accounts, and that's approx INR1 billion.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 0.1 post ECB repayment; strong liquidity with sizable undrawn credit lines
items.quote: Debt equity ratio now continues at 0.1 post ECB repayment in September quarter. Overall liquidity remains strong as we do have sizable credit lines, which are open with minimal utilization.

items.statement: Working capital improved YoY and QoQ; position remains comfortable
items.quote: Working capital has improved on a Y-o-Y basis as well as on a quarter-on-quarter basis on account of monitoring of the various levers and acting accordingly. The overall working capital position continues to be comfortable.

items.statement: Exports stable in CY24 despite Red Sea freight challenges; targeting higher share via tariff shifts, forex, and global coordination
items.quote: In 2024, I would say export remained stable in spite of having Red Sea influenced challenges on vessel availabilities or the sea freight and so on.

items.statement: Export contribution ~30% in CY24; management sees trajectory toward higher proportion but no specific target
items.quote: So it is definitely a very good question, I would say. Yes, there would be trend which will be improvement. I can't say whether it will be 45% or so, but there is -- as I said, 3 things: external positive environment; second, the forex; and then third, our own push.

items.statement: Centralized services and IT charges from parent rose to ~55% of EBITDA in CY24; management says arm's length benchmarked
items.quote: And in the past also, I mean, whatever the tax assessments which we have and all, we are able to justify that all transactions what we have at arm's length.

items.statement: Regulatory changes in EU and Southeast Asia driving sustainable packaging adoption; India adoption slower
items.quote: And we are also seeing that in the regulatory environment across the globe, certain countries are making changes in the regulatory requirements. I mean I don't want to go into the specifics, but at this moment, countries in some countries in European Union or in certain Southeast Asia are clearly ahead of the curve.

items.statement: Customer adoption barriers: testing protocols, global rollout timelines, cost-plus mindset, waiting for regulatory push, need for own investment
items.quote: So one is a technical or protocol-related challenge. The second one, sometimes some customers know that it is the right thing to do, but then they are waiting for some regulation to push because some of these solutions are cost plus.

items.statement: Heightened competition from small players in domestic packaging market impacting mix
items.quote: Heightened competition in the domestic market with the small time players entering into the packaging market is also impacting the mix.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2 per share for CY24, subject to AGM approval
items.quote: For full year 2024, the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR2 per share, which is subject to approval of the shareholders at the AGM of the company.

items.statement: Focus on safety performance as key tool for employee engagement and improving safety standards
items.quote: Focus area will continue to be improve upon our safety performance, which is clearly an important tool, which we use for employee engagement and improving the safety standards across the area of our businesses.

items.statement: Geopolitical impact on exports seen as temporary blip; inflation may continue to impact margins even if demand improves
items.quote: We are also noticing an impact of global geopolitical on the export side. However, we believe this is a one-off temporary blip and our strategy to focus on medium- to long-term growth initiatives and our resilience will help to see us through the same.

items.statement: Revenue CY24 INR24.5bn vs INR24.8bn (-1.2%); Q4 revenue INR6bn (+2.7% YoY, -5.3% QoQ)
items.quote: For the 12 months period ended on December '24, the top line stands at INR24.5 billion versus INR24.8 billion in 2023, a slight decrease in overall top line by 1.2%.

items.statement: Volumes flat YoY for full year CY24; Q4 volumes slightly up YoY but down QoQ
items.quote: The 12 months volume is almost flat if you compare with 2023.

items.statement: Backward integration equipment used for alternate structures; not yet accretive to margins until high-end blueloop scales
items.quote: So right now, yes, equipments are not idle, but they are used for alternate structures where we have a capability to buy in the marketplace and produce in-house. So when we compare, at this moment, it is not really helping us in terms of any accretive margin improvement.

items.statement: Cash balance ~INR300cr; no concrete deployment plan yet
items.quote: As of now, we'll continue with that. And in due course of time, we'll decide how we are going to deploy that. So no concrete action plan at this point of time.

items.statement: Tube laminates a key focus for blueloop adoption; currently domestic-focused with export expansion planned
items.quote: And maybe I would say this business and this type of customers are one of the forefront to adopt our blueloop structures. And so that is going in the right direction.

items.statement: Rural consumption showing promising improvement; urban recovery expected but timing uncertain
items.quote: But other side, if you look at rural economy is showing some promising improvement. However, urban is taking time. So expectation is that when we read the articles and something is there really expected that urban is also going to come back.

items.statement: Margin recovery expected as demand improves and blueloop high-end scales; no specific timeline given
items.quote: We shall see that in future quarters. We should see some revival.

items.statement: Revised FY25 consolidated EBITDA target to INR100 crores from earlier INR130 crores due to subsidiary underperformance
items.quote: So in the light of this, I would say that considering the good performance of standalone in Q4, we should be doing about INR100 crores of EBITDA for the full year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target 13-14% for FY26; consolidated subsidiary EBITDA margin target 6-7% for FY26
items.quote: At a standalone level, we should be able to achieve around 13% to 14%. And at a subsidiary level, including Canada, we should be between 6% to 7% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Revised FY25 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 13% on gross accounting basis from earlier 18% due to Canadian subsidiary drag
items.quote: We expect to close the year with gross accounting 13% of revenue growth as against the 18%, and mainly because of the drop in the subsidiary.

items.statement: No consolidated FY26 guidance given due to pending strategic decisions on Canadian subsidiary
items.quote: At this point of time, I wouldn't guide anything. Let us -- because we have certain actions to take in the Canadian subsidiary, perhaps we can see it in the next concall.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 6.9%, standalone 11.8%; margins impacted by Canadian subsidiary losses and France utilization delays
items.quote: The Q3 FY25 our consolidated EBITDA margins stood at 6.9% and standalone EBITDA margin stood at 11.8%. Our margins were impacted mainly due to the losses in the Canadian subsidiary and lower utilization due to delays in new project starts in France.

items.statement: Target to improve subsidiary margins to 7% in short term and 11-12% in subsequent years
items.quote: Our objective is to try to move that margin up to a 7% level or so in the short-term in the coming year, and then push it up further as growth comes in to 11% to 12% range in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Standalone BTS EBITDA margin 18-20%, EMS 11-13% on yearly basis; French engineering services ~4% but pulled down by Canadian losses
items.quote: BTS generally is about 18% to 20%, and EMS, it is between 11% to 13%. And that is what we are targeting and we are achieving on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR1,675 crores as of 31 Dec 2024; domestic BTS order book grew from INR376 crores (FY23) to INR563 crores (9M FY25)
items.quote: Our order book position stands at INR1,675 crores as on 31st December, 2024. Our pipeline continues t o remain strong for both Build t o Spec and EMS customers in our standalone

items.statement: Domestic BTS order book expected to further improve by end of FY25 with additional Q4 orders
items.quote: We expect this to further improve by the end of this financial year with some additional orders that we're expecting in Q4 as well.

items.statement: Recognized as platinum and panel supplier for engineering services by Airbus and Thales; strong engagement with multiple customers in France
items.quote: We have actually a very good feedback and engagement with multiple cust omers, including with Airbus, with Thales. In fact, just in the last few weeks we have been recognized as a platinum and panel supplier for their engineering services business

items.statement: Won over INR300 crores contract for satellite-based payloads for Electronic Warfare Applications; expecting substantial Q4 orders from radar domain for naval programs
items.quote: We've, just in the last year, won over INR300 crore s contract for satellite-based payloads for Electronic Warfare Applications. In Q4, we are also expecting some substantial orders, and we will receive them from the radar domain, and these are for naval programs

items.statement: Board approved fundraising via QIP or other means for growth capital to support standalone business opportunities
items.quote: We sought and got approval from our Board to be able to raise some funds through either a QIP or other means. And so we are pursuing those options, but we will be able to share that information maybe a bit later on.

items.statement: Fundraise approved by Board is growth capital for standalone business expansion opportunities
items.quote: The fund raise, which actually we've got the approval, but the timing-wise we need to get back, is essentially a growth capital. So that's what I wanted to add.

items.statement: France engineering services onshore/offshore split ~65% onshore, 35% offshore; shifting work from Canada to India for cost advantage
items.quote: So in terms of headcount, we are roughly about 60% -- you can say 2/3, so 65% or so in onshore and 35% offshore. That's a rough breakup.

items.statement: Created India team over last 12-18 months to execute Canadian work; majority of new contract execution now from India
items.quote: in the meanwhile what we've also been doing is, in the last 12 to 18 months, have created a team in India that is able to execute the similar kind of work. So we have been shifting a lot of the work from Canada to India, especially on some of the new c ontracts that we've won

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary losses dragging consolidated P&L; strategic decisions on Canadian operations expected in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We will be basically making some strategic decisions with regard to the Canadian operations in the next couple of quarters to ensure that it doesn't continue to drag the overall P&L.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary turnaround targeted by June 2025 best case, September 2025 worst case; may involve exceptional costs
items.quote: I would say June is a good estimate. The worst case before September we should be able to ensure that Canada is no longer a dragger.

items.statement: Exceptional provision for entire exposure in Ausar Energy (30% associate) referred to French court redressement judiciaire; four interested bidders, partial recovery hoped
items.quote: As a matter of abundant caution and prudence, we have provided for the entire exposure. But as it evolves, perhaps in the next month or so, we should be able to get a better clarity.

items.statement: Space sector: delivering full satellite payloads, won largest ever order for 3-satellite constellation; expect repeat constellations and ISRO opportunities
items.quote: this year marked -- or basically 2024 marked the biggest order that we've received in the space sector so far, wh ich was for a constellation of three satellites, payloads for that

items.statement: Domestic BTS order book grew from INR376 crores (FY23) to INR427 crores (FY24) to INR563 crores (9M FY25)
items.quote: Our domestic or standalone BTS order book, which has increased quite well from where it was at around INR376 crores at the end of FY '23 to INR427 crores at the end of FY '24 to INR563 crores at the end of 9 months.

items.statement: Gross value of net-accounted contracts INR32 crores in Q3 FY25 and INR71 crores for 9M FY25; adjusting for gross, Q3 revenue grew 13% QoQ and 9M grew 6% YoY
items.quote: The gross value of such contracts was INR32 crores in Q3 FY25 and INR71 crores for 9 months FY25. So adjusting for gross value, the revenue for Q3 FY '25 has grown by 13% quarter-on-quarter and for the 9 months FY25 by 6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone business heavily skewed to Q4 for Build-to-Spec defense/space revenue; EMS new customers in ramp-up phase
items.quote: a la rge part of the revenue for the Build To Spec business in the standalone entity is expected in Q4 of the financial year, and that should help improve the revenue and the margins

items.statement: Ausar Energy associate under French court redressement judiciaire process; provision made for full exposure
items.quote: This company has now been referred to redressement judiciaire which is a process by which the French court tries to revive the company towards its sustenance and growth.

items.statement: Board-level discussions ongoing on subsidiary strategy given shareholder feedback on time/resources spent; serious deliberation on Canadian operations
items.quote: These discussions are being deliberated very, very seriously at our Board level also. And as I mentioned, some of the decisions or discussions that we are having with regard to the Canadian operations as a first, but more generally, the subsidiary are being discussed and considered.

items.statement: Received STPI Export Award for FY23-24 for Best Performing Electronic Hardware Exports from Karnataka
items.quote: Centum also received an Export Award for FY'23-'24 recognizing the Best Performing Electronic Hardware Exports from STPI in Karnataka.

items.statement: Gross accounting difference between net and gross revenue expected to normalize from FY26
items.quote: Yes. FY '26, it should get normalized.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve from next financial year as annual procurement contracts expire on 31st March 2025
items.quote: See, the EBITDA margins should certainly improve going forward from coming year because our procurement contracts are for -- on an annual basis, which will expire by 31st of March this year.

items.statement: Top line growth expected at 8% to 10% for the industry overall
items.quote: Top line growth, we are certainly looking, as I was telling earlier to replying to a question that we expect made me to grow much faster than what we have shown so far. We have also said that agriculture business is definitely growing in India at a reasonable rate and we would be seeing a growth overall at 8% to 10% for the industry as a whole.

items.statement: Building Products segment to grow faster than current rates, targeting to double the rate of growth next year
items.quote: Building Products segment will grow faster than what we have grown so far. Thinking that the growth rates will be faster than what we have today.

items.statement: Agriculture segment to continue growing at regular 8% to 10% annual growth rate
items.quote: Agriculture will continue to grow as per the regular 8% to 10% annual growth rate.

items.statement: Industrial segment to remain limited and cautious, not pursuing aggressive growth
items.quote: As far as Industrial is concerned, I mean, after election is, almost new budget has also come, money allocation has been made. So there will be better demand in institutional business or supplies. But as I have been maintaining, we'll be careful. We will not go very aggressive on this.

items.statement: INR20 crores capex already spent in current year, expansion plans nearing finalization before end of financial year
items.quote: Already during this current year, INR20 crores capex has been -- payout has been already made, and we are further going ahead with our plans. Our plans are almost towards conclusion before end of this financial year before we make annual operating plan for the coming year.

items.statement: Fungible extrusion capacity exists; moulding capacity being augmented for Building Products
items.quote: There is a fungible capacity. Not everything, but quite a substantial portion of the extrusion is possible, but molding is specific to our business because molds are specific.

items.statement: Extrusion side has adequate capacity; moulding side needs further augmentation
items.quote: Extrusion side, we have adequate capacity. But moulding side, we still have to catch up with the requirement, which we have built up in last some time with this capex we have done. And we'll be further augmenting our moulding capacities.

items.statement: Building materials demand consistent across all regions, temporary impact of 10-15 days from unseasonal rains
items.quote: See, as far as building materials are concerned, the demand is consistent and across all segments across India. It is not affected by sudden rains or short rain cycles. There can be a temporary impact of 10 days, 15 days, nothing more.

items.statement: Industrial segment demand improving post-elections with new budget allocations
items.quote: The industrial segment is looking up now because now after elections, I think the new finances are getting cleared and those monies will flow.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA loss of INR1.4 crores and net loss of INR11 crores; 9M FY25 EBITDA margin at 4.83%
items.quote: There was an EBITDA loss of INR1.4 crores and a net loss of INR11 crores for this quarter. For the 9 months ended financial year 2025, our revenues were around INR584 crores, which declined by around 13% on Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA declined by 38% on Y-o-Y basis to INR28 crores with EBITDA margin reported at 4.83%.

items.statement: Building Products segment offers better EBITDA margins than Agri; industry EBITDA margins typically 16-20%
items.quote: I certainly feel that the building segment has offered much better EBITDA margins than Agri, and that's where our focus is. And if material price is correct, the EBITDA margin should be in line with the industry. And you will see generally industry is showing between 16% to 20% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Raw material procurement prices 7-9% above open market prices due to annual contracts linked to international benchmarks
items.quote: I mean, the difference between local market and the raw material manufacturers or landed prices were to the significant extent of 8%, 7%, 9% with month-to-month, they will be even higher than that.

items.statement: Local raw material manufacturers have started correcting prices in current month
items.quote: But now for the first time, you can see that even local manufacturers are correcting their prices.

items.statement: PVC raw material prices declining globally; India imports 60% of PVC demand; local market prices suppressed by high import volumes
items.quote: You see, the question is that you see when prices are on a declining trend, your imports normally arrive on Indian shore after 40 days or 45 days of shipments. So, there is a time lag between the price contracted to the material delivered. Number two, the local prices of local manufacturers generally are aligned with -- and the local market prices are aligned with a marginal difference maybe here

items.statement: Annual procurement contracts linked to Platt's international prices; contracts expire March 2025
items.quote: Prices are linked to Platt. This is an international exchange, which determines the prices. They are linked. So prices are linked and the local market operates on a buying selling. So there is a definite difference between two.

items.statement: Government has circulated country-wise manufacturer-wise anti-dumping duty on PVC; final notification awaited
items.quote: Government has already issued and circulated country-wise manufacture-wise ADD, which they would like to apply. The only notification is awaited, which we are still not…

items.statement: Major dumping of PVC identified from a neighboring country (China implied)
items.quote: I can't give you the exact numbers, but generally, what people discuss and industry talks is the major dumping is coming from a country next to us.

items.statement: Focus shifting to higher-margin Building Products; Agri at 78% of revenue; Industrial segment reduced 73%
items.quote: We will certainly look towards higher-margin products. And we will also look at the opportunities around which we would like to cash.

items.statement: Building Products volumes grew 30% YoY to 2,262 MT; Agri volumes grew 2% YoY to 16,511 MT; Industrial volumes declined 73% YoY to 931 MT
items.quote: The Agri segment volumes grew marginally by 2% year-on-year basis to 16,511 metric tons as compared to 16,230 metric tons in Q3 financial year '24. The Building Products segment total volumes grew by 30% year-on-year to 2,262 metric tons as compared to 1,753 metric tons in Q3 financial year '24. While the Industrial segment volumes declined significantly from 3,496 metric tons in Q3 financial year

items.statement: Institutional sales to EPC contractors reduced significantly due to payment cycle concerns; dealer network has firm payment cycles with minimal receivables
items.quote: We don't have outstanding receivables Saket because our policies are of very firm payment cycle from all the dealers. And we are mostly engaged with our own dealers. And as far as institutional sales are concerned, as you are saying, our sales have come down significantly. So I mean, there are hardly any outstanding as far as institutions are concerned because you would see that from a level of --

items.statement: Promoters converted INR17 crores of warrants into equity; remaining 50% conversion planned next financial year; company comfortably placed on debt
items.quote: Only promoters have converted about 17 crores worth of warrants into equity. And the reason I always explain, you see in the current stock exchange rules, if you are having acquisition of more than 5% on a basis, it triggers certain other rules. So we wanted to be very careful. That's why we want to divide into two financial years. So 50% conversion was done here and 50% will be done in the next f

items.statement: Net debt increased from INR105 crores to INR112 crores; company conservative on additional debt
items.quote: No. I mean as far as company's financial placement is concerned, we are comfortably placed. We don't have much debt on book. And we are working on a business plan where we will be conservative towards additional debt.

items.statement: Warrant funds to be drawn only when capex cycle starts; prudent financial management
items.quote: Because we will take funds only when we are starting our capex cycle. We don't want to take any money upfront and pass the money here. We must be very prudent in our financials.

items.statement: Worst of raw material price impact may be behind; Q4 FY25 still challenging; improvement expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: I think the things have started getting on a correction side. I would say that this Q4 may be still not that great. But from Q1 next year, we hope to be doing much better and what we expect because we'll be able to put all things behind us by then.

items.statement: Similar raw material price collapse experienced during 2008 global financial crisis
items.quote: I had experienced similar situation in 2008 at the time of world crisis financial crisis. Sivaramakrishna Kodali: In the global financial crisis. Shiv Singh Mehta: Financial crisis. At that time also, the prices dropped like nine pin almost. And this is, again, we are experiencing this year in the international market

items.statement: CPVC revenue target of INR170 crores being worked towards for next year
items.quote: Yes, we are definitely working towards that number. And I think you will see coming next year, our numbers would be far, far better than what probably we have so far achieved because our all efforts are to development of market and business in the building materials segment.

items.statement: SCD achieved 11.8% EBITDA margin in Q3 FY25, first time in double digits
items.quote: For the first time, it has declared a double-digit EBITDA margin of 12%, 11.8%.

items.statement: Chairman believes SCD margin improvement is sustainable due to operational excellence across plants
items.quote: Is it sustainable? I would believe so that it is sustainable. I think the operations continues to be pretty good going forward.

items.statement: SED installed a new SMT production line now fully operational to fill capacity
items.quote: To cater to the growing needs of our customers, we also inst alled a new SMT production line, which is now fully operational and will help us fill capacity and manage capacity going forward

items.statement: Morocco plant moved from 3-shift to 1-shift operation showing productivity gains
items.quote: we have, for example, moved from a 3-shift operation, we are moving to just about a 1-shift operation, which shows the kind of productivity improvements that we could have done on the same revenue and sales.

items.statement: SCD winning new electronic product contracts from major off-highway OEMs
items.quote: in the last quarter, we saw them winning business for the electronic products, at least for our electric EV division, like various sensors, starters from 2 of the major off-highway OEMs.

items.statement: SED margins impacted by product mix changes due to EV volume shifts
items.quote: This meant that revenue grew, but some of the margins were impacted by product mix changes.

items.statement: SED won throttle project from leading EV 2-wheeler customer and global off-highway electronics projects
items.quote: we won a very good throttle project from a key leading EV 2-wheeler customer. And we also secured global off-highway projects in electronics from these off-highway customers

items.statement: Shifting motor sourcing for Matamoros from France/China to India to reduce cost and supply chain pain
items.quote: we are also doing our part of the job to try to develop alternate motor source to avoid the motor duty issue and that would be from India.

items.statement: In-sourced electronic board production from external supplier to SCD India for Matamoros plant
items.quote: we used to buy these populated boards and PCBs for our Matamoros plant. And that we switched the source to India, that is SCD. Therefore, we in-sourced it within the group.

items.statement: Matamoros tariff case pending in court; engaging customers for cost recovery
items.quote: On the tariff front, we have gone to the court, as you know, and like any courts in any part of the world, justice moves very slowly. So having said that, we have not kept quiet. We have been engaging the customers, customer and also and trying to claw back and have some sort of a compensation.

items.statement: SCS second tranche (China and Canada) expected to close in Q4 FY25 or early Q1 FY26
items.period: Q4 FY25 or early Q1 FY26
items.quote: the second tranche was China and Canada, and that is under discussion. As you know, we've set up the entities to make these acquisitions in both Canada and China. But this is expected to close in Q4 or early Q1 of next year.

items.statement: SCS China and Canada business is profitable and will improve consolidated SCS performance from April 2025
items.quote: when the second tranche closes, the China and Canada part, that is actually a profitable part of that business. So, when you look at together as SCS, let's say, from 1st of April onwards, I think the numbers should look slightly better.

items.statement: Morocco plant strategically located for US/Europe supply; 4-5 days to US East Coast
items.quote: Morocco is very strategically located. And Tangier, where we have our plant is the sixth largest, I think, port in the world with just a few hours to Europe and probably less than a week, maybe 4, 5 days to U.S. to East Coast of U.S.

items.statement: Wescon non-auto business at bottom; margins improved via operational excellence despite volume decline
items.quote: I think we are in the bottom of the pit. I think in the next 1, 2 quarters, it should stabilize and start improving. The important point is that we have tightened our belt so much despite these low volumes, Wescon is turning out good margins.

items.statement: Poland plant closing in next 2 quarters; Germany warehouse moving near Hungary plant
items.quote: Poland plant will soon be closed. It's already dwindled down to a few team members only in the Poland plant, but now will be completely closed in the coming 2 quarters. And the Germany warehouse will be shifted to a location very close to Suprajit Hungary

items.statement: Total debt INR 627 crores; cash surplus INR 276 crores in mutual funds and bonds as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: The total debt level was INR627 crores as on 31st December 2024. The cash surplus invested in the mutual funds and bonds was INR276 crores as on 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Indian cable exports grew 35% in 9M FY25 showing global strategy strength
items.quote: Our Indian cable exports saw a fantastic 35% growth. This shows the underlying strength in our global strategy as to how we have moved literally almost, I would say, conquered the Western world.

items.statement: Forex gain in Q3 FY25; Q2 forex impact to be confirmed later
items.quote: Overall gain, Mumuksh.

items.statement: Deployed operational excellence team from India including MD to Morocco for SCS turnaround
items.quote: we have deployed our operational excellence team from India, including Mohan, as you know, who is now talking from Morocco, who is leading this effort as well.

items.statement: SED second SMT line installed but EV customer volumes collapsed causing underutilization
items.quote: We have set up another top line, SMT line, which went into production recently I mean, in that quarter. But the point is we also set up the overheads to set it up as well. But the volumes have not picked up because some of these EV players whose volumes have been projected and we have been pushing us to set up the second line, suddenly, the volumes have all collapsed.

items.statement: New SCD contracts at better margins replacing legacy low-priced contracts from LDC acquisition
items.quote: The legacy old products where we have bad pricing when we acquired, let's say, LDC, they are slowly going away and the newer contracts are getting in.

items.statement: No pre-buying by customers ahead of potential tariffs
items.quote: No. Answer is no. Nobody stocks up these things.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~26-27% for year; Q3 spike due to mutual fund/bond redemption tax
items.quote: Around 26%, 27% only. That will continue. There is no change in that. But in the quarter, this was an exceptional item actually.

items.statement: Products & Solutions revenue grew 10% YoY in Q3 FY25 driven by government and BFSI customers; retail expansion also contributed
