items.quote: The increase in revenue in the Products and Solutions vertical attributed to the increase in businesses with the government and BFSI customers. For the retail segment, where we are expanding our reach as a single point solution provider also contributed to an increase in revenue.

items.statement: Customer Support Services revenue grew 28% YoY in Q3 FY25 from higher volumes from existing customers and new business additions
items.quote: The increase in revenue in the customer support vertical is attributable to an increase in the volume from existing customers and addition of few new businesses.

items.statement: EBITDA was Rs 3 crore in Q3 FY25, up significantly YoY; net loss narrowed to Rs 70 lakh YoY and QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was around 3 crores, representing a significant increase year-on-year, and net loss was reported at approximately 70 lakhs, which has also reduced on both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA grew 27% YoY to Rs 9 crore; net loss was Rs 3 crore
items.quote: EBITDA for the 9 months was around 9 crores, representing a growth of 27% year-on-year, and the net loss was reported at approximately 3 crores.

items.statement: Captive SMT line usage may improve EBITDA by 1-2% over time; short-term impact minimal due to cost recovery
items.quote: From EBITDA perspective, we expect in the short run it may not have much impact as it is all newly started and there will be another recovery of cost. But over a period of time, we expect at least 1% to 2% improvement in EBITDA through these initiatives for the internal consumption, captive consumption.

items.statement: IATF certification for automotive EMS expected in a couple of quarters; SMT line currently used for captive consumption
items.quote: Work on that is going on, and we should be certified in a couple of quarters max because that needs some kind of preparation.

items.statement: Additional SMT lines will be added as EMS business grows; timeline depends on order inflow and could be a few quarters to several years
items.quote: The line can be set up really quickly. If the business grows really fast, those number of lines can come fast. If the business does not come in, those lines in 3 years also will not make any meaning.

items.statement: Solar O&M megawatts under management expected to reach 800-900 MW by year-end; revenue remains small relative to capacity
items.quote: Yes, we have added a few more megawatts, and I think we hope to end the year with about 800 to 900 megawatts under management, and it will consistently grow on that side.

items.statement: Infra Managed Services yet to win large customers; will announce when deals are closed
items.quote: On the IMF side, we are yet to crack any big customers, and when that happens, you will definitely hear from us.

items.statement: Mobile printers gaining traction in government last-mile digitisation projects, led by Department of Post
items.quote: Yes, that is where the traction is, because if you notice the Department of Post was one big customer, a couple of others who are looking at taking the print or the business to the last mile into much more of the heart of India, that is where the mobile printers are being used and commissioned and that is where the use case has increased.

items.statement: AIDC (barcode) products are a new initiative facing entry barriers; traction building gradually
items.quote: AIDC has been a new entrant. We have been a new entrant to AIDC. That is why we are concerned that's a new initiative, and it has to sort of as a new entrant all the entry barriers which we face, we continue to face. So we are working on that, and hopefully you will see how the traction transforms.

items.statement: Addressable market for Products & Solutions assessed at Rs 2,000 crore with 18-20% market share; market growing at 8-10% annually
items.quote: My understanding is the market is growing at about 8 to 10 percent. Last year and year before were particularly different, difficult market years. But I think overall it is about 8 to 10 percent of the growth that has been attributed to the segment, Mr. Patel.

items.statement: Make in India and PLI schemes evolving; industry and government need to collaborate further to curb cheap imports
items.quote: I think the government has done a lot for Make in India initiative. A lot more needs to be done. The scenarios are slowly evolving, and we do certainly, like you rightly pointed out, see a lot of imports, finished goods from overseas, which are disrupting the market. So I think the industry as a whole and the government needs to work together to see how to further ensure that the PLI or the Make i

items.statement: Employee costs ~Rs 19 crore/quarter; will rise faster than revenue initially as business development and operations teams expand, then stabilise
items.quote: Initially it will increase a little faster, but I think it will stabilize as the revenue grows a little faster than for the revenue growth of all the new initiatives.

items.statement: Government project rollouts (e.g., mobile printers) face delays due to elections and policy uncertainty; no real-time visibility on timing
items.quote: Without commenting on the way the government works, the hope that they will digitize soon and quickly. But every time there is an election, if there is something, these projects keep getting delayed. So we really do not have a real-time understanding of how these things work at this point.

items.statement: Management acknowledges investor frustration over limited forward guidance; commits to more structured communication at the right time
items.quote: I know the investor community is frustrated. I know the investor community thinks we are keeping them in the dark. Maybe not on purpose, but that is a policy which the company is following. We will find the right time and engage a little more if that makes sense at the right time.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM target to reach 22,000-23,000 by FY25 end, closer to pre-ban 24,000-25,000 level
items.quote: I think the year we should end at around 22, 23 and it will take maybe some more time to get to 25.

items.statement: Gold loan yields expected to normalize in FY26, with at least 1% recovery in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This year is -- so next financial year, maybe from first quarter itself, we'll see that the yield coming back to the normal levels. The whole year will be normal.

items.statement: MFI credit cost guidance of 8% to 8.5% for the current period
items.quote: On an average, we will be looking at a credit cost of around, for this, around 8% to 8.5% kind of a thing.

items.statement: Expect worst of provisions behind, improvement from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: I believe that we have taken, in case of MSME, our insurance cover starts from the loans, I think from September or October. In microfinance, I think some pain is still there, but it may not be as bad as the third quarter, which was the worst ever quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan volume growth strong, demand sufficient to approach pre-ban levels
items.quote: So for the time being, it looks like that our volume growth will be stronger. So we -- at the time of ban, we had 10,000, then we went up to 11,000 in the 10 days after the ban in September then 15,000.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio yield down ~2% due to competitive pricing to regain customers
items.quote: Gold loan volume growth is there, but the portfolio yield is down by almost 2%.

items.statement: Spread normalization expected in FY26 as cost of funds peaks and yields recover
items.quote: I think next financial year as a whole and, of course, the trend will be evident from the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Consolidated loan AUM at INR 71,410 crores, down 8% YoY, up 7% QoQ
items.quote: For the quarter, our consolidated loan AUM fell by 8% year-on-year and was up 7% quarter-on-quarter. It is now INR 71,410 crores.

items.statement: Assigned loan book at INR 12,472 crores, down 33% YoY and 11% QoQ due to RBI embargo limiting seasoned assets
items.quote: The assigned loan book stands at INR 12,472 crores, which is down 33% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Co-lending assets at INR 9,236 crores, down 20% YoY but up 9% QoQ
items.quote: We also have co-lending assets of INR 9,236 crores, which is down 20% year-on-year and up 9% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.4%, Net NPA 1%, up 70bps and 14bps YoY due to MFI, unsecured, small ticket LAP stress
items.quote: Our gross NPA stood at 2.4% and net NPA was at 1%, which is up 70 basis points and 14 basis points, respectively, when compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: MFI zero-day bucket forward flow declining, collections improving across most states
items.quote: I think the forward flow in the zero -day bucket is slowly coming down. So that was the initial thing. So yes, thing s -- I mean, the things have improved in the last 3, 4 months

items.statement: Quarterly average cost of borrowing at 9.16%, up 9bps YoY and 1bp QoQ
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing increased 9 basis points year-on-year and 1 basis point quarter-on-quarter to hit 9.16%.

items.statement: Dollar bond issued in January at near double-digit fully hedged cost, will impact Q4 weighted average cost
items.quote: The dollar bond that we have raised in the month of January with full hedging, the cost is significantly higher. It's almost kind of double digit, and that will impact the weighted average cost of fund going forward.

items.statement: Cost of funds appears to have peaked, incremental moderation expected post Q4
items.quote: I think that the cost of funds also seem to have peaked out. But the impact of -- okay, what happens is that, as I said that we raised high-cost money in the month of January. So your March quarter impact will be there of the cost of fund. But beyond that, I think the incrementally we see cost of funds moderating.

items.statement: Raised INR 9,964 crores via term loans, bonds, CP and INR 1,477 crores via assignment in Q3
items.quote: During the quarter, we raised INR 9,964 crores through term loans, bonds, and commercial paper and INR 1,477 crores was raised from assignment.

items.statement: Cash and committed credit lines at INR 5,656 crores as of Dec 31, adequate for 6 months maturities of INR 5,297 crores
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalent and committed credit lines from banks and institutions stood at INR5,656 crores. This is adequate to meet near-term liabilities, but also fund growth.

items.statement: Dollar bond proceeds received Jan 24, liquidity now back to normal levels above 6-month coverage
items.quote: The dollar bond issue money came on the 14th -- sorry, 24th of January in this quarter. So the liquidity as we speak is back to the normal level, but you don't see them in these results, you see them in the next quarter.

items.statement: Net gearing at 3.1x, positive ALM in all buckets
items.quote: We have a positive ALM in all buckets and our net gearing is at about 3.1x.

items.statement: Karnataka MFI ordinance causing temporary repayment disturbances despite exemption for regulated entities
items.quote: The Karnataka government's regulation on MFI, although targeted at unregulated entities, is affecting the borrower sentiment and the repayment culture.

items.statement: RBI guardrails reducing MFI loan limits to INR 2 lakh and lender count to 3-4, structurally limiting MFI growth
items.quote: Because the new guardrails, which restrict the loan amount to broadly say INR2 lakh instead of INR3 lakh, number of lenders from unlimited to 4 or maybe 3 going forward.

items.statement: Target portfolio mix: Home loan ~33%, Gold loan ~33%, MFI 8-10%, MSME 20-25% (70% secured), Unsecured <15%
items.quote: So both these will be around, say, 1/3, 1/3 of our total portfolio. And microfinance may be around 8% to 10%. And then another 20%, 25% will be MSME loan, 25% or so, which will have 2/3 or 70% will be secured and the remaining will be unsecured. Broadly speaking, our unsecured -- our target is to bring it to 15% or lower of the total portfolio.

items.statement: Capital adequacy: NBFC 22%, HFC 46.2%, Samasta 32.2%, all well above 15% minimum
items.quote: Our capital adequacy for the NBFC is at 22%, HFC at about 46.2%, and for Samasta Microfinance is 32.2%, which is well above the minimum threshold of 15%.

items.statement: MFI borrower sentiment impacted by credit restrictions, leading to voluntary defaults despite repayment capacity
items.quote: The borrowers as they know that they are not going to get new loan because of the restrictions on the number of loans or the amount of loan or also many microfinance companies pulling back, then they stop repaying the earlier loan and/or whatever they have because they say that, okay, we are not going to get new loans.

items.statement: ADIA invested for 7+ year horizon, no push for HFC demerger, will be done strategically when appropriate
items.quote: ADIA is a long-term investor. So I think there is some understanding that they are invested for at least 7 years in terms of their own investment horizon. So it will be done strategically whenever it's appropriate time.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 15-20% and EBITDA margin at 14.5-15%
items.quote: anywhere close to between 15% to 20% would be our estimate in terms of the top line growth. I think our endeavour is to continue to sustain and further expand these EBITDA margins in FY '26 as well

items.statement: FY25 full-year revenue expected around INR 3,500 crores with EBITDA margin similar to 9M
items.quote: we should be looking – to similar a 9 -monthFY25 growth, anywhere between 20% to 25%, which should ideally get the total consolidated revenues closer to around INR 3,500 crores, and we should be able to sustain a similar EBITDA margin in quarter 4 as well.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 maintained at INR 130-140 crores
items.quote: The guidance for the full year remains at INR 130 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Total order book INR 1,350 crores; 90% new business; 30% maturing FY26, 40% FY27, 30% FY28; ~40% EV
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product categories, are INR 1,350 crores, out of which 90% is new business. 30% order book value will mature in FY '26, 40% in FY '27 and remaining 30% in FY '28. EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14% in Q3 and 9M FY25; absolute EBITDA INR 127 cr (Q3) and INR 350 cr (9M)
items.quote: EBITDA margin stands at 14% for Q3. Absolute EBITDA for Q3 is at INR127 crores, a growth of 9% on a year -on-year basis. 9 months '25 margins stood at 14% with EBITDA growing by 15% at INR350 crores on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin ~10.5% for 9M FY25, up 60-70 bps YoY excluding other income
items.quote: the EBITDA margin, if we exclude the other income part, yes, it has grown by almost 60 to 70 basis points, which you said at closer to 10.5% for the 9 months.

items.statement: Aftermarket Q4 FY25 expected double-digit growth YoY; FY26 double-digit growth to continue; target to double Aftermarket revenue in 3 years driven by exports
items.quote: for quarter 4 stand alone, we should be looking at a good double-digit growth rate, which is pretty similar to what the Aftermarket division used to do up until FY '24. Giving you a horizon, I think this growth momentum in FY '26 will continue very healthy into a double-digit territory. And yes, our endeavor is still to double the Aftermarket revenues in the next 3-year time frame, given the fact

items.statement: PV share rose to 50% of 9M FY25 revenue from 47% YoY; 2/3W 25%, Aftermarket 12%, CV 8%, others 5%
items.quote: With increased focus on passenger vehicle segment and integration of IAC, our share of passenger vehicle stood at 50% in 9 months FY '25 as compared to 47% in last year. In 9 months, FY '25, 2/3-wheeler contribution to overall revenue is at 25%, Aftermarket at 12%, our CV at 8% and balance 5% was contributed by other categories.

items.statement: EV agnostic products contribute >90% of value; expected to remain so for 24-36 months
items.quote: more than 90% of the value contribution continues to come from EV agnostic products, and we don't see this trend changing at least over the next 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex INR 83 crores mainly for IAC and Lumax Alps new product SOPs; full year guidance INR 130-140 crores
items.quote: The capex outlay during 9 months has been at INR83 crores, majorly on account of new products SOPs in IAC and Lumax Alps. The guidance for the full year remains at INR 130 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Lumax FAE oxygen sensor capacity utilization to rise from ~10% to 45% in FY26 with OBD2 implementation; targeting 70% in FY27 with second OEM
items.quote: This will take care for a full year capacity utilization of about 45%, which was earlier hovering around 10% because of the non- implementation of OBD2. We are aggressively pursuing the second OEM then to fill up the remaining capacity and that's the reason FY '27 would be the e date of the second OEM.

items.statement: Raw material price increases seen but recoverable from OEMs in 3-6 months lag
items.quote: There are certain signs of raw material pricing going up. But again, that is a lag. We should be able to recover them from the OEMs in 3 to 6 months' time frame.

items.statement: OBD2 implementation from April 2025 to add INR 60-70 crores full-year revenue for Lumax FAE via secondary oxygen sensor
items.quote: We are anticipating almost INR 60 crores to INR70 crores increase in our top line revenues with the implementation of the secondary oxygen sensor, which now becomes mandatory from 1st April 2025.

items.statement: Long-term debt INR 462 crores as of 31 Dec 2024, up due to Greenfuel acquisition; debt/equity 0.53; free cash INR 315 crores
items.value: INR 462 crores debt; 0.53 D/E; INR 315 crores free cash
items.quote: The company is sitting on a healthy free cash of INR 315 crores as on 31st December, whereas the long-term debt is at INR462 crores, which has increased from previous quarter due to acquisition for the purchase consideration of Greenfuel Energy. The long-term debt equity ratio stands at 0.53 as on 31st December.

items.statement: Aftermarket exported ~2,000 CNG kits to Africa (PV and buses); exploring more geographies for conversion kits
items.quote: On the Aftermarket, yes, we have already supplied about 2,000 CNG kits to the African market. We do believe that there is a tremendous export potential of converting CNG kits in Africa. We've done this for passenger vehicles as well as buses, and we contin ue to explore further geographies and territories for penetrating this conversion

items.statement: Lumax Ituran Telematics received Hall of Fame Award from Daimler India Commercial Vehicles for 100% delivery and quality
items.quote: The subsidiary company, Lumax Ituran Telematics, received a prestigious Hall of Fame Award from Daimler India Commercial Vehicles for its role as a reliable telematics partner, achieving 100% delivery and quality performance.

items.statement: Mechatronics segment revenue expected to nearly double in FY26; all JVs (Telematics, Yokowo, Oxygen Sensor, Alps Alpine) firing with significant run-rate
items.quote: for the next year onwards, we do expect to almost double our revenue within the Mechatronics vertical. All the joint ventures which sit under the Mechatronics are expected to report a very handsome growth, although it was of a small base, but we have gained significant traction on all of them.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: ABLBL to start FY26 with INR700 cr debt; demerged ABFRL to have INR1,300-1,500 cr cash
items.quote: We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: ABLBL to become debt-free in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: Over next 2, 2.5 years, we expect this to become a debt-free company.

items.statement: Demerged ABFRL to be free cash flow generating in 3 years
items.quote: Over the next 3 years, we should be able to accelerate the growth of these new businesses to a point that at the end of that cycle, the company as a whole, which is the demerged ABFRL, will be free cash flow generating company.

items.statement: TMRW fundraise planned in next 9-12 months
items.quote: In terms of time line, we'll look at, when markets are right in the next 9 to 12 months, to raise this capital.

items.statement: ABLBL plans 300+ new stores in next 12 months
items.quote: Over the next 12 months, the brands are poised for an aggressive expansion with a significant rollout of 300 -plus new stores across the portfolio.

items.statement: Tasva to add 40-50 stores in FY26 from ~70 currently
items.quote: I think it would be in the range of 40 to 50 stores from the current level of about -- we end this year at about 70-odd stores, and we should be able to probably add closer to 50 stores next year.

items.statement: Style Up to end FY25 with 48-50 stores; plans to add ~50 stores in FY26
items.quote: We expect this year to end with a network between 45 to 50 stores -- 48 to 50 stores. Next year, we'll definitely, at the minimum level, double it.

items.statement: Pantaloons opened 13-15 stores in FY25, shut ~20; plans 15-20 new stores in FY26
items.quote: Next year, we are looking at, again, opening about 15 to 20 stores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 15.9% in Q3 FY25 vs 14.5% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA stood at INR683 crores, growing 13% Y -o-Y in absolute terms, with 15.9% margin as against 14.5% margin in Q3 last year.

items.statement: ABLBL EBITDA margin 16.5% in Q3 FY25, up 90 bps YoY
items.quote: ABLBL posted revenue of INR2,151 crores with EBITDA of INR355 crores in Q3 FY '25 and an EBITDA margin of 16.5%, 90 basis point expansion versus last year.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands EBITDA margin 19.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Brands posted revenue of INR1,817 crores with EBITDA of INR357 crores in Q3 FY '25 w ith EBITDA margin of 19.6%.

items.statement: Pantaloons EBITDA margin 19.3% in Q3 FY25, up 170+ bps YoY
items.quote: On profitability front, the segment reported an EBITDA margin of 19.3%, reflecting an improvement of over 170 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio EBITDA margin 19.2% in Q3 FY25, up 1,160 bps YoY
items.quote: Profitability for the overall portfolio also improved sharply with EBITDA margins reaching 19.2%, a remarkable 1,160 basis point Y-o-Y expansion.

items.statement: Tasva delivered first positive EBITDA in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The brand for the first time delivered a positive EBITDA this quarter, showcasing intrinsic potential of its business model.

items.statement: TCNS recorded second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA despite revenue decline
items.quote: Meanwhile, TCNS recorded its second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA despite a revenue decline of over 20% due to ongoing distribution optimization aimed at establishing profitable distribution.

items.statement: Overall consumption subdued; festive/wedding season robust but other periods inconsistent
items.quote: The overall consumption remains subdued this quarter as well with periods of high to moderate consumption. While the festive and wedding season witnessed robust demand, other periods experienced inconsistent footfalls.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands retail LTL growth 12% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Lifestyle Brands, the brands have seen a retail LTL growth of 12% across brands on a network of more than 2,500 stores.

items.statement: Pantaloons LTL negative 2.5% overall; positive 2.5% excluding East zone
items.quote: Excluding the East zone, Pantaloons recorded a positive LTL growth of 2.5%. At an overall level, the LTL was negative 2.5%.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio (ex-TCNS) grew 39% YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: While TCNS is still going through a distribution rationalization to focus on profitable channels, which led to its degrowth for rest of the portfolio, excluding TCNS, the growth has been 39%.

items.statement: Tasva sales grew >50% YoY in Q3 FY25 with 18% LTL
items.quote: Tasva, ably leveraged the festive and wedding season this quarter with sales growing by more than 50% versus last year. Tasva delivered an 18% LTL growth.

items.statement: TMRW sales grew 26% YoY in Q3 FY25 with margin improvement
items.quote: Our digital brand portfolios under TMRW posted a growth of 26% in sales year -on-year with an improvement in margin.

items.statement: Luxury Retail (Collective & Mono) grew 13% YoY with 10% LTL
items.quote: Luxury Retail, the Collective & Mono brands grew by 13% in Q3 FY '25, led by a strong LTL of 10% and robust e -commerce performance.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR4,305 cr in Q3 FY25, up 3% YoY
items.quote: The company delivered consolidated revenue of INR4,305 crores, a growth of 3% over same quarter last year.

items.statement: YTD revenue INR11,376 cr, up 7% YoY
items.quote: At YTD level, company recorded a revenue of INR11,376 crores, which is growth of 7% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt ~INR1,800 cr after QIP; to reduce further after preferential issue
items.quote: The total net debt of consolidated ABFRL at the end of Janu ary 2025 stood at approximately INR1,800 crores after receiving INR1,860 crores of QIP money. This will further come down post receipt of preferential issue of INR2,379 crores

items.statement: Raised USD 490 mn via QIP and preferential issue
items.quote: The company has successfully secured USD 490 mil lion equity capital through a mix of QIP and preferential issue.

items.statement: Demerger of western wear into ABLBL progressing; NCLT hearing in third week of March 2025
items.quote: First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months. The NCLT hearing is scheduled in third week of March 2025.

items.statement: Pantaloons focusing on private label; share improved slightly
items.quote: Our emphasis on private label has been there. Over the last few years, our share of private label has improved a little bit.

items.statement: Style Up is 100% private label; Pantaloons mixes private and external brands
items.quote: Style Up is a completely private label space with everything that is sold in the store is designed by us in -house. Pantaloons, as you know, has external brands.

items.statement: Style Up exit price points INR1,200-1,300; bulk below INR1,000; Pantaloons exit price ~2x
items.value: INR1,200-1,300 exit price for Style Up
items.quote: In case of Style Up, our exit price points are about INR1,200 to INR1,300, with bulk of our merchandise being below INR1,000. In case of Pantaloons, the exit price point is much higher, would be probably twice of that.

items.statement: Innerwear at ~INR500 cr revenue; needs 40-50% growth to reach single-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: So we are closer right now to about INR500 crores. I think we'll have to grow by another 40% to 50% from this level to get to that kind of margin structure.

items.statement: Forever 21 offline operations being phased out; positive EBITDA impact expected
items.quote: So it will be positive because we were not making money in that business. But obviously, we don't reveal details at the brand level. It wouldn't be right to give you the exact number. There will be a positive impact on EBITDA.

items.statement: Management says FY25 revenue will not reach Rs 2,000 crore target due to weak institutional sales and poor southern crop season
items.quote: So, 2000 plus looks may not be able to achieve that in this year because of the factor that the technical sales were little lower and also few of the important crops where we have very strong presence, especially in the south, did not pan out the way we thought.

items.statement: Management expects FY26 performance to be much better across all parameters with lower OPEX, full potential of patented products, and reduced inventory
items.quote: So, across all parameters, we will see that the performance will be much, much better in FY'26.

items.statement: Unseasonal rains and cyclones in South India disrupted crop cycles, reduced spray applications, and caused 35% drop in chilli prices, hurting farmer purchasing power
items.quote: The recent cyclones in South India brought unusual weather patterns, caused delays in the monsoon cycle and extended the period of rainfall. This pattern affected the crop cycle.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 32% in Q3 FY25 from 23% a year ago due to higher branded sales share, but EBITDA was negative Rs 6 crore and net loss Rs 24 crore
items.quote: There was significant improvement in the gross margins from 23% in Q3 FY'24 to 32% in Q3 FY'25 due to higher sales of branded products.

items.statement: Management targets reducing fixed costs as percentage of sales and improving cost efficiency to stabilize financial performance
items.quote: We intend to tighten our belt by reducing costs, by optimizing our operations, and extracting maximum efficiencies.

items.statement: Preferential issue of Rs 150 crore allocated: Rs 50 crore for capex, Rs 100 crore for working capital; 25% received, balance 75% pending
items.quote: earlier for 200 crores, we had mentioned that 70 crores will go for CAPEX. But now for 150, we hav e mentioned that 50 crores will go for CAPEX and balance 100 crores will go for working capital

items.statement: Management consolidating sales team and regions to improve per-employee productivity after over-hiring did not yield expected results
items.quote: We will be consolidating all those and ensuring that the per-employee performance is much better than what we had this year.

items.statement: Product prices reduced ~20% year-on-year due to Chinese dumping and aggressive competition, triggering price war across sector
items.quote: Further, there was around 20% reduction in the product prices.

items.statement: Branded business grew 50-70% over last 2 years; patented products expected to reach 40-50% of branded sales in FY26 from ~35% now
items.quote: We should be anywhere between 40 to 50% of our overall branded business coming from our patented products.

items.statement: Target branded vs institutional mix maintained at 65-70% branded, 30-40% B2B for assured payment cycles and product balancing
items.quote: The optimum percentage output would be anywhere between 25 to 30% for the B2B. So, at this particular point of time, we wish to continue with the same strategy of maintaining a mix of around 65% to 70% as the branded business.

items.statement: Dealer productivity low at ~Rs 10 lakh/dealer/year vs peers at Rs 25-30 lakh; management targeting improved dealer wallet share and per-employee efficiency in FY26
items.quote: compared to each dealer our number is lesser. And also as we mentioned ea rlier that compared to the number of people we have, the per person efficiency also was

items.statement: Chinese dumping and aggressive pricing by competitors led to 20% price reduction and margin pressure across industry
items.quote: Increased competition drove down prices across the sector. The aggressive push for sales triggered a price war, further tightening margins across the industry.

items.statement: Income tax issue from September 2023 appears closed with no further notices or demands, though no formal closure letter received
items.quote: Whatever we had issue last year, later on there was no notices and no responses, anything from the income tax side and what we believe is and what we understand from the department as well that the issue is closed from there end.

items.statement: Forex loss of Rs 11 crore in Q3 due to USD-INR spike; ~Rs 400 crore foreign currency payables outstanding
items.quote: We have close to 400 crores worth of foreign currency payable which we have to do.

items.statement: First export order received; pipeline of export deals progressing to generate dollar inflows and hedge currency exposure
items.quote: I can be happy to say that we have got the first export order, which we started after some time and the number of queries and the number of deals which are in progress are a few.

items.statement: 9-month operating cash flow positive Rs 175 crore; Q3 cash flow Rs 32 crore; inventory reduced to Rs 700 crore from higher levels last year
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for 9 months was positive Rs. 175 crores and from this quarter it was around Rs. 32 crores.

items.statement: B2B working capital cycle 90-120 days; B2C also ~120 days; management focusing on cash discounts and working capital reduction
items.quote: In B2B, working capital days would be close to 90 to 120 days. Komal: and what about B2C? Management: B2C also we are falling in that range itself, close to 120 days

items.statement: Preferential issue of Rs 150 crore at Rs 640/share; 25% received; management confident balance 75% will come as share price recovers
items.quote: We have already received the 25% committed amount from the investors and with respect to balance, obviously, this is a long-term investment which our investors have shown on us.

items.statement: Strategic MoU with Shanghai E-Tong Chemical for joint R&D, manufacturing, product registration, and potential JV for global markets
items.quote: During this quarter, we have announced the formation of a strategic partnership between Best Agrolife and Shanghai E-Tong Chemical Co, which is a publicly listed agrochemical manufacturer based in Shanghai, China.

items.statement: New proprietary herbicide 'Shot Down' (Haloxyfop + Imazethapyr) on track for Q4 launch; another insecticide to see traction in rabi season
items.quote: We are on track for this thing. We are just finalizing the right strategy to be able to take this forward.

items.statement: Management acknowledges repeated guidance misses due to weather dependency, over-hiring, and B2C transition costs; taking corrective actions on cost and sales agility
items.quote: We have not been able to match the 20% numbers, what we have been saying since the last 6 months or so. But the main reason for this is that first, we have built up the team. However, the sales based on climatic conditions and the seasonal factors, we are not able to achieve that.

items.statement: Sustainable NIM expected between 7.5% to 9% on a year-over-year basis, targeting 8% to 9%
items.quote: The net interest margin is usually between 7.5% to 9% is what a sustainable NIM is.

items.statement: Strategic initiatives including potential fundraising to be disclosed by end of January 2025
items.quote: We're very hopeful that by the end of this month, there will be something definitive that we can disclose to all investors through an exchange filing.

items.statement: NIM improved to 8.7% in Q3 FY25 from 8.2% in Q2 FY25 and 6.7% in Q3 FY24, up for three consecutive quarters
items.quote: Our net interest margin which was a pain point for us in fiscal 23 and 24 has now risen for three consecutive quarters to 8.7% versus 8.2% in September 2024, and 6.7% in December 2023.

items.statement: AUM at Rs 11.5 billion, down from Rs 12.2 billion in Q2 FY25 but up 36% YoY; 61% gold loans, 33% MSME, 5% green energy
items.quote: Assets Under Management, stood at 11.5 billion, up from 8.5 billion a year ago, but down from 12.2 billion in September 24.

items.statement: Disbursements at Rs 2.18 billion in Q3 FY25 vs Rs 2.68 billion in Q2 FY25 and Rs 3 billion in Q3 FY24 due to selective credit approach and tighter liquidity
items.quote: Quarter-over-quarter interest income declined by 3% due to lower disbursements, which were 2.18 billion in the quarter versus 2.68 billion in September and 3 billion in the December quarter of last year.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.8% vs 2.6% in Q2 FY25; absolute GNPA up only 2.2% but percentage higher due to AUM decline; slippages Rs 83M vs Rs 162M, recoveries Rs 76M vs Rs 12M
items.quote: Gross NPAs on the entire book stood at 2.8% versus 2.6% in September 2024. Please note that on an absolute basis, gross NPAs went up only 2.2% but on a percentage basis, gross NPAs are higher because the AUM has declined from 12.2 billion to 11.5 billion in the quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan GNPA just over 1%; recovered Rs 8M in Q3, Rs 7M+ in Q4 so far, anticipate Rs 10-15M more by quarter end; auction recoveries >106% of dues
items.quote: Gross NPAs in the gold loan book are just over 1% . In the December quarter, we recovered 8 million in gold GNP A accounts, while in the first half of this quarter so far we have already recovered more than 7 million in gold NPAs. We anticipate further recoveries of 10 to 15 million by the end of this current quarter.

items.statement: MSME GNPA steady at Rs 33M QoQ; recoveries Rs 68M vs Rs 9M, slippages Rs 34M vs Rs 126M in Q2; additional Rs 32M recovered in Jan
items.quote: Gross NPAs in this portfolio around 33 million from the previous quarter, due to higher recoveries of 68 million versus 9 million in September 2024 . From Jan 1, until today we have recovered an additional 32 million which is an encouraging sign.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved to 2.6x from 2.8x; CAR at 26% vs 25.3%; borrowed Rs 60-70 crore in Q3; FY26 maturities ~Rs 210-212 crore, FY27 ~Rs 140 crore
items.quote: Lastly, the debt-to-equity ratio declined to 2.6x from 2.8x in the previous quarter, while the capital adequacy ratio stood at 26% versus 25.3% in September 24.

items.statement: Rs 40 crore raised from impact investor in December deployed for onward lending to MSME borrowers
items.quote: So, that was in the month of December, so that gets deployed in lending. So that is part of a debt agreement that we have, which is used for onward lending to MSME borrowers.

items.statement: LAAS partnerships contribute 45% of AUM; co-lending model: partner provides 80% capital at hurdle rate, Trucap keeps spread above hurdle plus full yield on 20%
items.quote: Increasing share of business from our lending -as-a-service partnerships, which today contributes to 45% of AUM.

items.statement: Green finance at 5% of AUM, growing steadily from Rs 50-60 lakh/month to Rs 8-10 crore/month over 5 quarters; focused on e-rickshaws with OEM/dealer tie-ups
items.quote: Now that number has gone up over the last five quarters from 50 to 60 lakhs a month to about 8 to 9 crores, and one month was also 10 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan LAAS yield typically 10-11%; no benefit yet from 25bps repo rate cut as transmission limited for smaller NBFCs
items.quote: For the gold loan product it's usually between 10% and 11%.

items.statement: 123 branches total, 78 broken even; branches with 2-2.5 years vintage average AUM >Rs 6.5 crore; breakeven at Rs 4.5-5 crore AUM
items.quote: Today we have 123 branches about 78 branches have broken even.

items.statement: Branch consolidation in Madhya Pradesh and Delhi (3-4 branches) to improve AUM per branch and profitability
items.quote: In terms of branches, there's been some amount of consolidation with the branches just so that the AUM per branch would go up, and the profitability of the branch could be reached in much better fashion. This consolidation has happened largely in two geographies, which is in Madhya Pradesh and in Delhi, where three to four branches have been consolidated.

items.statement: Gold loans: 57,000+ active customers, avg ticket Rs 0.13M, tenure 12 months, avg maturity 6-7 months; MSME: ~34,000 borrowers, avg ticket Rs 0.11M
items.quote: The gold loan business has an active customer base of more than 57,000 and an average ticket size of 0.13 million. The tenure of these loans and origination is usually 12 months, but the average maturity on the books is typically six to seven.

items.statement: New-to-credit borrowers declined from ~28,000 to ~21,000 due to lower disbursement volumes, not strategy shift
items.quote: It's also because the disbursement number has come down, right . So when you have a larger disbursement number, you have a larger count in terms of the number of borrowers you are funding as well.

items.statement: BC relationship with Shivalik SFB stopped from August due to RBI guidelines requiring gold to be kept with bank partner; fees income declined sharply
items.quote: Unfortunately, from August that relationship we have to stop business given the fact that with the RBI guidelines in a BC relationship on gold loan, the gold had to be kept with the partner who is contributing the capital, which is the bank.

items.statement: Applied for corporate agency license, awaiting regulatory response
items.quote: The license which you are asking is corporate agency license and we have applied for that. We are waiting for their reply and accordingly we will let everyone know.

items.statement: Gold loan LTV maintained at ~70%; cautious on higher gold prices due to downside risk to collateral value
items.quote: So, average LTV was about 70% and the gold levels also, gold prices have been going up, but it's you usually we use the average of the last 30 days in terms of disbursement for this thing.

items.statement: MSME credit environment cyclical; September quarter tough, December better with lower slippages/higher recoveries; hopeful trend continues but macro headwinds persist
items.quote: December turned out to be a better quarter in terms of the MSME space, where you can see it's evident in the slippages and the recoveries number, both of them were much better relativ e to the September quarter

items.statement: Tighter NBFC liquidity conditions and cautious credit environment leading to slower growth and lower disbursements
items.quote: The decline was due to a more selective credit approach, coupled with tighter liquidity in the NBFC sector.

items.statement: Brand ambassadors are employees; no plans for external branding; tech platform developed by third party but servers hosted on-premise at Andheri HO
items.quote: For us, our brand visibility and customer engagement, we truly believe our brand ambassadors are our team members themselves.

items.statement: No new LAAS partners currently; any additions will be disclosed via exchange filing
items.quote: Nothing for now. If there's something that we need to, if there is a certain addition, et cetera we would definitely let market participants know, by the way of an exchange filing.

items.statement: Management declined to comment on promoter stake sales
items.quote: The company would not like to comment on the promoter stake sale where you are running the business on a day-to-day basis as part of management.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target around INR300 crores
items.quote: Yes, FY25 will be closing around 300.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target around INR400 crores
items.quote: Yes, 26 will be doing 400.

items.statement: Medium-term target INR500 crores revenue in next three years
items.quote: Our target is to achieve INR500 crores revenue in the next three years

items.statement: Long-term target INR1,000 crores revenue in next five years
items.quote: and INR1,000 crores in the next five years

items.statement: Net profit margin target of 5% post-tax in next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our target is net profit post-tax is 5%.

items.statement: Current expansion capex of INR60 crores (INR30 crores civil, INR30 crores machinery)
items.quote: Approximately, the capex into the civil which is the land, building and machinery, we have spent it around INR30 crores and in machinery around another INR30 crores.

items.statement: Future capex of INR150 crores for INR1,000 crores revenue target
items.quote: We will be requiring a capex -- this land, building and machinery would be roughly INR150 crores.

items.statement: Adding 150,000 sq ft facility, 70% capacity increase, commissioning in 4 months
items.quote: We are creating a 1,50,000 square feet additional area and now the paint work is g oing on and it is at the final stages and once that is done, so then the machine ry installation would be there. So, roughly 4 months more time is required to commission that expansion

items.statement: Peak revenue capacity of INR500 crores post current expansion
items.quote: That's INR500 crores.

items.statement: Current order book of INR130 crores (INR40-45 crores global, rest domestic)
items.quote: Order book, currently, if you see, we are having INR130 crores approximately orders. Out of INR130 crores, INR40 crores, INR45 crores are from the global market and rest are from the

items.statement: 15-month visibility from concept to delivery, orders already booked for new capacity
items.quote: We have already booked the orders for the new capacity to come. As I explained, this process is 15 months from concept to delivery. So, we have all the visibilities in which month what we have to do

items.statement: 15 current brands, negotiations with new global customers for expanded capacity
items.quote: Currently, we have 15 brands with whom we are doing business but negotiations are in the process with a few other globally customers to take them onboard for the upcoming bigger capacities.

items.statement: Adidas T1 supplier for outerwear, Puma T1 supplier, new categories under development for Adidas
items.quote: Adidas, we are currently developing the new category like denims, beanies, and gloves for them.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 50% sweaters, 30% jackets/outerwear, 20% t-shirts and shoe uppers
items.quote: Approximately 50% revenue is comi ng from sweaters, 30% from jackets, outerwear jackets and 20% balance from t-shirts as well as the shoes for business

items.statement: EBITDA margin 9% in Q3 FY25, 10.03% in 9M FY25; improvement driven by overhead absorption and value-added products
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR9.02 crores, registering a 66.11% year-on-year increase, with an EBITDA margin of 9%.

items.statement: Gross margin varies by product: 12-15% manufacturing, 8-9% retail distribution
items.quote: It depends upon product to product. It comes to 15, it comes to 12. It depends on product to product.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle 200-220 days (90-120 days manufacturing, 90-120 days credit)
items.quote: The total cycle is about 200 to 220 days because 90 to 120 days we require, give the credit to the brand and 90 to 120 days depending on the product is the manufacturing cycle.

items.statement: INR32 crores debt out of INR60 crores capex, funded by internal accruals and bank debt
items.quote: Against INR60 crores we have taken a debt of INR32 crores.

items.statement: Solar power plant commissioned covering 15% of contract demand
items.quote: have already commissioned last mont h a solar power plant which is 15 % of my current contract demand from the power

items.statement: 40-person product development and design team
items.quote: Currently, we have around 40 people who are into the product development team, design and product development.

items.statement: No direct competitor in India offering full design-to-retail under one roof
items.quote: Yes, we assume that Active won't have any competitor within -- no company in India is offering all services under one roof.

items.statement: US tariffs on China/Mexico benefit India; no tariffs on India currently
items.quote: Since you see, currently, India will be more benefited from these tariffs. As of now, the U.S. Government is not considering to put something on India.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 total income INR100.22 crores, up 89.18% YoY; 9M FY25 INR228.36 crores, up 30.70% YoY
items.quote: During Q3 FY '25, we achieved a total income of INR100.22 crores, marking an impressive year-on-year growth of 89.18%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 PAT INR3.14 crores, up 222.83% YoY; PAT margin 3.14%, up 130 bps
items.quote: The PA T came in at INR3.14 crores, reflecting a remarkable year -on-year growth of 222.83%, with the PA T margin improving by 130 basis points to 3.14%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA INR22.90 crores, up 40.47% YoY; EBITDA margin 10.03%, up 70 bps
items.quote: Our EBITDA reached INR22.90 crores, growing by 40.47% year -on-year, with the EBITDA margin improving by 70 basis points to 10.03%.

items.statement: Business model requires 200-220 day working capital cycle, short-term borrowings INR92 crores vs equity INR72.8 crores
items.quote: This is the nature of business, as I explained that the total cycle is between 200 to 220 days, where 90 to 120 days, depending upon the product -to-product is required for the manufacturer of the product, and 90 to 120 days is credited into the market.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guided at INR650-670 crores
items.quote: FY '25, INR650 crores, INR670 crores, somewhere in that range we will be ending up.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guided at INR950-1,000 crores with EBITDA margin 17-19%
items.quote: We are expecting revenue in the range of about INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores for FY '26. At the minimum EBITDA range between 17% to 19%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,250-1,300 crores with EBITDA margin ~18%
items.quote: In FY '26, INR1,000 FY '27, which we assume that we will be running both the plant right from day 1 on a full capacity should be in the range of about INR1,250 crores to INR1,300 crores, again, EBITDA margin in the range of about 18% plus/minus one.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 volume growth guided at 30-35% aggregate
items.quote: Current quarter we should be having a volume growth, aggregate growth of about 30%, 35% by end of the year as an aggregate growth.

items.statement: Pakhajan plant expected >50% capacity from March 2025
items.quote: Our Pakhajan facility is now running smoothly, and we expect the plant to run at more than 50% capacity from March 2025 onwards.

items.statement: Pakhajan plant Q3 utilization ~30%, Q4 blended 35-40%
items.quote: Well, in December, we were almost close to 30% utilization, okay . But the sales did not materialize.

items.statement: Pakhajan plant exit utilization 85-90% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: By the last quarter, we will be exiting 85% to 90%...

items.statement: INR125 crore fundraise: INR50 crore debt repayment, INR75 crore for working capital and future expansion
